# Flare: Market and competitive analysis

Source data: docs/research/00-challenge-and-field.md (813 Week 1 entries read through DevRelay and DEV's pages, plus all 17 Weekend winners). Snapshot Sat 2026-10-10, 16:46 UTC. Counts are keyword matches; small counts were checked by hand.

## 1. The market we compete in

There are two markets this weekend.

1. **The judges' attention.** 813 entries and counting, one Overall prize. Judges weight Writing Quality most. The Weekend Overall winner had 27 reactions; reactions only break ties.
2. **The friend group's attention.** Flare competes with the group chat itself: "anyone around?" in iMessage, a Telegram poll, or nothing. These cost nothing and fail in the ways listed in the BRD.

## 2. What's crowded

| Pattern | Share of 813 | Why it hurts to be here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gemma via Ollama on a laptop | 51% mention Gemma, 50% use Ollama | The model is not a differentiator |
| Walk, trail or route planner | 23% of titles | Many near-identical names (TrailMate, TrailQuest, GrassQuest) |
| "AI that wants you to stop using it" | 22% of titles | The framing is now a cliché |
| Quest, scavenger hunt, game | 16% of titles | Often single-player with photo proof |
| Photo proof checked by a model | 6% | Also on our out-of-scope list |
| Gemma prize category | 31% name it | Lowest odds per entry |
| Render prize category | 17% mention Render | Second most crowded |

## 3. What's missing

| Gap | Count in 813 | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A quorum ("only happens if enough say yes") | 0 | No entry protects people from a public no |
| Real-time group play in the same place | about 3 to 5 real cases | IRL Clash (location-matched photo battles), a friends treasure hunt, a bingo with shared codes |
| Built for people with disabilities | about 2 | GroundSignal (wheelchair and stroller routes), Sport fit |
| Proof of deletion | 0 | Many claim privacy, none show an audit |
| Telegram as the channel | 1 product (EcoTrace AI) | Plus one Weekend winner (PaidYet, Temporal) |
| Says it was tested on an iPhone | 7 | Side Quest's iPhone 12 tab crashed mid-download; Drift is the clean case |
| Describes a real outdoor test | 84 (10%) | The prompt gives bonus points for it |
| Night, haptics, sound design | 4%, 2%, 8% | Polish few bother with |

## 4. Closest competitors

| Entry | Overlap with Flare | Where Flare differs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [IRL Clash](https://dev.to/someshcoding/irl-clash-go-outside-take-a-shot-win-the-battle-592i) | Multiplayer, location, outdoors | Strangers matched by distance; competitive; screen-heavy rounds. Flare is friends, cooperative, seconds of screen |
| [Drift](https://dev.to/codeswithroh/i-built-an-ai-that-only-works-when-my-phone-is-in-my-pocket-3ipn) | Gemma 4 E2B in iPhone Safari; screen-on counter | Single person. Flare reuses the "screen seconds" idea as a group metric |
| [Side Quest](https://dev.to/sizzlebop/i-built-an-ai-game-that-wants-you-to-go-outside-3a6k) | Gemma 4 E2B ONNX in the browser; second most reacted | Model runs on a desktop; iPhone failed. Flare must show it on real phones |
| [TrailSnack](https://dev.to/aaronstark1/trailsnack-a-trail-companion-that-runs-gemma-with-zero-bars-and-never-says-eat-this-pig) | Tiered models with a capability gate | Same tier idea; Flare reports which tier ran for every job |
| [Zero-Screen Dungeon Master](https://dev.to/vidisha_gupta_/zero-screen-dungeon-master-the-voice-only-rpg-where-your-real-walk-drives-the-story-3m68) | Pocket-first audio while walking | Single player, stories pre-generated on a laptop |
| [FieldIssue](https://dev.to/himanshu_748/fieldissue-take-a-walk-report-a-problem-come-back-with-evidence-e40) | Private groups, approvals | Civic reporting, hosted models, 12 claimed categories |
| Group chat polls (iMessage, Telegram) | Coordination | Public answers, no threshold, no shrink, no access info, nothing for no signal |

## 5. What wins (from the 17 Weekend winners)

1. A named person and their problem, in their words, near the top.
2. A table of measured results, including failures.
3. A "what broke" section with real bugs.
4. Model writes words; code owns facts.
5. One specific line per prize category.
6. A demo or video. Length doesn't matter (one winner had about 900 words). Claiming many categories doesn't help (one win per entry).

## 6. Where Flare wins

Flare does not win on the model. It wins on four things no entry combines, each backed by proof in the post:

1. **The quorum with no visible no.** It answers "nobody wants to show up alone" with a mechanism, not a nudge. Zero entries have it.
2. **It shrinks instead of dying (Ember).** A failed plan becomes 15 minutes at the nearest bench with one friend.
3. **Access as equals.** Needs stay on the phone; the phone counts you in for the Ember without telling anyone why. The invite photo is spoken for screen readers. A talking compass finds friends without a map or signal.
4. **Proof, not promises.** A field test with four people and a table; a deletion audit with zero rows; the AI tier that actually ran on each real iPhone.

## 7. Prize category stance

- **Target: Overall.** Every category is judged automatically; we list only the ones we genuinely use, with one specific line each.
- **Gemma:** we use it on the phone and on the laptop hub. List it, but don't build for it.
- **Render:** list only if the server that runs the Flare engine (solver, bot) runs on Render. A front end alone did not win last round.
- **MongoDB Atlas:** list only if the architect picks Atlas and it does something Atlas is good at (for example TTL indexes enforcing deletion). The SSPL point (MongoDB's own FAQ: "not approved by the OSI") goes in the decision record either way.
- **Entire:** honest fit if we embed this build's agent session. Don't chase it.
- **Sentry Agent Tracing, ElevenLabs, others:** not planned. ElevenLabs would add a closed voice; on-device speech fits the story better.

# Flare: Product requirements (PRD)

Owner: Product. Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Requirement IDs (FR-, NFR-) are referenced by the backlog (05-backlog.md) and must not be renumbered.

## 1. Problem

Friends who want to meet outside don't, because asking is awkward, nobody wants to arrive alone, plans stall in the chat, some can't use the spot, and phones lose signal where the good places are. See 01-brd.md.

## 2. Vision

**Snap where you are. If enough friends quietly say yes, it's on.**

A good session is about 5 seconds of screen and an hour outside. The place, the season, the light and the people are the point. The app gets out of the way.

## 3. Target users

- **Host:** someone already outside, or about to be, who wants company without the risk of asking in public.
- **Invitee:** a friend in the same chat who decides in seconds, privately.
- **Invitee with needs:** a friend with low vision, limited mobility, or who needs a restroom nearby.
- Personas and journeys: 04-personas-journeys.md.

## 4. Success metric

**Headcount:** people physically together because of a Flare (host plus arrivals). Every other metric (light rate, Ember save rate, screen seconds) serves it. Definitions: 07-kpis.md.

## 5. Non-goals

Accounts, passwords, profiles, feeds, followers, streaks, points, badges, comments, ratings, a "No" button, proof that you went outside, AI-written itineraries, money in the product, mesh radios or hardware, SOS or safety features, mobility-aid navigation.

## 6. The "less tech, more nature" test

Every feature passes this test before it ships:

1. Does it get someone outside or together sooner? If not, cut it.
2. How many seconds of screen does it add for each person? Write the number down.
3. Can it work with the screen off (audio, haptics, lock screen)? Prefer that.
4. Does it disappear when the Flare is Gone?

## 7. Core concepts

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Group | A set of friends sharing one link or Telegram chat. No accounts. A group key lives in the link fragment. |
| Flare | One invite to meet now at one spot. |
| Quorum | Yes-count needed to light. Default 2 (host plus 1). The host may pick 2, 3 or 4. |
| Kindling, Lit, Ember, Gone | The four states (section 8). |
| Spark | One line in a person's own words, left after a Flare by someone who showed up. Opt-in. |
| Tier | Where an AI job ran: phone, hub (our laptop) or rules. |

## 8. State machine (Flare mode)

All times are relative to the moment the host sends (t0).

| State | Enters when | What everyone sees | Leaves when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Kindling** | Host sends at t0 | Photo, short invite, spot name, walking time, "Need N more" | Quorum reached (to Lit) or t0 + 30 min (to Ember) |
| **Lit** | Yes-count (including host) reaches quorum, with all accepted conditions satisfiable | "It's lit." Host line, spot, compass | Host taps Done, or t0 + 4 h (to Gone) |
| **Ember** | Not lit at t0 + 30 min | "Smaller plan: 15 min at {bench}." Quorum becomes 2 (host plus 1) | One yes (to Lit, counted as an Ember save) or t0 + 60 min (to Gone) |
| **Gone** | Done, timeout, or Ember expired | Lit Flares: "Thanks for coming." Unlit: "Not this time." Same text for everyone | Terminal. Data deletion starts (FR-PRIV-5) |

Rules:

- **FR-STATE-1** Once Lit, a Flare stays Lit. Later "can't make it" taps lower the expected count but never change the state.
- **FR-STATE-2** "Need N more" counts only yeses whose conditions can be met together (FR-COND-4).
- **FR-STATE-3** Unlit Flares end with the identical "Not this time" for everyone, so nobody can tell who didn't answer.
- **FR-STATE-4** The Ember spot is the nearest bench (OSM `amenity=bench` or `leisure=picnic_table`) within 400 m of the original spot that fits the needs of everyone who said yes. If none qualifies, use the original spot.
- **FR-STATE-5** State changes are decided on the server by one clock. Phones show what the server says; an offline phone shows the last known state and the time it was known.
- **FR-STATE-6** The host can cancel during Kindling. That ends in "Not this time" for everyone.

## 9. Functional requirements

### 9.1 Create (host)

- **FR-CRE-1** Opening the app goes straight to the camera. One tap takes the photo.
- **FR-CRE-2** The spot is the phone's location at capture, snapped to the nearest named OSM feature within 150 m ("Ford Woods Park, by the pond"). If none is found, use reverse geocoding to a street name. Never show raw coordinates.
- **FR-CRE-3** The AI drafts an invite of 6 words or fewer and a spoken scene of 20 words or fewer from the photo (FR-AI-1). Both appear for review; the host can edit or accept. "Send" sends.
- **FR-CRE-4** Quorum defaults to 2. One tap cycles 2, 3, 4. No other settings on this screen.
- **FR-CRE-5** Send produces three outputs at once: the link, the Telegram post (if the group uses the bot), and the plain-text version (FR-CH-4).
- **FR-CRE-6** Target: 15 screen seconds or less from open to sent.
- **FR-CRE-7** The host line defaults to "{Host} is waiting at {spot}." The host can change it.

### 9.2 Respond (invitee)

- **FR-RES-1** The link opens in Safari with no install and no account. It shows: photo, invite line, spot, walking time from the invitee's location (if they allow location), "Need N more", and one button: "I'm in".
- **FR-RES-2** "I'm in" is private. Nobody else sees who tapped. The only public signal is the count.
- **FR-RES-3** "Add a condition" is a small text link under the button. Free text, typed or dictated (FR-COND).
- **FR-RES-4** There is no No button. Not answering is the only way to decline.
- **FR-RES-5** After "I'm in", the screen says "You're in. We'll buzz you when it's lit." and can be closed. A web push notification (if allowed) or the Telegram bot announces Lit.
- **FR-RES-6** Target: 10 screen seconds or less from opening the link to "I'm in".
- **FR-RES-7** Before Lit, a person can take back their yes ("Take it back"). After Lit, the button becomes "Can't make it" (FR-STATE-1).

### 9.3 Conditions

- **FR-COND-1** Supported condition types: `with(person)` ("only if Amor comes"), `after(time)`, `back_by(time)`, `max_walk(minutes)`.
- **FR-COND-2** The phone parses free text into rules (FR-AI-2) and reads them back in one sentence: "Got it: only with Amor, back by 5 PM. Right?" with "Yes" and "Fix it".
- **FR-COND-3** Only the structured rule is sent. The free text never leaves the phone.
- **FR-COND-4** The solver picks the largest group whose rules can all be met. Ties go to more people, then the earlier start. A yes whose rules can't be met still counts toward nothing and is never shown as a no.
- **FR-COND-5** Unparseable text gets "I didn't catch that. Try 'after 2' or 'only with Amor'." and the yes stays unconditional only if the person confirms.

### 9.4 Lit and getting there

- **FR-LIT-1** On Lit, every yes gets a notification or bot message: "It's lit. {Host} is at {spot}."
- **FR-LIT-2** The Lit screen shows the host line, spot, walking time, the access line (FR-ACC-1) and two buttons: "Find them" (compass) and "I'm here".
- **FR-LIT-3** Everything needed after Lit (spot, compass target, access line, host line) is saved on the phone at the moment of Lit, so it works with no signal (FR-OFF-1).
- **FR-LIT-4** "I'm here" is tapped by the arriving person or by the host (+1 for each arrival, including friends without a phone). Headcount = host + arrivals, capped at yes-count + host + 3.
- **FR-LIT-5** The host taps "Done" when the group leaves. If nobody does, Gone at t0 + 4 h.

### 9.5 Talking compass

- **FR-CMP-1** The compass points from the person to the host's spot (or, if the host shares live location, to the host). It shows an arrow and distance, and speaks: "Fuego, 400 meters, slightly left."
- **FR-CMP-2** Speech repeats when the bearing changes by 30° or more, the distance halves, or every 60 s, whichever comes first. A haptic tick plays when facing within 15° of the target.
- **FR-CMP-3** It works with the screen locked where iOS allows audio to continue, and with no map tiles and no signal (target saved at Lit).
- **FR-CMP-4** Copy says what it is: "Finds your friend. Not for navigation or emergencies."
- **FR-CMP-5** The host's live location is opt-in, shared only while Lit, and only to people who said yes. It is never stored after Gone.

### 9.6 Access

- **FR-ACC-1** Access line: within 200 m of the spot, show counts and nearest distance from OSM: benches, restrooms, drinking water, and whether the walking route from the invitee has mapped steps. Example: "Bench 40 m · Restroom 180 m · No steps mapped".
- **FR-ACC-2** Needs profile, set once, stored only on the phone: avoid steps, max distance between rests (100, 200, 400 m), need a restroom within 300 m.
- **FR-ACC-3** If the spot fails a person's needs, their "I'm in" shows "This spot may not suit you. Count me in for a closer one?" If they agree, their yes counts only toward an Ember at a spot that fits. Nobody else learns why.
- **FR-ACC-4** Spoken scene: the invite photo carries the AI scene description (20 words or fewer) as alt text, read by VoiceOver.
- **FR-ACC-5** The whole respond flow and the compass work with VoiceOver, Dynamic Type up to the largest size, Reduce Motion, and without colour as the only signal.

### 9.7 Nature line

- **FR-NAT-1** Each Flare shows one line worth noticing, built only from real data: sunset time ("Sunset 6:57 PM"), a named natural feature from OSM within 200 m (water, a named tree, woods), or the season. Never invented. No AI-written facts.

### 9.8 After (Sparks)

- **FR-SPK-1** After Done, each person who tapped "I'm here" may write one line (140 characters or fewer) in their own words. No AI writing, no AI editing.
- **FR-SPK-2** Sparks are opt-in, encrypted with the group key, tied to the place name (not the pin), and shown on later Flares at the same place: "Your group met here 2 times." plus one Spark.
- **FR-SPK-3** The Spark prompt appears once and can be dismissed. It never reminds.

### 9.9 Channels

- **FR-CH-1** Link page (core): works in any chat. Full experience in Safari. Installable to the Home Screen.
- **FR-CH-2** Telegram bot: posts the invite to the group with a live "Need N more"; private yes via an inline button that opens a private chat or the link; conditions by private message; posts "It's lit"; deletes its own posts at Gone. Members tap Start once.
- **FR-CH-3** Until the founder approves wider use, the bot posts only in the private "Flare test" group.
- **FR-CH-4** Plain text, 200 bytes or fewer, for SMS or satellite texting: `FLARE K7Q2 Ford Woods Park pond. Need 1 more. Reply IN K7Q2. Ends 3:40PM`. A reply of `IN K7Q2` relayed by any group member through the link page counts as a yes.
- **FR-CH-5** iMessage and WhatsApp use the link with a rich preview (photo blurred, invite line, "Need N more"). The preview image must not reveal the exact location.

### 9.10 No signal

- **FR-OFF-1** After Lit, the phone stores the spot, compass target, access line, host line and nature line. The Lit screen works in airplane mode.
- **FR-OFF-2** An outbox stores taps made offline ("I'm here", "Done", a Spark) and sends them when signal returns. Each has an idempotency key; repeats are ignored.
- **FR-OFF-3** On-phone AI works offline after a one-time download on Wi-Fi.
- **FR-OFF-4** OSM data is fetched live and cached for 7 days. A ready pack for the Fairlane area ships with the app.
- **FR-OFF-5** The app shows "Offline. Saved at 2:14 PM." when it is working from stored data.

### 9.11 AI jobs

| ID | Job | Input | Output | Fallback tiers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FR-AI-1 | Photo to invite + spoken scene | Photo | Invite (6 words or fewer), scene (20 words or fewer) | Phone (Gemma 4 E2B in browser) → hub (Gemma 4 E4B via Ollama) → rules ("Outside at {spot}. Come?") |
| FR-AI-2 | Conditions to rules | Free text | JSON rules (FR-COND-1) | Phone → hub → regex rules for common phrases |
| FR-AI-3 | Needs check summary | Needs profile + OSM features | Pass or fail per need | Rules only (deterministic, no model) |

- **FR-AI-4** Every output is validated against a schema and length limit. Invalid output falls to the next tier.
- **FR-AI-5** Never describe faces, identities, age, race, or bodies. The prompt forbids it and a filter removes person words beyond "a person" or "people".
- **FR-AI-6** The tier that ran is recorded per job (as a counter) and shown in a small "made on this phone" note.
- **FR-AI-7** The phone tier is chosen by a runtime capability check (WebGPU present, adapter limits, memory hints, a timed warm-up), never by phone model name.
- **FR-AI-8** The model download is opt-in, on Wi-Fi, with size shown first. If it fails or stalls, the app keeps working on the next tier.

### 9.12 Privacy

- **FR-PRIV-1** Photos are encrypted on the phone with the group key. The key lives only in the link fragment (after `#`), which browsers do not send to the server.
- **FR-PRIV-2** Free-text conditions and needs profiles never leave the phone.
- **FR-PRIV-3** Who said yes is held only for the solve and to send Lit messages. It is never shown to others, and is deleted at Gone.
- **FR-PRIV-4** No accounts, no names on the server. Display names are encrypted with the group key.
- **FR-PRIV-5** Within 5 minutes of Gone, the server deletes the Flare record, the photo ciphertext, yes records, rules and live locations. Only counters remain (07-kpis.md) plus opt-in encrypted Sparks.
- **FR-PRIV-6** A deletion audit script lists every store and returns the count of remaining records per Flare. The post shows its output after the field test.
- **FR-PRIV-7** The privacy page states the limits honestly: Telegram sees what's posted in Telegram; in small groups people can sometimes guess who said yes; SMS and satellite texts are outside our control.

### 9.13 Capability page

- **FR-CAP-1** A page at `/check` shows, for the phone it runs on: iOS and Safari version, WebGPU yes/no and adapter info, storage estimate, geolocation, compass (device orientation), speech synthesis, web push, which AI tier would run, and a timed test of each. One button copies the report.

### 9.14 Website

- **FR-WEB-1** Pages: Home (what Flare is, in one screen), How it works (the four states), Privacy (promises and limits, the audit), Accessibility (statement, what we tested, known gaps), Run it yourself (self-hosting steps, license).
- **FR-WEB-2** The site follows the same copy rules and loads in under 2 s on a mid-range phone on 4G.

## 10. Non-functional requirements

- **NFR-1 Speed:** link page interactive in 2 s or less on iPhone 13 over 4G; "I'm in" acknowledged in 500 ms or less (optimistic UI).
- **NFR-2 Size:** link page JavaScript 150 KB gzipped or less before any model.
- **NFR-3 Accessibility:** WCAG 2.2 AA for every screen; VoiceOver flows tested on a real iPhone.
- **NFR-4 Reliability:** state changes survive a server restart. Duplicate taps are harmless.
- **NFR-5 Security:** no secrets in the client; the bot token and database credentials live only on the server.
- **NFR-6 Open source:** code under AGPL-3.0 (founder preference) so modified servers must publish source and the deletion promise stays checkable. The architect confirms.
- **NFR-7 Brand and feel:** full brand, motion and sound, premium on every phone. Motion respects Reduce Motion; sound respects the silent switch.
- **NFR-8 Copy:** buttons 3 words or fewer; messages 12 words or fewer; warm, a bit playful, always clear.

## 11. Plan mode

Plan mode ("Sunday afternoon outside?", a 4-step ladder, "I'm fading") is **Later**. The engine is designed so a Plan is a Flare with a deadline and a ladder of spots; the state machine and solver must not assume a single spot forever. See 06-scope.md.

# Flare: Personas and key journeys

Personas are composites, not our four testers. Names are invented so no real friend is labelled. Screen seconds are targets the journey must meet.

## Personas

### P1. Jo, the host (24)
- Walks to the park most weekends. Tired of "anyone around?" getting two thumbs-up and nobody showing.
- Wants: company without a public ask. Hates: chasing people.
- Phone: recent iPhone, good battery.

### P2. Sam, the lazy friend (25)
- Likes the group, rarely says yes first. Will come if it's clearly happening and close.
- Wants: to decide in one tap, without committing in front of everyone. Hates: long threads, being the only one who replies.
- Phone: iPhone 13, often on low battery.

### P3. Priya, low vision (29)
- Uses VoiceOver and large text. Can't see invite photos in chats, so she skips them.
- Wants: to know what the place looks like and to find her friends on arrival. Hates: maps she can't read, "it's by the thing".

### P4. Linda, older parent with a bad knee (63)
- Walks fine for 10 minutes, then needs to sit. Avoids steps. Says "you go ahead" rather than explain.
- Wants: to join without making it about her knee. Hates: being the reason a plan changes.

### P5. The group heading to no signal
- Four friends going to woods with patchy coverage. They lose each other at the trailhead.
- Wants: the plan to hold after the bars go. Hates: "where are you?" texts that never send.

## Journeys

### J1. Jo lights a Flare (host, happy path)
1. Jo is at the pond in Ford Woods Park. Opens Flare. Camera is already on. Taps once. (2 s)
2. Draft appears: "Golden pond, come sit" and the spot "Ford Woods Park, by the pond". Jo taps Send. (4 s)
3. Phone goes back in the pocket. Screen total: about 6 s.
4. 7 minutes later: buzz. "It's lit. Sam is coming."
5. Sam arrives. Jo taps "I'm here" for Sam (or Sam does). Headcount 2.
6. 70 minutes later Jo taps Done. Gone. Data deleted within 5 minutes.

Done when: Jo spent 15 s or less on screen; headcount recorded; audit shows 0 records for this Flare.

### J2. Sam says yes without saying it out loud (lazy friend)
1. Telegram shows the bot post: photo, "Golden pond, come sit", "Need 1 more".
2. Sam taps the post's "I'm in" button. Private. (3 s)
3. Bot replies privately: "You're in. We'll buzz you when it's lit."
4. Lit message arrives. Sam opens the link once to see walking time: 9 min. Locks phone. Walks.
5. If Sam had ignored it, the Flare would have ended with "Not this time" for everyone, and nobody would know Sam saw it.

Done when: Sam's screen time to "I'm in" is 10 s or less; no one else can tell whether Sam answered.

### J3. Priya hears the invite and finds the group (low vision)
1. iMessage link arrives. VoiceOver reads the preview: "Flare: Golden pond, come sit. Need 1 more."
2. Opens the link. VoiceOver reads the photo: "A pond with yellow trees and an empty bench." Then the access line: "Bench 40 meters. Restroom 180 meters. No steps mapped."
3. Double-taps "I'm in". Adds a condition by dictation: "after two". Hears: "Got it: after 2 PM. Right?" Double-taps Yes.
4. Lit. On arrival near the park, taps "Find them". Phone in hand at her side, she hears "Jo, 120 meters, slightly left", then a tick when facing the spot.
5. Taps "I'm here".

Done when: every step works with VoiceOver and the largest text size; she never needed to see the photo or a map.

### J4. Linda joins without explaining her knee
1. Earlier, Linda set her needs once: avoid steps, rest every 200 m, restroom within 300 m. They live only on her phone.
2. Jo's Flare is at a lookout with stairs. Linda's phone checks the spot against her needs and fails it.
3. Linda sees: "This spot may not suit you. Count me in for a closer one?" She taps Yes.
4. Nobody else sees anything different. Her yes counts only for an Ember.
5. 30 minutes pass without Lit. The Flare becomes an Ember: "Smaller plan: 15 min at the bench by the lot." That bench fits Linda's needs. Her yes now counts. Quorum is 2. It lights.
6. Jo walks down to the bench. Headcount 2. It counts as an Ember save.

Done when: no screen, message or log available to others reveals why Linda's yes moved; the Ember spot met all her needs.

### J5. The group walks out of coverage (no signal)
1. Flare lights at the trailhead lot with full signal. Every phone saves spot, compass target, access line and host line at Lit.
2. They walk in. Bars drop to zero. Ammo-style latecomer opens the Lit screen in airplane mode: it shows "Offline. Saved at 2:14 PM." and the compass still points to the saved spot.
3. Latecomer taps "I'm here" offline. It waits in the outbox.
4. On the way back, signal returns. The outbox sends; the server ignores the duplicate tap from the host who also counted them.
5. A friend without data sent `IN K7Q2` by SMS to the host before the walk; the host's link page relayed it.

Done when: the Lit screen and compass work in airplane mode; outbox delivers exactly once; headcount is correct after sync.

### J6. Nothing comes together
1. Jo sends a Flare with quorum 3. One yes in 30 minutes.
2. Ember: "Smaller plan: 15 min at the bench by the pond." Quorum 2. Nobody else answers by t0 + 60.
3. Everyone who could see it gets "Not this time." Same words for all.
4. Gone. Deleted. No record of who saw it or answered.

Done when: the final message is identical for all; audit shows 0 records.

# Flare: Prioritized backlog

Priority: **P0** must work in the Sunday 10 AM release candidate. **P1** must ship before the DEV deadline (Mon 06:59 UTC). **P2** Later. Each story lists its PRD requirements, the screen seconds it adds per person, and acceptance criteria (AC) written so QA can test them.

## E1. Flare engine (server) — P0

**E1-S1 Create a Flare.** As a host, I send a Flare so friends can join. (FR-CRE-5, FR-STATE-5)
- AC1: POST with encrypted photo, spot name, quorum (2 to 4) returns a Flare id and short code (4 to 5 characters, no ambiguous letters) in under 500 ms.
- AC2: State is Kindling with yes-count 1 (the host).
- AC3: Quorum outside 2 to 4 is rejected with a clear error.

**E1-S2 Timed transitions.** (FR-STATE table)
- AC1: Not lit at t0 + 30 min → Ember with quorum 2 and the Ember spot set (E6-S3).
- AC2: Ember not lit at t0 + 60 min → Gone.
- AC3: Lit Flare → Gone on Done or at t0 + 4 h.
- AC4: Transitions run from a server-side scheduler that survives a restart (test: restart mid-Kindling, transition still fires within 60 s of its time).

**E1-S3 Yes, take back, can't make it.** (FR-RES-2, FR-RES-7, FR-STATE-1)
- AC1: A yes with the same idempotency key twice counts once.
- AC2: Take back before Lit lowers the count; after Lit the state stays Lit.
- AC3: No API returns who said yes to anyone but the solver.

**E1-S4 Solver.** (FR-COND-4, FR-STATE-2)
- AC1: Given yes records with rules, returns the largest set whose rules all hold, tie-broken by size then earliest start.
- AC2: Unit tests cover: no rules; `with` chains (A only with B, B only with C); conflicting times; `max_walk`; a yes that can never be satisfied.
- AC3: "Need N more" equals quorum minus the solver's set size, never below 0.

**E1-S5 Deletion at Gone.** (FR-PRIV-5)
- AC1: Within 5 minutes of Gone, the Flare record, yes records, rules, photo ciphertext and live locations are deleted from every store.
- AC2: Only the counters in 07-kpis.md remain, keyed by an opaque group id.
- AC3: Deletion is enforced in two ways: an explicit delete job and a storage-level expiry (TTL or equivalent) set at creation to t0 + 5 h.

**E1-S6 Deletion audit.** (FR-PRIV-6)
- AC1: A script lists every store and prints remaining records per Flare id and in total.
- AC2: After the field test it prints 0 for every Flare record, photo and rule. Output is saved for the post.

## E2. Host flow (app) — P0

**E2-S1 Camera first.** (FR-CRE-1) Adds 2 s.
- AC1: Opening the installed app shows a live camera within 1.5 s on iPhone 13.
- AC2: One tap captures; retake is one tap.
- AC3: If camera permission is denied, show "Pick a photo" and the photo library.

**E2-S2 Spot naming.** (FR-CRE-2)
- AC1: Names the nearest OSM named feature within 150 m; falls back to street name; never shows coordinates.
- AC2: Works offline in the Fairlane pack area.

**E2-S3 Draft and send.** (FR-CRE-3, FR-CRE-4, FR-CRE-6) Adds 4 s.
- AC1: Invite and scene drafts appear within 6 s on the phone tier, 4 s on the hub tier, instantly on the rules tier.
- AC2: Quorum chip cycles 2, 3, 4.
- AC3: Median host time open-to-sent is 15 s or less over 5 trials.

**E2-S4 Share outputs.** (FR-CRE-5, FR-CH-4, FR-CH-5)
- AC1: After Send, the iOS share sheet opens with the link; a "Copy text" action copies the 200-byte plain-text version.
- AC2: The plain text is 200 bytes or fewer in UTF-8 for every spot name in the Fairlane pack (test all).
- AC3: Link preview shows a blurred photo and no coordinates.

**E2-S5 Host controls while Kindling and Lit.** (FR-STATE-6, FR-LIT-4, FR-LIT-5)

- AC2: "+1" adds an arrival; "Done" ends the Flare.

## E3. Invitee flow (link page) — P0

**E3-S1 Open and understand.** (FR-RES-1) Adds 5 s.

**E5-S3 Read-back.** (FR-COND-2, FR-COND-3) P0. Adds 3 s for those who use it.

**E6-S2 Access line.** (FR-ACC-1)
- AC1: Counts and nearest distance for benches, restrooms, drinking water within 200 m from OSM.

**E6-S5 Accessibility pass.** (FR-ACC-5, NFR-3)
- AC1: J3 completes on a real iPhone with VoiceOver on, recorded on video.
- AC2: axe-core shows 0 serious or critical issues on every screen.

**E7-S1 Bearing and distance.** (FR-CMP-1, FR-CMP-3)
- AC1: Uses device orientation (with the iOS permission prompt) and GPS; distance within 10 m of a reference at 100 m, bearing within 20° outdoors.
- AC2: Works in airplane mode with the saved target.

**E7-S2 Speech and haptics.** (FR-CMP-2)
- AC1: Speaks on the triggers in FR-CMP-2, using on-device speech synthesis.
- AC2: Haptic tick when within 15° (where the device supports vibration; iOS Safari limits are documented).

**E7-S3 Host live location.** (FR-CMP-5) P1.
- AC1: Opt-in, only while Lit, only to yeses; deleted at Gone.

**E8-S4 "Made on this phone" note.** (FR-AI-6) P0. Adds 0 s (passive).

# Flare: KPI definitions

Principle: we measure the group outcome, never the person. No KPI stores a name, phone number, location, photo, free text or a per-person history. Everything below is a counter or a bucketed number keyed by an opaque Flare id (deleted at Gone) and rolled up into an opaque group counter (kept).

## Stored counters (the only data that survives Gone)

Per group (opaque id, random, not derived from any personal data):

| Counter | Incremented when |
| --- | --- |
| `flares_created` | A Flare is created |
| `flares_lit` | A Flare enters Lit from Kindling |
| `embers` | A Flare enters Ember |
| `embers_lit` | An Ember enters Lit |
| `headcount_sum` | At Gone, by the Flare's final headcount (Lit Flares only) |
| `headcount_max` | Max of final headcounts |
| `screen_host_bucket[b]` | One per Flare: host's screen-seconds bucket |
| `screen_invitee_bucket[b]` | One per yes: invitee's screen-seconds bucket |
| `tier_ran[job][tier]` | Each AI job run, by tier (phone, hub, rules) |
| `lit_minutes_sum` | At Gone, minutes from Lit to Done (or timeout) |

Buckets for screen seconds: 0 to 5, 6 to 10, 11 to 20, 21 to 40, 41 to 90, over 90.

## KPI 1. Headcount (north star)

- **Definition:** for a Lit Flare, host (1) + arrivals tapped via "I'm here" or host "+1", capped at yes-count + 4.
- **Report:** sum and median per period; max.
- **Measured from:** `headcount_sum`, count of Lit Flares, `headcount_max`.
- **Not stored:** who arrived.
- **Known bias:** relies on taps. Undercounts if nobody taps; the host "+1" reduces this.

## KPI 2. Light rate

- **Definition:** Flares that reach Lit (directly or via Ember) ÷ Flares created.
- **Formula:** (`flares_lit` + `embers_lit`) ÷ `flares_created`.
- **Also report:** direct light rate = `flares_lit` ÷ `flares_created`.

## KPI 3. Ember save rate

- **Definition:** Embers that light ÷ Embers.
- **Formula:** `embers_lit` ÷ `embers`.
- **Report with n.** With 1 to 3 Embers on Sunday, report counts, not a percentage alone.

## KPI 4. Screen seconds

- **Definition:** seconds the Flare UI is visible and the screen is on, per person per Flare, from first open to the moment they're done:
  - Host: from app open to Send, plus any later foreground time on that Flare, excluding time the compass is in use.
  - Invitee: from first open of the link to "I'm in" (decision time), and total foreground time on that Flare excluding compass time.
- **How:** measured on the phone with the Page Visibility API and foreground timestamps. The phone sends only the bucket index at Gone (or with its last tap). No raw timestamps leave the phone.
- **Targets:** host decision 15 s or less; invitee decision 10 s or less (median).
- **Why compass time is excluded:** it's used to find people outside and is designed to work with the screen down. It is reported separately as its own bucket.

## KPI 5. Time together (supporting)

- **Definition:** minutes from Lit to Done for Lit Flares.
- **Formula:** `lit_minutes_sum` ÷ (`flares_lit` + `embers_lit`).

## KPI 6. Tier coverage (supporting)

- **Definition:** share of AI job runs per tier.
- **From:** `tier_ran`.

## What we never measure

Who said yes, who didn't answer, who arrived, where anyone was, how long a specific person looked at the screen, conditions text, needs, photos.

## Field test reporting

`E13-S2` exports a table for Sunday 11 AM to 3 PM ET: Flares created, lit, embers, embers lit, headcount per Lit Flare, screen-second bucket counts for hosts and invitees, tier counts per job, lit minutes. This table goes into the post as-is.

# Flare: Release plan

All times ET (EDT, UTC-4). Fixed points: release candidate Sun 10:00 AM; field test Sun 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM; DEV deadline Mon 2:59 AM ET (Sun 11:59 PM PDT, Mon 06:59 UTC). Sunset Sun 6:57 PM.

Roles hand over in order; each milestone ends with a handoff in docs/handoffs/ and a commit.

| # | Milestone | Owner | Done when | Target |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| M0 | Field scan | Research | docs/research/00 | Sat (done) |
| M1 | Product requirements | Product | docs/product/01 to 10, handoff 01 | Sat (this) |
| M2 | Analysis: requirement traceability, data and edge cases | Analyst | Every FR traced to a story and test; open questions closed | Sat evening |
| M3 | Brand and UX design | Design | Brand, screens for every story, motion and sound specs, copy deck | Sat night |
| M4 | Architecture and decisions | Engineering lead | Stack chosen with latest stable versions; storage decision (Postgres vs Atlas incl. SSPL); lab spikes reviewed | Sat night |
| M5 | Build P0 | Engineering, AI, maps, PWA | All P0 stories meet AC on a laptop and one iPhone | Sun 8:00 AM |
| M6 | QA and security pass on P0 | QA, Security | P0 AC pass; no high-severity issues | Sun 9:30 AM |
| M7 | Release candidate | Ops | Deployed (after founder's yes) to an unlisted HTTPS URL; bot in "Flare test" only; `/check` run on all four phones | **Sun 10:00 AM** |
| M8 | Field test | Everyone | Checklist complete; KPI export saved; consent recorded | **Sun 11 AM to 3 PM** |
| M9 | Fixes and P1 | Engineering | P1 stories meet AC; field bugs logged in BUGLOG | Sun 7:00 PM |
| M10 | Deletion audit and metrics | Ops, Security | Audit prints 0 rows; KPI table final | Sun 7:30 PM |
| M11 | Website and docs final | Docs | Five pages live (after yes); README notes any post-deadline commits rule | Sun 9:00 PM |
| M12 | DEV post draft | Docs, Product | Template followed; tables; what broke; agent session embedded | Sun 10:30 PM |
| M13 | Founder review and publish | Founder | Founder says yes; published | **Before Mon 2:00 AM** (1 h buffer) |

## Gates

- **Go/no-go for the field test (Sun 10:00 AM):** E1, E2, E3, E4-S1, E6-S2, E7-S1, E9-S1 pass AC on at least two of the four phones. If not, test what works and record what didn't; the post reports it.
- **Publish gate:** deletion audit output, KPI table, tier table, consent checklist all present.

## Approvals needed from the founder (asked one at a time, each prepared as one step)

1. Deploy the release candidate to Render (unlisted URL).
2. Allow the bot beyond "Flare test" (not planned this weekend).
3. Make the GitHub repo public (needed for the post's Code section).
4. Deploy the website.
5. Publish the DEV post.
6. Upload the demo video and make the agent session public.

# Flare: Risk register

Scale: likelihood and impact are Low, Medium, High. Owner is the role that holds the mitigation.

| ID | Risk | L | I | Mitigation | Trigger to act | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | Gemma 4 E2B (about 3.2 GB) won't load in iPhone Safari; Side Quest's iPhone 12 tab died about 500 MB into a 3.4 GB download | High | Medium | Capability check picks the tier at runtime; hub and rules tiers always work; test runtimes and formats early in lab (Drift ran E2B in iPhone Safari via MediaPipe at 2.5 GB); report the tier honestly | `/check` fails on a phone Sunday 9 AM | AI |
| R2 | iPhone 13 has 4 GB RAM; large model kills the tab | High | Low | Never auto-download; size shown first; hub tier for that phone | Memory warning or tab reload during warm-up | AI |
| R3 | The laptop hub is unreachable from phones in the field (no shared network) | Medium | Medium | Hub reachable through the deployed server as a relay, or the rules tier; drafts are optional, never blocking | Hub ping fails at 10 AM | Engineering |
| R4 | Web push on iOS needs the app on the Home Screen and permission | High | Medium | Telegram for two testers; open link page polls; host line tells people where to go regardless | Push test fails at RC | PWA |
| R5 | Compass is inaccurate (magnetic interference, iOS orientation permission) | Medium | Medium | Ask permission on a tap; show "Hold flat" hint; speak distance even when bearing is unsure; test in the open | Bearing error over 30° in test | Maps |
| R6 | Small groups can guess who said yes or didn't | High | Low | State it plainly on the privacy page; identical "Not this time"; no timestamps shown per yes | Always true; disclose | Product |
| R7 | Deletion misses a store (logs, backups, bot messages, CDN cache) | Medium | High | Inventory every store in architecture; storage-level expiry plus delete job; no request bodies in logs; audit covers all stores; bot deletes its posts | Audit shows any nonzero | Security |
| R8 | Founder approvals arrive late, blocking the RC | Medium | High | Prepare each approval as one step with what, where and why; ask at 9:30 AM for the 10 AM deploy | No reply by 9:45 AM | Ops |
| R9 | Weather on Sunday (rain, cold) | Medium | Medium | Ember to a covered bench if mapped; the test still measures the flow; report conditions | Forecast check Sunday 8 AM | Product |
| R10 | Scope is large for the time left | High | High | P0 list is the gate; P1 after the test; every Later item stays later; honest "what didn't ship" in the post | M5 slips past 8 AM | Product |
| R11 | Overpass API mirrors fail (seen Oct 10) | Medium | Medium | Ship the Fairlane pack; cache 7 days; send a User-Agent; fall back between mirrors | Fetch errors | Maps |
| R12 | Telegram bot posts somewhere it shouldn't | Low | High | Hard allow-list of the "Flare test" chat id in code; test that other chats are refused | Any post outside the group | Engineering |
| R13 | AI describes a person's face or body | Medium | High | Prompt rule, output filter, 20-photo test with people in frame | Any test output fails | AI |
| R14 | Secrets leak via logs, client or the agent session embed | Low | High | Server-only secrets; scrub the session before making it public; secret scan before every push | Scanner hit | Security |
| R15 | Our post reads like the 22% "AI that wants you to stop using it" entries | Medium | High | Lead with the four friends and the quorum; numbers from the field test; avoid the cliché phrasing | Draft review | Docs |
| R16 | MongoDB Atlas weakens the "open" story (SSPL not OSI-approved) | Medium | Low | Architect weighs Postgres vs Atlas on the merits and records the decision and the license fact | Decision record | Engineering lead |

## Glossary

| Term | Meaning |

## Key decisions and why

1. **Headcount is the north star.** It's the one number that means people were together. Everything else serves it.
2. **Flare mode only; Plan mode Later.** Founder marked Plan as later and Sunday tests "now" Flares. The engine must stay ladder-ready (a Flare holds a list of spots, not one).
3. **Timers: Kindling 30 min, Ember 30 min, Lit until Done or t0 + 4 h.** Ember quorum 2 at the nearest suitable bench within 400 m.
4. **Every AI job has three tiers (phone, hub, rules), chosen at runtime.** Rules and hub are P0; phone is P1 and enters the RC only if it's reliable by 10 AM Sunday. The tier that ran is always recorded.
5. **Privacy is built into the data model, not the copy.** Free text and needs stay on the phone; photos are encrypted with a key in the URL fragment; everything per-Flare is deleted within 5 minutes of Gone; only group counters remain.
6. **Accessibility is P0,** because two of five personas depend on it and it's one of the four things no other entry does.
7. **Evidence:** two founder figures are not usable as-is. The IPA page doesn't contain "45% have lied about why". Axios and CDC returned 403, so they need re-verification before the post cites them.

## What the analyst must do next

1. **Traceability matrix:** every FR and NFR in 03-prd.md maps to at least one story in 05-backlog.md and at least one test. Flag any requirement without a story, and any story without a requirement.
2. **Data model and store inventory:** list every piece of data (field, where it lives, who can read it, when it's deleted). This is the input for the deletion audit (E1-S6) and risk R7.
3. **Edge cases for the state machine and solver:** for example, quorum reached at exactly t0 + 30:00, a take-back at the same moment as Lit, host offline when Lit fires, every yes "Ember only", a `with` rule naming someone not in the group, clock skew between phones.
4. **Copy inventory:** list every UI string the stories imply, with the word-count limits (buttons 3, messages 12), for the design role.
5. **Verify or replace the two unverified sources** (Axios ATUS, CDC) with the primary tables.
6. **Re-run the Fairlane Overpass query** with a defined centre and tag set, so BRD, the offline pack and the post use the same numbers. Our query: centre 42.3233, -83.2105, radius 3 km, `amenity=bench` nodes, `leisure=picnic_table` nodes, `amenity=toilets`, `amenity=drinking_water`, `leisure=park` ways: 48, 9, 6, 1, 22.

## Things the next roles must know

- **Approvals:** every deploy, public repo, post, upload or message to people needs the founder's yes, one at a time, prepared as one step. The bot may post only in the private "Flare test" group until approved.
- **People:** first names only (Fuego, Amor, Shilp, Ammo). No faces or voices unless each says yes on Sunday.
- **Phones:** never pick behaviour by phone model. `/check` (FR-CAP-1) runs on all four phones Sunday morning.
- **lab/** is a separate spike session. Don't edit or commit it. The engineering lead reviews its reports.
- **Storage choice** is the architect's, with MongoDB's own FAQ fact that the SSPL "has not been approved by the OSI" recorded either way.
- **Writing rules** apply to every string and doc. Banned-word scan passed on docs/ at this commit.

## Change requests

None against earlier phases. The research doc was corrected in this phase (813 entries, cleaned text extraction); details in BUGLOG.

s=s[:i]+'''## 11. Plan mode (P0)

A Plan is a planned ask for a later time with a deadline to answer, a ladder of four options from big to small, private conditions, and a solver that picks the biggest group at the highest step. It uses the same engine, channels, privacy and access rules as a Flare. Version 1.1 change: Plan mode moved from Later to P0 (founder change request, Oct 10).

### 11.1 States (Plan)

All times are absolute (the host picks them). D = answer deadline. S = start time. D must be at least 10 minutes after creation and at least 10 minutes before S.

| State | Enters when | What everyone sees | Leaves when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Kindling** | Host sends | Ask line, ladder, start time, deadline, "Need N more" | D reached (to Lit, Ember or Gone) |
| **Lit** | At D, the solver finds a group of at least quorum at some step | "It's on: {step} at {time}." The chosen step only | Host taps Done, or S + step duration + 60 min (to Gone) |
| **Ember** | At D, no group reaches quorum at any step, but at least 2 people (host included) fit step 4 | "Smaller plan: {step 4} at {time}." | Immediately Lit at step 4 with those people |
| **Gone** | Done, timeout, cancel, or nothing fits at D | Lit: "Thanks for coming." Otherwise: "Not this time." | Terminal. Deletion (FR-PRIV-5) |

- **FR-PLAN-1** A Plan is lit only at D, not before, so late yeses can still raise the step. Exception: if every invited person has said yes before D with no conditions, it lights early at the top fitting step.
- **FR-PLAN-2** Default quorum 3 (host included). Host may pick 2 to 6.
- **FR-PLAN-3** The ladder has exactly 4 steps, step 1 the biggest. Each step has a name, a place (OSM feature or "home"), a duration in minutes, and an access summary. Example: 1 "Ford Woods loop, 60 min"; 2 "Park loop, 30 min"; 3 "Short walk, 15 min"; 4 "20 min on the porch".
- **FR-PLAN-4** The ladder is drafted from weather, sunset and nearby places (FR-AI-4b) and the host can edit any step in place. A deterministic template fills any step the AI can't.
- **FR-PLAN-5** Step durations must end before sunset unless the host turns that check off; the app says "Ends after sunset" next to any step that doesn't.

### 11.2 Answering a Plan

- **FR-PLAN-6** Same private "I'm in" as a Flare, plus conditions. Conditions add a fifth type: `max_step(n)` ("just the short one" means step 3 or smaller, "porch only" means step 4).
- **FR-PLAN-7** The read-back names the step: "Got it: step 3 or smaller, back by 5 PM. Right?"
- **FR-PLAN-8** "Need N more" shows the count needed at the highest step that could still light.

### 11.3 Solver (Plan)

- **FR-PLAN-9** At D, for each step from 1 to 4, find the largest set of yeses whose conditions all hold at that step. Pick the step and set by: most people first, then the higher step (smaller number), then the earlier start. The set must be at least quorum, except under Ember (FR-PLAN-11).
- **FR-PLAN-10** Needs check per step: each phone checks its own needs profile against each step's place and reports pass or fail per step id. A failed step behaves like `max_step` for that person. No reason is sent.
- **FR-PLAN-11** If no step reaches quorum but at least 2 people fit step 4, the Plan lights at step 4 (counted as an Ember save).

### 11.4 I'm fading

- **FR-PLAN-12** Any person in the solved group of a Lit Plan can privately tap "I'm fading" until S + 50% of the step duration.
- **FR-PLAN-13** Each fade moves the Plan down one step (never below 4) and re-runs the solver at the new step with the same people. Each person can fade once per Plan.
- **FR-PLAN-14** Everyone sees "Smaller plan: {step}." Nobody sees who faded or how many fades there were.

### 11.5 Sunday use

The founder sends a real Plan ("Fairlane walk at 11?") after the release-candidate deploy, with a deadline before 11 AM. Plan mode must therefore be in the 10 AM release candidate.

## 12. Hot spots (P0)

- **FR-HOT-1** A group's Hot spots list shows place names where the group lit a Flare or Plan, with the number of times and the most recent Spark. Ordered by count, then most recent.
- **FR-HOT-2** Stored as one blob per group, encrypted on the phone with the group key. The server cannot read place names. Updated by the host's phone at Gone.
- **FR-HOT-3** "Your group met here N times." shows on a new Flare or Plan at a place when N is 1 or more, with one Spark if any. (Version 1.1: threshold lowered from 2 to 1 so the test day shows real history.)
- **FR-HOT-4** Opening the list is optional and never prompted. It adds 0 s unless opened.

## 13. Bench to Bench rest loop (P1)

- **FR-REST-1** Input in plain words, typed or spoken: "Knee's bad, 40 minutes, want trees". The phone parses it to: duration (minutes), max distance between rests (metres, defaults from the needs profile), preferences (trees, water, quiet), avoid steps (from needs). Read back for confirmation.
- **FR-REST-2** The loop starts and ends at the chosen spot, follows OSM paths a person can walk (`highway=footway|path|pedestrian|living_street|residential`, excluding `highway=steps` when avoid steps is on), and passes a bench (or picnic table) at least every max-rest-distance metres.
- **FR-REST-3** Total walking time at 3 km/h (slow pace) is within ±20% of the requested duration, not counting rest stops.
- **FR-REST-4** If no loop meets the rest limit, say so: "No loop keeps benches that close. Try 300 m?" Never return a loop that breaks the limit.
- **FR-REST-5** Output: a large-print card (A4 or Letter, 18 pt minimum body text, high contrast) with a simple sketch, numbered turns in words, each bench with distance from the last, restrooms and water. Printable from the share sheet as PDF.
- **FR-REST-6** The card is the walking interface; no screen use is needed on the walk. The app also offers the same turns as spoken audio.

## 14. Fix the map (P1)

- **FR-MAP-1** On a walk or after, a person photographs a bench, restroom, drinking fountain, or steps that OSM is missing or has wrong.
- **FR-MAP-2** The AI drafts OSM tags from the photo (for example `amenity=bench`, `backrest=yes`, `material=wood`) using only keys from a fixed allow-list. Location comes from the phone.
- **FR-MAP-3** A person reviews every tag: keep, change or remove. Nothing is saved without a review.
- **FR-MAP-4** Output is an export only: OSM Note text (location plus description) or an `.osm` change file. **Nothing is sent to OpenStreetMap from the app.** Publishing waits for the founder's yes.
- **FR-MAP-5** The photo is not included in the export and is deleted after drafting.
'''

input.content:
# Flare: Business rules catalog

Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Owner: Analyst. Source: PRD v1.1 (docs/product/03-prd.md). Each rule is atomic, has one ID, and is referenced by SRS requirements and tests. Where the PRD left something open, the rule records the decision and marks it **[Analyst decision]**.

Notation: `t0` = Flare send time (server). `D` = Plan answer deadline. `S` = Plan start time. All times are server UTC; phones display them in the group time zone (BR-TIME-2).

## 1. Identity and membership

| ID | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| BR-ID-1 | A group is identified by a random 128-bit group id. It is not derived from any personal data. |
| BR-ID-2 | Each person in a group is a member with a random 128-bit member id, created on their phone the first time they open the group's link (or by the bot for a Telegram user). |
| BR-ID-3 | Display names are chosen by the member and stored only encrypted with the group key. The server never holds a readable name. **[Analyst decision]** |
| BR-ID-4 | A member id is per group. The same person in two groups has two unrelated ids. |
| BR-ID-5 | For Telegram members, the bot keeps a map from Telegram user id to member id for that group. The map is deleted when the member leaves the group or the group is inactive for 30 days. |
| BR-ID-6 | A plain-text reply (`IN <code>`) relayed by a member counts as an anonymous yes with no member id and no conditions. At most 3 anonymous yeses per gathering. **[Analyst decision]** |

## 2. Quorum

| ID | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| BR-Q-1 | Yes-count always includes the host as 1. |
| BR-Q-2 | Flare quorum is 2, 3 or 4; default 2. Plan quorum is 2 to 6; default 3. |
| BR-Q-3 | A gathering lights when the solver's chosen set (BR-S-1) has at least quorum members. |
| BR-Q-4 | "Need N more" = max(0, quorum − size of the solver's current best set). For a Plan, it is computed at the highest step that could still light. |
| BR-Q-5 | No interface or API shows who is in the set, who answered, or when anyone answered. Only N. |
| BR-Q-6 | "Ember only" yeses (BR-A-3) are excluded from Kindling counts and included at Ember. |

## 3. Conditions

| ID | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| BR-C-1 | Condition types: `with(member_id)`, `after(time)`, `back_by(time)`, `max_walk(minutes)`, `max_step(n)` (Plans only). |
| BR-C-2 | A yes may carry 0 to 4 conditions. All must hold (logical AND). |
| BR-C-3 | `with(X)` holds when X is in the same chosen set. Names are resolved to member ids on the phone, where names can be decrypted. |
| BR-C-4 | `with(X)` naming nobody in the group cannot be saved. The phone says "Amor isn't in this group." |
| BR-C-5 | `after(T)` holds when the gathering's start is at or after T. For a Flare, the start is the Lit time. |
| BR-C-6 | `back_by(T)` holds when start + duration ≤ T. Flare duration is taken as 60 minutes for this check. Plan duration is the chosen step's minutes. **[Analyst decision]** |
| BR-C-7 | `max_walk(M)` holds when the person's walking time to the spot at 4.8 km/h straight-line distance × 1.3 is ≤ M. The phone evaluates it and reports pass or fail per spot id. **[Analyst decision]** |
| BR-C-8 | `max_step(n)` holds when the chosen step number ≥ n (step 4 is smallest). |
| BR-C-9 | Free text never leaves the phone. Only the structured rule is sent. |
| BR-C-10 | A condition is saved only after the person confirms the read-back. |

## 4. Solver

| ID | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| BR-S-1 | The solver picks the set of yeses (and the step, for Plans) that maximizes, in order: (1) number of people, (2) higher step (smaller step number), (3) earlier start. |
| BR-S-2 | A yes with no conditions fits every set. |
| BR-S-3 | `with` dependencies are resolved as a fixed point: repeatedly remove members whose `with` targets are not in the set until nothing changes. |
| BR-S-4 | Group sizes are at most 12 in this release, so the solver may search exhaustively. Groups larger than 12 are rejected at creation. **[Analyst decision]** |
| BR-S-5 | The solver runs on every yes, take-back, condition change, fade and timer event. It is deterministic: the same inputs give the same output. |
| BR-S-6 | Ties after all three criteria are broken by the lowest member ids (stable, not by answer time). **[Analyst decision]** |

## 5. Flare timeline

| ID | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| BR-F-1 | Kindling lasts until t0 + 30:00. |
| BR-F-2 | An event received by the server at or before t0 + 30:00.000 belongs to Kindling. If it completes quorum, the Flare is Lit, even if the Ember timer is already queued. |
| BR-F-3 | At t0 + 30:00, if not Lit, the Flare enters Ember with quorum 2 at the Ember spot (BR-E). |
| BR-F-4 | Ember lasts until t0 + 60:00. If not Lit by then, Gone with "Not this time". |
| BR-F-5 | Lit lasts until the host taps Done or t0 + 4:00:00, whichever comes first. |
| BR-F-6 | The host may cancel only during Kindling or Ember. Cancel ends in "Not this time". |
| BR-F-7 | Lit is permanent for the gathering (no return to Kindling). |
| BR-F-8 | Timer transitions fire within 30 seconds of their scheduled time, including after a server restart. |

## 6. Ember

| ID | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| BR-E-1 | Ember spot = the nearest `amenity=bench` or `leisure=picnic_table` by straight-line distance within 400 m of the original spot that passes the needs check of every yes and every "Ember only" yes. |
| BR-E-2 | If no bench qualifies, the Ember spot is the original spot. |
| BR-E-3 | Needs checks for candidate benches run on each phone; each phone reports pass or fail per candidate bench id. The server picks the nearest bench that passed for all. |
| BR-E-4 | Phones that haven't reported within 60 s of Ember start are treated as pass for all candidates. **[Analyst decision]** |
| BR-E-5 | Ember duration on screen is "15 min". Ember quorum is 2. |
| BR-E-6 | A Flare lit during Ember counts as an Ember save. |

## 7. Plan timeline and downshifting

| ID | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| BR-P-1 | D ≥ creation + 10 min and D ≤ S − 10 min. |
| BR-P-2 | A Plan lights only at D, except: if every member of the group has said yes with no conditions before D, it lights at once at step 1. |
| BR-P-3 | At D, the solver picks step and set (BR-S-1). If no step reaches quorum but at least 2 people (host included) fit step 4, it lights at step 4 and counts as an Ember save. Otherwise Gone. |
| BR-P-4 | A ladder has exactly 4 steps, numbered 1 (biggest) to 4 (smallest). Durations are strictly decreasing. |
| BR-P-5 | Any member of the chosen set may fade once per Plan, from Lit until S + 50% of the current step's minutes. |
| BR-P-6 | Each fade lowers the step by 1, never below 4. The set is re-solved at the new step; members who now fit are added, nobody is removed. **[Analyst decision]** |
| BR-P-7 | The displayed change is "Smaller plan: {step name}." No count of fades, no names. |
| BR-P-8 | A Lit Plan becomes Gone at Done or at S + step minutes + 60 min. |
| BR-P-9 | Steps ending after sunset show "Ends after sunset" unless the host turned the check off. |

## 8. Arrival and host +1

| ID | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| BR-H-1 | Headcount = 1 (host) + arrivals. |
| BR-H-2 | An arrival is recorded by the person tapping "I'm here" or by the host tapping +1. |
| BR-H-3 | A member's own "I'm here" and a host +1 for the same member count once only if the host +1 is attached to that member; anonymous +1s are separate. The host's +1 list shows names (decrypted on the host's phone) and an "Someone else" entry. **[Analyst decision]** |
| BR-H-4 | Headcount ≤ yes-count + 3 (yes-count includes the host). Taps beyond the cap are ignored. |
| BR-H-5 | Arrivals are accepted only while Lit. Offline arrivals from the outbox are accepted if their recorded time is within the Lit window. |

## 9. Expiry and deletion

| ID | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| BR-D-1 | At Gone, the server deletes within 5 minutes: the gathering record, yes records, rules, fades, arrivals, photo ciphertext, live locations, bot message references, and solver state. |
| BR-D-2 | Every per-gathering record also carries a storage-level expiry at t0 + 5 h (Flare) or S + 24 h (Plan), so deletion happens even if the delete job fails. |
| BR-D-3 | The bot deletes every message it posted for the gathering at Gone. |
| BR-D-4 | Survivors after Gone: group counters (docs/product/07-kpis.md), the encrypted Hot spots blob, opt-in encrypted Sparks, member ids, push subscriptions, and the Telegram map. |
| BR-D-5 | Push subscriptions and Telegram maps are deleted after 30 days without a gathering in the group. Sparks and the Hot spots blob are deleted after 180 days without a gathering, or at once when any member taps "Forget this group". **[Analyst decision]** |
| BR-D-6 | Logs never contain request bodies, photos, names, locations, conditions, or link fragments. Logs are kept 7 days. |
| BR-D-7 | The deletion audit counts remaining per-gathering records in every store listed in the data dictionary, by gathering id and in total. Passing = 0. |

## 10. Sparks and Hot spots

| ID | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| BR-K-1 | Only members with an accepted arrival may leave a Spark for that gathering. One Spark per member per gathering. |
| BR-K-2 | A Spark is 1 to 140 characters, written by the person. No AI generation or editing is offered. |
| BR-K-3 | The Spark prompt appears once, after Done, and can be dismissed. No reminders. |
| BR-K-4 | A Spark is encrypted with the group key before leaving the phone and is tied to the place key: the OSM element id of the spot, or the place name if no id. |
| BR-K-5 | "Your group met here N times." shows when N ≥ 1, where N counts Lit gatherings at that place key. It shows the newest Spark at that place, if any. |
| BR-K-6 | The Hot spots blob is one encrypted record per group: a list of {place key, place name, count, last date, newest Spark id}. The host's phone updates it at Gone. Conflicts merge by taking the max count per place. |

## 11. Access and needs

| ID | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| BR-A-1 | Needs profile fields: avoid steps (yes or no), max distance between rests (100, 200, 400 m or none), restroom within 300 m (yes or no). Stored only on the phone. |
| BR-A-2 | A spot fails "avoid steps" when any `highway=steps` lies within 20 m of the straight line from the person to the spot or within 50 m of the spot. A spot fails "restroom" when no `amenity=toilets` is within 300 m. A spot fails "rest distance" when the nearest bench is farther than the limit. |
| BR-A-3 | A person whose needs fail may choose "Count me in for a closer one". Their yes is flagged "Ember only" and carries no reason. |
| BR-A-4 | Access line copy never says "step-free". It says "No steps mapped" or "Steps mapped". |

## 12. Time

| ID | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| BR-TIME-1 | The server clock (UTC, NTP-synced) decides every transition. Phone clocks are never trusted for transitions. |
| BR-TIME-2 | The group time zone is the host phone's time zone at creation. Times in conditions are interpreted in it. |
| BR-TIME-3 | Phones show the server time remaining and the time the state was last confirmed. |

## 13. Channels

| ID | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| BR-CH-1 | The bot posts only in allow-listed chat ids. At release the list has one entry: "Flare test". |
| BR-CH-2 | The plain-text form is ≤ 200 bytes UTF-8. If the spot name would exceed it, the name is truncated with "…". |
| BR-CH-3 | Short codes use 5 characters from `REDACTED` (no 0, 1, I, L, O). Codes are unique among live gatherings. |
| BR-CH-4 | Link previews show a blurred photo and the invite line only; never coordinates or the spot name below street level. **[Analyst decision]** |

## 14. AI

| ID | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| BR-AI-1 | Tier order is phone, then hub, then rules. A tier is skipped if unavailable, times out (phone 8 s, hub 6 s), or returns output that fails validation. |
| BR-AI-2 | Output never describes faces, identity, age, race, gender or bodies. A filter replaces any person words with "a person" or "people", or drops the sentence. |
| BR-AI-3 | Every AI run records job and tier as a counter. No inputs or outputs are stored server-side. |
| BR-AI-4 | Fix the map drafts use only the tag key allow-list in PRD FR-MAP-2 / backlog E17-S1. |

# Flare: Software requirements specification (SRS)

Structure follows ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 (section 9.6, SRS content). Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Owner: Analyst.

## 1. Introduction

### 1.1 Purpose
This SRS states every requirement the Flare app, server, Telegram bot and website must meet for the DEV Hacktoberfest Week 1 entry. Engineers build to it; QA tests against it; the traceability matrix (05-rtm.csv) links each requirement to stories, acceptance criteria, design, code, tests and proof.

### 1.2 Scope
Flare lets a host send a Flare (meet now) or a Plan (meet later) to friends. Friends say yes privately; it happens only if enough say yes; it shrinks instead of failing; it works for friends with low vision or limited mobility and with no signal; and it deletes itself. Products: the **app** (installable web app for iPhone, plus the link page), the **server** (engine, solver, scheduler, API), the **Telegram bot**, and the **website**.

### 1.3 Definitions
See docs/product/10-glossary-and-decisions.md. Additional terms: **gathering** = a Flare or a Plan; **place key** = OSM element id of a spot, else its name; **group key** = symmetric key in the link fragment.

### 1.4 References
- docs/product/03-prd.md (PRD v1.1), 05-backlog.md, 06-scope.md, 07-kpis.md, 09-risks.md
- docs/requirements/03-business-rules.md (BR-*), 04-data-flow-and-dictionary.md, 02-use-cases.md
- docs/requirements/evidence/README.md (pinned numbers)
- WCAG 2.2, https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/
- ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018

### 1.5 Requirement format
Each requirement has: **ID**; a statement using "shall"; **Pri** (P0 = in the Sun 10 AM release candidate; P1 = before the DEV deadline; P2 = later); **Source** (PRD or BR id, or founder); **Story** (backlog story and AC); **V** = verification method (T test, D demonstration, I inspection, A analysis). A requirement is met only when its fit criterion (the number or condition in the statement) is observed.

## 2. Overall description

### 2.1 Product perspective
New, standalone system. External systems: Telegram Bot API, Web Push (Apple Push for Safari), OpenStreetMap Overpass API, the hub (Ollama with Gemma 4 E4B on the team's Mac), on-device model files from a public model host, SMS or satellite messaging (outside the system).

### 2.2 User classes
Host; invitee; invitee with access needs (low vision, limited mobility); Telegram member; text-only member (SMS relay); operator (the team: deploy, audit, metrics). No accounts exist for any class.

### 2.3 Operating environment
- Phones: iPhone 13, 16 Pro Max, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max. iOS versions unknown until Sunday; behaviour must be chosen by runtime capability detection only.
- Browser: Safari on iOS (link page and installed Home Screen app). Desktop Chrome, Firefox and Safari current versions for development and the website.
- Server: hosted HTTPS service (Render is the candidate; deploy needs the founder's yes).
- Hub: macOS laptop with Ollama and `gemma4:e4b`.

### 2.4 Constraints
DEV rules (new work in the window; template; tag; deadline Mon 06:59 UTC); open models only for AI jobs; no hardware; no end-user accounts; founder approval for every public action; first names only in public materials until consent; writing rules (docs/product/01-brd.md section 6).

### 2.5 Assumptions and dependencies
- AS-1 At least two of the four phones run iOS with Safari web push support for Home Screen apps; otherwise Telegram or the open page carries Lit notices.
- AS-2 OSM data near Fairlane is current enough (pinned Oct 10, 17:07 UTC).
- AS-3 The hub laptop has internet during the field test, or the rules tier is used.
- AS-4 The lab session supplies the phone-tier model choice (MediaPipe Gemma 4 E2B, or a vision model under 600 MB).

## 3. Specific requirements

### 3.1 External interfaces

| SRS-MAP-2 | Export shall stay disabled until every tag is reviewed (keep, change, remove). | P1 | FR-MAP-3 | E17-S2 | T |
| SRS-MAP-3 | Export shall produce OSM Note text or an `.osm` file only; the app shall make no request to any openstreetmap.org host. | P1 | FR-MAP-4 | E17-S3 AC1 | T |
| SRS-MAP-4 | The photo shall be deleted after drafting and excluded from the export. | P1 | FR-MAP-5 | E17-S3 AC2 | T |

### 3.16 Functional: capability page and website

| ID | Requirement | Pri | Source | Story | V |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SRS-CAP-1 | `/check` shall report iOS and Safari version, WebGPU and adapter limits, storage estimate, geolocation, device orientation, speech synthesis, web push, recommended tier and a timed test of each, with "Copy report". | P0 | FR-CAP-1 | E8-S1 | D |
| SRS-WEB-1 | The website shall have Home, How it works, Privacy, Accessibility, and Run it yourself pages. | P0 | FR-WEB-1 | E12-S1 | I |
| SRS-WEB-2 | The Privacy page shall state the limits in FR-PRIV-7, R19 and R22, and show the latest deletion audit output. | P0 | FR-PRIV-7 | E12-S1 | I |

### 3.17 Performance

| ID | Requirement | Pri | Source | Story | V |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SRS-PERF-1 | The link page shall be interactive in ≤ 2.0 s (Lighthouse mobile, simulated 4G, iPhone 13 class) and on a real iPhone 13 over cellular. | P0 | NFR-1 | E3-S1 AC1 | T |
| SRS-PERF-2 | Link page JavaScript shall be ≤ 150 KB gzipped, excluding model files. | P0 | NFR-2 | E3-S1 | I |
| SRS-PERF-3 | API p95 latency shall be ≤ 300 ms for yes, take-back and arrival under 20 concurrent clients. | P0 | NFR-1 | E1-S3 | T |
| SRS-PERF-4 | The website shall score ≥ 90 performance and 100 accessibility in Lighthouse mobile. | P0 | E12-S2 | E12-S2 | T |

### 3.18 Offline

| SRS-OFF-2 | The Lit screen and compass shall work in airplane mode, showing "Offline. Saved at {time}." | P0 | FR-OFF-5 | E3-S4 AC2 | T |
| SRS-OFF-3 | Offline taps shall queue in the outbox and be sent exactly once on reconnect (BR-H-5). | P0 | FR-OFF-2 | E9-S2 | T |
| SRS-OFF-4 | The app shell shall load offline after first visit (service worker). | P0 | FR-CH-1 | E9-S1 | T |
| SRS-OFF-5 | The Fairlane pack shall be the pinned query result (evidence/README.md) and record its OSM timestamp. | P0 | FR-OFF-4 | E9-S3 | I |

### 3.19 Privacy and data retention

| ID | Requirement | Pri | Source | Story | V |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SRS-PRIV-1 | Free-text conditions, needs profiles, rest-loop requests, map photos and capability reports shall never leave the phone. | P0 | FR-PRIV-2 | E5-S3, E6-S1 | T |
| SRS-PRIV-2 | Per-gathering data shall be deleted within 5 min of Gone (BR-D-1) and carry storage expiry (BR-D-2). | P0 | FR-PRIV-5 | E1-S5 | T |
| SRS-PRIV-3 | Surviving data shall be limited to BR-D-4, with retention per BR-D-5. | P0 | FR-PRIV-5 | E1-S5 AC2 | T |
| SRS-PRIV-4 | Logs shall follow BR-D-6. | P0 | R7 | E1-S5 | I |
| SRS-PRIV-5 | The deletion audit shall follow BR-D-7 and print 0 after the field test. | P0 | FR-PRIV-6 | E1-S6 | T |

| SRS-PRIV-7 | No analytics, ads, third-party trackers or fonts loaded from third parties shall be present in the app or link page. | P0 | Privacy promise | E3-S1 | I |

### 3.20 Security

| SRS-SEC-1 | Secrets (bot token, database credentials, Render key, hub secret) shall exist only in server environment variables, never in the client, repo or logs. | P0 | NFR-5 | all | I |
| SRS-SEC-2 | A secret scan shall run before every push and pass. | P0 | R14 | E14-S3 | T |
| SRS-SEC-3 | Photo encryption shall use an authenticated cipher (AES-256-GCM via WebCrypto) with a random 96-bit nonce per photo. | P0 | FR-PRIV-1 | E1-S1 | I |
| SRS-SEC-4 | The API shall require the gathering id plus a per-member write token for every write; tokens are random 128-bit values stored only on the phone. | P0 | BR-Q-5 | E1-S3 | T |
| SRS-SEC-5 | The API shall rate-limit writes to 30 per minute per member and 300 per minute per gathering. | P0 | Abuse | E1-S3 | T |
| SRS-SEC-6 | The app shall send a Content-Security-Policy that blocks third-party scripts and inline script execution. | P0 | SRS-PRIV-7 | E3-S1 | T |
| SRS-SEC-7 | The agent session embed shall be scrubbed of keys and personal data before it is made public. | P1 | R14 | E14-S3 | I |

### 3.21 Accessibility

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SRS-A11Y-1 | Every screen shall meet WCAG 2.2 AA. | P0 | NFR-3 | E6-S5 | T |
| SRS-A11Y-2 | axe-core shall report 0 serious or critical issues on every screen. | P0 | E6-S5 AC2 | E6-S5 | T |
| SRS-A11Y-3 | Journey J3 (low vision) shall complete with VoiceOver on a real iPhone, recorded. | P0 | E6-S5 AC1 | E6-S5 | D |
| SRS-A11Y-4 | Text shall reflow at the largest Dynamic Type size with no clipped controls. | P0 | FR-ACC-5 | E6-S5 | T |
| SRS-A11Y-5 | Motion shall respect Reduce Motion; sound shall respect the silent switch where the platform exposes it; colour shall never be the only signal. | P0 | NFR-7, FR-ACC-5 | E11-S2 | T |
| SRS-A11Y-6 | Touch targets shall be ≥ 44 × 44 pt. | P0 | WCAG 2.5.8 (AA 24 px; we use Apple's 44 pt) | E11-S1 | I |

### 3.22 Compatibility

| ID | Requirement | Pri | Source | Story | V |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SRS-COMP-1 | All P0 flows shall work in Safari on all four test phones (iPhone 13, 16 Pro Max, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max) on the iOS version each runs on Sunday. | P0 | Founder | E13-S1 | D |
| SRS-COMP-2 | Features shall be enabled by capability detection; a missing capability shall degrade to the next option, never block a P0 flow. | P0 | Founder Q4 | E8-S1 | T |
| SRS-COMP-3 | The link page shall work inside the Telegram in-app browser and when opened from iMessage and WhatsApp. | P0 | FR-CH-1 | E3-S1 | D |
| SRS-COMP-4 | The website shall work in current Safari, Chrome and Firefox on desktop and mobile. | P0 | FR-WEB-2 | E12-S2 | T |

### 3.23 Reliability

| ID | Requirement | Pri | Source | Story | V |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SRS-REL-1 | Gathering state shall survive a server restart with no lost yes, fade or arrival. | P0 | NFR-4 | E1-S2 AC4 | T |
| SRS-REL-2 | Duplicate requests with the same idempotency key shall have no additional effect. | P0 | NFR-4 | E1-S3 AC1 | T |

### 3.24 Usability and copy

| ID | Requirement | Pri | Source | Story | V |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SRS-COPY-1 | Button labels shall be ≤ 3 words; messages ≤ 12 words. | P0 | NFR-8 | E11-S1 | I |
| SRS-COPY-2 | No UI string or doc shall contain a word from the banned list in docs/product/01-brd.md section 6. | P0 | Writing rules | all | I |

### 3.25 Maintainability and licensing

| ID | Requirement | Pri | Source | Story | V |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SRS-MNT-1 | Source shall be released under the license the architect confirms (AGPL-3.0 recommended), with a LICENSE file and third-party notices. | P0 | NFR-6 | E12-S1 | I |
| SRS-MNT-2 | Commits after the DEV deadline shall be listed in the README. | P0 | DEV rules | E14-S1 | I |
| SRS-MNT-3 | "Run it yourself" shall let a developer start the server, bot and hub from a clean machine with documented commands. | P0 | FR-WEB-1 | E12-S1 | D |

### 3.26 Field test and post

| ID | Requirement | Pri | Source | Story | V |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SRS-FLD-1 | A KPI export shall print the table in 07-kpis.md for a given time window. | P0 | E13-S2 | E13-S2 | T |
| SRS-FLD-2 | A consent checklist shall record, per person, yes or no for first name, face and voice. | P0 | Founder Q3 | E13-S3 | I |
| SRS-FLD-3 | A real Plan shall be sent Sunday morning after the RC deploy, with D before 11 AM ET. | P0 | CR-1 | E15-S5 | D |
| SRS-FLD-4 | The DEV post shall follow the template, include the KPI table, tier table, deletion audit output and "what broke", and be published by the founder before Mon 06:59 UTC. | P1 | BRD 5 | E14-S1 | I |

## 4. Verification

Every requirement above names its method. QA owns the test plan and fills the Test and Proof columns of 05-rtm.csv. A requirement is closed only with proof (test output, screenshot, video or audit printout) linked in the matrix.

## 5. Open issues

None blocking. Decisions taken by the analyst where the PRD was open are marked **[Analyst decision]** in 03-business-rules.md and listed in the design handoff for review.
