input.content:
# Flare: Use cases

Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Owner: Analyst. Each use case lists the main path, alternate paths (A) and failure paths (F). Requirement IDs refer to 01-srs.md; rules to 03-business-rules.md.

## Use-case diagram

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Host([Host])
  Inv([Invitee])
  Needs([Invitee with needs])
  TG([Telegram member])
  Txt([Text-only friend])
  Op([Operator])
  Clock([Server clock])

  subgraph Flare system
    UC1(UC-01 Send a Flare)
    UC2(UC-02 Say I'm in)
    UC3(UC-03 Add a condition)
    UC4(UC-04 Solve and light)
    UC5(UC-05 Shrink to Ember)
    UC6(UC-06 Send a Plan)
    UC7(UC-07 Fade a Plan)
    UC8(UC-08 Get there with the compass)
    UC9(UC-09 Record arrivals and end)
    UC10(UC-10 Leave a Spark and see history)
    UC11(UC-11 Join from a spot that doesn't suit)
    UC12(UC-12 Use it with no signal)
    UC13(UC-13 Build a Bench to Bench card)
    UC14(UC-14 Draft a map fix)
    UC15(UC-15 Delete and audit)
    UC16(UC-16 Check a phone)
  end

  Host --> UC1
  Host --> UC6
  Host --> UC9
  Inv --> UC2
  Inv --> UC3
  Inv --> UC7
  Inv --> UC8
  Inv --> UC10
  Needs --> UC11
  Needs --> UC13
  TG --> UC2
  TG --> UC3
  Txt --> UC2
  Inv --> UC12
  Inv --> UC14
  Clock --> UC4
  Clock --> UC5
  Clock --> UC15
  Op --> UC15
  Op --> UC16
  UC2 -. includes .-> UC4
  UC3 -. extends .-> UC2
  UC11 -. extends .-> UC2
  UC5 -. extends .-> UC4
  UC7 -. extends .-> UC4
```

## UC-01 Send a Flare
- **Actor:** Host. **Pre:** Host is in a group (has its link) or creating a new one. **Post:** Gathering in Kindling; invite delivered on the host's chosen channels.
- **Main:**
  1. Host opens the app; camera is live (SRS-CRE-1).
  2. Host taps to capture.
  3. App names the spot (SRS-CRE-3) and drafts invite and scene (SRS-CRE-4, SRS-AI-1).
  4. Host accepts or edits; optionally taps the quorum chip (SRS-CRE-5).
  5. Host taps Send. Photo is encrypted (SRS-CRE-6); server creates the Flare; link, text form and bot post are produced (SRS-CRE-7).
- **A1** Camera denied: host picks a photo (SRS-CRE-2).
- **A2** No named feature within 150 m: street name used.
- **A3** AI tiers unavailable: template invite "Outside at {spot}. Come?" (rules tier).
- **A4** New group: app creates group id, key and the host's member id (SRS-ID-1, SRS-ID-3).
- **F1** No signal at Send: Flare is queued in the outbox with "Sends when you're back online." No timer starts until the server accepts it (t0 = server receipt).
- **F2** Group has 12 members already and the host adds one: "Groups max out at 12." (SRS-ID-5).

## UC-02 Say I'm in
- **Actor:** Invitee, Telegram member, or text-only friend. **Pre:** Gathering in Kindling or Ember. **Post:** Yes recorded privately; counts updated.
- **Main:**
  1. Invitee opens the link (SRS-RES-1); photo decrypts with the fragment key.
  2. Invitee taps "I'm in"; sees "You're in." (SRS-RES-3).
  3. Server records the yes and re-runs the solver (includes UC-04).
- **A1** Telegram: member taps "I'm in" on the bot post; bot confirms privately (SRS-CH-2).
- **A2** Text-only: friend replies `IN K7Q2` by SMS; a member enters it (SRS-CH-6, BR-ID-6).
- **A3** Take it back before Lit (SRS-RES-6).
- **A4** Gathering already Lit: page shows the Lit screen; a new yes joins if the solver can add them (BR-P-6 for Plans; for Flares any yes after Lit is added to the set).
- **F1** Missing key: "This link is missing its key." (SRS-RES-2).
- **F2** Gathering Gone: "Not this time." (or "Thanks for coming." if it was Lit).
- **F3** Offline: tap queued in outbox (SRS-OFF-3).

## UC-03 Add a condition
- **Actor:** Invitee. **Pre:** Saying yes (UC-02). **Post:** Structured rules attached to the yes.
- **Main:**
  1. Invitee taps "Add a condition", types or dictates text.
  2. Phone parses (rules or hub tier; phone tier when available) (SRS-COND-1, 3, 4).
  3. Phone reads back in ≤ 12 words (SRS-COND-5). Invitee taps Yes.
  4. Only the rules are sent (SRS-COND-6).
- **A1** "Fix it": back to step 1 with the text kept.
- **A2** Telegram member sends the condition by private message; bot reads back (SRS-CH-3).
- **F1** Unparseable: hint message (SRS-COND-8).
- **F2** `with` names nobody in the group (SRS-COND-7).

## UC-04 Solve and light
- **Actor:** Server clock (and any change event). **Pre:** Gathering in Kindling, Ember, or at Plan deadline. **Post:** "Need N more" updated; possibly Lit.
- **Main (Flare):**
  1. On each event the solver picks the best set (SRS-SOL-1).
  2. If the set reaches quorum, state becomes Lit (BR-F-2).
  3. Every member in the set is notified within 10 s (SRS-LIT-1); phones save offline data (SRS-OFF-1).
- **Main (Plan):** at D the solver picks step and set (SRS-PLAN-5); Lit at that step.
- **A1** Plan: everyone said yes unconditionally before D: lights early at step 1 (BR-P-2).
- **A2** Yes and take-back arrive in the same second: processed in server receipt order (BR-TIME-1).
- **F1** Push unavailable for a member: the open page polls; bot message for Telegram members.

## UC-05 Shrink to Ember
- **Actor:** Server clock. **Pre:** Flare not Lit at t0 + 30:00. **Post:** Ember with quorum 2 at the Ember spot; or Gone at t0 + 60:00.
- **Main:**
  1. At t0 + 30:00 server asks phones to check candidate benches (BR-E-3).
  2. After reports (or 60 s), server picks the Ember spot (BR-E-1, BR-E-4).
  3. All see "Smaller plan: 15 min at {bench}." (SRS-EMB-2).
  4. One more yes (or an "Ember only" yes already present) lights it (BR-E-6).
- **A1** No suitable bench: original spot (BR-E-2).
- **F1** Nobody joins by t0 + 60:00: "Not this time." for all (SRS-ST-3).

## UC-06 Send a Plan
- **Actor:** Host. **Pre:** In a group. **Post:** Plan in Kindling with a 4-step ladder.
- **Main:**
  1. Host types or says the ask ("Fairlane walk at 11?") and picks S and D (SRS-PLAN-1).
  2. App drafts the ladder from weather, sunset and nearby places (SRS-PLAN-2).
  3. Host edits any step; sunset warnings shown (SRS-PLAN-3).
  4. Host picks quorum (default 3) and sends.
- **A1** Hub unavailable: template ladder.
- **F1** D too close to now or to S: "Give friends at least 10 minutes." (BR-P-1).
- **F2** Nothing fits at D: Gone, "Not this time."

## UC-07 Fade a Plan
- **Actor:** Member of the chosen set. **Pre:** Plan Lit, before S + 50% of step minutes, member hasn't faded. **Post:** Plan one step smaller.
- **Main:**
  1. Member taps "I'm fading" (private).
  2. Server lowers the step and re-solves (BR-P-6).
  3. All see "Smaller plan: {step}." (BR-P-7); offline data and compass update (SRS-PLAN-8).
- **A1** Already at step 4: tap accepted, no change, no message. **[Analyst decision]**
- **F1** Second fade by the same member: button no longer shown.

## UC-08 Get there with the compass
- **Actor:** Member in the set. **Pre:** Lit; target saved. **Post:** Member reaches the spot.
- **Main:**
  1. Member taps "Find them"; grants orientation permission if asked.
  2. Arrow, distance and speech guide them (SRS-CMP-1, 2, 3).
- **A1** Host shares live location (P1): target follows the host (SRS-CMP-6).
- **A2** Screen locked: speech continues where iOS allows.
- **F1** Orientation unavailable or noisy: distance-only speech, "Hold your phone flat."
- **F2** GPS unavailable: "Can't find you yet." and the host line stays visible.

## UC-09 Record arrivals and end
- **Actor:** Host, arriving member. **Pre:** Lit. **Post:** Headcount final; gathering Gone.
- **Main:**
  1. Arriving member taps "I'm here" or host taps +1 (SRS-LIT-3).
  2. Host taps Done (SRS-LIT-4); state Gone; deletion begins (SRS-PRIV-2).
- **A1** Nobody taps Done: Gone at the timeout (BR-F-5, BR-P-8).
- **F1** Arrival tapped offline: outbox, accepted per BR-H-5.
- **F2** Taps over the cap: ignored (BR-H-4).

## UC-10 Leave a Spark and see history
- **Actor:** Member with an accepted arrival. **Pre:** Gathering Done. **Post:** Encrypted Spark stored; Hot spots updated.
- **Main:**
  1. App shows the Spark prompt once (BR-K-3).
  2. Member writes ≤ 140 characters and saves; it is encrypted (BR-K-4).
  3. Next gathering at that place shows "Your group met here N times." and the Spark (SRS-SPK-2).
- **A1** Member dismisses: no Spark, no reminder.
- **A2** Member opens Hot spots (SRS-HOT-1).

## UC-11 Join from a spot that doesn't suit
- **Actor:** Invitee with needs. **Pre:** Needs profile set (SRS-ACC-1). **Post:** "Ember only" yes recorded with no reason.
- **Main:**
  1. Phone checks the spot (BR-A-2) and it fails.
  2. Phone asks "This spot may not suit you. Count me in for a closer one?"
  3. Member taps Yes; an "Ember only" yes is sent (SRS-ACC-3).
  4. At Ember, the bench is chosen to suit them (BR-E-1) and their yes counts.
- **A1** Plan: failed steps act as `max_step` for them (SRS-PLAN-6).
- **F1** No suitable bench within 400 m: the original spot is used; their yes still counts toward Ember. **[Analyst decision: the person chose to be counted; the app shows them the access line so they can decide.]**

## UC-12 Use it with no signal
- **Actor:** Member. **Pre:** Gathering Lit while online. **Post:** Offline taps synced later.
- **Main:**
  1. At Lit, data is saved (SRS-OFF-1).
  2. Offline, the Lit screen and compass work (SRS-OFF-2).
  3. Taps queue and send once on reconnect (SRS-OFF-3).
- **A1** A fade happens while a member is offline: their screen shows the last saved step and "Offline. Saved at {time}." until they reconnect.
- **F1** Phone never online after Lit: the member still has the saved plan; their arrival isn't counted until they reconnect within the Lit window.

## UC-13 Build a Bench to Bench card (P1)
- **Actor:** Member with needs. **Pre:** A spot chosen. **Post:** PDF card and audio turns.
- **Main:** request in words (SRS-REST-1) → read-back → loop (SRS-REST-2, 3) → card (SRS-REST-5) → print or save; audio available (SRS-REST-6).
- **F1** No loop fits (SRS-REST-4).

## UC-14 Draft a map fix (P1)
- **Actor:** Member. **Post:** Exported Note text or `.osm` file; nothing published.
- **Main:** photo → draft tags (SRS-MAP-1) → review every tag (SRS-MAP-2) → export (SRS-MAP-3); photo deleted (SRS-MAP-4).
- **F1** AI unavailable: manual tag form with the allow-list.

## UC-15 Delete and audit
- **Actor:** Server clock, operator. **Pre:** Gathering Gone. **Post:** 0 per-gathering records remain.
- **Main:** delete job runs within 5 min (SRS-PRIV-2); bot deletes its posts (SRS-CH-4); storage expiry backs it up; operator runs the audit (SRS-PRIV-5) and saves the output.
- **F1** Delete job fails: storage expiry removes records by t0 + 5 h (Flare) or S + 24 h (Plan); the audit flags them until then.
- **F2** Bot message older than 48 h can't be deleted by Telegram rules: logged as a known limit (can't happen inside the 4 h Flare window).

## UC-16 Check a phone
- **Actor:** Operator or tester. **Main:** open `/check`, run tests, copy report (SRS-CAP-1). **Post:** Tier per phone known before the field test.

# Flare: Logical data flow and data dictionary

Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Owner: Analyst. This is logical: it names data and flows, not tables or technologies. The architect maps each store to a physical one and keeps the store list in sync with the deletion audit (BR-D-7).

Legend: **E** external entity, **P** process, **DS** data store. Stores marked *(phone)* never leave the device.

## Level 0 (context)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Host[E1 Host]
  Inv[E2 Invitee]
  TG[E3 Telegram Bot API]
  Push[E4 Web Push service]
  OSM[E5 OpenStreetMap / Overpass]
  Hub[E6 Hub: Ollama on team laptop]
  Models[E7 Model file host]
  Op[E8 Operator]
  SYS((P0 Flare system))

  Host -- photo ciphertext, spot, quorum, ask, ladder, Done, +1 --> SYS
  SYS -- link, text form, state, counts --> Host
  Inv -- yes, rules, take-back, fade, arrival, Spark ciphertext --> SYS
  SYS -- state, Need N more, Lit notice --> Inv
  TG -- button taps, private messages --> SYS
  SYS -- posts, edits, deletes, private replies --> TG
  SYS -- notice payloads --> Push
  Push -- notices --> Inv
  OSM -- benches, restrooms, water, steps, paths, names --> SYS
  SYS -- draft requests: photo, text, context --> Hub
  Hub -- drafts --> SYS
  Models -- model weights --> SYS
  Op -- audit and export commands --> SYS
  SYS -- audit output, KPI table --> Op
```

Note: OSM, model files and hub calls flow into the phone part of P0 for phone-side processes; photos sent to the hub go only over the authenticated route (SRS-IF-5) and are not stored there.

## Level 1

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  Host[E1 Host]; Inv[E2 Invitee]; TG[E3 Telegram]; Push[E4 Web Push]; OSM[E5 OSM]; Hub[E6 Hub]; Op[E8 Operator]

  P1[P1 Capture and draft]
  P2[P2 Create gathering]
  P3[P3 Respond and condition]
  P4[P4 Solve and schedule]
```

| P13 | Metrics and audit | Counters, every store | KPI table, audit output | BR-D-7 | SRS-PRIV-5, SRS-FLD-1 |

## Data dictionary

Types: `id128` = 128 random bits, base32 text; `ts` = UTC timestamp to the millisecond; `ct` = ciphertext (AES-256-GCM, nonce prepended) under the group key; `enum(...)`.

### DS1 Gatherings (deleted at Gone, expiry backup)

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| gathering_id | id128 | Primary key |
| group_id | id128 | |
| kind | enum(flare, plan) | |
| state | enum(kindling, lit, ember, gone) | |
| short_code | 5 chars | BR-CH-3 |
| host_member_id | id128 | |
| quorum | int | 2 to 4 (Flare), 2 to 6 (Plan) |
| created_at | ts | t0 for a Flare |
| deadline_at, start_at | ts | Plans only |
| tz | IANA tz name | BR-TIME-2 |
| spot | {place_key, name_ct, lat, lon} | lat/lon needed for Ember search and compass; deleted at Gone |
| invite_ct, scene_ct, host_line_ct | ct | Text encrypted on the phone |
| ladder | list of 4 {step, name_ct, place_key, lat, lon, minutes} | Plans only |
| current_step | int 1 to 4 | Plans |
| ember_spot | {bench_osm_id, lat, lon} | Set at Ember |
| chosen_set | list of member_id | Solver output; never sent to clients |
| lit_at, done_at | ts | |
| headcount | int | |
| expires_at | ts | Storage expiry (BR-D-2) |

### DS2 Responses (deleted at Gone)

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| gathering_id | id128 | |
| member_id | id128 or null | null for anonymous text yes (BR-ID-6) |
| status | enum(yes, taken_back, cant_make_it) | |
| ember_only | bool | BR-A-3 |
| rules | list of {type, value} | BR-C-1; no free text |
| spot_checks | map of candidate id → pass/fail | From P6 |
| faded | bool | Plans |
| arrived | bool, arrived_at ts | |
| idem_keys | set | For dedupe |
| write_token_hash | hash | SRS-SEC-4 |

### DS3 Photo ciphertext (deleted at Gone)
`gathering_id`, `photo_ct` (≤ 1.5 MB after on-phone resize to 1600 px long edge, JPEG quality 80), `blur_preview` (server-stored only as a 32 px blurred JPEG made on the phone, for link previews; deleted at Gone).

### DS4 Scheduler jobs (deleted at Gone)
`job_id`, `gathering_id`, `kind enum(ember, gone, plan_deadline, delete)`, `due_at ts`.

### DS5 Group and members (kept while the group is active)
`group_id`, `created_at`, `last_gathering_at`; members: `member_id`, `name_ct`, `joined_at`, `write_token_hash`. Deleted per BR-D-5 or "Forget this group".

### DS6 Push subscriptions
`member_id`, `endpoint`, `keys`, `created_at`. Deleted 30 days after the group's last gathering (BR-D-5).

### DS7 Telegram map and message refs
Map: `telegram_user_id → member_id` per group (BR-ID-5). Message refs: `gathering_id`, `chat_id`, `message_id` (deleted after bot deletes at Gone).

### DS8 Sparks ciphertext (opt-in, 180 days)
`spark_id`, `group_id`, `place_key_hash` (HMAC of place key with a key derived from the group key, so the server can't read places), `text_ct`, `created_at`.

### DS9 Hot spots ciphertext (180 days)
`group_id`, `blob_ct`, `version`. Plain content (on phone only): list of {place_key, place_name, count, last_date, newest_spark_id}.

### DS10 Counters (kept)
Exactly the counters in docs/product/07-kpis.md, keyed by `group_id`, plus `tier_ran[job][tier]` global totals. No timestamps finer than the day.

### DS11 Live locations (P1; deleted at Gone)
`gathering_id`, `member_id` (host), `lat`, `lon`, `at`. Overwritten in place; no history.

### DS12 Server logs (7 days)
Method, route template (no ids in path segments beyond a hashed form), status, latency, time. Never bodies, fragments, names, locations or tokens (BR-D-6).

### Phone stores (never sent)

| Store | Contents | Lifetime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PH1 | Group keys, member ids, write tokens, display names (plain), free-text conditions | Until "Forget this group" |
| PH2 | Needs profile (BR-A-1) | Until the person clears it |
| PH3 | Saved Lit data (SRS-OFF-1) | Deleted when the phone learns Gone, or 24 h after Lit |
| PH4 | Outbox items {idem_key, kind, payload, recorded_at} | Until accepted or 24 h |
| PH5 | Fairlane pack, Overpass cache | 7 days (cache); pack ships with the app |
| PH6 | Model files | Until the person removes them |
| PH7 | Screen timer (foreground start/stop per gathering) | Deleted after the bucket is sent |
| PH8 | Map drafts (photo deleted after drafting; tags kept until export) | Until exported or discarded |
| PH9 | Rest-loop cards (PDF) | Saved where the person puts them |
| PH10 | Capability report | Until closed |

## Deletion audit coverage

The audit (BR-D-7) must count per-gathering records in DS1, DS2, DS3, DS4, DS7 (message refs), DS11, and search DS12 for any gathering id or short code. Passing = 0 for gatherings that are Gone. It also reports totals for DS5 to DS10 so retention (BR-D-5) can be checked.

# Handoff 02: Analyst to Design

From: Business and systems analyst. Date: Sat 2026-10-10. Next role: Brand and UX design.

## What was delivered (docs/requirements/)

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| 01-srs.md | SRS in ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 layout: 159 numbered "shall" requirements (140 P0, 19 P1), each with priority, source, story and verification method. Covers functional, performance, offline, privacy and retention, security, accessibility, compatibility with our four iPhones, reliability, copy, licensing, field test |
| 02-use-cases.md | Use-case diagram (Mermaid) and 16 use cases with main, alternate and failure paths |
| 03-business-rules.md | 84 atomic rules in 14 groups: identity, quorum, conditions, solver, Flare timeline, Ember, Plan and downshifting, arrival and host +1, expiry and deletion, Sparks and Hot spots, access, time, channels, AI |
| 04-data-flow-and-dictionary.md | Level 0 and level 1 data flow diagrams (Mermaid), 13 process descriptions, data dictionary for 12 server stores and 10 phone stores, deletion audit coverage |
| 05-rtm.csv, 05-rtm.md | Traceability matrix: requirement ↔ PRD source ↔ business rules ↔ stories ↔ acceptance criteria, with empty design, code, test and proof columns |
| tools/trace.py | Generates the matrix and checks every link both ways |
| fixtures/conditions-60.json | 40 core and 20 hard condition phrases with expected rules, for SRS-COND-2 to 4 |
| evidence/ | Pinned Overpass query and result; verified source table |

Also updated: docs/product/01-brd.md evidence rows (small fix to an earlier phase, logged here); docs/BUGLOG.md BUG-004 (Overpass busy and stale mirrors) and BUG-005 (BLS and CDC block scripts).

## Proof

- Traceability check passes: 159 requirements; 84 of 84 rules, 105 of 105 PRD requirements, 61 of 61 stories traced. First run found 33 gaps; all closed (see 05-rtm.md).
- All 3 Mermaid diagrams parse and render with Mermaid 11.4.1 (checked in a browser on localhost: "d0: ok, d1: ok, d2: ok").
- Banned-word and em-dash scan over docs/product, docs/requirements and docs/handoffs: 0 hits.
- Evidence:
  - Fairlane (pinned, OSM 2026-10-10 17:07 UTC, 3 km around way 168151050): 54 benches, 7 picnic tables, 7 restrooms, 3 drinking fountains, 32 parks, 28 steps.
  - CDC DHDS 2022: mobility 12.2%, vision 5.5% (verified from data.cdc.gov).
  - BLS ATUS 2025: 30% socialized on an average day vs 38% in 2015 (verified).
  - The Axios "ages 15 to 24, 61 to 35 min" figure is **unverified**: not in the primary release, do not cite.

## Decisions the analyst took (marked [Analyst decision] in 03-business-rules.md)

1. Display names exist on the server only as ciphertext; conditions name people by member id, resolved on the phone (BR-ID-3, BR-C-3).
2. Anonymous text yeses: max 3, no conditions (BR-ID-6).
3. `back_by` treats a Flare as 60 minutes; `max_walk` uses straight-line distance × 1.3 at 4.8 km/h (BR-C-6, BR-C-7).
4. Groups max 12 people; solver ties broken by lowest member id (BR-S-4, BR-S-6).
5. Ember: phones that don't report within 60 s count as pass (BR-E-4).
6. Fades add people who now fit and never remove anyone; fading at step 4 does nothing and shows nothing (BR-P-6, UC-07 A1).
7. Plans must start within 36 h so the bot can always delete its posts inside Telegram's 48 h limit (BR-P-1).
8. Retention after Gone: push subscriptions and Telegram maps 30 days idle; Sparks and Hot spots 180 days idle or "Forget this group" (BR-D-5).
9. Link previews: blurred photo and invite line only (BR-CH-4).
10. Spot coordinates are held on the server until Gone (for the Ember search and compass). The privacy page must say so.

## What design must produce from this

- **Screens for every P0 and P1 SRS requirement** that has a UI: create (camera, draft, quorum chip), link page, conditions read-back, Lit screen, compass, Ember notice, Plan create and ladder edit, Plan answer, fade, arrival and +1, Done, Spark prompt, Hot spots, needs profile, access line, "Count me in for a closer one", offline state, `/check`, rest-loop request and card, map draft review, website pages.
- **Copy deck** for every string, within the limits (buttons ≤ 3 words, messages ≤ 12). Fixed strings already set by requirements must be used as written, for example "Not this time.", "You're in.", "It's lit. {Host} is at {spot}.", "Smaller plan: 15 min at {bench}.", "This link is missing its key.", "Finds your friend. Not for navigation or emergencies.", "Check the path. Map data can be wrong." If a fixed string doesn't work in design, raise a change request; don't change it silently.
- **Motion and sound specs** for Kindling, Lit, Ember, fade and Gone, with Reduce Motion and silent alternatives (SRS-A11Y-5).
- **Accessibility annotations:** accessible names, VoiceOver order, Dynamic Type at the largest size, 44 pt targets (SRS-A11Y-1 to 6).
- **The large-print card** layout: 18 pt or larger body text, 7:1 contrast (SRS-REST-5).
- Fill the **design** column in 05-rtm.csv with screen or spec ids, then run `python3 docs/requirements/tools/trace.py`.

## Things to keep in mind

- Screen-second targets are requirements, not wishes: host ≤ 15 s to send, invitee ≤ 10 s to "I'm in" (SRS-CRE-9, SRS-RES-7). Design for one primary action per screen.
- No screen may reveal who said yes, who faded, or why someone's yes moved to Ember (SRS-RES-4, SRS-ACC-4, BR-P-7).
- No No button, no streaks, no badges, no feed (SRS-RES-5; docs/product/06-scope.md Out).
- The phone may be on any of four iPhones and any iOS version; design must degrade gracefully when a capability is missing (SRS-COMP-2).
- lab/ belongs to the spike session. Don't edit or commit it.

## Change requests

None against earlier phases. Small fix applied: BRD evidence rows now use the verified figures.

# Flare: Brand strategy

Owner: Brand. Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Inputs: docs/product/ (BRD, PRD v1.1, personas), founder direction (Oct 10).

## Story

Every friend group has a quiet afternoon when someone thinks "we should go outside" and nobody says it, because asking feels like a risk. Flare takes the risk out. You snap where you are. Your friends get a small flame. Each private yes makes it grow. When enough say yes, it catches, and you go. If it doesn't catch, it doesn't die in public: it glows low as a smaller plan, and then it drifts away like smoke, leaving nothing behind.

The fire is the whole brand: a small flame that grows (Kindling), catches (Lit), glows low (Ember) and drifts off (Gone).

## Positioning

**For** friend groups who want to meet outside more often than they do,
**Flare is** the private yes that turns "anyone around?" into an hour outside together,
**unlike** group chats and event apps, where every answer is public and plans either happen or die,
**because** it only goes ahead when enough friends quietly say yes, and when it doesn't, it shrinks instead of failing.

## Brand promise

Seconds on the screen, an hour outside, nothing left behind.

## Personality

| We are | We are not |
| --- | --- |
| Warm, like a campfire after sunset | Hot, loud, urgent |
| Outdoorsy, a Michigan fall afternoon: maple, birch, pine, dusk | Techy, glassy, neon, "AI magic" |
| A little playful (a flame that wobbles, smoke that drifts) | Cute at the cost of clarity |
| Quiet and discreet (nobody sees a no) | Social-feed, gamified, competitive |
| Plain-spoken, short sentences | Jargon, hype, exclamation marks |
| Inclusive by default (big type, spoken scenes, benches) | An afterthought "accessibility mode" |

## What Flare is and isn't

| Flare is | Flare isn't |
| --- | --- |
| A way to ask without asking in public | A social network, feed or profile |
| A meetup that happens only when enough say yes | An event planner with RSVPs and reminders |
| A plan that shrinks when people are tired | A fitness tracker or streak counter |
| Open-source AI on your own phone, used for a few words | An AI companion or chatbot |
| Gone when it's over | A memory archive (Sparks are opt-in, one line) |

## Voice

Rules: buttons ≤ 3 words, messages ≤ 12 words, no exclamation marks, no AI words, never guilt.

| Moment | Say | Don't say |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Send | "Send it" | "Launch your Flare now!" |
| Waiting | "Need 2 more." | "Only 2 more friends to unlock the fun!" |
| Lit | "It's lit. Fuego is at the pond." | "Congratulations, your event is confirmed." |
| Ember | "Smaller plan: 15 min at the bench." | "Your Flare failed. Try again?" |
| Gone, unlit | "Not this time." | "Nobody could make it." |
| Fade | "Smaller plan: the short loop." | "Someone is tired." |
| Offline | "Offline. Saved at 2:14 PM." | "Error: network unavailable" |

## Tagline system

- **Primary:** "If enough friends say yes, it's on."
- **Short:** "Snap it. Say yes. Go."
- **Promise line:** "Seconds of screen. An hour outside."

## Why this wins attention in the field

Of 813 Week 1 entries, 22% use the "AI that wants you to stop using it" line and almost all visuals are green leaves, trails or chat bubbles (docs/research/00). Flare's look is fire at dusk, its subject is people, and the AI is never the hero of the brand. That is the gap.

# Flare: Name check

Checked Sat 2026-10-10. Raw results in [evidence/](evidence/). Not legal advice; a trademark search was **not** done (see the last section).

## App Store (US)

Query: `itunes.apple.com/search?term=flare&entity=software&country=us&limit=50` returned 45 apps; 18 names start with "Flare".

| App | Seller | Category | Ratings | Overlap with us |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Flare - For Groups** | Flare App, Inc. | Social Networking | 6,674 (4.9 avg), updated 2026-09-22 | **Direct.** Groups, events, RSVPs, attendance by geolocation. Same users, same job. |
| Flare Account | Netspend Corporation | Finance | 4,737 | Name only |
| FlareFlow | FlareFlow Pte. Ltd. | Entertainment | 11,065 | Name only |
| Flare - Social Network Client | Sujiteku LLC | Social Networking | 9 | Category, not job |
| Flare: UGC & Brand Deals, Flare Fitness, Flare: Arthritis Support, Flare - Chronic Pain Tracker, Flare AI | various | various | 0 to 79 | Name only |
| AsiaFlare, Solflare, LensFlare | various | various | | Partial word |

## npm

- `flare` is taken (an "applicative-style UIs" library, last modified 2023-08-10).
- 813 packages match "flare". Notable: `@flareapp/*` is **Flare** by flareapp.io, an error-tracking product used by developers; `@flarenetwork/*` is the Flare blockchain.
- Free on Oct 10: `flare-outside`, `flareoutside`, `@flare-outside/app`.

## GitHub

- 12,718 repositories have "flare" in the name. Top results are security tools (Mandiant FLARE), Cloudflare utilities (FlareSolverr, 15,843 stars) and a Mastodon client (DimensionDev/Flare). None is a friends-outside app.
- "flare friends outside": 0 repositories.

## DEV field

No Week 1 entry has "Flare" in its title (813 checked).

## Risk

| Area | Risk | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| This weekend (open-source web app, DEV post, no store listing) | **Medium** | A real, active, well-rated app named Flare does group events. Judges won't confuse them, but a reader searching "Flare app" finds them first. |
| An App Store listing named "Flare" | **High** | Same category and job as "Flare - For Groups". Likely trademark conflict. |
| npm or GitHub naming | **Low** | Crowded but unrelated; use a distinct package and repo name. |

## Decisions and recommendation

1. **Keep "Flare" as the product name for this weekend.** The brand system is built around fire states; the name is short and memorable; the risk this weekend is confusion, not exclusion.
2. **Always pair it with a descriptor in public** where the name stands alone: "Flare, for getting friends outside" on the site title, OG image and post title area. Never "Flare app" alone.
3. **Package and repo names:** use `flare-outside` (free on npm). The private GitHub repo can stay `flare`; if made public, `flare-outside` avoids search collisions. (Founder's call; renaming a repo needs their yes when public.)
4. **Before any store listing or commercial use:** run a USPTO and EUIPO trademark search and get legal advice. If the conflict holds, the fire-state system survives a rename; keep the mark and rename the word.

## Not done

- **Trademark search.** USPTO's search (tmsearch.uspto.gov) needs an interactive session we did not run. Treat "Flare" as possibly registered by Flare App, Inc. for social and event software until checked.
- Domain availability and Google Play were not checked.

# Flare: Brand book

Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Every asset here is generated by `brand/tools/build.mjs` from `brand/tools/palette.mjs`. To change a color or shape, edit the source and run `npm run build` in `brand/tools`; never edit exported files by hand.

![Contact sheet](../../brand/export/contact-sheet.png)

## 1. The mark

The mark is an **upside-down map pin**. A pin points down at a place; Flare's flame points up from it, with the pin's round hole at its base. It reads as "a place, lit." The hole is the one detail that makes it ours; never fill it.

| File | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `brand/logo/flare-mark-maple.svg` | Default on light backgrounds |
| `brand/logo/flare-mark-glow.svg` | Maple flame with a gold "you are here" dot; app icon, splash, dark backgrounds |
| `brand/logo/flare-mark-ink.svg` | One-color print, fax-grade, stamps |
| `brand/logo/flare-mark-birch.svg` | One-color on dark or photos |

Geometry (100-unit grid): flame from y 4 to 96; tongue notch on the left; hole centre (50, 67), radius 12; the gold dot is radius 6. The source path is `FLAME` in build.mjs.

### Wordmark
"flare", lowercase, **Fraunces SemiBold (600)**, tracking −1%, converted to outlines (no font needed). Files: `flare-wordmark-{ink,birch,maple}.svg`. The wordmark is always lowercase; in running text the product name is written "Flare".

### Lockups
| File | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `flare-lockup-horizontal-light.svg` | Site header, docs, light UI |
| `flare-lockup-horizontal-dark.svg` | Dark UI, slides (with gold dot) |
| `flare-lockup-horizontal-ink.svg`, `-birch.svg` | One-color |
| `flare-lockup-stacked-light.svg`, `-dark.svg` | Splash, square spaces, stickers |

Horizontal: the mark is 1.08 × the wordmark's ascender height and sits on the text baseline. Stacked: the mark is 1.6 × that, centred above the word.

### Clear space and minimum size
- **Clear space = one hole** (the hole's diameter, 24% of the mark's height) on every side. Nothing enters it: text, edges, other logos.
- **Minimum size:** mark 16 px (favicon) digital, 6 mm print. Horizontal lockup 96 px wide; stacked 64 px wide. Below 24 px use the plain maple mark, not the glow version (the dot disappears).

### Misuse (don't)
1. Don't fill, move or resize the hole.
2. Don't rotate, mirror or skew the flame. It leans right on purpose.
3. Don't add outlines, drop shadows, glows, bevels, gradients or glass blur.
4. Don't recolor outside the four approved colorways.
5. Don't put the maple mark on maple, gold or busy photos without a birch or dusk plate.
6. Don't retype the wordmark in another font or capitalize it.
7. Don't add sparkles, stars or "AI" glyphs near the mark.
8. Don't use the state marks (below) as the logo.

## 2. The four states

State is shown by **shape first, color second**, so it works in one color and for color-blind people.

| State | Shape | Light | Dark | Files |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Kindling | Small flame (55% size), same baseline | maple-600 | gold-400 | `brand/logo/states/flare-kindling-{light,dark,currentColor}.svg` |
| Lit | Full flame | maple-600 | maple-500 + gold dot | `flare-lit-*` |
| Ember | Low dome with a small hole | ember-700 | maple-600 | `flare-ember-*` |
| Gone | Dashed ring and a smoke wisp drifting up and right | smoke-500 | smoke-300 | `flare-gone-*` |

`currentColor` versions take their color from CSS, for UI use. Kindling's growth toward Lit is the main progress visual: the flame scales from 55% to 100% as "Need N more" counts down (product design sets the steps).

## 3. Color

Source: `brand/tools/palette.mjs`. Tokens: `brand/tokens/tokens.css` and `tokens.json`.

| Token | Hex | Name and role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| birch-50 | #FBF8F2 | Birch white; cards, text on maple |
| birch-100 | #F6F1E7 | Paper; light background |
| birch-200 | #E8DFCE | Lines on light |
| ink-900 | #211A16 | Bark ink; text |
| ink-700 | #4A3F38 | Secondary text |
| maple-500 | #E2622A | Flame on dark |
| maple-600 | #D9531E | **Brand maple**; flame on light |
| maple-700 | #A93C12 | Accent text and buttons on light |
| ember-700 | #9E2C17 | Ember on light |
| gold-400 | #F2B33D | Aspen gold; dot, Kindling on dark |
| gold-300 | #F7CB72 | Accent text on dark |
| pine-700 | #1F4D3A | Pine; positive, ground shapes |
| pine-500 | #2F6B52 | Pine light |
| dusk-900 | #16233A | Dusk; dark background |
| dusk-800 | #1B2A41 | Dark surfaces |
| dusk-700 | #2E4A6B | Lines on dark; icon glow |
| dusk-300 | #A9BCD2 | Secondary text on dark |
| smoke-500 | #6F7987 | Gone on light |
| smoke-300 | #B7BDC5 | Gone on dark |

Proportions on a screen: birch 70%, ink 20%, maple 8%, the rest 2%. Maple is a spark, not a wash.

### Accessible pairs, indoors and in the sun

Every pair product design may use is checked by `brand/tools/contrast.mjs` (WCAG 2.2 ratio, plus an outdoor model with screen reflection R = 0.15 for bright shade and R = 0.40 for open sun). Full table: [contrast-table.md](contrast-table.md). All 22 pairs pass WCAG.

What the outdoor numbers show:

- **Light mode survives daylight; dark mode doesn't.** Body text on birch keeps 6.4:1 in bright shade; maple on dusk drops to 2.4:1 and 1.6:1 in sun.
- **Sun mode rule:** screens used outside (Lit, compass, Ember, arrival) set `data-sun` on `<html>`. That forces the light roles and scales text by 1.15, whatever the system theme. Dark mode is for evenings and indoors.
- **Buttons:** primary buttons are maple-700 with birch-50 text (5.93:1). Ink text on maple-600 fails (4.25:1) and is not allowed.
- **Never use gold for text on light** (1.65:1). Gold is for the dot and dark mode only.

## 4. Type

Both families are open-licensed (SIL Open Font License 1.1). Files and licenses: `brand/fonts/`. Packages for the app: `@fontsource/fraunces@5.3.0`, `@fontsource/atkinson-hyperlegible-next@5.3.0`.

| Family | Use | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Fraunces** (400, 600, 400 italic) | Wordmark; display and titles ≥ 22 px | Soft, warm "old style" serif; feels like a trail sign or a park guide |
| **Atkinson Hyperlegible Next** (400, 700, 400 italic) | Everything else: UI, body, labels, numbers | Designed by the Braille Institute for readers with low vision; distinct letterforms (I l 1, 0 O) |

Scale (from tokens.json; px at default text size, set in rem so Dynamic Type scales it):

| Style | Family | Size / line | Weight |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| display | Fraunces | 40 / 44 | 600 |
| title | Fraunces | 28 / 34 | 600 |
| heading | Atkinson | 22 / 28 | 700 |
| body | Atkinson | 18 / 26 | 400 |
| label (buttons) | Atkinson | 16 / 22 | 700 |
| small | Atkinson | 15 / 20 | 400 |
| sun (outdoor primary line) | Atkinson | 22 / 30 | 700 |

Rules: body text never below 15 px; no all-caps runs over 3 words; numbers in Atkinson; left-aligned text.

## 5. Iconography

Files: `brand/icons/*.svg` (16 icons). Grid 24 × 24, 2 px stroke, round caps and joins, no fills, `currentColor`.

camera, compass, bench, restroom, water, steps, here (arrived), fade (step down), spark, hotspots, plan, card (print), mapfix, offline, sunset, plusone.

Rules: draw new icons on the same grid and stroke; one idea per icon; real objects from the outdoors over abstract symbols; no sparkles, stars, magic wands, robots or chat bubbles for AI; the only filled shapes in the system are the flame states.

## 6. Illustration and texture

- **Flat shapes, no gradients** except the dusk radial glow in the app icon.
- **Ground line:** a soft pine horizon shape at the bottom of large surfaces (see the OG image), 55% opacity.
- **Paper grain:** `brand/texture/paper-grain.svg` (SVG filter) or `paper-grain-256.png` (tile), 4 to 8% opacity, on backgrounds only, never on text or the mark. Skip it on low-power devices and in Reduce Transparency.
- **No glass blur, no neon, no purple gradients, no 3D.**

## 7. Photography

Most photos in Flare are the users' own invite photos; the brand never filters or crops them. For our site, post and social:

- Real places near Fairlane (Ford Woods Park, the Rouge River paths, benches by the water), shot on our phones.
- Natural light, ideally the last two hours before sunset (sunset Oct 11: 6:57 PM EDT).
- People at a distance, from behind or as hands and feet, unless that person has given consent on the day (product rule: first names only, no faces or voices without a yes).
- Show the things the product cares about: benches, paths, water, trees, a group arriving.
- No stock photos, no phones held up to the camera, no screens glowing in the dark.

## 8. Motion and sound direction

Product design specifies exact timings; the brand sets the character.

| State change | Motion | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A yes lands (Kindling grows) | Flame grows one step, soft overshoot, 260 ms | Small dry tick, like a twig |
| Lit | Flame catches: grows to full, the dot lights gold, one gentle pulse, 480 ms; one haptic | A low warm "whump", under 600 ms |
| Ember | Flame settles down into the dome, 480 ms | A soft low note |
| Gone | Smoke drifts up and right and fades, 900 ms | Silence |

Easing: `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)` out; durations 160, 260, 480 ms (tokens). With Reduce Motion: crossfade only, 0 ms durations in tokens. Sound respects the silent switch where the platform exposes it.

## 9. Exported assets

| Asset | Files | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App icon master | `brand/icon/app-icon.svg`, `app-icon-maskable.svg` | 1024 × 1024 |
| PWA icons | `brand/export/icons/icon-{16,32,48,64,120,152,167,180,192,256,384,512,1024}.png` | |
| Maskable | `icon-maskable-192.png`, `icon-maskable-512.png` | Flame inside the 80% safe circle |
| Apple touch | `apple-touch-icon.png` (180), plus 152, 167, 120 in the set | iOS adds no rounding gloss; our square art is full-bleed |
| Favicon | `brand/export/favicon/favicon.svg`, `favicon.ico` (16, 32, 48), `favicon-{16,32,48}.png` | |
| Splash (apple-touch-startup-image) | `brand/export/splash/{iphone-13, iphone-17-pro, iphone-16-17-pro-max}-{portrait,landscape}-{light,dark}.png` (12 files) | 1170 × 2532, 1206 × 2622, 1320 × 2868. `<link>` tags with media queries: `head-tags.html` |
| Social share | `brand/export/social/og-image-1200x630.png` | Open Graph and X |
| DEV cover | `brand/export/social/dev-cover-1000x420.png` | DEV's cover ratio |
| Texture | `brand/texture/paper-grain.svg`, `paper-grain-256.png` | |

# Handoff 03: Brand to Product design

From: Brand designer. Date: Sat 2026-10-10. Next role: Product (UX and UI) design.

## What was delivered

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| docs/brand/01-strategy.md | Story, positioning, promise, personality, is and isn't, voice table, taglines |
| docs/brand/02-name-check.md | App Store, npm, GitHub and DEV checks with risk levels and a recommendation; raw data in docs/brand/evidence/ |
| docs/brand/03-brand-book.md | Mark, wordmark, lockups, clear space, minimum sizes, misuse, the four state marks, color system, sun mode, type, icons, illustration and texture, photography, motion and sound direction, asset index, manifest and head snippets |
| docs/brand/contrast-table.md | 22 color pairs: WCAG ratio plus outdoor ratios (bright shade, open sun) |
| brand/logo/ | 25 SVGs: 4 marks, 3 wordmarks, 6 lockups, 12 state marks (light, dark, currentColor) |
| brand/icons/ | 16 UI icons (24 grid, 2 px stroke, currentColor) |
| brand/icon/ | App icon masters (standard and maskable) |
| brand/export/ | 13 PNG icon sizes, 2 maskable, apple-touch-icon, favicon.svg/.ico/PNGs, 12 splash screens with `<link>` tags, OG image, DEV cover, contact sheet |
| brand/tokens/ | tokens.css (light, dark, sun mode, reduced motion) and tokens.json (colors, roles, type scale, radii, spacing, motion) |
| brand/fonts/ | Fraunces and Atkinson Hyperlegible Next WOFF2 files with OFL licenses |
| brand/tools/ | palette.mjs (single source), build.mjs (generates everything), contrast.mjs (pass/fail gate) |

## Proof

- `npm run build` regenerates all assets: logo=25, icons=16, icon=2, export=37, texture=2, tokens=2, fonts=8 files.
- `npm run contrast`: all 22 pairs pass WCAG 2.2 (body text ≥ 7:1, secondary and accent ≥ 4.5:1, large UI ≥ 3:1). The first run failed one pair (ink on maple button, 4.25:1); fixed by making buttons maple-700 with birch text (5.93:1).
- Visual review: every logo SVG, the contact sheet, the OG image, the DEV cover and a splash were rendered and inspected. Fixed during review: choppy Gone smoke, a broken "g" in outlined text (BUG-006), an undersized mark in lockups, unclear restroom and fade icons.
- Sizes checked: favicon.ico holds 16, 32 and 48; icons 512 and maskable 512 are 512 × 512; apple-touch-icon is 180 × 180; OG 1200 × 630; DEV cover 1000 × 420; splash files match each phone (1170 × 2532, 1206 × 2622, 1320 × 2868, and landscape).
- Export folder cut from 40 MB to 2.4 MB by removing grain from icons and splash screens.
- Tooling: @resvg/resvg-js 2.6.2, opentype.js 2.0.0, @fontsource 5.3.0 packages, png-to-ico 3.0.2; `npm install` reported 0 vulnerabilities.

## Key decisions and why

1. **The mark is an upside-down map pin:** a flame with the pin's hole at its base. It ties fire to place and is distinct from flame emoji and other "Flare" logos. The hole is never filled.
2. **State is shape first, color second:** Kindling (small flame), Lit (full), Ember (low dome), Gone (dashed ring and smoke). In light mode Kindling and Lit share maple; size tells them apart. Works in one color and for color-blind people.
3. **Sun mode:** outdoor screens force light roles and 1.15× text (`data-sun`), because dark pairs lose most of their contrast in daylight (maple on dusk: 4.50 indoors, 1.56 in open sun).
4. **Type:** Fraunces for the wordmark and titles; Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, designed for low-vision readers, for everything else.
5. **Name:** keep "Flare" this weekend, with a descriptor; risk is Medium now and High for any App Store listing ("Flare - For Groups", 6,674 ratings, same category). Trademark not searched. Package name `flare-outside` is free on npm.

## What product design must do next

- Design every screen listed in docs/handoffs/02-analyst.md using `brand/tokens/tokens.css` roles (never raw hex), the 16 icons (draw new ones on the same grid), and the state marks for Kindling, Lit, Ember and Gone.
- Turn the motion and sound direction (brand book section 8) into exact specs: Kindling growth steps per yes, Lit catch, Ember settle, Gone drift; with Reduce Motion and silent alternatives.
- Apply sun mode to Lit, compass, Ember and arrival screens.
- Keep fixed strings from the SRS as written; the voice table in 01-strategy.md shows the tone for new ones (buttons ≤ 3 words, messages ≤ 12).
- Fill the `design` column in docs/requirements/05-rtm.csv and run `python3 docs/requirements/tools/trace.py`.

## Things to know

- Gold is never used for text on light backgrounds (1.65:1).
- Primary buttons: maple-700 background, birch-50 label. Ink on maple is not allowed.
- The glow mark (gold dot) needs at least 24 px; below that use the plain maple mark.
- Founder decision needed later: public repo name and any store listing name (02-name-check.md).
- `lab/` is not ours to edit.

## Change requests

None against earlier phases.

The brand is done and committed locally (`3df1d19`, plus `3ae61ec` to remove a banned word). Nothing is pushed or public, and I've sent the summary to your manager session.

**One decision for you: the name.** The App Store has "Flare - For Groups" by Flare App, Inc. It's a social networking app with 6,674 ratings (4.9 average), last updated Sep 22, and it does group events, RSVPs and attendance. That's our category and our job.
- **This weekend:** medium risk. We're an open-source web app with no store listing, but anyone searching "Flare app" will find them first.
- **Any App Store listing:** high risk.
- I did not do a trademark search.

My recommendation: keep "Flare" this weekend, always with a descriptor ("Flare, for getting friends outside"), and use `flare-outside` for the package and public repo name; it's free on npm. Decide on a rename before any store listing or commercial use. Details are in [docs/brand/02-name-check.md](docs/brand/02-name-check.md).

**The brand:**
- **The mark** is an upside-down map pin: a flame pointing up, with the pin's round hole at its base. "A place, lit."
- **The four states:** Kindling is a small flame, Lit a full flame with a gold dot, Ember a low dome, and Gone a dashed ring with smoke drifting off. Shape carries the state first and color second, so it works in one color and for color-blind people.
- **Palette:** maple orange, birch white, pine green, dusk blue and aspen gold, with paper grain on large surfaces only.
- **Type:** Fraunces for the wordmark and titles. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, which was designed for low-vision readers, for everything else. Both are open-licensed.
- **Assets:**
  - 25 logo files
  - 16 UI icons
  - app icons in 13 sizes, plus maskable and Apple touch versions
  - a favicon set
  - 12 splash screens covering our three iPhone screen sizes, in portrait and landscape, light and dark
  - a social share image and a DEV cover
  - design tokens for the app's colors, type and motion

  A script in `brand/tools` regenerates everything.

**Checks:**
- All 22 color pairs product design may use pass WCAG contrast.
- The outdoor-light check found that dark mode collapses in sun: maple on dusk drops from 4.5:1 to 1.6:1. So screens used outside (Lit, compass, Ember, arrival) get a "sun mode" that forces the light colors and 15% larger text.
- I rendered and looked at every asset. That caught and fixed choppy smoke on Gone, a broken "g" in the outlined text (logged as BUG-006), a lockup flame that was too small, and two unclear icons.
- Removing grain from the splash screens and icons cut the export folder from 40 MB to 2.4 MB.

Your two architect notes are now open questions in the analyst handoff: keep coordinates off the server, and what happens to "only the long one" after a fade. The brand book is [docs/brand/03-brand-book.md](docs/brand/03-brand-book.md), and the handoff to product design is [docs/handoffs/03-brand.md](docs/handoffs/03-brand.md).

Another Claude session sent a message:
<cross-session-message from="uds:<socket>" from-session="local_beb3cc8c-e162-46cc-bd0a-f870e8717ebd" from-name="Dev relay login" from-mode="prompting">
Good work on the brand. The pin-flame mark is clever, the state shapes read without color, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next is the right UI font, and catching sun mode by measuring outdoors is exactly the kind of proof I want.

Name: I agree. Keep "Flare" this weekend with a descriptor, and use `flare-outside` for the repo and package. I'll decide on a rename before any store listing.

One thing isn't at the bar yet: **the share images.** The DEV cover shows in the feed and is the first thing judges see. Right now it's flat navy with a lot of empty space, and it doesn't feel like a Michigan fall afternoon outside.
- Push it further with 2 or 3 directions:
  - an illustrated outdoor scene (horizon at golden hour, maple leaves, a bench or path), with the flame states living in the scene instead of in a row of labels
  - paper grain that you can actually see
  - a tighter, bigger tagline
- Pick the strongest and apply it to the OG image too.
- Also check the app icon at home-screen size (60 and 120 px) next to real iOS icons. Make sure the inner dot doesn't turn to mush.
- Small fix, then hand off.

Then bring in the product designer:

You're a UI/UX designer with 10 years designing playful, game-like consumer apps that people love. Read the handoffs and design Flare completely. It should feel modern, interactive, warm and natural, never boring, and make people want to go outside. Taking or opening a photo should feel magical. It must stay accessible.

Direction from me:
- Built for outside: readable in bright sun on an iPhone, big type, one main action per screen, and thumb reach. Dark mode is for evenings. Use the sun mode the brand found.
- The photo moment: the picture develops like a print while the six words appear.
- The phone should want to go back in your pocket. The last screen of every flow points outside, not to more app.
- Premium is the bar. Use the latest production-grade UI libraries you'd actually ship with (check current versions), for example a modern component system with accessible primitives. Build the mockups and prototype with them, so they carry straight into the app. The architect confirms the stack in a decision record.
- The website is part of this: one scroll that shows what Flare is, how it works in 3 steps, the privacy promise, the accessibility statement, and "run it yourself."

Deliver, all finished (design/ and docs/design/):
- Design brief and a competitive UX scan of the existing entries
- User flows and information architecture, covering both Flare (now) and Plan (later) modes
- Wireframes for every screen
- High-fidelity screens for every screen and every state (empty, loading, error, offline, success), light, dark and sun mode. Build them as real code in design/prototype/, and export PNG screenshots for docs.
- Clickable prototype of the key moments: send a Flare, say yes (with a condition), it lights, find your friend, it shrinks to an Ember, answer a Plan, leave a Spark
- Website design, all sections, mobile and desktop
- Design system: color, type, spacing, radius, elevation and motion tokens (as CSS variables + JSON), and every component with all its states
- Accessibility annotations: contrast, focus order, screen reader labels, touch target sizes

Done = engineering can build every screen pixel-for-pixel from your files. Write the handoff for motion and copy.

input.content:
# Flare: Design brief and competitive UX scan

Owner: Product design. Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Inputs: handoffs 01 to 03, PRD v1.1, SRS, brand book.

## 1. Brief

**Problem.** Friends want to meet outside but asking is awkward, nobody wants to arrive alone, and plans stall in the chat (BRD section 1).

**Design goal.** Make saying yes take one tap and a few seconds, make "it's on" feel like a small celebration, and make the last screen of every flow point outside.

**Targets (from the SRS, they are requirements):**

| Moment | Target |
| --- | --- |
| Host: open to sent | ≤ 15 s (SRS-CRE-9) |
| Invitee: open to "I'm in" | ≤ 10 s (SRS-RES-7) |
| Link page interactive | ≤ 2.0 s on iPhone 13 over 4G (SRS-PERF-1) |
| Contrast | WCAG 2.2 AA everywhere; body text ≥ 7:1 (brand contrast table) |
| Touch targets | ≥ 44 × 44 pt (SRS-A11Y-6); primary actions 56 pt tall |

**Principles**

1. **One main action per screen,** in the thumb zone (bottom 40% of the screen), full width, 56 pt tall.
2. **Built for outside.** Screens used outdoors run in sun mode: light roles, 1.15× text, no thin type, no low-contrast decoration (brand book section 3).
3. **The phone wants to go back in your pocket.** Every flow ends on a screen whose message points outside ("Go. They're by the pond.") with no further navigation, and whose primary action is optional.
4. **The flame is the interface.** Progress, success and failure are shown by the flame's state (Kindling grows, Lit catches, Ember settles, Gone drifts), not by spinners, badges or bars.
5. **Magic moments, earned.** The photo develops like a print while the six words type in. Lit is a short celebration with sound and one haptic. Both respect Reduce Motion.
6. **Private by construction.** No screen ever shows who said yes, who faded, or why someone moved to an Ember (SRS-RES-4, SRS-ACC-4).
7. **Accessible equals.** Every screen works with VoiceOver, the largest text size, and without color.

**Out of scope for design:** feeds, profiles, streaks, badges, a No button, chat (PRD non-goals).

## 2. Competitive UX scan

Source: 813 Week 1 entries (docs/research/00), the 12 top entries read in full, and the 17 Weekend winners. What their interfaces do, and what we take or avoid.

| Pattern seen | Where | Our move |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat-style AI screen as the main UI | Most "trail planner" and "quest" entries (23% and 16% of titles) | Avoid. No chat. AI output is six words and a 20-word scene. |
| "Screen-off" counter or lock screen | Drift (screen-on 2m5s), DeskBreak (locks the screen), ZSDM (screen-off score) | Take the idea, measure it privately (screen seconds as a bucket, KPI 4), never show a score. |
| Audio-first while walking | ZSDM, Drift | Take it: the talking compass works with the screen down. |
| Printable card instead of a screen | TrailTruth (weekly go/no-go card), Nature Bingo | Take it: Bench to Bench large-print card. |
| Photo proof judged by AI | 6% of entries, Side Quest | Avoid (out of scope). The photo is an invitation, not evidence. |
| Gamified XP, levels, creatures | Side Quest (hatches creatures), TouchGrass (XP, level 5 unlocks) | Avoid. Delight comes from the flame and from people arriving. |
| Map-heavy screens | 10% use Leaflet/MapLibre maps | Avoid as the main view. A compass and a sentence beat a map outdoors. |
| Weather or frost dashboards | PLOT, FrostWise, Tendril | Avoid dashboards. One nature line per Flare. |
| Desktop-first layouts | Side Quest runs on a desktop "home base" | Avoid. Phone-first, iPhone Safari, one column. |
| Group play | IRL Clash (strangers, competitive rounds) | Different: friends, cooperative, private. |
| Long setup before value | Many: model downloads, accounts, settings | Avoid. Value in the first 10 s; model download is opt-in later. |

Gaps no entry fills, which our UI owns: a private yes with a visible count only; a plan that shrinks on screen instead of failing; an access line under every invite; a spoken scene for screen readers; a last screen that sends you outside.

## 3. Stack for the prototype (proposed; the architect confirms)

The prototype is real code meant to carry into the app.

| Choice | Version (checked Oct 10) | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Svelte | 5.57.2 | Compiles away; small bundles fit the 150 KB gzipped cap on the link page (SRS-PERF-2) |
| SvelteKit | 3.0.1 | Routing, static export, service worker support |
| Vite | 8.3.4 | Build tool used by SvelteKit |
| Bits UI | 2.19.5 | Headless, accessible primitives for Svelte 5 (dialog, toggle group, slider, tabs) with keyboard and screen reader support |
| @fontsource Fraunces and Atkinson Hyperlegible Next | 5.3.0 | Self-hosted OFL fonts (no third-party font requests, SRS-PRIV-7) |
| playwright-core | 1.64.0 | Screenshots through the installed Chrome (no browser download) |
| axe-core | latest stable | Automated accessibility checks on every screen |

Considered: React 19.3.0 with React Aria Components 1.22.1 (excellent accessibility, larger runtime) and Radix. Motion: the Web Animations API and Svelte transitions, no animation library, to stay inside the size budget.

# Flare: User flows and information architecture Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Screen ids (H, I, P, O, W) are used in wireframes, hi-fi exports, the prototype and the RTM `design` column. ## 1. Information architecture There is no home feed and no tab bar. The app opens to the camera; everything else is reached from a gathering's link or a small menu. ```mermaid flowchart TB open([Open Flare]) --> H1[H1 Camera] H1 --> H2[H2 Develop: photo + six words] H2 --> H3[H3 Send it: quorum, host line] H3 --> H4[H4 Sent: share + pocket it] H4 --> H5[H5 Host: Kindling] H5 --> H6[H6 Host: Lit, arrivals] H5 --> I9[I9 Ember] H6 --> I11[I11 Spark] H1 -- menu --> M[O0 Menu sheet] M --> P1[P1 Plan: ask] M --> O1[O1 Hot spots] M --> O2[O2 My needs] M --> O5[O5 Bench to Bench] M --> O6[O6 Fix the map] M --> O4[O4 Phone check] M --> O8[O8 On-phone AI] link([Open a link]) --> I0[I0 Join group: your name] I0 --> I1[I1 Invite] link --> I1 link --> P4[P4 Plan invite] ``` Routes (prototype and app): | Route | Screens | | --- | --- | | `/` | H1 to H4 (create) | | `/g/{group}#key` | I0 join; group menu | | `/f/{id}#key` | I1 to I12 (Flare, by state); H5, H6 for the host | | `/p/new` | P1, P2, P3 | | `/p/{id}#key` | P4 to P7 | | `/hot` | O1 | | `/needs` | O2 | | `/loop` | O5 | | `/mapfix` | O6 | | `/check` | O4 | | `/ai` | O8 | | `/site` (website, separate deploy) | W1 to W6 | ## 2. Screen inventory | Id | Screen | Mode | States designed | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | H1 | Camera | light/dark | live, permission ask, denied (pick a photo), loading | | H2 | Develop | light/dark | developing, drafted, AI failed (template), offline | | H3 | Send it | light/dark | ready, editing, sending, error, offline (queued) | | H4 | Sent | light/dark | success | | H5 | Host: Kindling | sun | 0 of N, growing, near lit, offline | | H6 | Host: Lit | sun | lit, arrivals, +1 sheet, done confirm | | I0 | Join group | light/dark | empty, typing, error | | I1 | Invite | light/dark/sun | Kindling, loading, missing key, already lit, gone | | I2 | Add a condition | light/dark | empty, typing, dictating, didn't catch, name not in group | | I3 | Read-back | light/dark | confirm | | I4 | You're in | light/dark | success, queued offline | | I5 | Spot may not suit you | light/dark | prompt | | I6 | Lit | sun | lit, offline saved, smaller plan (after fade) | | I7 | Find them (compass) | sun | pointing, facing, no orientation, no GPS, offline | | I8 | I'm here | sun | success | | I9 | Ember | sun | ember waiting, ember lit | | I10 | Not this time | light/dark | gone | | I11 | Spark | light/dark | empty, typing, saved, skipped | | I12 | Go outside (end) | light/dark | end of flow | | P1 | Plan: ask | light/dark | empty, typing, time pickers, deadline error | | P2 | Ladder | light/dark | drafting, drafted, editing a step, after-sunset warning | | P3 | Plan sent | light/dark | success | | P4 | Plan invite | light/dark | open, need N more, with condition | | P5 | Plan lit | sun | lit at step n | | P6 | I'm fading | sun | confirm, smaller plan notice | | P7 | Plan not this time | light/dark | gone | | O0 | Menu sheet | light/dark | open | | O1 | Hot spots | light/dark | empty, list | | O2 | My needs | light/dark | empty, set | | O3 | Offline banner | all | component | | O4 | Phone check | light/dark | running, report | | O5 | Bench to Bench | light/dark | request, read-back, loop + card preview, no loop fits | | O6 | Fix the map | light/dark | drafting, review, export ready | | O8 | On-phone AI | light/dark | not downloaded, downloading, ready, failed | | W1 to W6 | Website sections | mobile/desktop | see 06-website.md | ## 3. Key flows ### F1 Send a Flare (host), target ≤ 15 s ```mermaid flowchart LR A[H1 Camera live] -->|tap shutter| B[H2 Develop
print develops,
six words type in] B -->|Use these| C[H3 Send it] C -->|Send it| D[H4 Sent
share sheet opens] D -->|Pocket it| E((Phone away)) B -.AI fails.-> B2[Template words
'Outside at the pond. Come?'] C -.offline.-> C2[Queued: 'Sends when you're back online.'] ``` ### F2 Say yes, with a condition (invitee), target ≤ 10 s ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Link in iMessage / Telegram] --> B[I1 Invite
photo, six words,
Need 1 more] B -->|I'm in| D[I4 You're in
'We'll buzz you when it's lit.'] B -->|Add a condition| C[I2 Condition] --> C3[I3 Read-back] -->|Yes| D B -.spot fails my needs.-> S[I5 'Count me in for a closer one?'] --> D D --> E((Phone away)) ``` ### F3 It lights, find your friend ```mermaid flowchart LR N[Buzz: It's lit] --> L[I6 Lit
sun mode] -->|Find them| K[I7 Compass
speaks, ticks] -->|arrive| H[I8 I'm here] --> X[I12 Go outside
'They're by the pond.'] ``` ### F4 Shrinks to an Ember ```mermaid flowchart LR K[H5 Kindling, 30 min] --> E[I9 Ember
'Smaller plan: 15 min at the bench.'] E -->|one yes| L[I6 Lit at the bench] E -->|60 min| G[I10 Not this time] ``` ### F5 Answer a Plan, then fade ```mermaid flowchart LR A[P4 Plan invite
ladder of 4] -->|I'm in| Y[I4 You're in] A -->|Just the short one| C[I3 Read-back: step 3 or smaller] --> Y Y -->|deadline| L[P5 Lit at step 2] L -->|I'm fading| F[P6 Smaller plan: step 3] ``` ### F6 Leave a Spark ```mermaid flowchart LR D[Host taps Done] --> S[I11 Spark: one line, optional] -->|Save| X[I12 Go outside] S -->|Skip| X ``` ## 4. Navigation rules - No back stacks deeper than 2. Close (×) returns to the previous screen; the flow end screen has no "home" button, only "Close". - Sheets (Bits UI Dialog) for secondary actions: +1, menu, condition, Done confirm. - Every screen has exactly one primary button. Secondary actions are text buttons. - The menu (O0) opens from a 44 pt button on the camera screen; it is the only global navigation.

<!--
  The flame: Flare's main status visual.
  state: kindling | lit | ember | gone. progress (0..1) grows Kindling from 55% to 90% of full size.
  The lab recommends a WebGL shader for the live flicker in the app; this SVG/CSS
  version is the fallback and the design reference.
-->
<script lang="ts">
  import { FLAME, HOLE, DOME, ring, type FlameState } from "$lib/brand";

  let {
    state = "lit",
    progress = 0,
    size = 120,
    dot = true,
    animate = true,
    label = "",
  }: { state?: FlameState; progress?: number; size?: number; dot?: boolean; animate?: boolean; label?: string } = $props();

  const scale = $derived(state === "kindling" ? 0.55 + 0.35 * Math.min(1, Math.max(0, progress)) : 1);
  const color = $derived(
    state === "kindling" ? "var(--kindling)" : state === "lit" ? "var(--lit)" : state === "ember" ? "var(--ember)" : "var(--gone)",
  );
  const flameD = `${FLAME} ${ring(HOLE.cx, HOLE.cy, HOLE.r)}`;
  const emberD = `${DOME} ${ring(50, 81, 8)}`;
  const name = $derived(label || { kindling: "Kindling", lit: "Lit", ember: "Ember", gone: "Gone" }[state]);
</script>

<svg
  class="flame {state}"
  class:animate
  width={size}
  height={size}
  viewBox="0 0 100 100"
  role="img"
  aria-label={name}
  style:--flame-color={color}
>
  {#if state === "kindling" || state === "lit"}
    <g class="grow" style:transform="translate(50px, 96px) scale({scale}) translate(-50px, -96px)">
      <g class="flicker">
        <path fill-rule="evenodd" d={flameD} fill="var(--flame-color)" />
        {#if dot && state === "lit"}
          <circle class="dot" cx={HOLE.cx} cy={HOLE.cy} r="6" fill="var(--c-gold-400)" />
        {/if}
      </g>
    </g>
  {:else if state === "ember"}
    <path class="settle" fill-rule="evenodd" d={emberD} fill="var(--flame-color)" />
  {:else}
    <g class="drift" fill="none" stroke="var(--flame-color)">
      <circle cx="50" cy="86" r="7" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="3.2 3.2" opacity="0.7" />
      <path d="M50 76 C41 67 59 60 51 49 C45 40 58 33 61 22" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" />
      <path d="M66 18 C70 13 67 8 72 3" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.5" />
    </g>
  {/if}
</svg>

<style>
  .flame { overflow: visible; flex: none; }
  .grow { transition: transform var(--dur-base) var(--ease-spring); transform-origin: 0 0; }
  .animate .flicker { transform-origin: 50px 96px; animation: flicker 2.6s var(--ease-in-out) infinite; }
  .animate.lit .dot { animation: glow 2.6s var(--ease-in-out) infinite; }
  .animate .settle { transform-origin: 50px 95px; animation: settle var(--dur-slow) var(--ease-out) both; }
  .animate .drift { animation: drift var(--dur-drift) var(--ease-out) both; }
  @keyframes flicker {
    0%, 100% { transform: scale(1, 1) skewX(0deg); }
    30% { transform: scale(1.015, 0.985) skewX(-1.2deg); }
    60% { transform: scale(0.99, 1.02) skewX(1deg); }
  }
  @keyframes glow { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.82; } }
  @keyframes settle { from { transform: scaleY(1.6); opacity: 0.6; } to { transform: scaleY(1); opacity: 1; } }
  @keyframes drift { from { transform: translate(0, 6px); opacity: 0.2; } to { transform: translate(0, 0); opacity: 1; } }
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    .animate .flicker, .animate.lit .dot, .animate .settle, .animate .drift { animation: none; }
  }
</style>

content.text: Now the website: one scroll covering what Flare is, how it works in 3 steps, the privacy promise, the accessibility statement and "run it yourself".

input.content:
Flare, for getting friends outside
How it worksPrivacyAccessibilityRun it

Flare, for getting friends outside

If enough friends say yes, it's on.

Snap where you are. Friends get a short invite and answer in private. It only happens if enough say yes, and nobody ever sees a no.

Try the prototype See how

Seconds of screen. An hour outside.

How it works

  1. 1 Snap where you are

    The photo develops like a print while an open model writes six words. Send it to iMessage, WhatsApp or Telegram.

  2. 2 Friends say yes, in private

    Each yes grows the flame. Everyone sees the count, never the names. Add a condition like "only if Amor comes".

  3. 3 It's lit. Go.

    When enough say yes, everyone gets the spot. A talking compass finds your friend, even with no signal.

It shrinks instead of dying

Plans fail in group chats. Flare plans get smaller.

  • KindlingWaiting for yeses, up to 30 min.
  • LitEnough said yes. Go.
  • EmberDidn't catch? 15 min at the nearest bench. One friend is enough.
  • Gone"Not this time." Same words for everyone. Then it's deleted.

Plans for later have four sizes, from a long loop to 20 minutes on a bench. Anyone who's tired can quietly make it one step smaller.

The privacy promise

  • Photos are encrypted on your phone. The key is in the link, after the #, and never reaches our server.
  • Conditions and access needs stay on your phone. Only rules like "back by 5 PM" are sent.
  • Nobody's no is ever shown or stored.
  • Within 5 minutes of the end, the Flare, its photo and every yes are deleted. A few counts remain.
  • No accounts, no ads, no trackers.

Deletion audit, after our Sunday field test

Audit output appears here after the field test (Sun Oct 11).
It counts leftover records in every store; passing is 0.

Limits we're honest about: Telegram sees what's posted in Telegram. In a small group, people can sometimes guess who said yes. Text and satellite messages are outside our control.

Built for friends who need more

  • Every invite shows benches, restrooms and mapped steps near the spot.
  • Set your needs once, on your phone. If a spot doesn't suit you, Flare counts you in for a closer one, and nobody learns why.
  • The talking compass says "Fuego, 400 meters, slightly left." No map to read.
  • The invite photo has a spoken description for screen readers.
  • Bench to Bench prints a large-print walking card with a seat every 200 m.

Target: WCAG 2.2 AA on every screen, body text at 7:1 contrast or more, touch targets 44 pt. Tested with VoiceOver and the largest text size. Known gaps are listed on GitHub.

Why benches: they raise the chance a mobility-impaired senior goes for a walk from 60% to 75% (Netspar). 12.2% of US adults have a mobility disability and 5.5% a vision disability (CDC, 2022).

Run it yourself

Flare is open source. The AI is open-weight Gemma 4 running on your own laptop, so your photos never touch a closed API.

git clone https://github.com/<owner>/flare-outside
cd flare-outside
ollama pull gemma4:e4b
npm ci && npm run dev

The repository link goes live when the repo is public. Full setup steps are in the README.

Made for the DEV Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge, Week 1: Touch Grass. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors.

# Flare: Design system

Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Tokens: [design/system/tokens.css](../../design/system/tokens.css) and [tokens.json](../../design/system/tokens.json), generated by `node design/system/build-tokens.mjs` from the brand palette (`brand/tools/palette.mjs`). Components: `design/prototype/src/lib/components/` (Svelte 5, Bits UI primitives). Live catalog: `/components` in the prototype; export: [components-light-dark-sun.png](../../design/exports/pages/components-light-dark-sun.png).

## 1. Tokens

### Themes
Apply on `:root` or any element: `[data-theme="light"]`, `[data-theme="dark"]`, `[data-sun]` (outdoor screens; wins over theme). Without an attribute, `prefers-color-scheme` decides. `[data-reduce-motion]` or `prefers-reduced-motion` sets every duration to 0.

| Role variable | Light | Dark | Sun |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--bg` | birch-100 #F6F1E7 | dusk-900 #16233A | birch-100 |
| `--surface` | birch-50 #FBF8F2 | dusk-800 #1B2A41 | birch-50 |
| `--line` | birch-200 #E8DFCE | dusk-700 #2E4A6B | birch-200 |
| `--text` | ink-900 #211A16 | birch-100 | ink-900 |
| `--text-muted` | ink-700 #4A3F38 | dusk-300 #A9BCD2 | ink-700 |
| `--accent-bg` (primary button) | maple-700 #A93C12 | maple-500 #E2622A | maple-700 |
| `--on-accent` | birch-50 | ink-900 | birch-50 |
| `--accent-text` | maple-700 | gold-300 #F7CB72 | maple-700 |
| `--lit` / `--kindling` | maple-600 #D9531E | maple-500 / gold-400 | maple-600 |
| `--ember` | ember-700 #9E2C17 | maple-600 | ember-700 |
| `--gone` | smoke-500 #6F7987 | smoke-300 #B7BDC5 | smoke-500 |
| `--positive` | pine-700 #1F4D3A | gold-300 | pine-700 |
| `--text-scale` | 1 | 1 | 1.15 |

All pairs are checked by `brand/tools/contrast.mjs` (22 pairs pass WCAG 2.2; table in docs/brand/contrast-table.md).

### Type (rem; multiplied by `--text-scale`)

| Style | Family | Size / line | Weight | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| display | Fraunces | 2.5 / 1.1 | 600 | State headlines: "It's lit." |
| invite | Fraunces | 2 / 1.12 | 600 | The six words |
| title | Fraunces | 1.75 / 1.2 | 600 | Screen titles |
| heading | Atkinson Hyperlegible Next | 1.375 / 1.27 | 700 | Sheet titles, counts |
| sun | Atkinson | 1.375 / 1.35 | 700 | The one line read outdoors |
| body | Atkinson | 1.125 / 1.45 | 400 (500 sun) | Body |
| label | Atkinson | 1.0625 / 1.3 | 700 | Buttons |
| small | Atkinson | 0.9375 / 1.35 | 400 | Notes, hints |

### Space, radius, elevation, motion, layout

| Group | Tokens |
| --- | --- |
| Space | `--s-0` 0 · `--s-1` 4 · `--s-2` 8 · `--s-3` 12 · `--s-4` 16 · `--s-5` 20 · `--s-6` 24 · `--s-7` 32 · `--s-8` 40 · `--s-9` 48 · `--s-10` 64 (px) |
| Radius | `--r-sm` 8 · `--r-md` 14 · `--r-lg` 22 · `--r-xl` 32 · `--r-photo` 18 · `--r-pill` 999 |
| Elevation | `--e-1` hairline + 2 px; `--e-2` 6/14 px warm ink shadow; `--e-3` 18/32 px. No blur glass, no colored glow (brand). |
| Duration | `--dur-instant` 90 · `--dur-quick` 160 · `--dur-base` 260 · `--dur-slow` 480 · `--dur-develop` 2400 · `--dur-drift` 900 (ms) |
| Easing | `--ease-out` cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) · `--ease-in-out` (0.6, 0, 0.3, 1) · `--ease-spring` (0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1) |
| Layout | `--l-max-width` 480 px · `--l-gutter` 20 px · `--l-primary-height` 56 px · `--l-touch` 44 px · thumb zone 40% |
| Texture | `.grain` adds paper grain (`static/brand/paper-grain-ui-256.png`, 16% alpha tile) at 0.9 opacity, 0.55 in sun mode, 0.35 screen-blended in dark; hidden with `prefers-reduced-transparency` |

## 2. Components

Every component exists in code with all states; the catalog renders each in light, dark and sun.

| Component | Props | States | Accessibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Button** | variant: primary, secondary, text, danger; icon; loading; disabled; pressed; full | default, hover, pressed, focus-visible (3 px gold or dusk ring), loading (spinner, `aria-busy`), disabled (45% opacity) | Native `<button>`; ≥ 44 px; labels ≤ 3 words |
| **Flame** | state: kindling, lit, ember, gone; progress 0..1; size; dot; animate | Kindling grows 55% to 90%; Lit flicker and gold dot; Ember settle; Gone drift | `role="img"` with state name |
| **FlameMeter** | have, quorum, state, note | Need N more, catching, lit, ember | `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`; dots `aria-hidden`; count only |
| **Hearth** | state, progress, size, celebrate, horizon | with sparks on Lit; without horizon | Decoration `aria-hidden`; the Flame carries the name |
| **PhotoPrint** | state: blank, developing, developed; scene; src; height; tilt | develop animation 2.4 s; instant with reduced motion | Image `role="img"` with the 20-word scene as name |
| **TypeWords** | text, play, step | word-by-word | Full line announced once via `aria-live` |
| **TextField** | label, value, placeholder, hint, error, mic, listening, max, multiline | empty, typing, focus, dictating, error, with counter | Visible label, `aria-describedby` message, `aria-invalid` |
| **Choice** | label, value, options | off, on, focus | Bits UI ToggleGroup: roving focus, arrow keys, labelled group |
| **Sheet** | title, description, open, inline | open (rises 260 ms) | Bits UI Dialog: focus trap, Escape, labelled, focus restored |
| **NeedCount** | have, quorum, lit | need N, enough, lit | `role="status"` |
| **InfoLines** | bench, restroom, water, steps, nature, compact | with or without each item | List labelled "Near the spot"; never says "step-free" |
| **Compass** | name, meters, bearing, status: pointing, facing, no-orientation, no-gps | rings tighten with closeness; facing glow | Spoken line in `aria-live`; dial `aria-hidden` |
| **Ladder** | steps, current, editable, editing | default, current (lit border), past (muted), editing (dashed) | Ordered list "Plan steps, biggest first"; current step announced |
| **Screen** | theme, title, heading, close, menu, offline, grain, actions, overlay | with offline banner; with sheet overlay | One `<main>` (keyboard scrollable), optional visually hidden h1 |
| **Scenery** | people, width, height | with or without people | Decorative |
| **Icon** | name, size, label | 24 icons from brand/icons | Hidden unless `label` |

## 3. Rules

1. One primary button per screen. Secondary actions are text buttons.
2. Use role variables, never raw hex, in product code.
3. State is shown by the flame's shape first and color second.
4. Outdoor screens (Lit, compass, Ember, arrival, host waiting) use `data-sun`.
5. Motion uses tokens only, so reduced motion turns it off everywhere.
6. No new component without all states (empty, loading, error, offline, success where relevant) in the catalog.
