# Flare: Accessibility annotations

Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Target: WCAG 2.2 AA on every screen (SRS-A11Y-1), body text ≥ 7:1, touch targets ≥ 44 pt (SRS-A11Y-6).

## Proof (automated, Oct 10)

| Check | Tool | Scope | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 A and AA rules plus best practice | axe-core 4.14.0 (`npm run a11y`) | 193 targets: 189 screen states in every theme, the site at 390 and 1440 px, the prototype, the component catalog | **0 violations.** First run: 90 (17 serious): missing h1 on 9 screens, scroll region not keyboard-reachable, site without a `main` landmark, one muted ladder step at 50% opacity. All fixed. Report: design/exports/a11y-report.json |
| Keyboard focus order and touch targets | `scripts/focus-audit.mjs` (Tab through every state in Chrome) | 92 screen states | **0 targets under 44 px.** First run found the H3 "Edit where you'll be" button squeezed to 37 px; fixed with `flex: none`. Full order per screen: [07-annex-focus-order.md](07-annex-focus-order.md) |
| Color pairs, indoors and in sun | brand/tools/contrast.mjs | 22 role pairs | All pass WCAG; sun mode chosen because dark pairs drop to 1.5:1 to 2.4:1 in open sun (docs/brand/contrast-table.md) |
| Horizontal scroll | scrollWidth check | site at 390 and 1440 px, prototype, invite | None |

Not automated, and still to do on real phones (Sunday morning, SRS-A11Y-3): VoiceOver walkthrough of journey J3 (low vision) on an iPhone, recorded; largest Dynamic Type size on every P0 screen.

## Contrast

- Text uses only the role variables in 05-design-system.md; every role pair is in the brand contrast table.
- Body text: ink-900 on birch-100 15.24:1 (light, sun); birch-100 on dusk-900 13.97:1 (dark).
- Primary button label: birch-50 on maple-700 5.93:1; dark: ink-900 on maple-500 4.91:1.
- Gold is never used for text on light backgrounds (1.65:1).
- Paper grain darkens the background by at most about 9% (16% alpha tile at 0.55 opacity in sun mode); ink on the darkest grain pixel stays above 13:1.
- State is never shown by color alone: the flame changes shape (small flame, full flame with dot, dome, smoke); counts are text; ladder current step has a border and a hidden "(this is the plan)" label.

## Focus order (rules; measured order per state in the annex)

1. Top bar: Menu (camera only) → Close.
2. Content region (`<main tabindex="0">`, so keyboard users can scroll long content).
3. Interactive content in reading order (fields, choices, edit buttons, list rows).
4. Action area: primary button, then the text button.
5. Sheets (Bits UI Dialog): focus moves to the sheet title on open, is trapped inside, Escape closes, and focus returns to the control that opened it. In static screenshots sheets are rendered inline and are not trapped; the live components are.

## Screen reader labels

| Element | Accessible name or behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Shutter (H1) | "Take the photo" |
| Menu, Close | "Menu", "Close" |
| Invite photo (I1, H2, H3) | The 20-word spoken scene, for example "A pond with yellow trees and an empty bench." (SRS-ACC-5) |
| Invite words | The page's h1 on I1 |
| TypeWords (H2) | Announces the full six words once when complete (`aria-live="polite"`) |
| FlameMeter, NeedCount | `role="status"`: "Need 1 more." plus "1 in, 2 to go ahead. Nobody sees who." Dots are hidden |
| Flame states | `role="img"`: "Kindling", "Lit", "Ember", "Gone" |
| Compass | Spoken line in `aria-live`: "Fuego, 400 meters, slightly left." / "Fuego is straight ahead." The dial is hidden |
| Mic button | "Dictate" / "Stop dictation", `aria-pressed` |
| Edit buttons | "Edit where you'll be", "Edit step 2" |
| Ladder | Ordered list "Plan steps, biggest first"; the lit step adds "(this is the plan)" |
| Fix the map tag actions | Group "Review amenity"; Keep, Change, Remove with `aria-pressed` |
| Download progress (O8) | `role="progressbar"` with value and label |
| Offline banner | `role="status"` |
| Errors | `role="alert"` (send failed, deadline too close); field errors linked by `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid` |

## Touch targets

- Every button, link and control is ≥ 44 × 44 CSS px (measured). Primary buttons are 56 px tall and full width; the shutter is 84 px; choice pills are 48 px tall and at least 56 px wide.
- Primary actions sit in the bottom 40% of the screen (thumb zone).

## Motion, sound, text size

- All durations come from tokens and drop to 0 with `prefers-reduced-motion` or `data-reduce-motion`: no flicker, no develop animation (the final print shows at once), no sparks, no word-by-word reveal.
- Sound respects the silent switch where the platform exposes it; every sound has a visual equivalent.
- Type is in rem; on iPhone the app opts into Dynamic Type (`html.dynamic-type` uses `-apple-system-body`). Layouts are single-column and wrap; no fixed-height text containers except the 56 px buttons, which grow with content.

## Known gaps

- Real-device VoiceOver and Dynamic Type passes are scheduled for Sunday morning on the four phones.
- Haptics: iOS Safari doesn't support `navigator.vibrate`; the compass "facing" tick falls back to a short tone (SRS-CMP-3).

# Handoff 04: Product design to Motion and Copy

From: UI/UX designer. Date: Sat 2026-10-10. Next roles: Motion and sound, then Copy (UX writing).

## What was delivered

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| docs/design/01-brief-and-ux-scan.md | Brief, targets, 7 principles, competitive UX scan, proposed stack |
| docs/design/02-flows-and-ia.md | IA, routes, screen inventory (33 screens), 6 flows (Mermaid) |
| docs/design/03-wireframes.md | 33 wireframes, rendered from the same code with `data-wire` |
| docs/design/04-hifi-screens.md | Index of 189 hi-fi PNGs (every state × theme) and the layout spec |
| docs/design/05-design-system.md | Tokens (CSS + JSON) and 16 components with props, states, accessibility |
| docs/design/06-website.md | Website sections W0 to W7, mobile and desktop |
| docs/design/07-accessibility.md, 07-annex-focus-order.md | Contrast, focus order (measured), labels, targets, motion, known gaps |
| docs/design/08-copy-deck.md | 85 extracted button and headline strings with word counts |
| design/system/ | `build-tokens.mjs` → `tokens.css`, `tokens.json` |
| design/prototype/ | SvelteKit 3.0.1 + Svelte 5.57.2 + Bits UI 2.19.5 prototype: `/proto` (7 key moments), `/screens`, `/screens/{id}`, `/components`, `/site` |
| design/exports/ | screens/ (189), wireframes/ (33), pages/ (site mobile and desktop, components, prototype), a11y-report.json, focus-audit.json |

## Proof

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run check` (svelte-check, TypeScript 6.0.3) | 0 errors, 0 warnings, 697 files |
| `npm run build` | static site written |
| `npm run export` | 189 screen PNGs, 33 wireframes, 4 full pages, 0 page errors |
| `npm run a11y` (axe-core 4.14.0) | 193 targets, 0 violations (first run 90, 17 serious; all fixed) |
| `scripts/focus-audit.mjs` | 92 states, 0 targets under 44 px (first run 4; fixed) |
| `scripts/copy-lint.mjs` | 85 strings, 0 over the limits, 0 banned words |
| JS weight (gzipped, measured in Chrome) | invite screen 51.1 KB; website 48.5 KB (budget 150 KB, SRS-PERF-2) |
| Horizontal scroll | none at 390 and 1440 px |
| `npm audit` | 0 vulnerabilities (after the override in BUG-007) |

Run it: `cd design/prototype && npm ci && npm run build && npm run preview`, then open `http://127.0.0.1:5318/proto/`.

## Key decisions and why

1. **The flame is the interface** (founder feedback folded in). FlameMeter puts the live flame and the count together on the invite, the host's draft, the Ember and the Plan invite. Hearth places it on ground with a pine horizon and sparks on Lit.
2. **The photo moment:** the print develops over 2.4 s while six words arrive one every 220 ms. The lab measured the hub at about 3.0 s per photo, so the develop covers the wait. If the hub can't be reached, a six-word field appears with a template placeholder.
3. **Compass as a warm light:** the brand pin-flame is the pointer, with its hole on the dial centre. Three rings pull in as distance halves; facing within 15° lights the gold dot and a breathing glow.
4. **Sun mode** on every outdoor screen (H5, H6, I6, I7, I8, I9, P5, P6).
5. **Stack:** Svelte 5 + SvelteKit 3 + Bits UI. Headless, accessible primitives, and small bundles (51 KB on the invite). The architect confirms in a decision record. SvelteKit 3 needed migration work (BUG-008).
6. **Honesty in UI:** the "AI on this phone" screen says photo AI doesn't fit in a phone browser yet (lab result). The privacy page leaves a block for the real audit output instead of fake numbers.

## For Motion and sound (exact specs to produce)

What exists in code now (tokens: `--dur-*`, `--ease-*`; all off with reduced motion):

| Moment | Prototype now | Motion role must specify |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kindling grows per yes | Flame scales 55% → 90% with `--ease-spring`, 260 ms; glow widens | Step sizes per quorum (2 to 6), overshoot, and the sound (brand: "small dry tick") |
| Lit catches | Flicker loop, gold dot pulse, 9 sparks rising for 1.6 s, ground glow | The catch sequence (brand: grow to full, dot lights gold, one pulse, 480 ms), the "warm whump" under 600 ms, one haptic, and the WebGL shader (lab: 1.9 KB) vs CSS fallback |
| Ember settles | Dome settles from scaleY 1.6, 480 ms | Settle curve, the soft low note |
| Gone drifts | Smoke drifts up 6 px and fades in, 900 ms | Drift path and timing; silence |
| Print develops | Sepia, blur and brightness to full over 2.4 s | Whether to sync the reveal to the hub response, plus a "chemical" edge or flash |
| Six words | Word-by-word, 220 ms each, spring rise | Timing relative to the develop |
| Compass | Rings move with distance; facing glow breathes 1.8 s | Speech cadence (SRS-CMP-2), the facing tick tone (iOS has no `navigator.vibrate`) |
| Sheets | Rise 24 px with fade, 260 ms | Enter and exit, drag to dismiss |
| Buttons | Press scale 0.985, 90 ms | Final press feel |

## For Copy (UX writing)

- Start from docs/design/08-copy-deck.md (85 strings) and the dynamic templates below. Keep the fixed strings from the SRS exactly as written.
- Dynamic templates used: "{Host} is waiting at {spot}.", "Need {N} more.", "{N} in, {Q} to go ahead. Nobody sees who.", "Met here {N} times", "Smaller plan: 15 min at {bench}.", "It's on: {step} at {time}.", "{Name}, {meters} meters, {direction}.", "{Name} is straight ahead.", "Answer by {time}.", "Got it: {rules}. Right?"
- Still to write (no UI string exists yet): the Telegram bot messages (post, private reply, lit, cleanup), the 200-byte plain-text form for every Fairlane spot name, push notification text, the iOS share-sheet text and link preview text, the empty and error copy for `/check` failures beyond the samples, and the README.
- Tone reference: docs/brand/01-strategy.md voice table.

## Things to know

- Screen components take `view`, not `state`, because `state` collides with the `$state` rune.
- Imports use `#lib/...` with the file extension; tokens and icons are copied in by `scripts/sync-assets.mjs` before dev, build and check.
- Sample content (names, places, distances, the Spark line) lives in `src/lib/sample.ts`. The pond scene is an illustration; replace it with real field photos after Sunday.
- The RTM `design` column is filled: 72 UI requirements point to screens or components; the other 87 are marked "No UI". The trace check passes.
- Sheets in static exports are drawn inline; the live Sheet uses Bits UI Dialog with a focus trap.
- `lab/` is read-only for us.

## Change requests

None against earlier phases. Small fixes made during this phase: brand icon set grew from 16 to 24 icons (close, mic, menu, edit, share, chevron, info, warning) in brand/tools/build.mjs.

Use port 5321 (not 5318) for any `vite preview` you start, to avoid clashing with a parallel session.

YOUR FILE OWNERSHIP (a UX writer works in parallel in another worktree and owns all user-facing strings in src/lib/screens/*.svelte, src/routes/site, src/lib/sample.ts, docs/content). Do NOT change text strings in screens. You may edit: design/motion/** (new), docs/design/motion.md (new), docs/handoffs/05-motion.md (new), design/prototype/src/lib/components/{Flame,FlameMeter,Hearth,Compass,PhotoPrint,TypeWords,Button,Sheet}.svelte, new files under design/prototype/src/lib/motion/, design/prototype/src/routes/+layout.svelte, design/prototype/src/routes/proto/+page.svelte (motion/sound hooks only), new routes design/prototype/src/routes/lab/** (test pages), design/prototype/static/sounds/**, the motion section of design/system/build-tokens.mjs (then regenerate tokens). If you must touch a screen file to wire a hook, change only markup attributes/event handlers, never text.

DELIVER, all finished (no TODOs/placeholders), in design/motion/ and docs/design/motion.md:
1. Motion principles and motion tokens (durations, easings, springs), added to design/system tokens (CSS + JSON) and documented.
2. The flame: a real-time animated flame across all four states (Kindling, Lit, Ember, Gone) using the brand pin-flame silhouette (FLAME path in src/lib/brand.ts; the round hole must stay). 3. Every micro-interaction specified (duration, easing, values) and BUILT in the prototype: the yes-tap, the count ticking, the flame catching (Lit), the photo developing, the compass locking on (facing), the Ember settling, the smoke when Gone, sheet enter/exit, button press, and page transitions using the View Transitions API (document.startViewTransition with SvelteKit onNavigate) with graceful fallback.

Sound design: a small set of ORIGINAL sounds you synthesize yourself (generate WAV files with a Node script using simple synthesis: e.g. "small dry tick" for a yes, "low warm whump" under 600 ms for Lit, "soft low note" for Ember, a short tone for compass facing; Gone is silent), encode to small files the browser plays (WAV or AAC/M4A via macOS `afconvert` if available), with a mixing table (peak/LUFS-ish levels you measure from the samples), when each plays, and rules (respect a user mute, never auto-play before a user gesture, iOS audio unlock on first tap). Put the generator script in design/motion/ so sounds are reproducible. No third-party audio unless CC0 with sources cited.
6. Haptics fallback for iPhone Safari: research (web search + DEV via DevRelay MCP tools if available, cite sources) whether the iOS 18+ `<input type="checkbox" switch>` toggling produces a system haptic and how to use it responsibly (only as feedback for a real user action, never spam). Build /lab/haptics test page so the team can verify on their iPhones Sunday; implement a haptics helper with: navigator.vibrate where supported, the switch-input technique where research supports it, and audio+visual fallbacks. Be honest about what's verified.

PROOF REQUIRED: run `npm run check` (0 errors/warnings), `npm run build`, `node scripts/a11y.mjs` (must stay 0 violations; it uses port 5318 internally, so first edit it to accept a PORT env var or run it when you're sure nothing else uses 5318; prefer adding `process.env.PORT ?? 5318` support to scripts/export.mjs, a11y.mjs, focus-audit.mjs and passing PORT=5321), and record measurement outputs in docs/design/motion.md. Take before/after screenshots of key states with playwright for your own review (look at them with the Read tool) and fix what looks wrong. Log any problem you solve in docs/BUGLOG.md (next id after the last one; read it first).

WRITING RULES for every doc and string: plain words, short sentences, concrete numbers; no em dashes; banned words: seamless, leverage, robust, empower, unlock, elevate, delve, cutting-edge, revolutionize, game-changer, harness, synergy, holistic, paradigm, next-level, supercharge, effortless, ecosystem, tapestry, testament, "in today's fast-paced world", "it's not just X, it's Y", "let's dive in". Every claim gets a number, a link or proof; if unknown, say so.

FINISH: write docs/handoffs/05-motion.md (what was delivered, key decisions and why, measurements, what the architect must know, what is unverified until Sunday's iPhone check), then `git add` your files and commit in your worktree with a clear message ending with the line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. MOTION AND SOUND (4c)
- Flame: keeps the lab's WebGL + CSS approach, but the shader is redrawn on the actual brand shapes (flame, dome, smoke), so the round hole stays crisp in all four states.

- Frame rate: 60 fps in all 14 runs (Chrome on M4, CPU throttled 1x, 4x and 6x), p95 frame time 16.7 to 16.8 ms, 0 dropped frames, even with 4 shader flames at 6x.
  - Throttling doesn't slow the GPU, so this can't stand in for an iPhone 13. The /lab/fps page is ready for Sunday morning.
- Shader cost: 954 B of shader source; the WebGL code is a 3.6 KB chunk loaded only when needed; the shape texture takes a one-time 17 ms at 1x and 57 to 87 ms throttled.
- Micro-interactions: all 10 built, each with a reduced-motion version. Yes-tap, count tick, Lit catch, photo develop, compass lock-on, Ember settle, Gone smoke, sheet with drag-to-dismiss, button press, and page transitions with the View Transitions API.
- Sounds: 4 original ones, synthesized by a seeded script. Peak and RMS levels measured: yes −6/−24.6 dBFS, lit −3/−16.6 (520 ms), ember −9/−21.6, facing −10/−23. They total 24.5 KB, are fetched after the first tap, the silent switch mutes them, and Gone is silent.
- Haptics: navigator.vibrate on Android, the iOS switch-overlay technique, and sound and visual fallbacks, with a /lab/haptics test page.
  - Research says scripts can no longer fire the switch haptic from iOS 26.5 on; only a real finger tap on the switch should still work. This isn't confirmed by Apple; we test it Sunday.

COPY (4d)

- I resolved the conflicts and renumbered the bug log (copy has BUG-009 to 013, motion BUG-014 to 019).

DECISIONS FOR YOU

  - the yes-tap and the count tick
  - the flame catching, settling to Ember and drifting away as smoke
  - the photo developing and the compass locking on
  - sheets you can drag to dismiss, button presses, and page transitions
- **Sounds:** four original ones, generated by a script, 24.5 KB in total. Nothing plays before your first tap, the silent switch mutes them, and Gone is silent.
- **Haptics:** iPhone support is uncertain. Research says that from iOS 26.5, only a real finger tap on a switch can trigger the haptic. Apple hasn't confirmed this, so it's on the Sunday test list with `/lab/haptics`.

- Buttons are 3 words at most and messages 12. Readability averages about grade 2, and the slop and inclusive-language checks found nothing.

Seven questions for the architect are written up in `docs/handoffs/06-copy.md`. The main ones: whether the server needs spot coordinates, and how the Telegram bot and notifications handle text the server only holds encrypted.

## What the build team must know

1. **Photo AI runs on the hub, not the phone.** Gemma 4 E2B cannot run in iPhone Safari: it needs one 1.12 GiB GPU buffer against a 1 GiB iOS cap, and used 11–13 GB vs a ~2 GB tab limit ([01](01-gemma-browser.md)).
2. **The hub model is `gemma4:e4b-it-q4_K_M` with `think:false`, prompt-only.** 3.0 s per photo, 20/20 usable after `enforce()`, quality 39/40 ([02](02-ollama-hub.md)). Leaving out `think` gave 0/20 answers. Plain `gemma4:e4b` on Homebrew is an MLX build where `format` returns 501 ([02](02-ollama-hub.md)).
3. **Reach the hub with an outbound WebSocket relay through the Render app.** CPU-only Ollama took 126–215 s per photo, so no Ollama on Render ([08](08-hub-reach.md)). Send a 768 px binary JPEG; the 1024 px median is 431 KB ([08](08-hub-reach.md)).
4. **Conditions are parsed on the phone by the rules parser only.** 40/40 core, 15/20 hard, 0 bytes. The best small model added 1/20 and hung Safari ([07](07-phone-text-model.md)). Always read back: model mistakes look valid ([07](07-phone-text-model.md)).
5. **Offline Flares are typed (≤ 6 words) with map-pack chips; no on-phone vision model.** SmolVLM got 2/20 right ([09](09-smolvlm-fallback.md)).
6. **Run `enforce()` and prompt v2** (`spikes/common/validate.mjs`) on every model answer. On E2B, v2 took validity from 13/20 to 20/20 ([01](01-gemma-browser.md)).
7. **Ship the map pack as a static file:** 6.7 KB (1.8 KB brotli), 128 places. Overpass refuses a default User-Agent (406) and often answers 504 ([05](05-map-data.md)).
8. **Flame: WebGL2 shader (1.9 KB) with a CSS fallback (1.1 KB).** All variants ran 60 fps on the M4; the iPhone 13 is still unmeasured ([06](06-flame.md)).
9. **HTTPS on phones from day one.** Compass, location, camera, WebGPU and service workers need it ([04](04-iphone-check.md)).
10. **Telegram:** `answerCallbackQuery` for private replies, ephemeral messages as a bonus. Edit one message per flare. 20 messages per minute per group, delete within 48 h ([03](03-telegram.md)).
11. **If caching models in a browser, use OPFS, not the Cache API.** Chrome rejected the 1.5 GB files mid-load ([01](01-gemma-browser.md)).

# 02 Laptop hub: Ollama + Gemma 4 E4B

## Question

Can the laptop run `gemma4:e4b` as a hub for the 20-photo task (photo in, JSON `{invite, alt}` out)? How fast is it, how good, and what setup gives reliable JSON, given the known issue that Ollama may skip the JSON schema when a thinking model answers?

## Answer

Yes. Use the GGUF build `gemma4:e4b-it-q4_K_M`:

- `think: false`, prompt-only (no `format`)
- temperature 0
- run the app's `enforce()` guard on every answer

Result: 20 of 20 answers parsed as JSON, 18 of 20 met every rule as returned, 20 of 20 after the guard. Median 3.0 s per photo on the M4. Quality was the best we measured: place descriptions 39/40, invites 39/40.

Two traps:

1. **Thinking ate the answer.** Gemma 4 defaults to thinking ON in Ollama. With thinking on (or `think` left out), the model spent its whole 256-token budget thinking and returned empty content on 20 of 20 photos.
2. **No schema support on the default build.** On Apple Silicon, the Homebrew Ollama 0.40.2 bottle resolves `gemma4:e4b` to an MLX build that cannot do JSON schemas at all (HTTP 501).

## Method

- **Same task as spike 1:** the same 20 Wikimedia Commons photos (`data/photos/photos.json`), the same prompt v2 (`spikes/common/validate.mjs`), the same validator.
- **Request:** `POST /api/chat` with the image as raw base64, `temperature: 0`, `seed: 42`, `num_predict: 256`, `keep_alive: 30m`.
- **Configs** (`spikes/02-ollama-hub/run.mjs`):

  | Config | Endpoint | think | format (JSON schema) | Sampling |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | A | /api/chat | false | yes | temp 0 |
  | B | /api/chat | true | yes | temp 0 |
  | C | /api/chat | omitted (model default = true) | yes | temp 0 |
  | D | /api/chat | false | no, prompt only | temp 0 |
  | E | /v1/chat/completions | `reasoning_effort: none` | `response_format` json_schema strict | temp 0 |
  | F | /api/chat | false | yes | temp 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64 |

- **One model at a time:** after each build finished, it was unloaded (`keep_alive: 0`, `ollama stop`). No browser test ran during these runs.
- **Memory:** sum of the physical footprint (`top` MEM) of all `ollama` processes, sampled every second.
- **Quality:** graded by hand against the photos. Description accuracy 0-2 (2 = correct and nothing invented), invite fit 0-2 (2 = specific to the place and inviting). Max 40 each.

## Environment

- MacBook with Apple M4 (10 cores), 24 GB RAM, macOS 26.6.2
- Ollama 0.40.2 (Homebrew bottle), `ollama serve` with `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1`
- `gemma4:e4b`: on this Mac it resolved to the **MLX** build. 8.1B params, nvfp4, 9.5 GB on disk, MLX runner 0.32.3.
- `gemma4:e4b-it-q4_K_M`: the **GGUF** build. 7.5B params, Q4_K_M, 6.58 GB download (68 s), llama.cpp runner (`llama-server`).
- Pull time for `gemma4:e4b`: 9.5 GB in 156 s.

## Raw numbers

### Load and text speed (MLX build)

- Cold load 4,128 ms. Total first request 5,947 ms.
- Warm text: 109 tokens at 44.9 tok/s decode, prompt eval 117 ms.
- GGUF build cold: the first photo took 14,375 ms, with load_duration 7,659 ms.

### Photo task, side by side

| Build / config | Valid (all rules) | JSON parsed | Median wall per photo | Max | Decode tok/s (median) | Peak Ollama memory |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **MLX D** (prompt only, think false) | **20/20** | 20/20 | 3,954 ms | 9,347 ms | 19.5 | 12.3 GB |
| MLX A, B, C, E, F (any `format`) | 0/20 | 0/20 | 12 ms | | | |
| **GGUF A** (grammar schema, think false) | 18/20 | 20/20 | 6,022 ms | 14,375 ms (cold) | 19.0 | 8.8 GB |
| GGUF B (schema, think true) | 0/20 | 0/20 | 20,772 ms | | 17.1 | 10.3 GB |
| GGUF C (schema, think default) | 0/20 | 0/20 | 16,910 ms | | 15.4 | 10.3 GB |
| **GGUF D** (prompt only, think false) | 18/20 | 20/20 | **3,007 ms** | | 13.0 | 11.3 GB |
| GGUF E (/v1 json_schema, reasoning none) | 15/20 | 20/20 | 9,212 ms | | n/a | 11.3 GB |

- The MLX A–F rows each failed in 12 ms with HTTP 501 (see "What failed").
- **After `enforce()`:** 20/20 usable answers for MLX D, GGUF A, GGUF D and GGUF E. 0/20 for B and C, because there was no content to fix.
- **Why the 2–5 failures:** in GGUF A, D and E, every failure was an `alt` of 21–24 words. A grammar can force JSON shape but cannot count words.
- **Prompt tokens:** 775 per photo (image plus prompt), on both builds.

### Quality (hand graded, out of 40)

| Model | Description accuracy | Invite fit | Notable misses |
|---|---|---|---|
| E4B MLX, config D | 39 | 37 | Called the shopping cart a "red recycling bin"; "manhole" invite |
| E4B GGUF, config A | 39 | 39 | Called the shopping cart a "red mesh trash receptacle" |
| (spike 1) E2B in browser, budget 140 | 29 | 26 | Tennis court instead of basketball, mural read as a real coastline, invented sunsets |

E4B read signs ("Scentral Bark", "Friends, Shopping, Long Lunches"). It identified the drinking fountain as a fountain and the painted sea wall as a mural. It wrote no face, gender, age or clothing terms on any photo, including the group photo (p20) and the musician (p09).

## What failed

1. **HTTP 501 "structured output is unavailable" on the MLX build.** Every request with `format` (or `/v1` `response_format`) failed in about 12 ms. The server log at model load reads:
   `Structured output is unavailable ... xgrammar library not found at .../libexec/lib/ollama/mlx_metal_v3/libollama_xgrammar.dylib`
   The Homebrew bottle does not ship that library. Ollama 0.40.0 made MLX the default on Apple Silicon, and the plain `gemma4:e4b` tag pulls the MLX build there (9.46 GB, the same as the registry's `e4b-mlx` tag). The registry's default `e4b` manifest is the 6.58 GB GGUF. On the manager's approval we pulled the GGUF tag explicitly and kept the Homebrew install.
2. **Thinking ran out of tokens.** With `think: true` (B), or with `think` omitted (C, where the default is true per `ollama show`), all 20 answers had empty `content`, about 930 characters of `thinking`, and `done_reason: length` at `num_predict: 256`.
   - Each photo took 17–21 s instead of 3–6 s.
   - The known bug **ollama/ollama#18774** ("Gemma4: JSON schema format is not enforced when think:true answers directly without reasoning", open since 2026-10-03) did not show up, because the model never answered directly.
   - The older **ollama/ollama#15260** (think=false broke format for gemma4) is closed and did not reproduce: GGUF A with `think:false` plus format gave 20/20 parsed JSON.
3. **The OpenAI-compatible path (E) was slowest** of the working configs (9.2 s median), with the most length failures (5).

## Recommendation for the hub

**Use the GGUF build, `think: false`, prompt-only, plus `enforce()`.** It was the fastest (3.0 s median), used the least disk (6.6 GB vs 9.5 GB), and graded best. Every answer parsed. Request body:

```json
{
  "model": "gemma4:e4b-it-q4_K_M",
  "stream": false,
  "think": false,
  "keep_alive": "30m",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "<PROMPTS.v2 from spikes/common/validate.mjs>"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Here is the photo. Reply with the JSON.", "images": ["<raw base64, no data: prefix>"]}
  ],
  "options": {"temperature": 0, "seed": 42, "num_predict": 128}
}
```

- **Always send `think: false` explicitly.** Leaving it out gives empty answers.
- **Keep `format` off for this task.** On GGUF it doubled latency (6.0 s vs 3.0 s) and caught nothing the prompt plus `enforce()` didn't already handle. Turn it on only if a future prompt starts producing broken JSON. It works on GGUF, never on the Homebrew MLX build.
- **Retry once on a parse failure**, then fall back to a template invite ("Meet me here, right now").
- **Warm up at hub start:** send one dummy request so the first friend doesn't wait the 7.7–14 s cold load.
- **Memory:** 8.8–11.3 GB peak. Run nothing else heavy on the hub Mac.
- **Exposing the hub to phones:** start it with `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 ollama serve` on the trusted Wi-Fi only. Ollama has no authentication, so anyone on that network can call it. Better: put the hub behind the Flare server and call Ollama only from there.

## Files

- `spikes/02-ollama-hub/run.mjs`: runner for configs A-F (`--model`, `--config`, `--prompt`)
- `spikes/02-ollama-hub/results/gemma4_e4b-*.jsonl`: MLX build results
- `spikes/02-ollama-hub/results/gemma4_e4b-it-q4_K_M-*.jsonl`: GGUF build results
- `spikes/common/validate.mjs`: prompts, validator, `enforce()` guard
- Logs: `logs/ollama-serve.log` (contains the xgrammar warning), `logs/ollama-runs.log`, `logs/ollama-gguf-runs.log`

## Sources

- ollama/ollama#18774, "Gemma4: JSON schema format is not enforced when think:true answers directly without reasoning" (open; checked with `gh` 2026-10-10): https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/18774
- ollama/ollama#15260, "`think=false` breaks `format` (structured output) for `gemma4`" (closed): https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/15260
- Structured-output change for thinking models, PR #18479: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/18479 (from research pass)
- Ollama 0.40.0 makes MLX the default on Apple Silicon: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases (from research pass)
- `/api/chat` fields, `think`, `format`, durations in ns: https://docs.ollama.com/api/chat ; thinking: https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/thinking ; structured outputs: https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/structured-outputs
- Gemma 4 tags and sizes: https://ollama.com/library/gemma4/tags ; registry manifests read directly from `https://registry.ollama.ai/v2/library/gemma4/manifests/<tag>` (e4b and e4b-it-q4_K_M 6.58 GB, e4b-mlx 9.46 GB)
- `OLLAMA_HOST`, `OLLAMA_ORIGINS`: https://docs.ollama.com/faq ; exposure risk: https://blog.leakix.net/2026/02/ollama-exposed/
- Missing xgrammar library: our own server log, `logs/ollama-serve.log` (line with `grammar.go:74`)
- DEV: "Ollama skips your JSON schema when a thinking model answers without thinking", homelabpm, https://dev.to/homelabpm/ollama-skips-your-json-schema-when-a-thinking-model-answers-without-thinking-2916

## Answer

**Relay through the Render app.** The hub opens an outbound WebSocket to the Flare server on Render. The phones only ever talk to the Flare server, which forwards photo jobs over that socket.

- Nothing on the Mac is exposed, and there is no new vendor, account or install.
- There is one origin for the phones, so no CORS issues and the existing app auth is reused.
- It adds one hop, tens of milliseconds next to the 3 s model time.

**Ollama on Render is not viable.**
- Measured CPU-only, E4B takes **126 s per photo on all 10 M4 cores and 207–215 s on 4 threads**, versus 3.0 s on the M4 GPU.
- It needs the $225/month 16 GB plan.

**Fallback if the relay code isn't ready by Sunday:** Tailscale Funnel. It needs no code and is end-to-end encrypted, but it's a public URL and a new install, so it waits for your yes. Cloudflare quick tunnels are the fastest to start, but the URL changes on every restart and Cloudflare sees the photos in plaintext.

## Local measurements (2026-10-10, M4 Mac, Ollama 0.40.2, `gemma4:e4b-it-q4_K_M`)

| Setup | Per photo (wall) | Image + prompt encode | Decode | Valid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPU (Metal), from report 02 | 3.0 s median | 0.18 s | 13 tok/s | 18/20 strict, 20/20 after `enforce()` |
| **CPU only, `num_gpu: 0`, 10 threads** | **126.3 s, 123.7 s** | 116.5 s, 121.9 s | 14.7, 19.7 tok/s | 2/2 |
| **CPU only, 4 threads** (about a 4-vCPU cloud box) | **215.2 s, 207.4 s** | 203.2 s, 205.5 s | 13.3, 17.5 tok/s | 2/2 |

Almost all of the time is encoding the 775-token image prompt. Render's shared vCPUs are slower than M4 performance cores, so expect worse than 3.5 minutes per photo there (inference).

Payload per photo: the 1024 px JPEGs in our set are 431 KB median (1.27 MB max), or 575 KB median as base64. **Recommendation:** downscale on the phone to 768 px at JPEG quality 0.7, and send binary, not base64. That should be under about 150 KB (inference, not measured).

## Option facts (sources checked by the research pass on 2026-10-10; F = documented, I = inference)

### Cloudflare Tunnel
- **F:** quick tunnels (`*.trycloudflare.com`, no account) have no uptime guarantee and a new random hostname on every start. Max 200 in-flight requests, no SSE, "not for production".
  https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-networks/do-more-with-tunnels/trycloudflare/
- **F:** outbound-only connector, so no router change. Proxy read timeout 125 s (524), request body up to 100 MB on Free.
  https://developers.cloudflare.com/support/troubleshooting/http-status-codes/cloudflare-5xx-errors/error-524/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits
- **I:** TLS ends at Cloudflare's edge, so Cloudflare can read photos and responses. Named tunnels plus Access need a domain on Cloudflare; Access is free up to 50 users (third-party sources).

### Tailscale Funnel
- **F:** needs Tailscale (open-source macOS variant) on the Mac, MagicDNS + HTTPS, and a `funnel` attribute in the tailnet policy. Phones need nothing; they open `https://<mac>.<tailnet>.ts.net`. Ports 443, 8443 or 10000 only.
  https://tailscale.com/kb/1223/funnel
- **F:** TLS terminates on the Mac; the relays cannot decrypt (end to end). Bandwidth is "subject to non-configurable bandwidth limits", with no number published.
- **F:** the free Personal plan covers up to 6 users. Whether Funnel is on the current free plan is not clearly stated on the pricing page.
  https://tailscale.com/pricing
- **Private variant:** each phone installs Tailscale and joins the tailnet (WireGuard end to end, no public URL). That's 4 installs and 4 sign-ins.

### Ollama on Render (CPU only)
- **F (third-party price list, unchanged as of Aug 2026):** Pro Plus 4 CPU / 8 GB $175, Pro Max 4 CPU / 16 GB $225, Pro Ultra 8 CPU / 32 GB $450. No GPU plans. Persistent disk $0.25/GB/month.
  https://jwatte.com/blog/render-com-platform-review.md ; https://render.com/docs/compute-plans-update ; https://render.com/docs/disks
- **F:** private services can listen on 11434 (no public URL).
  https://render.com/docs/private-services
- **Measured here:** about 2–3.5 min per photo even on faster cores. Not usable for a "snap and invite" flow.

### Relay through the Render app
- **F:** Render supports WebSockets with no maximum duration. Connections drop when an instance is replaced (deploys), with a 30–300 s shutdown window. Ping/pong keepalives are recommended.
  https://render.com/docs/websocket
- **F:** free web services sleep after 15 minutes without inbound traffic (about 1 min to wake), and Render may restart them at any time.
  https://render.com/docs/free
  **I:** the hub's keepalive pings count as traffic and keep it awake, but a paid Starter instance ($7) removes the risk for the test day.
- **F (forum, not docs):** a user hit 413 with large base64 bodies. Test a 600 KB upload early, or send binary over the socket.
  https://community.render.com/t/413-payload-too-large-error-request-size-limit/38333
- **I:** TLS ends at Render's load balancer, so Render can see the photo in transit. The Flare server already sees everything the app sends, so this adds no new party.

5:On Sunday our phones will be on cellular near Fairlane, and the hub (this M4 Mac running Ollama) will be at home. How should the phones reach it? Compare Cloudflare Tunnel, Tailscale Funnel, Ollama on a Render instance (CPU only), and a relay through the Render app. Cover latency, reliability, privacy, cost and setup. content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary request and intent**
   - The user is entering the DEV Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1, "Touch Grass". Deadline: Sun Oct 11, 11:59 PM PDT (Mon 06:59 UTC; 2:59 AM ET).
   - The work runs "like a real software company, waterfall style": one specialist at a time. Each specialist:
     - reads docs/handoffs/
     - owns their scope completely
     - leaves no TODOs or placeholders
     - verifies with proof
     - writes docs/handoffs/NN-role.md
     - commits
   - Keep docs/BUGLOG.md. Fix small earlier-phase issues and log them; write change requests for big ones.
   - Follow-ups come via the manager session ("Those messages come from me, so treat them the same as mine").
   - **Security and constraints, verbatim from the user:**
     - "Secrets are already in .env, at <project>/flare/.env (if you're running in a worktree copy, read them from that path). They cover MongoDB Atlas, the Telegram bot, and RENDER_KEY for the Render API. Never print, log or commit them. .gitignore already protects .env."
     - "Anything public waits for my yes: deploying under my accounts, making the repo public, publishing, posting, uploading, or messaging people."
     - "Already approved, no need to ask: npm installs; installing Ollama with Homebrew and pulling gemma4:e4b; downloading the Gemma 4 E2B ONNX model (~3.2 GB) for browser tests; creating a private GitHub repo named flare on my account and pushing to it; keeping the Mac awake (caffeinate) during long work."
     - "A separate lab session is running technical spikes in lab/ (git-ignored). Don't edit or commit lab/. The engineering lead will review its reports and import what we keep."
     - "Real iPhone checks happen when we're awake. Build whatever page or script makes that quick, and we'll run it on our phones."
   - **Writing rules:**
     - Plain words, short sentences, concrete numbers. Every claim gets a number, link or proof.
     - No em-dash chains, no emoji decoration in docs, no empty intros or outros.
     - Banned words: seamless, leverage, robust, empower, unlock, elevate, delve, cutting-edge, revolutionize, game-changer, harness, synergy, holistic, paradigm, next-level, supercharge, effortless, ecosystem, tapestry, testament, "in today's fast-paced world", "it's not just X, it's Y", "let's dive in".
     - UI copy: buttons 3 words max, messages 12 words max, warm and a bit playful, never cute at the cost of clarity.
   - **Quality bar:** no timeboxes, no scope cuts. Each role produces its discipline's standard docs. Latest stable versions, checked first. Tests, types, error handling, docs. No stubs, no fake data. Premium feel.
   - **Fixed points:** the Sunday daytime field test (11 AM to 3 PM ET near Fairlane Town Center, Dearborn MI; RC by 10 AM), then the deadline.
   - **Current request (architect, from the manager):**
     - Deliver in docs/architecture/:
       - System architecture document with C4 diagrams (context, containers, components) and a deployment diagram.
       - Physical DFDs at levels 0, 1 and 2 for the sensitive flows (photo, conditions, needs profile, location, deletion), with trust boundaries marked.
       - Sequence diagrams, and state machines for Flare and Plan.
       - ERD and data dictionary.
       - Tech-stack ADRs with current versions, including the UI and motion libraries and the storage decision: Postgres vs MongoDB Atlas, weighing deletion guarantees, the "fully open" story and the partner prize.
       - API contract for every endpoint and event: OpenAPI for HTTP, AsyncAPI for live events, covering the Telegram bot, the hub relay and the plain-text format.
       - Offline and sync design, and on-device vs server AI placement with fallbacks.
       - Security and privacy design, and privacy-safe observability.
       - Performance budgets for the iPhone 13.
       - Testing strategy and coding standards.
     - Also deliver:
       - A repo scaffold with tooling and scripts.
       - An env config checker that reports set or missing only, never values.
       - CI running clean.
       - LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT and SECURITY.md.
     - Done = the repo builds, tests run, and a hello world runs end to end (phone page → server → hub relay → Ollama → back).
     - Write handoff 07 for the engineering lead.
     - Decide the 7 open questions from handoff 06 in ADRs. The founder's lean:
       - Telegram conditions: don't process free text; "Add a condition" opens the link page; free-text DMs get the link back and are dropped.
       - Readable text for bot posts and pushes: acceptable only for groups that chose Telegram. The host's phone sends the six words, place name and host name in plaintext, kept until Gone, disclosed on the privacy page.
       - Photo to the laptop: the hub keeps nothing, processes in memory only, proven with a test.
     - Build on the lab results:
       - Photo AI runs on the hub, gemma4:e4b-it-q4_K_M, think:false, prompt-only, enforce(); 3.0 s per photo, quality 39/40.
       - Outbound WebSocket relay from the Mac to the Render app. No Ollama on Render.
       - Rules-only condition parser on the phone (40/40 core), always read back.

"/", "http://x"); if (url.pathname !== "/hub" || !secretMatches(bearer(req), env.hubSecret)) { socket.write("HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"); socket.destroy(); log.warn({ event: "hub.refused" }, "hub upgrade refused"); return; } wss.handleUpgrade(req, socket, head, (ws) => relay.attach(ws)); }); const stop = async () => { relay.close(); wss.close(); server.close(); await db?.close(); process.exit(0); }; process.on("SIGTERM", stop); process.on("SIGINT", stop);

1	# Flare: Software requirements specification (SRS)
2	
3	Structure follows ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 (section 9.6, SRS content). Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Owner: Analyst.
4	
5	## 1. Introduction
6	
7	### 1.1 Purpose
8	This SRS states every requirement the Flare app, server, Telegram bot and website must meet for the DEV Hacktoberfest Week 1 entry. Engineers build to it; QA tests against it; the traceability matrix (05-rtm.csv) links each requirement to stories, acceptance criteria, design, code, tests and proof.
9	
10	### 1.2 Scope
11	Flare lets a host send a Flare (meet now) or a Plan (meet later) to friends. Friends say yes privately; it happens only if enough say yes; it shrinks instead of failing; it works for friends with low vision or limited mobility and with no signal; and it deletes itself. Products: the **app** (installable web app for iPhone, plus the link page), the **server** (engine, solver, scheduler, API), the **Telegram bot**, and the **website**.
12	
13	### 1.3 Definitions
14	See docs/product/10-glossary-and-decisions.md. Additional terms: **gathering** = a Flare or a Plan; **place key** = OSM element id of a spot, else its name; **group key** = symmetric key in the link fragment.
15	
16	### 1.4 References
17	- docs/product/03-prd.md (PRD v1.1), 05-backlog.md, 06-scope.md, 07-kpis.md, 09-risks.md
18	- docs/requirements/03-business-rules.md (BR-*), 04-data-flow-and-dictionary.md, 02-use-cases.md
19	- docs/requirements/evidence/README.md (pinned numbers)
20	- WCAG 2.2, https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/
21	- ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018
22	
23	### 1.5 Requirement format
24	Each requirement has: **ID**; a statement using "shall"; **Pri** (P0 = in the Sun 10 AM release candidate; P1 = before the DEV deadline; P2 = later); **Source** (PRD or BR id, or founder); **Story** (backlog story and AC); **V** = verification method (T test, D demonstration, I inspection, A analysis). A requirement is met only when its fit criterion (the number or condition in the statement) is observed.
25	
26	## 2. Overall description
27	
28	### 2.1 Product perspective
29	New, standalone system. External systems: Telegram Bot API, Web Push (Apple Push for Safari), OpenStreetMap Overpass API, the hub (Ollama with Gemma 4 E4B on the team's Mac), on-device model files from a public model host, SMS or satellite messaging (outside the system).
30	
31	### 2.2 User classes
32	Host; invitee; invitee with access needs (low vision, limited mobility); Telegram member; text-only member (SMS relay); operator (the team: deploy, audit, metrics). No accounts exist for any class.
33	
34	### 2.3 Operating environment
35	- Phones: iPhone 13, 16 Pro Max, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max. iOS versions unknown until Sunday; behaviour must be chosen by runtime capability detection only.
36	- Browser: Safari on iOS (link page and installed Home Screen app). Desktop Chrome, Firefox and Safari current versions for development and the website.
37	- Server: hosted HTTPS service (Render is the candidate; deploy needs the founder's yes).
38	- Hub: macOS laptop with Ollama and `gemma4:e4b`.
39	
40	### 2.4 Constraints
41	DEV rules (new work in the window; template; tag; deadline Mon 06:59 UTC); open models only for AI jobs; no hardware; no end-user accounts; founder approval for every public action; first names only in public materials until consent; writing rules (docs/product/01-brd.md section 6).
42	
43	### 2.5 Assumptions and dependencies
44	- AS-1 At least two of the four phones run iOS with Safari web push support for Home Screen apps; otherwise Telegram or the open page carries Lit notices.
45	- AS-2 OSM data near Fairlane is current enough (pinned Oct 10, 17:07 UTC).
46	- AS-3 The hub laptop has internet during the field test, or the rules tier is used.
47	- AS-4 The lab session supplies the phone-tier model choice (MediaPipe Gemma 4 E2B, or a vision model under 600 MB).

1	# Flare: Business rules catalog
2	
3	Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Owner: Analyst. Source: PRD v1.1 (docs/product/03-prd.md). Each rule is atomic, has one ID, and is referenced by SRS requirements and tests. Where the PRD left something open, the rule records the decision and marks it **[Analyst decision]**.
4	
5	Notation: `t0` = Flare send time (server). `D` = Plan answer deadline. `S` = Plan start time. All times are server UTC; phones display them in the group time zone (BR-TIME-2).
6	
7	## 1. Identity and membership
8	
9	| ID | Rule |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| BR-ID-1 | A group is identified by a random 128-bit group id. It is not derived from any personal data. |
12	| BR-ID-2 | Each person in a group is a member with a random 128-bit member id, created on their phone the first time they open the group's link (or by the bot for a Telegram user). |
13	| BR-ID-3 | Display names are chosen by the member and stored only encrypted with the group key. The server never holds a readable name. **[Analyst decision]** |
14	| BR-ID-4 | A member id is per group. The same person in two groups has two unrelated ids. |
15	| BR-ID-5 | For Telegram members, the bot keeps a map from Telegram user id to member id for that group. The map is deleted when the member leaves the group or the group is inactive for 30 days. |
16	| BR-ID-6 | A plain-text reply (`IN <code>`) relayed by a member counts as an anonymous yes with no member id and no conditions. At most 3 anonymous yeses per gathering. **[Analyst decision]** |
17	
18	## 2. Quorum
19	
20	| ID | Rule |
21	| --- | --- |
22	| BR-Q-1 | Yes-count always includes the host as 1. |
23	| BR-Q-2 | Flare quorum is 2, 3 or 4; default 2. Plan quorum is 2 to 6; default 3. |
24	| BR-Q-3 | A gathering lights when the solver's chosen set (BR-S-1) has at least quorum members. |
25	| BR-Q-4 | "Need N more" = max(0, quorum − size of the solver's current best set). For a Plan, it is computed at the highest step that could still light. |
26	| BR-Q-5 | No interface or API shows who is in the set, who answered, or when anyone answered. Only N. |
27	| BR-Q-6 | "Ember only" yeses (BR-A-3) are excluded from Kindling counts and included at Ember. |
28	
29	## 3. Conditions
30	
31	| ID | Rule |
32	| --- | --- |
33	| BR-C-1 | Condition types: `with(member_id)`, `after(time)`, `back_by(time)`, `max_walk(minutes)`, `max_step(n)` (Plans only). |
34	| BR-C-2 | A yes may carry 0 to 4 conditions. All must hold (logical AND). |
35	| BR-C-3 | `with(X)` holds when X is in the same chosen set. Names are resolved to member ids on the phone, where names can be decrypted. |
36	| BR-C-4 | `with(X)` naming nobody in the group cannot be saved. The phone says "Amor isn't in this group." |
37	| BR-C-5 | `after(T)` holds when the gathering's start is at or after T. For a Flare, the start is the Lit time. |
38	| BR-C-6 | `back_by(T)` holds when start + duration ≤ T. Flare duration is taken as 60 minutes for this check. Plan duration is the chosen step's minutes. **[Analyst decision]** |
39	| BR-C-7 | `max_walk(M)` holds when the person's walking time to the spot at 4.8 km/h straight-line distance × 1.3 is ≤ M. The phone evaluates it and reports pass or fail per spot id. **[Analyst decision]** |
40	| BR-C-8 | `max_step(n)` holds when the chosen step number ≥ n (step 4 is smallest). |
41	| BR-C-9 | Free text never leaves the phone. Only the structured rule is sent. |
42	| BR-C-10 | A condition is saved only after the person confirms the read-back. |
43	
44	## 4. Solver
45	
46	| ID | Rule |
47	| --- | --- |
48	| BR-S-1 | The solver picks the set of yeses (and the step, for Plans) that maximizes, in order: (1) number of people, (2) higher step (smaller step number), (3) earlier start. |
49	| BR-S-2 | A yes with no conditions fits every set. |
50	| BR-S-3 | `with` dependencies are resolved as a fixed point: repeatedly remove members whose `with` targets are not in the set until nothing changes. |
51	| BR-S-4 | Group sizes are at most 12 in this release, so the solver may search exhaustively. Groups larger than 12 are rejected at creation. **[Analyst decision]** |
52	| BR-S-5 | The solver runs on every yes, take-back, condition change, fade and timer event. It is deterministic: the same inputs give the same output. |
53	| BR-S-6 | Ties after all three criteria are broken by the lowest member ids (stable, not by answer time). **[Analyst decision]** |
54	
55	## 5. Flare timeline
56	
57	| ID | Rule |
58	| --- | --- |
59	| BR-F-1 | Kindling lasts until t0 + 30:00. |
60	| BR-F-2 | An event received by the server at or before t0 + 30:00.000 belongs to Kindling. If it completes quorum, the Flare is Lit, even if the Ember timer is already queued. |
61	| BR-F-3 | At t0 + 30:00, if not Lit, the Flare enters Ember with quorum 2 at the Ember spot (BR-E). |
62	| BR-F-4 | Ember lasts until t0 + 60:00. If not Lit by then, Gone with "Not this time". |
63	| BR-F-5 | Lit lasts until the host taps Done or t0 + 4:00:00, whichever comes first. |
64	| BR-F-6 | The host may cancel only during Kindling or Ember. Cancel ends in "Not this time". |
65	| BR-F-7 | Lit is permanent for the gathering (no return to Kindling). |
66	| BR-F-8 | Timer transitions fire within 30 seconds of their scheduled time, including after a server restart. |
67	
68	## 6. Ember
69	
70	| ID | Rule |
71	| --- | --- |
72	| BR-E-1 | Ember spot = the nearest `amenity=bench` or `leisure=picnic_table` by straight-line distance within 400 m of the original spot that passes the needs check of every yes and every "Ember only" yes. |
73	| BR-E-2 | If no bench qualifies, the Ember spot is the original spot. |
74	| BR-E-3 | Needs checks for candidate benches run on each phone; each phone reports pass or fail per candidate bench id. The server picks the nearest bench that passed for all. |
75	| BR-E-4 | Phones that haven't reported within 60 s of Ember start are treated as pass for all candidates. **[Analyst decision]** |
76	| BR-E-5 | Ember duration on screen is "15 min". Ember quorum is 2. |
77	| BR-E-6 | A Flare lit during Ember counts as an Ember save. |
78	
79	## 7. Plan timeline and downshifting
80	
81	| ID | Rule |
82	| --- | --- |
83	| BR-P-1 | D ≥ creation + 10 min, D ≤ S − 10 min, and S ≤ creation + 36 h, so every bot post can still be deleted inside Telegram's 48 h limit. **[Analyst decision]** |
84	| BR-P-2 | A Plan lights only at D, except: if every member of the group has said yes with no conditions before D, it lights at once at step 1. |
85	| BR-P-3 | At D, the solver picks step and set (BR-S-1). If no step reaches quorum but at least 2 people (host included) fit step 4, it lights at step 4 and counts as an Ember save. Otherwise Gone. |
86	| BR-P-4 | A ladder has exactly 4 steps, numbered 1 (biggest) to 4 (smallest). Durations are strictly decreasing. |
87	| BR-P-5 | Any member of the chosen set may fade once per Plan, from Lit until S + 50% of the current step's minutes. |
88	| BR-P-6 | Each fade lowers the step by 1, never below 4. The set is re-solved at the new step; members who now fit are added, nobody is removed. **[Analyst decision]** |
89	| BR-P-7 | The displayed change is "Smaller plan: {step name}." No count of fades, no names. |
90	| BR-P-8 | A Lit Plan becomes Gone at Done or at S + step minutes + 60 min. |
91	| BR-P-9 | Steps ending after sunset show "Ends after sunset" unless the host turned the check off. |
92	
93	## 8. Arrival and host +1
94	
95	| ID | Rule |
96	| --- | --- |
97	| BR-H-1 | Headcount = 1 (host) + arrivals. |
98	| BR-H-2 | An arrival is recorded by the person tapping "I'm here" or by the host tapping +1. |
99	| BR-H-3 | A member's own "I'm here" and a host +1 for the same member count once only if the host +1 is attached to that member; anonymous +1s are separate. The host's +1 list shows names (decrypted on the host's phone) and an "Someone else" entry. **[Analyst decision]** |
100	| BR-H-4 | Headcount ≤ yes-count + 3 (yes-count includes the host). Taps beyond the cap are ignored. |
101	| BR-H-5 | Arrivals are accepted only while Lit. Offline arrivals from the outbox are accepted if their recorded time is within the Lit window. |
102	
103	## 9. Expiry and deletion
104	
105	| ID | Rule |
106	| --- | --- |
107	| BR-D-1 | At Gone, the server deletes within 5 minutes: the gathering record, yes records, rules, fades, arrivals, photo ciphertext, live locations, bot message references, and solver state. |
108	| BR-D-2 | Every per-gathering record also carries a storage-level expiry at t0 + 5 h (Flare) or S + 24 h (Plan), so deletion happens even if the delete job fails. |
109	| BR-D-3 | The bot deletes every message it posted for the gathering at Gone. |
110	| BR-D-4 | Survivors after Gone: group counters (docs/product/07-kpis.md), the encrypted Hot spots blob, opt-in encrypted Sparks, member ids, push subscriptions, and the Telegram map. |
111	| BR-D-5 | Push subscriptions and Telegram maps are deleted after 30 days without a gathering in the group. Sparks and the Hot spots blob are deleted after 180 days without a gathering, or at once when any member taps "Forget this group". **[Analyst decision]** |
112	| BR-D-6 | Logs never contain request bodies, photos, names, locations, conditions, or link fragments. Logs are kept 7 days. |
113	| BR-D-7 | The deletion audit counts remaining per-gathering records in every store listed in the data dictionary, by gathering id and in total. Passing = 0. |
114	
115	## 10. Sparks and Hot spots
116	
117	| ID | Rule |
118	| --- | --- |
119	| BR-K-1 | Only members with an accepted arrival may leave a Spark for that gathering. One Spark per member per gathering. |
120	| BR-K-2 | A Spark is 1 to 140 characters, written by the person. No AI generation or editing is offered. |
121	| BR-K-3 | The Spark prompt appears once, after Done, and can be dismissed. No reminders. |
122	| BR-K-4 | A Spark is encrypted with the group key before leaving the phone and is tied to the place key: the OSM element id of the spot, or the place name if no id. |
123	| BR-K-5 | "Your group met here N times." shows when N ≥ 1, where N counts Lit gatherings at that place key. It shows the newest Spark at that place, if any. |
124	| BR-K-6 | The Hot spots blob is one encrypted record per group: a list of {place key, place name, count, last date, newest Spark id}. The host's phone updates it at Gone. Conflicts merge by taking the max count per place. |
125	
126	## 11. Access and needs
127	
128	| ID | Rule |
129	| --- | --- |
130	| BR-A-1 | Needs profile fields: avoid steps (yes or no), max distance between rests (100, 200, 400 m or none), restroom within 300 m (yes or no). Stored only on the phone. |
131	| BR-A-2 | A spot fails "avoid steps" when any `highway=steps` lies within 20 m of the straight line from the person to the spot or within 50 m of the spot. A spot fails "restroom" when no `amenity=toilets` is within 300 m. A spot fails "rest distance" when the nearest bench is farther than the limit. |
132	| BR-A-3 | A person whose needs fail may choose "Count me in for a closer one". Their yes is flagged "Ember only" and carries no reason. |
133	| BR-A-4 | Access line copy never says "step-free". It says "No steps mapped" or "Steps mapped". |
134	
135	## 12. Time
136	
137	| ID | Rule |
138	| --- | --- |
139	| BR-TIME-1 | The server clock (UTC, NTP-synced) decides every transition. Phone clocks are never trusted for transitions. |
140	| BR-TIME-2 | The group time zone is the host phone's time zone at creation. Times in conditions are interpreted in it. |
141	| BR-TIME-3 | Phones show the server time remaining and the time the state was last confirmed. |
142	
143	## 13. Channels
144	
145	| ID | Rule |
146	| --- | --- |
147	| BR-CH-1 | The bot posts only in allow-listed chat ids. At release the list has one entry: "Flare test". |
148	| BR-CH-2 | The plain-text form is ≤ 200 bytes UTF-8. If the spot name would exceed it, the name is truncated with "…". |
149	| BR-CH-3 | Short codes use 5 characters from `REDACTED` (no 0, 1, I, L, O). Codes are unique among live gatherings. |
150	| BR-CH-4 | Link previews show a blurred photo and the invite line only; never coordinates or the spot name below street level. **[Analyst decision]** |
151	
152	## 14. AI
153	
154	| ID | Rule |
155	| --- | --- |
156	| BR-AI-1 | Tier order is phone, then hub, then rules. A tier is skipped if unavailable, times out (phone 8 s, hub 6 s), or returns output that fails validation. |
157	| BR-AI-2 | Output never describes faces, identity, age, race, gender or bodies. A filter replaces any person words with "a person" or "people", or drops the sentence. |
158	| BR-AI-3 | Every AI run records job and tier as a counter. No inputs or outputs are stored server-side. |
159	| BR-AI-4 | Fix the map drafts use only the tag key allow-list in PRD FR-MAP-2 / backlog E17-S1. |
