# ADR-0001: npm workspaces monorepo, TypeScript run directly by Node

Status: Accepted. Date: 2026-10-10.

## Context
Four parts share code: the server, the hub, the web app and the shared rules (photo prompt and `enforce()`, short codes, plain-text forms, hub protocol). The team has under 40 hours to the deadline and wants the fewest moving parts.

## Decision
- One repository, npm workspaces: `packages/shared`, `apps/server`, `apps/hub`, `apps/web`.
- TypeScript 6.0.3, strict, with `erasableSyntaxOnly`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `allowImportingTsExtensions`.
- Node 24.21.0 LTS ("Krypton") in production and CI (`.nvmrc`, `engines >=24.21.0`). Node strips types itself, so the server and hub run `.ts` with no build step and no bundler. Imports carry the `.ts` extension.
- Vitest 5.0.3 for tests, Biome 2.5.15 for lint and format, PGlite 0.5.8 for an in-memory Postgres in tests.

## Versions checked (npm, 2026-10-10)
typescript 6.0.3 (7.0.2 exists, but SvelteKit 3.0.1 pins `typescript ^6`), hono 4.13.13, @hono/node-server 2.1.4, ws 8.22.0, pino 10.4.0, zod 4.6.5, pg 8.23.1, vitest 5.0.3, @biomejs/biome 2.5.15, playwright-core 1.64.0, @redocly/cli 2.62.1, @asyncapi/parser 3.6.3.

## Consequences
- No `tsc` build, no source maps to ship; stack traces point at the real files.
- Parameter properties, enums and namespaces are not allowed (not erasable). BUG-020 records the one we hit.
- Proof: `npx -y node@24.21.0 node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run` passes 38 tests; the same on Node 26.8.1.

## Options weighed
| Option | Why not |
| --- | --- |
| pnpm or Turborepo | One more tool to install on a clean machine (SRS-MNT-3) for 4 packages |
| tsc or esbuild build step | Adds a dist folder and a watch process; type stripping does the job |
| TypeScript 7 (native) | Not accepted by SvelteKit 3.0.1's peer range |
EOF

- Prototype invite route: 61.6 KB gzipped JS (handoff 05), 41% of the budget. Current `apps/web` build: 57.1 KB for all routes (`npm run budget`).

Status: Accepted. Date: 2026-10-10. Founder decisions 1 and 2 (Oct 10).

## Context
The flame is the product's state signal (kindling, lit, ember, gone). Lab report 06 measured seven variants on an M4 at 1x and 4x CPU throttle.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Lottie | 41 KB | 20x the shader, still needs a fallback |
| Rive | 334 to 800 KB | Over the budget on its own; editor-only authoring |
| CSS only | 1.1 KB | Kept as the fallback; less depth |

## Open
The iPhone 13 frame rate is unmeasured. `/lab/fps` in the prototype runs on the phones Sunday; the gate above makes a slow phone fall back by itself.

# ADR-0004: PostgreSQL, not MongoDB Atlas

Status: Accepted. Date: 2026-10-10. Answers founder question Q6 and risk R16.

## Context
The data is small (at most 12 members per group, one live gathering at a time, about 20 rows per gathering) but the deletion promise is strict: everything about a gathering gone within 5 minutes of Gone (BR-D-1), with a storage-level expiry as a backstop (BR-D-2), and an audit that prints 0 (BR-D-7). Both Postgres and MongoDB Atlas credentials were available. The founder asked for a decision on the merits, weighing deletion guarantees, the "fully open" story and the MongoDB Atlas partner prize ($100, one of 10 partner categories).

## Decision
PostgreSQL (Render Postgres in production, PGlite 0.5.8 in tests, `pg` 8.23.1 driver). The MongoDB settings stay in `.env.example` marked unused.

How deletion works:
1. **Cascade.** Every per-gathering table references `gatherings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`. One `DELETE FROM gatherings WHERE id = $1` removes the photo, answers, jobs, bot message refs, live location and bind tokens in one transaction. Test: `apps/server/test/db.test.ts`, "deleting a gathering removes every per-gathering row".
2. **Expiry column.** Every per-gathering row has `expires_at` (t0 + 5 h for a Flare, S + 24 h for a Plan). Test: "every per-gathering table has an expiry column".
3. **Sweeper.** The server deletes gatherings that are Gone or past `expires_at` every 30 s and once at boot. Reads also filter `expires_at > now()`, so an expired row is never served even in the seconds before the sweep.
4. **Independent backstop.** A Render Cron Job runs `npm run sweep` every 5 minutes as its own process, so a crashed web service cannot stop deletion. It needs the founder's yes with the deploy.
5. **Audit.** `GET /api/v1/audit` counts expired rows per table with plain SQL.

## Options weighed

| Criterion | PostgreSQL | MongoDB Atlas |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Deletion by the database itself | No built-in TTL; sweeper in the app plus a cron backstop | TTL index: the server's TTL monitor runs every 60 s and deletes expired documents, even if our app is down. A real strength |
| Deleting everything about a gathering at once | One transactional `DELETE` with `ON DELETE CASCADE` across 7 tables | No foreign keys; embed answers in the gathering document, keep the photo (up to 1.5 MB) in its own collection, delete both |
| "Fully open" story | PostgreSQL License, OSI approved | Server Side Public License; MongoDB's own FAQ says it "has not been approved by the OSI" (https://www.mongodb.com/legal/licensing/server-side-public-license/faq) |
| Partner prize | None | Eligible for the $100 category. Research: 33 Week 1 entries (4%) mention Atlas; Weekend winners won it with something only Atlas does well (GridFS byte ranges, hybrid vector search). A TTL index is good, but a sweeper does the same job here |
| Short codes unique among live gatherings | Partial unique index `WHERE state <> 'gone'` | Partial unique index with `partialFilterExpression`; equal |
| Tests | PGlite: real Postgres in memory, 0 downloads beyond npm, 13 server tests in 0.7 s | mongodb-memory-server downloads a server binary per platform |
| Running near the app | Render Postgres in the same region and private network as the web service | Separate provider; Render needs a static outbound IP plan or a 0.0.0.0/0 allow-list |
| Self-hosting ("Run it yourself") | `docker run postgres` or any host | MongoDB Community under SSPL, or Atlas account |
| Code already written | Schema, migrations, tests passing | Rewrite |

Atlas wins on one criterion that matters (deletion that runs without our code). Postgres wins on the open license, transactional cascade, tests and operations. The cron backstop closes most of Atlas's lead, so we take Postgres and skip the Atlas category rather than claim it for a database we would use only for the prize.

## Consequences
- The DEV post claims no MongoDB category.
- The sweeper and the cron job are P0 code with tests (deletion within 5 minutes, SRS-PRIV-2).
- Render's free Postgres expires after 30 days; the test needs the paid Basic plan or the free one created within the window. The founder approves either.
EOF

# ADR-0005: One Render web service plus Render Postgres; HTTPS from day one

Status: Accepted (deploy itself waits for the founder's yes). Date: 2026-10-10.

## Context
Phones need HTTPS for the camera, geolocation, device orientation, service workers and Web Push (lab report 04). The hub needs a server it can dial out to (ADR-0006). RENDER_KEY is available for the Render API. Ollama cannot run on Render: CPU-only E4B took 126 to 215 s per photo (lab report 08).

## Decision
- **Web service** `flare-outside`: Node 24.21.0, build `npm ci && npm run build`, start `npm start`. Serves the API, the hub WebSocket on `/hub`, the SSE streams and the static web build. Starter plan ($7/month) on test day so it does not sleep; the free plan sleeps after 15 minutes idle, which would drop the hub socket and add a cold start.
- **Postgres**: Render Postgres, same region (Ohio, closest to Dearborn), internal URL.
- **Cron job**: `npm run sweep` every 5 minutes (ADR-0004).
- **TLS**: Render's managed certificate on `*.onrender.com`; `Strict-Transport-Security` from the app.
- **Health check path**: `/api/v1/health`.
- **Secrets**: set in the Render dashboard or by API from `.env`, never in `render.yaml`.
- One instance only: the hub relay and SSE fan-out keep state in memory. Two instances would split the hub from half the phones.

## Consequences
- A deploy restarts the process; the hub reconnects within 1 to 30 s (backoff), phones' SSE reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`, and timers are rebuilt from the `jobs` table (SRS-ST-2).
- Scaling past one instance would need the relay and fan-out in Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY`; not needed for 4 phones and groups of 12.

## Options weighed
| Option | Why not |
| --- | --- |

# ADR-0006: The Mac hub dials out to the server over a WebSocket

Status: Accepted. Date: 2026-10-10. From lab report 08.

## Context
Photo AI runs on the team's Mac (Gemma 4 E4B, 3.0 s per photo on its GPU). Phones in the field are on cellular. The Mac is behind home NAT and must not be exposed to the internet.

## Decision
The hub (`apps/hub`) opens `wss://{server}/hub` with `Authorization: Bearer {HUB_SECRET}` and keeps it open. The server sends jobs down it and waits for results. Protocol `flare-hub.v1`, in [asyncapi.yaml](../contracts/asyncapi.yaml):
- Text frames carry JSON (`hello`, `job`, `result`, `ping`, `pong`), validated by zod on both ends (`packages/shared/src/hub-protocol.ts`).
- A photo is one `job` header then one binary frame (the 768 px JPEG, about 13 to 150 KB). No base64 on the wire.
- Server pings every 20 s; the hub reconnects with backoff 1 s to 30 s; a new hub replaces the old one (close code 4000).
- Budgets: 6 s per photo job (BR-AI-1), 8 s per ladder job (SRS-PLAN-2). Late results are dropped; the phone already has the template.
- The secret is compared with `timingSafeEqual`; a wrong secret gets HTTP 401 and no upgrade.

## Numbers
`npm run e2e:hello` (docs/architecture/evidence/e2e-hello.txt): browser round trip 3.85 s, hub job 3.5 s, upload 13 KB. The relay adds about 0.3 s on localhost; lab report 08 estimates 50 to 150 ms more through Render.

## Consequences
- Nothing on the Mac listens on a port. If the Mac sleeps or loses Wi-Fi, `/api/v1/health` says `hub: absent` and every draft falls to the typed template within the 6 s budget.
- The hub re-warms the model every 20 minutes so Ollama's 30-minute `keep_alive` never unloads it; a cold load (7 to 14 s) would always miss the 6 s budget.
- Keep the Mac awake during the test (`caffeinate -dims`, pre-approved).

## Options weighed
| Option | Why not |
| --- | --- |
| Ollama on Render | 126 to 215 s per photo on CPU; GPU plans start near $225/month |
| Tailscale Funnel to the Mac | Public `ts.net` URL straight to Ollama; kept as backup, needs the founder's yes |
| Cloudflare quick tunnel | URL changes every run; Cloudflare terminates TLS and sees the photo |
| Phone talks to the hub directly | Needs the Mac reachable from cellular, same exposure problem |
EOF

# ADR-0008: Group key in the link fragment; sealing on the phone

Status: Accepted. Date: 2026-10-10. Implements SRS-ID-1, SRS-ID-2, SRS-ID-4, SRS-CRE-6, SRS-SEC-3.

## Decision
- The creator's phone makes a 256-bit group key with `crypto.getRandomValues` and imports it as a non-extractable AES-GCM `CryptoKey` after writing the raw bytes once into the link.
- Links look like `https://{host}/g/{gatheringId}#k={key base64url}`. Browsers never send the `#fragment` to servers, and our server never logs URLs with fragments (it cannot see them). Link previews are built server-side without the key (ADR-0017).
- Every readable thing is sealed with AES-256-GCM (WebCrypto), a fresh random 96-bit nonce per seal, nonce prepended, base64url. The additional authenticated data binds the ciphertext to its place, so a sealed field cannot be moved:

| Sealed field | AAD |
| --- | --- |
| Gathering blob `sealed` | `g:{gatheringId}` |
| Photo | `p:{gatheringId}` |
| Notice `notice_ct` | `n:{gatheringId}` |
| Member name `name_ct` | `m:{groupId}:{memberId}` |
| Spark `text_ct` | `s:{groupId}:{sparkId}` |
| Hot spots `blob_ct` | `h:{groupId}` |
| Live location `location_ct` | `l:{gatheringId}` |

- Place keys for Sparks are hashed, not sealed: `HMAC-SHA-256(HKDF(groupKey, info="flare place v1"), placeKey)`, so equal places match without the server learning which place.
- The phone keeps keys, member ids and write tokens in IndexedDB (per origin; the service worker reads it for push).

## Consequences
- Anyone who gets the link can read the gathering. That is the sharing model; the link is the invitation. The privacy page says so.
- Losing the link means losing access; there is no recovery by design (no accounts).
- A key rotation is not offered in this release. "Forget this group" (ADR-0015) is the exit.
- Telegram groups post the link in Telegram, so Telegram can read that group (ADR-0013).

## Options weighed
| Option | Why not |
| --- | --- |
| Server-held keys | The server could read everything; breaks FR-PRIV-1 |
| Per-member keys (MLS, Signal-style) | Correct, but weeks of work and no browser library we trust at this size |
| Key in a query string | Sent to the server and kept in logs and browser history on the server side |
EOF

# ADR-0009: No coordinates or readable places on the server

Status: Accepted. Date: 2026-10-10. Adopts OQ-1 (handoff 02) as variant B and supersedes analyst decision 10 (DS1 `spot` with `lat`, `lon`).

## Context
The founder asked that the server not hold spot coordinates. The data dictionary had `spot {place_key, name_ct, lat, lon}`, `ember_spot {bench_osm_id, lat, lon}`, Plan ladder places with `lat, lon`, and DS11 live locations in plain `lat, lon`. The server used coordinates for two jobs: choosing the Ember bench (BR-E-1) and the compass target.

## Decision
1. **The phone picks the candidates.** At send time the host's phone runs the BR-E-1 search on its map pack: benches and picnic tables within 400 m, nearest first, at most 12. It seals their names and coordinates into the gathering blob.
2. **The server sees labels, not places.** The server gets `ember_candidates: ["c1", ..., "cN"]` in distance order. Phones report pass or fail per label (BR-E-3). At Ember the server picks the first label that passed for every yes and every "Ember only" yes (BR-E-1), or `spot` if none did (BR-E-2), and sends only the label.
3. **OSM ids are not sent either.** The analyst's proposal kept "candidate OSM ids" on the server, but an OSM node id resolves to exact coordinates with one public API call (`api.openstreetmap.org/api/0.6/node/{id}`). Opaque per-gathering labels close that gap (BUG-023).
4. **Plans the same way:** steps carry `place: "step:1"` to `"step:4"`; names and coordinates are sealed.
5. **Live location sealed:** `location_ct` (DS11) is ciphertext; the server stores it overwritten in place and deletes it at Gone.
6. **The compass works from the sealed blob,** saved on the phone at Lit (SRS-OFF-1).
7. **Schema test:** `apps/server/test/db.test.ts` fails if any table outside the counters has a column named `lat`, `lon`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `spot`, `place_name` or `name`.

## Consequences
- The copy deck's `privacy.coords` variant switches from A to B (done in this phase; the website and privacy statement follow).
- The server cannot check "within 400 m" itself; a host's phone with a modified client could send far candidates. Acceptable: the host chooses the place anyway.
- If no phone reports within 60 s of Ember, all candidates count as pass (BR-E-4) and `c1`, the nearest bench, wins.
- Telegram groups are the disclosed exception: the place name is in the bot post (ADR-0013). Coordinates never are.
EOF

# ADR-0011: Photos for the AI live only in memory

Status: Accepted. Date: 2026-10-10. Answers question 5 of handoff 06 with the founder's lean.

## Context
To write six words the photo must be readable by the model, so it leaves the phone unsealed (FR-AI-1). The privacy page should be able to say "and it isn't stored".

## Decision
- The phone sends a separate 768 px JPEG (quality 0.7) to `POST /api/v1/drafts`. The sealed photo for friends is a different upload.
- **Server:** reads the body into one `Uint8Array` (at most 1.5 MB, JPEG magic bytes checked), sends it down the hub socket, and zero-fills it in a `finally` block. It is never logged (the request logger records method, route template, status and time only), never written to disk, never in the database.
- **Hub:** takes the binary frame, base64-encodes it for Ollama's `/api/chat` in memory, zero-fills its buffer after the call, and imports neither `node:fs` nor `node:child_process`.
- **Ollama:** runs on localhost, `stream:false`. It keeps no request history on disk; its log at default level records method, path, status and time.

## Proof
`apps/hub/test/hub.test.ts`:
1. reads the hub's source and fails if it imports `node:fs`, `fs`, or `node:child_process`;
2. runs a job end to end against a fake Ollama and checks the request had `think:false` and the image;
3. checks no new file appeared in the OS temp folder during the job.
`apps/server/test/app.test.ts` checks the draft route answers and the buffer path returns the template when the hub is absent.

## Consequences
- The privacy page and `privacy.photoHub` copy can say: "To write the six words, your photo goes to our laptop over an encrypted link. It isn't stored."
- Swap or a crash dump could still hold bytes from memory; we say "isn't stored", not "can't be recovered".
EOF

# ADR-0012: Plain-text forms cut with "..." to stay GSM-7

Status: Accepted. Date: 2026-10-10. Accepts the change request in handoff 06 (decision 8) and amends BR-CH-2.

## Context
BR-CH-2 cut long spot names with "…" (U+2026). That character is not in the GSM-7 alphabet, so one "…" switches the whole SMS to UCS-2, where a segment holds 70 characters instead of 160, and a 200-byte message splits into 3 segments.

Cut with "..." (three ASCII full stops). Cut whole code points so the text stays valid UTF-8. Spec: [contracts/plain-text.md](../contracts/plain-text.md). Code: `packages/shared/src/plaintext.ts`, 9 tests.

A Telegram post needs readable text (the six words, the place, the host's first name) and buttons that open the link. The server holds only sealed data for link groups. From then on the host's phone sends `telegram: {host, invite, place, link, ember_places, step_names}` in plain text with each gathering. The server keeps it in `gatherings.telegram_plain` until Gone and deletes it with the row. The photo for the post goes from memory to `sendPhoto` and is not stored.
2. **The link with its key is posted on the buttons,** so Telegram, and our server while the gathering is live, could read that group's sealed data. The app says this before the bot is added, and the privacy page lists it as a limit.
3. **No free text.** The bot never parses, stores or logs message text. "Add a condition" opens the link page through a personal bind link; any other private message gets the link back and is dropped. Conditions are always made by the phone's rules parser and read back.
4. **Private replies** by `answerCallbackQuery` (always shown only to the tapper); an ephemeral group message (Bot API 10.2) as a bonus because its delivery isn't guaranteed (lab 03).
5. **One message per gathering, edited.** A new notifying message only when it lights or shrinks. Deleted at Gone with `deleteMessages` (BR-D-3).
6. **Pushes for link groups stay sealed** (ADR-0014); this exception covers the Telegram channel only.

## Consequences
- Copy changes in this phase: `bot.dm.condAsk`, `bot.dm.condExample`, `bot.dm.condPrivacy`, `bot.dm.yesBtn` and `bot.dm.saved` (the bot-side condition dialogue) are replaced by `bot.dm.link` and `bot.post.condition`; the privacy text no longer says conditions pass through Telegram, and gains the Telegram link limit.
- A Telegram member made by a tap has no sealed name; others see "A Telegram friend" until that person opens their personal link and picks a name.
- `with(...)` conditions naming a Telegram-only member are not possible until they bind a phone.
EOF
cat > 0014-live-updates-sse-and-sealed-push.md <<'EOF'
# ADR-0014: Server-Sent Events for live views; Web Push with a sealed notice

Status: Accepted. Date: 2026-10-10. Implements SRS-SOL-3 (5 s), SRS-LIT-1 (10 s), SRS-IF-3. Contract: `gatheringEvents` and `push` in [asyncapi.yaml](../contracts/asyncapi.yaml).

## Decision
- **Open pages** subscribe to `GET /api/v1/gatherings/{id}/events` (SSE, via Hono's `streamSSE`). Each change sends the whole view (under 25 KB, mostly the sealed blob; the photo is separate). Keepalive comment every 15 s, under common 30 to 60 s proxy idle limits. Pages also poll every 30 s while visible, and reload on `visibilitychange` to visible.
- **Closed apps** get Web Push (RFC 8291 encryption, VAPID RFC 8292, `web-push` 3.6.7). Push needs the app on the Home Screen on iOS 16.4 and later; capability detection decides (SRS-COMP-2).
- **The payload carries `notice_ct`,** sealed by the host's phone at creation with the host name, spot, Ember bench names and step names. The service worker reads the group key from IndexedDB, opens it and writes "It's lit. Fuego is at Ford Woods Park pond." If it can't, it shows "It's lit. Open Flare to see where." The server never writes a readable notice for a link group.
- Who gets a Lit notice: members of the chosen set (SRS-LIT-1). The solver's set is used for addressing only and never leaves the server (SRS-PRIV-8).

## Options weighed
| Option | Why not |
| --- | --- |
| WebSockets for phones | Needs a socket library on the phone and sticky handling through proxies; SSE is plain HTTP, reconnects by itself with `Last-Event-ID` |
| Polling only | 5 s updates would mean a request every 5 s per open page |
| Readable push text from the server | The server would need names and places (ADR-0009) |
EOF
cat > 0015-forget-this-group.md <<'EOF'
# ADR-0015: "Forget this group"

Status: Accepted. Date: 2026-10-10. Settles the conflict between BR-D-5 ("any member's tap deletes Sparks and Hot spots") and SRS-ID-6 ("only if they are the last member"), question 7 of handoff 06.

## Decision
SRS-ID-6 wins, with one addition:
- Any member's tap deletes **their own** data: member row, push subscription, Telegram map entry, their answers in live gatherings (the solver re-runs), and the Sparks they wrote, found by the per-Spark delete tokens the phone kept (`spark_delete_tokens`). Then the phone deletes its keys and saved data.
- If they were the **last member**, the group goes too: Hot spots blob, all Sparks, counters (`ON DELETE CASCADE` from `groups`).
- A host who forgets a group with a live gathering cancels it first ("Not this time.").

## Why
One member shouldn't erase memories that belong to the whole group, but everyone should be able to take back what they wrote. Spark rows carry no author id, so the delete token is how a writer proves authorship without the server learning who wrote what.

## Consequences
- BR-D-5's last sentence is amended to match (BUG-026). The copy "You're the last one, so its Sparks go too." stays.
- Contract: `DELETE /api/v1/groups/{groupId}/members/{memberId}` returns `{last_member, sparks_deleted}`.
EOF
cat > 0016-fades-and-min-step.md <<'EOF'
# ADR-0016: After a fade nobody is removed; add `min_step`; a private "Still coming?"

Status: Accepted. Date: 2026-10-10. Settles OQ-2 (handoff 02) with the founder's preference.

## Decision
1. **Keep everyone.** BR-P-6 stands: a fade lowers the step by one, re-solves, adds members who now fit, removes nobody.
2. **Add `min_step(n)`:** holds when the chosen step number ≤ n (step 1 is biggest). "Only the long one" parses to `min_step(1)`; "at least the park loop" to `min_step(2)`. The solver uses it at the deadline like any rule (BR-S-1).
3. **Private note.** After a fade, any member of the set whose own rules fail at the new step gets `still_coming: true` on `GET /me` and a push "Plan changed to {step}. Still coming?" (`push.stillComing`). No action is needed; "Can't make it" is there if they want it. Nobody else learns anything.
4. Read-back fragment: "step {k} or bigger" (`readback.rule.minStep`), already in the copy deck.

## Consequences
- Change request CR-A1 to the analyst: add `min_step` to BR-C-1 and SRS-COND-1, and 4 phrases to `docs/requirements/fixtures/conditions-60.json` ("only the long one", "the full walk or nothing", "at least the park loop", "step 2 or bigger"). The rules parser gets them in the same pull request.
- The OpenAPI `Rule` schema already has `min_step`.
EOF
cat > 0017-link-previews-safe.md <<'EOF'
# ADR-0017: Link previews show the brand card and the count

Status: Accepted. Date: 2026-10-10. Settles question 6 of handoff 06; amends BR-CH-4.

## Context
BR-CH-4 asked for a blurred photo and the invite line in link previews. The server can't read the invite line (sealed, ADR-0008), and previews are fetched and cached by iMessage, WhatsApp and Telegram on their own servers, where our 5-minute deletion can't reach.

## Decision
`GET /g/{gatheringId}` returns the app HTML with Open Graph tags built from what the server can read: title "A Flare from a friend", description "Need {n} more. Open it to say yes in private.", image the brand OG card (1200 x 630, `brand/export/social/og.png`). No photo, no blur, no place, no words. This is the copy deck's `og.link` variant `safe`, already in force.

## Consequences
- Nothing about the gathering is left in other companies' preview caches after Gone, except a count.
- `photos.blur_preview` is dropped from the schema.
- BR-CH-4 is amended to point here (BUG-026).
EOF
cat > 0018-ids-codes-tokens.md <<'EOF'
# ADR-0018: Ids, short codes and tokens

Status: Accepted. Date: 2026-10-10.

## Decision
| Thing | Format | Made by | Stored as | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Group, member, gathering, Spark id | UUID v4 (122 random bits) | Phone, `crypto.randomUUID()` | Postgres `uuid` | Native type and index; 2^122 is far past guessing. SRS-ID-1's "128-bit" is met in spirit; the dictionary now says "UUID v4" (BUG-026) |
| Write token | 128 random bits, base64url (22 chars) | Phone | SHA-256 hash | SRS-SEC-4. A database leak gives no tokens |
| Short code | 5 of `REDACTED` | Server, rejection sampling | Text, unique among live gatherings | BR-CH-3; 28,629,151 codes. FR-CH-4's 4-character example is a typo (handoff 06, decision 9) |
| Idempotency key | 16 to 64 of `A-Za-z0-9_-` | Phone, per action | `idempotency.key`, 24 h | SRS-IF-1 |
| Telegram link and bind tokens | 128 random bits | Server | SHA-256 hash, 15 and 10 min | ADR-0013 |
| Hub secret | 32+ random bytes, base64url | Operator | Environment only | ADR-0006 |

Client-made ids let the phone seal with the id as AAD before the first request, and make creation idempotent.

## Consequences
The short code is the only thing a guesser could try, and it only allows an anonymous yes entered by the host, capped at 3 (BR-ID-6). It never opens the gathering.
EOF
cat > 0019-license-agpl.md <<'EOF'
# ADR-0019: AGPL-3.0-or-later

Status: Accepted. Date: 2026-10-10. Confirms SRS-MNT-1.

## Decision
The code is released under GNU AGPL 3.0 or later. Full text in `LICENSE` (from the SPDX license list 6.12.0, `AGPL-3.0-or-later`, OSI approved).

## Why
Flare's promise is privacy. AGPL section 13 means anyone who runs a modified Flare server for others must offer their source, so users of a fork can check its privacy too. MIT or Apache 2.0 would let a hosted fork close its changes.

## Third parties
All runtime dependencies are MIT, ISC, Apache-2.0 or BSD, which AGPL can include. Assets: Fraunces and Atkinson Hyperlegible Next (SIL Open Font License 1.1), OpenStreetMap data (ODbL 1.0, attribution shown in the app), Gemma 4 (Gemma terms of use; weights are not in the repo). `npm run licenses` (engineering, P1) writes THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md from the lockfile.
EOF
cat > 0020-observability.md <<'EOF'
# ADR-0020: Structured logs with redaction, counters, no third-party telemetry

Status: Accepted. Date: 2026-10-10. Details in [09-observability.md](../09-observability.md).

## Decision
- **Logs:** pino 10.4.0, JSON to stdout, Render keeps them 7 days (BR-D-6). One line per request: method, route template (ids replaced by `:id`), status, milliseconds. Redaction paths drop `authorization`, `cookie`, tokens, bodies. Events use fixed names (`hub.hello`, `tg.refused`, `sweep.deleted`) with counts, never content.
- **Metrics:** the KPI counters in `counters` and `global_counters` (07-kpis.md), nothing finer than the day.
- **Health:** `/api/v1/health` (hub connected or absent, database ok or down).
- **Audit:** `/api/v1/audit` (ADR-0004).
- **No** Sentry, analytics, APM or third-party scripts (SRS-PRIV-7). Errors are logged with a stack and a fixed event name; the stack never includes request data because handlers don't put it in error messages.

## Consequences
Debugging a user's problem means reproducing it, not reading their data. The field test runs with the team watching the Render log stream.
EOF

# Flare: Physical data flow diagrams Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Owner: Architect. Maps the analyst's logical DFD ([04-data-flow-and-dictionary.md](../requirements/04-data-flow-and-dictionary.md)) onto real processes, stores and wires. Level 0 is the whole system, level 1 the containers, level 2 one diagram for each sensitive flow: photo, conditions, needs profile, location, deletion. ## Trust zones | Zone | What runs there | Who controls it | Trust | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **P** Phone | Web app, service worker, IndexedDB | The person | Trusted with their own data and the group key | | **S** Server | Render web service, Postgres, cron | Us, on Render's hardware | Trusted to run code honestly; **not** trusted with readable content. Designed so a full database dump reveals no names, places, photos or conditions of a link group | | **H** Hub | Team Mac: hub process, Ollama | Us | Sees one photo at a time in memory; keeps nothing | | **X** Third parties | Telegram, Apple and browser push services, the friend's SMS carrier, Overpass at build time | Them | Untrusted. Push services get ciphertext; Telegram gets what Telegram groups chose to post | Boundaries are drawn as `=== TB` labels. Every arrow that crosses one is TLS 1.2+ (HTTPS or WSS), except SMS, which the host sends from their own phone. # Flare: Sequence diagrams

Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Owner: Architect. Endpoints and messages refer to [openapi.yaml](contracts/openapi.yaml) and [asyncapi.yaml](contracts/asyncapi.yaml). Times are budgets from the SRS.

## S1. Send a Flare (SRS-CRE-1 to 9, median ≤ 15 s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor H as Host
  participant A as Host app
  participant S as Server
  participant R as Hub relay
  participant O as Hub + Ollama
  H->>A: Open app (camera live ≤ 1.5 s)
  H->>A: Shutter
  par draft
    A->>S: POST /api/v1/drafts (768 px JPEG)
    S->>R: job header + binary frame
    R->>O: /api/chat think:false
    O-->>R: {invite, alt} ~3.0 s
    R-->>S: result
    S->>S: enforce(); zero-fill buffer
    S-->>A: {invite, alt, tier: hub}
  and place
    A->>A: Nearest named feature ≤ 150 m, Ember candidates ≤ 400 m (map pack)
  end
  Note over A: Six words type in while the print develops (2.4 s)
  H->>A: Edit or keep words, tap quorum (2, 3, 4), Send
  A->>A: Seal blob (AAD g:id) and notice (AAD n:id), seal 1600 px photo (AAD p:id)
  A->>S: POST /groups/{g}/gatherings (Idempotency-Key)
  S->>S: Insert, host = 1 yes, short code, jobs: ember at t0+30 min
  S-->>A: 201 Gathering {short_code, need: 1}
  A->>S: PUT /gatherings/{id}/photo (ct)
  A->>H: Share sheet: link with #k=key, "Copy as text"
```

If the hub is absent or misses 6 s, step 8 returns `tier: rules` with the template and the app shows the typed six-word field with map-pack chips.

## S2. A friend says yes with a condition (SRS-RES-3, SRS-COND-5, ≤ 10 s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor F as Friend
  participant W as Link page
  participant S as Server
  F->>W: Open link (key in #fragment)
  W->>S: GET /gatherings/{id}
  S-->>W: view (need, sealed, server_time)
  W->>S: GET /gatherings/{id}/photo
  W->>W: Open blob and photo with key
  alt first visit
    W->>S: POST /groups/{g}/members {id, name_ct, write_token}
  end
  W->>S: GET /gatherings/{id}/events (SSE)
  F->>W: Add a condition: "after 2, only with Amor"
  W->>W: Rules parser: after(14:00 local → UTC), with(Amor's member id)
  W->>F: "Got it: after 2 PM, only with Amor. Right?"
  F->>W: Yes
  W->>W: Show "You're in." now (optimistic, ≤ 500 ms)
  W->>W: Needs check per label (spot, c1..cN)
  W->>S: PUT /gatherings/{id}/me {answer: yes, rules, checks}
  S->>S: Lock gathering row, save, solve, version + 1
  S-->>W: Me {answer: yes}
  S--)W: SSE gathering {need: 0 or N}
```

The typed words stay in IndexedDB on the friend's phone. Only the two rules cross the network.

## S3. It lights (SRS-LIT-1, ≤ 10 s to every member of the set)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant S as Server
  participant DB as Postgres
  participant P as Push services
  participant T as Telegram
  participant W as Friend phones
  S->>DB: Transaction: solver set ≥ quorum → state lit, lit_at, chosen_set, version + 1
  S->>DB: Cancel ember job; add gone job at Done or t0 + 4 h
  S--)W: SSE gathering {state: lit} (open pages)
  loop each member in the chosen set with a subscription
    S->>P: Web Push {g, event: lit, notice_ct} TTL 600, urgency high
    P--)W: Service worker opens notice_ct: "It's lit. Fuego is at Ford Woods Park pond."
  end
  opt Telegram group
    S->>T: editMessageCaption "It's lit..." (buttons removed)
    S->>T: sendMessage (notifies the chat)
  end
  W->>W: Save Lit data (spot, target, lines, time) in IndexedDB
```

## S4. Shrinks to an Ember (BR-F-3, BR-E-1 to 6)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant J as Scheduler
  participant S as Engine
  participant W as Phones
  J->>S: ember job due (t0 + 30:00)
  S->>S: Not lit → state ember, quorum 2, version + 1
  S--)W: SSE {state: ember, ember_choice: null}
  W->>S: PUT /me/checks {c1: false, c2: true, ...} (within 60 s)
  Note over S: At Ember start + 60 s, missing reports count as pass (BR-E-4)
  S->>S: Pick first label passed by every yes and every Ember-only yes, else spot
  S--)W: SSE {ember_choice: "c2", need: 1}
  W->>W: "Smaller plan: 15 min at {bench name from sealed blob}."
  Note over S: Ember-only yeses now count (BR-Q-6). Lit before t0 + 60 min increments embers_lit.
```

## S5. A Plan solves at the deadline, then someone fades (BR-P-2 to 7)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant J as Scheduler
  participant S as Engine
  participant W as Phones
  J->>S: plan_deadline job due (D)
  S->>S: For each step 1..4: best set (most people, higher step, earlier start)
  alt some step reaches quorum
    S->>S: lit at that step
  else ≥ 2 fit step 4
    S->>S: lit at step 4, Ember save
  else
    S->>S: gone, "Not this time."
  end
  S--)W: SSE + push "It's on: {step} at {time}."
  actor M as Member in the set
  M->>W: I'm fading
  W->>S: POST /gatherings/{id}/fade
  S->>S: Check window (S + 50% of step) and once per member
  S->>S: step + 1 (max 4), re-solve, add new fits, remove nobody
  S->>S: Members whose own rules now fail: still_coming = true
  S--)W: SSE {current_step} "Smaller plan: {step}."
  S--)W: Push to those members only: "Plan changed to {step}. Still coming?"
```

## S6. I'm here with no signal (BR-H-5, SRS-OFF-3)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor F as Friend
  participant W as Phone
  participant Q as Outbox (IndexedDB)
  participant S as Server
  F->>W: I'm here (airplane mode)
  W->>Q: {idem_key, POST /arrivals, {for: self, recorded_at}}
  W->>F: "You made it." (local)
  Note over W: Compass and Lit screen run from saved data: "Offline. Saved at 2:41 PM."
  W->>W: online event
  Q->>S: POST /gatherings/{id}/arrivals (Idempotency-Key)
  S->>S: recorded_at inside the Lit window? headcount + 1 (cap yes + 3)
  S-->>Q: 200 → remove item
  Q->>S: Retry of the same key (lost response)
  S-->>Q: Same 200 from the idempotency table, no second count
```

## S7. Telegram tap, then a condition (contracts/telegram.md)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor U as Telegram user
  participant T as Telegram
  participant S as Server
  participant W as Link page
  U->>T: Tap [I'm in] in the group
  T->>S: webhook callback_query y:{id}
  S->>S: Member via telegram, yes, solve
  S->>T: answerCallbackQuery "You're in. Only you see this."
  S->>T: editMessageCaption "Need 1 more."
  U->>T: Tap [Add a condition]
  T->>S: callback_query c:{id}
  S->>S: bind token (10 min, hash stored)
  S->>T: answerCallbackQuery url=t.me/FairlaneFlareBot?start=b_{token}
  T->>U: Private chat opens; user taps Start
  T->>S: /start b_{token}
  S->>T: sendMessage [Add a condition] → link?via=tg&bind={token}#k=...
  U->>W: Open link
  W->>S: POST /groups/{g}/members (phone's own member)
  W->>S: POST /gatherings/{id}/telegram-bind {token}
  S->>S: Move the Telegram yes onto this member; delete the tap-made member
  Note over W: Condition flow as in S2
```

## S8. Gone and deletion (BR-D-1 to 3)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor H as Host
  participant S as Server
  participant DB as Postgres
  participant T as Telegram
  participant W as Phones
  H->>S: POST /gatherings/{id}/done
  S->>DB: state gone, ended thanks_for_coming, jobs: delete at +60 s
  S--)W: SSE gone {ended}
  W->>W: Delete saved Lit data; show Spark prompt once (arrived only)
  opt Telegram group
    S->>T: edit to "Thanks for coming."
    S->>T: deleteMessages [ids]
  end
  S->>DB: +60 s: DELETE FROM gatherings WHERE id (cascade)
  S->>DB: counters + 1 (day bucket)
  Note over DB: Backstops: sweeper every 30 s, cron every 5 min, expires_at on every row
```

## S9. Hub connects, drops, comes back (ADR-0006)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant O as Ollama
  participant Hb as Hub
  participant S as Server
  Hb->>O: Warm-up chat (7 to 14 s cold)
  Hb->>S: WSS /hub, Authorization: Bearer HUB_SECRET
  S->>S: timingSafeEqual; wrong → 401
  Hb->>S: hello {protocol flare-hub.v1, model, ready: true}
  loop every 20 s
    S->>Hb: ping
    Hb->>S: pong
  end
  Note over Hb,S: Wi-Fi drops: socket closes, health shows hub absent, drafts use the template
  Hb->>S: Reconnect after 1, 2, 4 ... 30 s
  Hb->>S: hello
  loop every 20 min
    Hb->>O: Warm-up chat (keeps the 30 min keep_alive from expiring)
  end
```

# Flare: State machines

Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Owner: Architect. Source rules: BR-F (Flare), BR-P (Plan), BR-E (Ember), BR-H (arrival). The server clock decides every transition (BR-TIME-1). The engine implements each machine as a pure function `transition(state, event, now) → {state, effects}`; the transition tables below are its test cases.

Notation: `t0` = server time the Flare was created; `S` = Plan start; `D` = Plan deadline; `best` = size of the solver's best set including the host; `q` = quorum.

## 1. Flare

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR
  [*] --> Kindling: create (host = 1 yes)
  Kindling --> Lit: yes/rule change and best ≥ q\n(event received ≤ t0+30:00.000)
  Kindling --> Ember: timer t0+30:00, not lit
  Kindling --> Gone: host cancels\n"Not this time."
  Ember --> Lit: best ≥ 2 incl. Ember-only yeses\n(counts as Ember save)
  Ember --> Gone: timer t0+60:00, not lit\n"Not this time."
  Ember --> Gone: host cancels\n"Not this time."
  Lit --> Gone: host taps Done\n"Thanks for coming."
  Lit --> Gone: timer t0+4:00:00\n"Thanks for coming."
  Gone --> [*]: delete within 5 min
```

| # | From | Event | Guard | To | Effects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | none | create | quorum in {2, 3, 4}, group ≤ 12 | Kindling | host yes; short code; job `ember` at t0+30:00; expires_at t0+5 h |
| F2 | Kindling | yes, take-back, rule change, checks | solve(); best ≥ q; received ≤ t0+30:00.000 (BR-F-2) | Lit | lit_at; chosen_set; cancel `ember`; job `gone` at t0+4 h; push and bot "It's lit."; SSE |
| F3 | Kindling | same | best < q | Kindling | need = q − best; SSE; bot edit |
| F4 | Kindling | timer `ember` | not Lit | Ember | quorum = 2; job `ember_pick` at +60 s; job `gone` at t0+60:00; push and bot "Smaller plan: 15 min at {bench}." |
| F5 | Ember | checks or timer `ember_pick` | missing checks count as pass after 60 s (BR-E-4) | Ember | ember_choice = first label passed by all, else `spot` |
| F6 | Ember | any answer event | solve() with Ember-only yeses (BR-Q-6), best ≥ 2 | Lit | as F2; counter `embers_lit` + 1 |
| F7 | Ember | timer `gone` | not Lit | Gone | ended = not_this_time; push "Not this time." |
| F8 | Kindling or Ember | host cancel | host only | Gone | ended = not_this_time |
| F9 | Lit | host Done, or timer `gone` (t0+4 h) | | Gone | ended = thanks_for_coming; Spark prompt on phones with a ticket |
| F10 | Lit | yes from a new member | | Lit | counts toward headcount cap only (BR-H-4); nobody leaves the set (BR-F-7) |
| F11 | Lit | "Can't make it" | | Lit | answer cant_make_it; state unchanged (SRS-RES-6) |
| F12 | Lit | take-back | | Lit | refused: 409 `already_lit` |
| F13 | Gone | any | | Gone | 410 `gone` |
| F14 | Gone | timer `delete` (+60 s) or sweeper | | deleted | cascade delete; counters |

Race rule (BR-F-2): an answer and the `ember` timer both lock the gathering row (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`). The answer wins if its server receive time is ≤ t0 + 30:00.000, even when the timer job is already running; the timer re-reads the state after taking the lock and does nothing if Lit.

## 2. Plan

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR
  [*] --> Kindling: create (ladder of 4, S, D)
  Kindling --> LitStep1: every member said yes,\nno rules, before D
  Kindling --> Lit: timer D, best step reaches q
  Kindling --> LitStep4: timer D, no step reaches q,\n≥ 2 fit step 4 (Ember save)
  Kindling --> Gone: timer D, < 2 fit\n"Not this time."
  Kindling --> Gone: host cancels
  state Lit {
    direction LR
    Step1 --> Step2: fade
    Step2 --> Step3: fade
    Step3 --> Step4: fade
  }
  LitStep1 --> Lit
  LitStep4 --> Lit
  Lit --> Gone: Done, or S + step minutes + 60 min\n"Thanks for coming."
  Gone --> [*]: delete within 5 min
```

| # | From | Event | Guard | To | Effects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | none | create | D ≥ now+10 min; D ≤ S−10 min; S ≤ now+36 h (BR-P-1); 4 steps, minutes strictly decreasing (BR-P-4); quorum 2 to 6 | Kindling | job `plan_deadline` at D; expires_at S+24 h |
| P2 | Kindling | answers | every member yes with no rules, before D (BR-P-2) | Lit, step 1 | as F2 |
| P3 | Kindling | answers | otherwise | Kindling | need at the highest step that could still light (BR-Q-4, SRS-PLAN-11) |
| P4 | Kindling | timer D | max over steps of best ≥ q; pick by people, then higher step, then earlier start (BR-S-1) | Lit, step k | current_step = k; job `gone` at S + minutes(k) + 60 min; push "It's on: {step} at {time}." |
| P5 | Kindling | timer D | no step reaches q; ≥ 2 fit step 4 (BR-P-3) | Lit, step 4 | Ember save counter; push "Smaller plan: {step} at {time}." |
| P6 | Kindling | timer D | < 2 fit any step | Gone | "Not this time." |
| P7 | Lit, step k < 4 | fade by a set member | once per member; now ≤ S + 50% of minutes(k) (BR-P-5) | Lit, step k+1 | re-solve, add fits, remove nobody (BR-P-6); still_coming for members whose rules fail (ADR-0016); "Smaller plan: {step}." (BR-P-7); move `gone` job |
| P8 | Lit, step 4 | fade | same guards | Lit, step 4 | fade recorded; no step change (BR-P-6 "never below 4") |
| P9 | Lit | fade | guard fails | Lit | 409 `fade_used` or `fade_window_closed` |
| P10 | Lit | Done or timer `gone` | | Gone | thanks_for_coming |
| P11 | Kindling | host cancel | | Gone | not_this_time |

## 3. One member's answer

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR
  [*] --> None
  None --> Yes: I'm in (rules 0 to 4)
  Yes --> Yes: change rules or checks (before Lit)
  Yes --> None: Take it back (before Lit)
  Yes --> CantMakeIt: Can't make it (after Lit)
  None --> Yes: I'm in after Lit\n(headcount only)
  Yes --> Arrived: I'm here (Lit only)
  CantMakeIt --> Arrived: I'm here anyway
  Arrived --> [*]: Gone (spark ticket kept on phone)
```

Arrival rules: headcount = 1 + arrivals (BR-H-1), capped at yes-count + 3 (BR-H-4); a self "I'm here" and a host +1 for the same member count once (BR-H-3); outbox arrivals count if `recorded_at` is inside the Lit window (BR-H-5).

## 4. Hub connection (server view)

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR
  [*] --> Absent
  Absent --> Connected: upgrade with the right secret + hello ready
  Connected --> Absent: socket closed or replaced
  Connected --> Connected: job → result ≤ 6 s
  Connected --> Connected: job timeout → template, late result dropped
```

`/api/v1/health` reports `hub: connected` only in Connected with `ready: true`.

input.content:
# Flare: ERD and data dictionary

Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Owner: Architect. Physical model for PostgreSQL ([ADR-0004](adr/0004-storage-postgres.md)). Source of truth: [apps/server/src/db/migrations/0001_init.sql](../../apps/server/src/db/migrations/0001_init.sql). Logical stores DS1 to DS12 are from the analyst's dictionary ([04-data-flow-and-dictionary.md](../requirements/04-data-flow-and-dictionary.md)); changes from it are listed in section 4.

Types: `uuid` = UUID v4 made on the phone (ADR-0018); `ct` = `bytea` holding AES-256-GCM ciphertext from a phone (12-byte nonce first); `hash` = `bytea` SHA-256 of a 128-bit token.

## 1. ERD

```mermaid
erDiagram
  groups ||--o{ members : has
  groups ||--o{ gatherings : has
  groups ||--o{ sparks : keeps
  groups ||--o| hotspots : keeps
  groups ||--o{ counters : counts
  groups ||--o{ spark_tickets : issues
  groups ||--o{ telegram_links : issues
  members ||--o{ gatherings : hosts
  members ||--o| push_subscriptions : has
  members ||--o{ responses : gives
  gatherings ||--o| photos : has
  gatherings ||--o{ responses : collects
  gatherings ||--o{ jobs : schedules
  gatherings ||--o{ bot_messages : posts
  gatherings ||--o{ live_locations : shares
  gatherings ||--o{ telegram_binds : binds
  members ||--o{ live_locations : sends
  members ||--o{ telegram_binds : claims

  groups {
    uuid id PK
    text channel "link or telegram"
    bigint telegram_chat_id UK
    timestamptz created_at
    timestamptz last_gathering_at
  }
  members {
    uuid id PK
    uuid group_id FK
    bytea name_ct "ct, null for tap-made Telegram members"
    bytea write_token_hash "hash"
    text via
    bigint telegram_user_id
    timestamptz joined_at
  }
  gatherings {
    uuid id PK
    uuid group_id FK
    text kind
    text state
    text short_code "unique while not gone"
    uuid host_member_id FK
    smallint quorum
    text tz
    integer version
    bytea sealed "ct"
    bytea notice_ct "ct"
    jsonb telegram_plain "Telegram groups only"
    smallint text_yes
    text_arr ember_candidates "labels c1..c12"
    text ember_choice
    jsonb plan_steps
    smallint current_step
    uuid_arr chosen_set
    timestamptz expires_at
  }
  photos {
    uuid gathering_id PK, FK
    bytea ct "ct"
    timestamptz expires_at
  }
  responses {
    uuid id PK
    uuid gathering_id FK
    uuid member_id FK
    text status
    boolean ember_only
    jsonb rules
    jsonb spot_checks "label to bool"
    boolean faded
    boolean still_coming
    timestamptz arrived_at
    timestamptz expires_at
  }
  jobs {
    uuid id PK
    uuid gathering_id FK
    text kind
    timestamptz due_at
    timestamptz expires_at
  }
  bot_messages {
    bigint chat_id PK
    bigint message_id PK
    uuid gathering_id FK
    timestamptz expires_at
  }
  live_locations {
    uuid gathering_id PK, FK
    uuid member_id PK, FK
    bytea ct "ct"
    timestamptz at
    timestamptz expires_at
  }
  push_subscriptions {
    uuid member_id PK, FK
    text endpoint
    text p256dh
    text auth
  }
  sparks {
    uuid id PK
    uuid group_id FK
    bytea place_key_hash "HMAC"
    bytea text_ct "ct"
    bytea delete_token_hash "hash"
    date created_on
  }
  spark_tickets {
    bytea token_hash PK
    uuid group_id FK
    timestamptz expires_at
  }
  hotspots {
    uuid group_id PK, FK
    bytea blob_ct "ct"
    integer version
  }
  counters {
    uuid group_id PK, FK
    text name PK
    text bucket PK
    bigint value
  }
  telegram_links {
    bytea token_hash PK
    uuid group_id FK
    timestamptz expires_at
  }
  telegram_binds {
    bytea token_hash PK
    uuid gathering_id FK
    uuid member_id FK
    timestamptz expires_at
  }
```

Not drawn (no foreign keys): `global_counters (name, bucket, value)`, `idempotency (key, response, expires_at)`, `schema_migrations (name, applied_at)`.

## 2. Data dictionary

### Per-gathering tables (deleted at Gone; every row has `expires_at`)

| Table | Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gatherings (DS1) | id | uuid | PK, made by the host's phone | AAD for its sealed fields |
| | group_id | uuid | FK groups, cascade | |
| | kind | text | `flare` or `plan` | |
| | state | text | `kindling`, `lit`, `ember`, `gone` | 04-state-machines.md |
| | short_code | text | 5 of the BR-CH-3 alphabet; partial unique index while not gone | |
| | host_member_id | uuid | FK members, cascade | Counts as 1 yes (BR-Q-1) |
| | quorum | smallint | 2 to 4 Flare, 2 to 6 Plan; set to 2 at Ember | |
| | tz | text | IANA name from the host's phone | BR-TIME-2 |
| | version | integer | + 1 on every change | SSE event id, ETag |
| | state_since | timestamptz | | |
| | ended | text | `not_this_time`, `thanks_for_coming` | Same for every member (SRS-ST-3) |
| | sealed | ct | ≤ 16 KB plaintext; AAD `g:{id}` | host name, six words, scene, host line, spot, candidates, steps, access and nature lines |
| | notice_ct | ct | ≤ 2,100 bytes; AAD `n:{id}` | Copied into push payloads (ADR-0014) |
| | telegram_plain | jsonb | Telegram groups only | `{host, invite, place, link, ember_places, step_names}` (ADR-0013) |
| | text_yes | smallint | 0 to 3 | Anonymous yeses (BR-ID-6) |
| | ember_candidates | text[] | labels `c1`..`c12` in distance order | Places only in `sealed` (ADR-0009) |
| | ember_choice | text | a label or `spot` | |
| | plan_steps | jsonb | `[{step, minutes, place}]`, 4 items, minutes strictly decreasing | Names only in `sealed` |
| | current_step | smallint | 1 to 4 | Plans |
| | chosen_set | uuid[] | Solver output | Never sent to clients (SRS-PRIV-8) |
| | created_at, deadline_at, start_at, lit_at, done_at | timestamptz | Server clock | |
| | headcount | smallint | 1 + arrivals, ≤ yes + 3 | BR-H-1, BR-H-4 |
| | expires_at | timestamptz | t0 + 5 h (Flare), S + 24 h (Plan) | BR-D-2 |
| photos (DS3) | gathering_id | uuid | PK, FK cascade | |
| | ct | ct | ≤ 1.5 MB; AAD `p:{id}` | 1600 px JPEG q0.8 before sealing |
| responses (DS2) | id | uuid | PK, server-made | |
| | gathering_id, member_id | uuid | FKs cascade; unique pair | |
| | status | text | `yes`, `taken_back`, `cant_make_it` | |
| | ember_only | boolean | | BR-A-3, carries no reason |
| | rules | jsonb | 0 to 4 of `with`, `after`, `back_by`, `max_walk`, `max_step`, `min_step` | No free text (BR-C-9) |
| | spot_checks | jsonb | label → bool | BR-E-3, SRS-PLAN-6 |
| | faded | boolean | once per Plan | BR-P-5 |
| | still_coming | boolean | | ADR-0016 |
| | arrived_at | timestamptz | Lit window only | BR-H-5 |
| jobs (DS4) | kind | text | `ember`, `ember_pick`, `gone`, `plan_deadline`, `delete` | Rebuilt into memory at boot; 1 s tick |
| | due_at | timestamptz | | Fires within 30 s (SRS-ST-2) |
| bot_messages (DS7 refs) | chat_id, message_id | bigint | PK | Deleted after `deleteMessages` |
| live_locations (DS11) | ct | ct | AAD `l:{gathering id}`; overwritten in place | Host only, Lit only (SRS-CMP-6) |
| telegram_binds | token_hash | hash | 10 min | ADR-0013 |

### Group tables (survive Gone; BR-D-4 and BR-D-5)

| Table | Column | Type | Rules | Retention |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| groups (DS5) | id | uuid | PK, phone-made | Until the last member forgets it (ADR-0015) or 180 days without a gathering |
| | channel | text | `link`, `telegram` | |
| | telegram_chat_id | bigint | unique | |
| | last_gathering_at | timestamptz | | Drives the 30 and 180 day sweeps |
| members (DS5) | name_ct | ct | AAD `m:{group}:{member}`; ≤ 150 bytes | Until "Forget this group" |
| | write_token_hash | hash | | |
| | via, telegram_user_id | text, bigint | DS7 map | `telegram_user_id` set to null after 30 days without a gathering (BR-ID-5) |
| push_subscriptions (DS6) | endpoint, p256dh, auth | text | | Deleted 30 days after the group's last gathering, or on 404/410 from the push service |
| sparks (DS8) | place_key_hash | HMAC-SHA-256 | key from HKDF(group key) | 180 days without a gathering |
| | text_ct | ct | AAD `s:{group}:{spark}`; 1 to 140 characters before sealing | |
| | delete_token_hash | hash | | Lets the writer delete it (ADR-0015) |
| | created_on | date | day only | |
| spark_tickets | token_hash | hash | single use | 24 h after Gone |
| hotspots (DS9) | blob_ct | ct | AAD `h:{group}`; If-Match on `version` | 180 days without a gathering |
| counters (DS10) | name, bucket, value | | Exactly the counters in 07-kpis.md; day buckets at most | With the group |
| telegram_links | token_hash | hash | 15 min, single use | |

### System tables

| Table | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| global_counters | `tier_ran.{job}.{tier}` totals (BR-AI-3); no group, no time |
| idempotency | `{memberId or anon}:{key}` → first response, 24 h (SRS-REL-2) |
| schema_migrations | Applied migration names |

### Columns that must never exist

`apps/server/test/db.test.ts` fails if any table except `schema_migrations`, `counters` and `global_counters` has a column named `lat`, `lon`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `spot`, `place_name` or `name`, and if `sparks` has a `member_id` or a timestamp finer than a day.

## 3. Deletion audit mapping (BR-D-7)

| Logical store | Table | Per gathering | Audit counts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DS1 | gatherings | yes | rows with `expires_at < now()` or `state = 'gone'` older than 5 min |
| DS2 | responses | yes | rows with `expires_at < now()` |
| DS3 | photos | yes | same |
| DS4 | jobs | yes | same |
| DS7 refs | bot_messages | yes | same |
| DS11 | live_locations | yes | same |
| (new) | telegram_binds | yes | same |
| DS5 | groups, members | no | totals; members of groups past 180 days |
| DS6 | push_subscriptions | no | totals; rows past 30 days |
| DS7 map | members.telegram_user_id | no | non-null past 30 days |
| DS8, DS9 | sparks, hotspots | no | totals; past 180 days |
| DS10 | counters | no | totals |

# Flare: API overview

Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Owner: Architect. The contracts are the source of truth; this page is the map.

| Contract | Covers | Checked by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [contracts/openapi.yaml](contracts/openapi.yaml) (OpenAPI 3.1.1) | Every HTTP endpoint: 30 operations across 24 paths, the Telegram webhook, SSE endpoint, schemas, errors | Redocly 2.62.1 `recommended-strict`; route drift check |
| [contracts/asyncapi.yaml](contracts/asyncapi.yaml) (AsyncAPI 3.0.0) | Hub relay WebSocket, gathering SSE events, Web Push payload | @asyncapi/parser 3.6.3; hub zod schemas vs contract |
| [contracts/telegram.md](contracts/telegram.md) | Bot setup, updates handled, callback data, posts, edits, cleanup, limits | Engineering tests against a fake Bot API |
| [contracts/plain-text.md](contracts/plain-text.md) | SMS and satellite forms, reply parsing | 9 unit tests |

`npm run contracts` runs all checks; CI runs it on every push. A server route missing from openapi.yaml fails the build (`scripts/lib/contracts.ts`, tested both ways in `scripts/test/contracts.test.ts`).

## Conventions

| Topic | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Base path | `/api/v1`; breaking changes go to `/api/v2` |
| Auth | `Authorization: Bearer {memberId}.{writeToken}`; server compares SHA-256 of the token with `timingSafeEqual` |
| Idempotency | `Idempotency-Key` on every write; stored 24 h per member; a repeat returns the stored response with header `Idempotent-Replay: true` |
| Rate limits | 30 writes per minute per member, 300 per minute per gathering, 20 drafts per minute per IP; 429 with `Retry-After` |
| Errors | `{code, message}`; `code` from a fixed list of 25; phones map codes to copy deck strings, never show `message` |
| Validation | zod schemas generated by hand from the contract live in `packages/shared/src/api.ts`; bodies outside the schema get 400 `bad_request` with no echo of the input |
| Time | UTC ISO 8601 with milliseconds; every view carries `server_time` |
| Sealed fields | `*_ct` and `sealed`: base64url ciphertext; size caps in the schema |
| Caching | Views: `ETag` = version, `Cache-Control: no-store`; photo ciphertext: `private, max-age=3600, immutable` |
| CORS | Same origin only; no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` |
| Body limits | JSON 64 KB; photo 1.5 MB |

## Endpoints by job

| Job | Endpoint | Requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Health, config, audit | `GET /health`, `GET /config`, `GET /audit` | SRS-WEB-2 |
| Create and join a group | `POST /groups`, `POST /groups/{g}/members`, `GET /groups/{g}` | SRS-ID-1 to 5 |
| Rename, forget | `PATCH`, `DELETE /groups/{g}/members/{m}` | SRS-ID-6, ADR-0015 |
| Send | `POST /groups/{g}/gatherings`, `PUT /gatherings/{id}/photo` | SRS-CRE-6, -7, SRS-PLAN-1 |
| Read and follow | `GET /gatherings/{id}`, `/photo`, `/events` | SRS-RES-1, SRS-SOL-3 |
| Answer | `GET`, `PUT`, `DELETE /gatherings/{id}/me`, `PUT /me/checks` | SRS-RES-3, -6, SRS-COND-6, SRS-ACC-3 |
| Text yes | `POST /gatherings/{id}/text-yes` | SRS-CH-6 |
| Plans | `POST /gatherings/{id}/fade` | SRS-PLAN-7 |
| Lit | `POST /arrivals`, `PUT`, `GET`, `DELETE /live-location`, `POST /done`, `POST /cancel` | SRS-LIT-3, -4, SRS-CMP-6, SRS-ST-4 |
| Places | `POST`, `GET /groups/{g}/sparks`, `GET`, `PUT /groups/{g}/hotspots` | SRS-SPK-1, -2, SRS-HOT-1, -2 |
| Push | `PUT`, `DELETE /groups/{g}/push-subscriptions` | SRS-IF-3 |
| AI | `POST /drafts`, `POST /drafts/ladder` | SRS-AI-1, SRS-PLAN-2 |
| Telegram | `POST /groups/{g}/telegram-link`, `POST /gatherings/{id}/telegram-bind`, `PUT /gatherings/{id}/telegram-photo`, `POST /telegram/webhook` | SRS-CH-1 to 4 |

Pages that are not API: `GET /g/{id}` (app HTML with safe Open Graph tags, ADR-0017), `GET /check` (capability page), static app files.

## Built now

| Endpoint | Code | Tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/health` | apps/server/src/app.ts | app.test.ts |
| `POST /api/v1/drafts` | apps/server/src/app.ts, hub/relay.ts | app.test.ts (hub, timeout, template, 413, 415, 400), e2e-hello |
| `/hub` WebSocket | main.ts, hub/relay.ts, apps/hub | app.test.ts (401), hub.test.ts |

Everything else is specified and waits for engineering (handoff 07).

# Flare: Offline, sync and AI placement Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Owner: Architect. Decisions: [ADR-0010](adr/0010-offline-first.md) (offline), [ADR-0007](adr/0007-ai-placement.md) (AI), [ADR-0014](adr/0014-live-updates-sse-and-sealed-push.md) (live updates). ## Part A. Offline and sync ### A1. What works with no signal | Situation | Works | How | | --- | --- | --- | | App opened before, now offline | App shell, all screens | Service worker precache (SvelteKit `$service-worker` build + files lists) | | Lit, then signal lost | Lit screen, compass, speech, access and nature lines, "I'm here" | Saved Lit data in IndexedDB; compass needs only GPS and the saved target (SRS-CMP-7) | | Host with no signal wants to send | Photo, typed six words, place name, plain-text form | Map pack; no hub; "Copy as text" shares the SMS form; the Flare itself is created when the outbox reaches the server | | Friend with no data at all | Reads the SMS, replies `IN K7Q2M` to the host | Plain-text form (contracts/plain-text.md) | | Link never opened online | Nothing | Needs one online open; the SMS form covers this friend | ### A2. Phone stores (IndexedDB database `flare`, version 1) | Object store | Key | Contents | Lifetime | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `groups` | groupId | raw key bytes wrapped as non-extractable CryptoKey, memberId, write token, display names (opened) | Until "Forget this group" | | `needs` | `profile` | Needs profile (BR-A-1) | Until cleared | | `conditions` | gatheringId | Free text the person typed (never sent) | Until Gone | | `lit` | gatheringId | Saved Lit data: spot, target lat/lon, access line, host line, nature line, state time, `server_time` offset | Gone or Lit + 24 h | | `outbox` | idemKey | `{method, path, body, recorded_at, attempts}` | Until 2xx/4xx or 24 h | | `tickets` | gatheringId | Spark ticket | Used or 24 h after Gone | | `seen` | gatheringId | Last view version | Until Gone | ### A3. Outbox protocol 1. Every write builds `{idemKey: random 16 bytes base64url, method, path, body, recorded_at: Date.now()}` and stores it **before** the request. 2. The UI updates at once (optimistic; "You're in." ≤ 500 ms, SRS-RES-3). 3. Send now if online. On 2xx: store any response data (tickets), delete the item. On 4xx: delete it and show the mapped copy (for example `already_lit` → "It's already lit."). On 5xx or network error: keep it. 4. Flush order is creation order, one at a time, so a take-back can't overtake its yes. 5. Triggers: `online` event, `pageshow`, `visibilitychange` to visible, and a 15 s timer while visible. Safari has no Background Sync, so a closed app sends on next open. 6. Items older than 24 h are dropped and the person is told once: "Some taps didn't send." 7. The server stores `{memberId}:{idemKey}` → first response for 24 h; replays get the same response and `Idempotent-Replay: true` (SRS-REL-2). 8. Arrivals carry `recorded_at`; the server accepts them if that time is inside the Lit window, even when they arrive after Gone, up to the moment the gathering row is deleted (BR-H-5). After deletion they get 410 and are dropped. ### A4. Live view sync - On open: `GET /gatherings/{id}` → render; then SSE `/events` with `Last-Event-ID: {seen version}`. - Every view has `version` and `server_time`. Phones keep `offset = server_time − Date.now()` (smoothed over the last 5 views) and show times and countdowns from `Date.now() + offset` (BR-TIME-3). They never decide transitions. - A view with a lower version than `seen` is ignored. - While visible, poll every 30 s as a backstop; on `gone`, close SSE, delete `lit` and `conditions`, keep `tickets`. - "Offline. Saved at {time}." shows when SSE has been down for 10 s and the last poll failed. ### A5. Map pack - `apps/web/static/maps/fairlane.json`, built by `scripts/build-map-pack.ts` from the pinned Overpass query in docs/requirements/evidence/ (User-Agent `flare-outside/0.1 (+repo URL)`, overpass-api.de only). - 128 features within 3 km of TEST_AREA (lab 05): benches, picnic tables, toilets, drinking water, steps, parks, natural features, named paths. Integer-micro-degree coordinates, short keys: 6.7 KB, 1.8 KB brotli. - Carries `timestamp_osm_base`; the build fails if it is older than 7 days (SRS-IF-4, SRS-OFF-5). The app shows ODbL attribution on map-derived lines. - Precached with the shell; served `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400`. ## Part B. AI placement ### B1. Tiers ```mermaid flowchart LR photo[Photo taken] --> online{Online and
hub connected?} online -- yes --> hub[Hub: Gemma 4 E4B
≤ 6 s] hub -- valid after enforce() --> show[Show six words
'Made on our laptop'] hub -- timeout, error, invalid --> typed online -- no --> typed[Typed: ≤ 6 words,
map-pack chips
'Made from a template'] typed --> show2[Show] ``` | Job | Phone | Hub | Template (floor) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Photo → six words + scene | Resize to 768 px only | Gemma 4 E4B, 3.0 s, 39/40 quality | Typed words with chips from the map pack (nearest named feature, amenity words); scene from map facts: "A bench near Ford Woods Park pond." | | Conditions | Rules parser, 40/40 core, 15/20 hard | Not used (founder decision: no free text off the phone) | Rephrase hint | | Plan ladder | Places from the map pack, sunset (NOAA) | Labels and minutes, ≤ 8 s | Step minutes = total × 1, 0.5, 0.25, then the 10-minute bench; labels from the copy deck | | Needs, nature line, access line | Deterministic rules | Never | Never needed | | Rest loop request (P1) | Rules parser | Never | Pickers | | Fix the map tags (P1) | Photo resize | Gemma with the tag allow-list | Manual tag picker | ### B2. Validation (SRS-AI-2) - Photo drafts: `enforce()` in `packages/shared/src/photo.ts` on the hub and again on the server. Clips the invite to 6 words and the scene to 20, strips emoji and `#`, rejects person words (face, smile, man, woman, boy, girl, child, kid, age, race, skin, body, hair, wearing...) and identity words. Rejected → template. - Ladder drafts: exactly 4 steps; minutes integers, strictly decreasing, each ≥ 5; labels ≤ 4 words and pass the same person filter. - The tier shown to people is the tier that produced the final text (SRS-AI-4). ### B3. Model settings (lab 02) `{model: "gemma4:e4b-it-q4_K_M", stream: false, think: false, keep_alive: "30m", options: {temperature: 0, seed: 42, num_predict: 128}}`, prompt v2 (`SYSTEM_PROMPT`, credited to the lab in photo.ts). Retry once on an unusable answer inside the budget. Warm at hub start and every 20 minutes. ### B4. Capability detection (SRS-AI-5, SRS-COMP-2) The app checks features, never device names: `HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.toBlob`/`OffscreenCanvas` for resize, `'PushManager' in window` and `display-mode: standalone` for push, `DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission` for the compass on iOS, `speechSynthesis` for speech, `navigator.vibrate` or the iOS switch-overlay for haptics, WebGL2 plus a frame-time probe for the shader. `/check` shows each result with a timed test and "Copy report" (SRS-CAP-1).

# Flare: Security and privacy design

Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Owner: Architect. Requirements: SRS-PRIV-1 to 8, SRS-SEC-1 to 7, BR-D-1 to 7, BR-Q-5. Trust zones and flows: [02-data-flows.md](02-data-flows.md). Observability: [09-observability.md](09-observability.md).

## 1. Promises and how each is kept

| Promise (privacy page) | Mechanism | Proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nobody sees who said yes | API returns counts only; `chosen_set` never serialized; `GET /me` is about the caller only | Contract schemas have no member list on gatherings; engineering test T-PRIV-1 diffs two members' views |
| We can't read your photo, words, names or places (link groups) | Sealed on the phone, AES-256-GCM, key in the `#fragment` (ADR-0008); places as labels (ADR-0009) | Schema test: no place columns; T-PRIV-3 dumps the DB after a full flow and greps for the test words and place names: 0 hits |
| Conditions stay on your phone | Rules parser on the phone; only rules sent; bot never reads text (ADR-0013) | T-PRIV-2: network capture during a typed condition contains no typed words |
| Your needs stay on your phone | Needs checks on the phone; only pass/fail per label | Contract: `Checks` holds booleans only |
| It deletes itself | Cascade, expires_at, sweeper, cron, audit (ADR-0004) | `db.test.ts` cascade test; audit prints 0 after the field test (SRS-PRIV-5) |
| The photo for the six words isn't stored | Memory only, zero-filled (ADR-0011) | `hub.test.ts`: no fs import, no temp files |
| No trackers | No third-party scripts, fonts or analytics; CSP | CSP test; `connect-src` lists only self and api.weather.gov |

## 2. Honest limits (also on the privacy page, SRS-WEB-2)

1. Anyone with the link can open the Flare. The link is the invitation.
2. In a group of 3 or fewer, friends may guess who said yes. P6 says so at the moment it matters (R19).
3. To write the six words, the photo goes to our laptop over an encrypted link. It isn't stored.
4. Telegram groups: Telegram, and our server until the Flare ends, can read what Flare posts there, including the link (ADR-0013).
5. Safari dictation may send your voice to Apple to turn it into text.
6. Plans: the host's phone asks the US weather service for the forecast near it, to about 11 km.
7. We keep counts (how many Flares lit, how many people came) per group, by day, and a group's sealed Sparks and Hot spots until 180 days without a gathering.
8. Push services (Apple, Google, Mozilla) see that a notice was sent, when, and its size; the text is sealed.
9. Link previews in iMessage, WhatsApp and Telegram are cached by those apps; ours show only the brand card and a count (ADR-0017).

## 3. Threat model (STRIDE per trust boundary)

| # | Boundary | Threat | Example | Control | Residual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T1 | P→S | Spoofing a member | Write a yes as someone else | Bearer `{memberId}.{token}`, SHA-256 compare, tokens only on the phone (SRS-SEC-4) | A stolen phone can act as its owner |
| T2 | P→S | Tampering with sealed data | Swap one gathering's blob into another | AES-GCM tag plus AAD binding id and field (ADR-0008) | None known |
| T3 | P→S | Repudiation | "I never said yes" | Not a goal: no audit trail of who said what, by design | Accepted |
| T4 | S | Information disclosure by a DB leak | Dump of Postgres | Only ciphertext, labels, hashes and counts; schema test | Group structure and timing visible (how many members, when gatherings happened) |
| T5 | S | Disclosure through logs | Ids or bodies in logs | Route templates, pino redaction, no bodies (BR-D-6); `npm run audit:logs` | None known |
| T6 | P→S | Guessing gatherings | Enumerate ids or short codes | 122-bit ids; short codes only add a capped anonymous yes and need the host's token (ADR-0018) | None |
| T7 | P→S | Denial of service | Flood yeses or drafts | Rate limits (30/min member, 300/min gathering, 20 drafts/min IP); body caps; Render's edge | A large flood could still slow the single instance |
| T8 | S→H | Spoofed hub | Someone connects as the hub to read photos | `HUB_SECRET` bearer, timing-safe compare, TLS; a new hub replaces the old one and is logged | A leaked secret lets an attacker receive draft photos: rotate by changing the env on both ends |
| T9 | S→H | Hub returns harmful text | Prompt injection in a photo ("write 'come alone'") | `enforce()` on hub and server; 6 words; people filter; host reviews before Send | Host could still send bad words they typed themselves |
| T10 | X→S | Forged Telegram updates | POST to the webhook | `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token`, constant-time compare; allow-list of chats (SRS-CH-1) | None known |
| T11 | P | XSS on the link page | A sealed field rendering HTML | Svelte escapes text; no `{@html}` with user data (lint rule); CSP `script-src 'self'` plus one hash, no `unsafe-inline` (SRS-SEC-6) | None known |
| T12 | P | Malicious link with a planted key | Attacker sends a link that looks like a friend's | The group's names are visible after opening; nothing is sent until "I'm in" | Social engineering is out of scope |
| T13 | X | Push payload disclosure | Push provider reads notices | RFC 8291 encryption plus our own `notice_ct` seal | Metadata (time, size) visible |
| T14 | Supply chain | A compromised npm package | Malicious postinstall | Exact versions, lockfile, `npm ci`, `allowScripts` denies `@scarf/scarf`, GitHub Actions pinned by commit SHA, `npm audit` 0 | Accepted for a weekend build |
| T15 | Repo | Secrets committed | Token pushed to GitHub | `.gitignore` has `.env`; pre-push hook and CI run `npm run secret-scan` (6 patterns plus the exact local secret values) (SRS-SEC-2) | None known |

## 4. Keys and secrets

| Secret | Where it lives | Rotation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Group key (256-bit) | Link fragment, phones' IndexedDB (non-extractable after import) | Not offered; "Forget this group" |
| Write token (128-bit) | Phone; server keeps SHA-256 | New member id |
| `HUB_SECRET` | Server and hub env | Change both; the hub reconnects |
| `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | Server env | BotFather revoke, update env |
| `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Server env, given to Telegram at `setWebhook` | Re-run setWebhook |
| `DATABASE_URL` | Server and cron env | Render rotates credentials |
| `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` | Server env | New pair means phones resubscribe |
| `RENDER_KEY` | Operator's `.env` only, never on the server | Render dashboard |

`npm run check-env` reports set or missing per app and never prints a value, a prefix or a length (`scripts/lib/env-spec.ts`, 4 tests).

## 5. HTTP hardening (built, `apps/server/src/app.ts`)

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Content-Security-Policy | `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'sha256-…'` (hash of SvelteKit's one inline bootstrap, computed per HTML file); `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` (Svelte style attributes cannot run code); `img-src 'self' data: blob:`; `connect-src 'self' https://api.weather.gov`; `object-src 'none'`; `frame-ancestors 'none'`; `base-uri 'self'`; `form-action 'self'` |
| Strict-Transport-Security | `max-age=15552000; includeSubDomains` (Hono default) |
| Referrer-Policy | `no-referrer` (the fragment never leaks; the path doesn't either) |
| Permissions-Policy | camera, geolocation, microphone, motion sensors: self only |
| X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Cross-Origin-*-Policy | Hono secure-headers defaults |

Tests: `apps/server/test/static.test.ts` (hash present, no `unsafe-inline` in `script-src`, base policy on API responses, HSTS), `app.test.ts` (headers on API). `npm run e2e:hello` fails on any console error or CSP violation in Chrome.

Static files: paths are resolved and must stay inside the build folder (sibling-prefix attack tested); unknown paths return 404.

## 6. Deletion guarantees

| Layer | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Engine schedules delete at Gone + 60 s | 60 s |
| Sweeper every 30 s in the web service | 90 s worst case while it runs |
| Render cron `npm run sweep` every 5 min | 5 min if the web service is down |
| Reads filter `expires_at > now()` | Expired rows never served |
| Telegram `deleteMessages` | 5 min, 3 retries |
| Phone saved data | On learning Gone, else 24 h after Lit |
| Audit `GET /api/v1/audit` | Shows 0 when it worked |

## 7. Data minimization checklist for every new endpoint

1. Does it accept anything readable? If yes, can the phone seal it or reduce it to a label, count or boolean?
2. Does any response depend on another member's answer or needs? It must not (SRS-ACC-4, BR-Q-5).
3. Does the new table have `expires_at` and cascade from `gatherings`, or a retention rule from BR-D-5?
4. Is the route in openapi.yaml with a size cap on every string?
5. Do logs for it contain only the route template, status and time?

# Flare: Privacy-safe observability

Version 1.0, Sat 2026-10-10. Owner: Architect. Decision: [ADR-0020](adr/0020-observability.md). Rule: we can tell whether Flare works without learning anything about the people using it (BR-D-6, SRS-PRIV-4, SRS-PRIV-6).

## 1. Signals

| Signal | Source | Contains | Never contains | Kept |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Request log | pino, one line per request | method, route template (`/api/v1/gatherings/:id/me`), status, ms | ids, codes, bodies, headers, IPs, user agents, query strings | Render, 7 days |
| Event log | pino, fixed event names | event name, counts, durations, error codes | content of any kind | Render, 7 days |
| Health | `GET /api/v1/health` | ok, version, hub connected or absent, db ok, down or not configured | | live |
| Counters | `counters`, `global_counters` | the KPI counters in docs/product/07-kpis.md, day buckets; `tier_ran.{job}.{tier}` | anything per person, any time finer than a day | with the group; global forever |
| Deletion audit | `GET /api/v1/audit` | expired rows per table | ids | live, cached 60 s |
| Screen-time bucket | phone sends a bucket index (0 to 5) once per gathering | bucket index | seconds, timestamps | counter |

## 2. Event names

| Event | Fields | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `listen` | port | server up |
| `db.migrated` | applied | boot |
| `hub.hello` | model, ready | hub connects |
| `hub.closed`, `hub.replaced`, `hub.refused` | | hub socket changes; wrong secret |
| `hub.job` | kind, ok, error, ms | each AI job |
| `gathering.transition` | kind, from, to | every state change (no id) |
| `sweep.deleted` | gatherings, rows | each sweep with work |
| `push.sent` | event, ok, status | each push (status 404/410 deletes the subscription) |
| `tg.refused` | reason | unlisted chat or bad secret |
| `tg.delete_failed` | count | cleanup retries exhausted |
| `rate.limited` | scope (member, gathering, ip) | 429 |
| `error` | code, stack | unhandled error |

## 3. Redaction

`apps/server/src/log.ts` sets `base: undefined` (no hostname or pid) and redacts `req.headers`, `headers`, `authorization`, `body`, `photo`, `draft`, `invite`, `alt`, `name`, `spot`, `lat`, `lon`, `ip`, `token`, `secret`. `routeTemplate()` replaces UUIDs and any path segment of 20+ token characters with `:id`. Handlers never put request data in `Error` messages, so stacks carry none.

The team watches three things on a laptop:
1. Render log stream filtered to `hub.` and `error` events.
2. `curl https://{host}/api/v1/health` every 30 s (hub must stay `connected`).
3. `GET /api/v1/audit` after the last gathering: `pass: true`.

KPI table after the test: `npm run kpi -- --from 2026-10-11T15:00Z --to 2026-10-11T19:00Z` (SRS-FLD-1, engineering).

## 5. Checks

- `npm run audit:logs -- <exported log>` greps for any UUID, short code, coordinate-shaped number pair or known test word; passing = 0 matches (engineering, P0).
- `apps/server/test/app.test.ts` and a log-capture test assert a full request leaves only `{level, time, m, r, s, ms, msg}`.
