input.command:
cd "<project>/flare" && cat > docs/architecture/adr/0022-digitalocean-cloud-tier.md <<'EOF'
# ADR-0022: DigitalOcean Serverless Inference as a cloud tier

Status: Accepted (founder decision, Sun 2026-10-11 02:45 ET). Amends ADR-0007's tier table. Off until a scoped model access key is configured.

## Context
When the laptop hub is off or unreachable, every AI job falls to the template. The founder asked for DigitalOcean Serverless Inference (OpenAI-compatible, `inference.do-ai.run`) with an open Gemma model as a cloud tier, without weakening the privacy model.

## Decision
- **Model:** `gemma-4-31B-it`, an open Gemma 4 model DigitalOcean serves; it accepts images. Probe on 2026-10-11 with our own illustration fixture and the Plan ask "Fairlane walk at 11?": ladder 20.9 s, 309 tokens; photo 27.2 s, 541 tokens; both answers passed `enforceLadder()` and `enforce()`.
- **What may go there, and when:**

| Job | Goes to DigitalOcean when | Sends |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plan ladder | the hub is absent | the ask line (≤ 80 characters, no place) and the step-1 minutes |
| Photo to six words | the hub is absent **and** the host tapped "Ask DigitalOcean" for that Flare (`?cloud=1`) | the 768 px JPEG and the fixed prompt |
| Conditions, rest-loop requests, needs, places | never | nothing (SRS-PRIV-1: they stay on the phone) |

- **Never while the hub is up.** A slow hub answer still falls to the template; the cloud is not a second try that doubles the wait.
- **Guards:** the same `enforce()` and `enforceLadder()` as the hub. Server budget 35 s; phones wait up to 40 s only when `/config` says the tier is on.
- **No spend cap exists per key** at DigitalOcean (prepaid balance only, docs checked 2026-10-11). The server caps calls per UTC day (`DO_DAILY_MAX_CALLS`, default 60) and 200 output tokens per call.
- **Key type:** only a scoped model access key. An account-wide token (`dop_v1_…`) in `DO_MODEL_ACCESS_KEY` leaves the tier off, fails `npm run check-env`, and makes `npm run deploy:render` refuse to send it (packages/shared/src/token-guard.ts).
- **Disclosed:** `/config.cloud_ai`, the "AI on this phone" screen (`/ai/`, "When DigitalOcean is used"), the privacy page limit `site.privacy.l.cloud`, the H2 note under the button, and the tier label "Made by DigitalOcean".
- **Traced:** the call is a `chat gemma-4-31B-it` span with provider `digitalocean` (ADR-0021), outcome only.

## Consequences
- With a scoped key, a Plan still gets a drafted ladder with the Mac off; photos stay typed unless the host chooses otherwise.
- Field test: off unless the founder adds a scoped key; the hub is the path.
- Proof: apps/server/test/cloud.test.ts (7 tests: off for a missing key or an account token, ladder when the hub is absent, no photo without opt-in, opted-in photo sends only the prompt and the image, nothing while the hub is up, daily cap, `/config`).
EOF

input.message:
The DigitalOcean tier is done and pushed (be46334, ADR-0022). It stays off until a scoped model access key is in .env.

First, a disclosure. Before your warning about the key arrived, I had already used DO_MODEL_ACCESS_KEY for four calls:
- one GET /v1/models;
- one ladder completion with the ask "Fairlane walk at 11?";
- one photo completion with our own pond illustration fixture.

No personal data went out, and the key was never printed. Since then the code refuses that token. The founder may want to rotate it, since it's an account-wide token.

What those calls showed:
- `gemma-4-31B-it` is offered and accepts images.
- Ladder took 20.9 s and photo 27.2 s, far over the hub's 6 and 8 s. Both answers passed ML's guards.

Design, per your rulings:
- **Ladder:** goes to DigitalOcean only when the hub is absent.
- **Photo:** only when the hub is absent and the host taps "Ask DigitalOcean" on the typed-fallback screen (`?cloud=1`).
- **Never while the hub is up.** Rest-loop, conditions, needs and places never go there.
- **Budgets:** server 35 s; the phone waits 40 s only when /config says the tier is on.
- **Cost limits:** DigitalOcean has no per-key spend cap, only the prepaid balance. So the server caps calls per UTC day (DO_DAILY_MAX_CALLS, default 60) and 200 output tokens per call.
- **Disclosed in:** /config `cloud_ai`, the /ai/ screen ("When DigitalOcean is used"), the privacy page, the note under the button, and the label "Made by DigitalOcean".
- **Traced:** a `chat gemma-4-31B-it` span with provider digitalocean, outcome only.
- **Tests:** 7.

Token guards (packages/shared/src/token-guard.ts):
- check-env fails `dop_v1_` in DO_MODEL_ACCESS_KEY and `sntryu_`/`sntrys_` in SENTRY_DSN, saying why without printing the values.
- `npm run deploy:render` refuses to send either kind to Render, in the plan and again at deploy.

CI is green: 653 tests; link page JS 133.8 KB of 150.

For the founder: a Sentry project DSN, and a DigitalOcean model access key scoped to gemma-4-31B-it (Control Panel → Serverless Inference → Model access keys). With neither, the field test runs on the hub alone.

Next: QA, a11y and security on the field-test path, then deploy prep.

input.message:
The DigitalOcean tier is done and pushed (be46334, ADR-0022). It stays off until a scoped model access key is in .env.

First, a disclosure. Before your warning about the key arrived, I had already used DO_MODEL_ACCESS_KEY for four calls:
- one GET /v1/models;
- one ladder completion with the ask "Fairlane walk at 11?";
- one photo completion with our own pond illustration fixture.

No personal data went out, and the key was never printed. Since then the code refuses that token. The founder may want to rotate it, since it's an account-wide token.

What those calls showed:
- `gemma-4-31B-it` is offered and accepts images.
- Ladder took 20.9 s and photo 27.2 s, far over the hub's 6 and 8 s. Both answers passed ML's guards.

Design, per your rulings:
- **Ladder:** goes to DigitalOcean only when the hub is absent.
- **Photo:** only when the hub is absent and the host taps "Ask DigitalOcean" on the typed-fallback screen (`?cloud=1`).
- **Never while the hub is up.** Rest-loop, conditions, needs and places never go there.
- **Budgets:** server 35 s; the phone waits 40 s only when /config says the tier is on.
- **Cost limits:** DigitalOcean has no per-key spend cap, only the prepaid balance. So the server caps calls per UTC day (DO_DAILY_MAX_CALLS, default 60) and 200 output tokens per call.
- **Disclosed in:** /config `cloud_ai`, the /ai/ screen ("When DigitalOcean is used"), the privacy page, the note under the button, and the label "Made by DigitalOcean".
- **Traced:** a `chat gemma-4-31B-it` span with provider digitalocean, outcome only.
- **Tests:** 7.

Token guards (packages/shared/src/token-guard.ts):
- check-env fails `dop_v1_` in DO_MODEL_ACCESS_KEY and `sntryu_`/`sntrys_` in SENTRY_DSN, saying why without printing the values.
- `npm run deploy:render` refuses to send either kind to Render, in the plan and again at deploy.

CI is green: 653 tests; link page JS 133.8 KB of 150.

For the founder: a Sentry project DSN, and a DigitalOcean model access key scoped to gemma-4-31B-it (Control Panel → Serverless Inference → Model access keys). With neither, the field test runs on the hub alone.

Next: QA, a11y and security on the field-test path, then deploy prep.

# Release candidate and deploy runbook (Sun 2026-10-11)

Owner: Engineering lead. Every step that touches the founder's accounts waits for the founder's yes, marked **YES**. Commands run from the repo root on the hub Mac. Nothing below prints a secret.

## 08:00 Integration point 3

```bash
git pull && npm ci && npm run ci
```

## 08:30 Device checklist

[05-device-checklist.md](05-device-checklist.md). It includes the Telegram live test from `lab/`, which must run **before** any `setWebhook`. Record the chat id it prints.

## 09:30 Tag the release candidate

```bash

   npm run deploy:render -- --yes
   ```
   It finds or creates `flare-db` (Postgres, Ohio), `flare-outside` (web, 1 instance, health `/api/v1/health`) and `flare-sweep` (cron every 5 min), sets env, and starts a deploy. It prints the `https://….onrender.com` URL. First deploy takes about 5 minutes.

## 09:45 Connect the hub

On the hub Mac, with every other app closed and the Mac plugged in:

```bash
FLARE_SERVER_URL=wss://flare-outside.onrender.com npm run hub:field
```

The health line every 30 s must show the server link up and the model loaded. Keep the load below about 10, or photos miss the 6 s budget and fall back to typed words.

## 09:50 Smoke test

```bash
npm run smoke -- https://flare-outside.onrender.com
npm run smoke -- https://flare-outside.onrender.com
```

Run it twice: the first photo draft after a hub start pays a one-time model cost. Pass bar: all required checks ok; on the second run `photo draft: hub`.

## 09:55 Telegram (**YES**: setWebhook)

1. Put the chat id from the device check in `.env` as `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS`.
2. `npm run deploy:render -- --yes` again (updates env, redeploys).
3. `npm run telegram:webhook -- --yes`, then `npm run telegram:status` (webhook set, 0 pending).

## 10:00 Phones

Each phone opens `https://flare-outside.onrender.com/app/`, adds it to the Home Screen, opens it from the icon and allows notifications when asked. Then the founder sends the real Plan (E15-S5) before 11:00.

## During the test (11:00 to 15:00)

- Render log stream filtered to `hub.` and `error`.
- `curl -s https://flare-outside.onrender.com/api/v1/health` every few minutes: `hub` must stay `connected`.
- Sentry (if `SENTRY_DSN` is set): AI spans `invoke_agent flare-photo` and `flare-ladder` with tiers.

## After the test

```bash
curl -s https://flare-outside.onrender.com/api/v1/audit
npm run kpi -- --from 2026-10-11T15:00Z --to 2026-10-11T19:00Z
```

The audit must show `pass: true` for the post.

## Rollback

- Bad deploy: Render dashboard → flare-outside → Deploys → redeploy the previous one. The hub reconnects within 30 s.
- Hub trouble: drafts fall to typed words automatically; restart with the hub command above.
- Telegram trouble: the field test runs on links and the plain-text form; the bot can be removed from the group.

## BUG-{n:03d}: "Short one only" sent a rule that constrains nothing

- **Date:** 2026-10-11
- **Area:** Frontend link page (Plan answer), found in the lead's coverage check
- **Symptom:** Tapping "Short one only" on a Plan sent `min_step(4)`. Under ADR-0016 `min_step(n)` holds when the step number is at most n, so `min_step(4)` is true for every step: the friend could be counted for the 60-minute step 1.

- **Fix:** `shortOnly()` sends `max_step(4)`; the test asserts it.
- **Proof:** flow tests 37/37; the engine test for max_step keeps the member out of steps 1 to 3.
'''
open(p,"w").write(s)

input.message:
Entire is working in this session, no restart needed. Every commit since enable carries an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer, and 53 checkpoints are now on the private origin (refs/entire/*).

Hooks:
- Entire put its hooks in .githooks (our core.hooksPath) and chains our original pre-push as pre-push.pre-entire. That file now runs the file secret scan, then the new `npm run scan-sessions`, which scans Entire's session logs for secrets with the same rules plus the 9 local secret values.
- Last push: 949 files and 180 session files scanned, 0 findings.

SRS-SEC-7 (before anything public): `npm run scan-sessions -- --public` also flags personal data. It finds **100 email addresses** in the session transcripts today. So before the repo goes public, the session logs must be scrubbed, or refs/entire kept off the public remote. That's a decision for the founder at the "repo public" YES.

Keys:
- SENTRY_DSN: valid DSN. The deploy plan sends it to Render.
- DO_MODEL_ACCESS_KEY: still wrong, now a **`doo_v1_` DigitalOcean OAuth token**, also account-level. The guard keeps the cloud tier off and the deploy plan lists it as "not sent: account token". I made no call with it.
  - A Serverless Inference model access key comes from Control Panel → Agent Platform / Serverless Inference → Model Access Keys. It is not a doo_/dop_ token.
  - Once it's in, I'll run the one ladder fixture check you asked for.

I also found and fixed a real Plan bug in the coverage check. "Short one only" sent `min_step(4)`, which every step satisfies, so it constrained nothing. It now sends `max_step(4)` (BUG-057).

Continuing the coverage check and closing the gaps: Plan first, then Sparks.

content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary request and intent**

   **Project and deadline.** Flare is an entry for the DEV Hacktoberfest Week 1 "Touch Grass" challenge.
   - Deadline: Mon 06:59 UTC.
   - Field test: Sun 11 AM to 3 PM ET near Fairlane Town Center, Dearborn. The release candidate (RC) must be ready by 10 AM.
   - The work runs "like a real software company, waterfall style": one specialist at a time, each producing docs, proof, a handoff, and commits, plus a BUGLOG.
   - Manager-session messages are to be treated as the user's.

   **Security and constraints (verbatim from the user, still in force):**
   - "Secrets are already in .env, at <project>/flare/.env (if you're running in a worktree copy, read them from that path). … Never print, log or commit them. .gitignore already protects .env."
   - "Anything public waits for my yes: deploying under my accounts, making the repo public, publishing, posting, uploading, or messaging people."
   - "Already approved, no need to ask: npm installs; installing Ollama with Homebrew and pulling gemma4:e4b; downloading the Gemma 4 E2B ONNX model (~3.2 GB) for browser tests; creating a private GitHub repo named flare on my account and pushing to it; keeping the Mac awake (caffeinate) during long work."
   - "A separate lab session is running technical spikes in lab/ (git-ignored). Don't edit or commit lab/."

   **Writing rules.**
   - Plain words, and a number or proof for every claim.
   - Banned words: seamless, leverage, robust, empower, unlock, elevate, delve, cutting-edge, revolutionize, game-changer, harness, synergy, holistic, paradigm, next-level, supercharge, effortless, ecosystem, tapestry, testament.
   - Buttons are 3 words at most; messages 12 words at most.
   - No TODOs, stubs or fake data.

   **Sequence of requests in this stretch:**
   - **Architect role:** done (handoff 07).
   - **Engineering lead role:** WBS, ICD, spikes, dependencies and process, device checklist, handoff 08. Done.
   - **Nine specialists in parallel worktrees:** done (engine, backend, integrations, ML, on-device-ai, maps, frontend, pwa, website).
   - **Manager's change of approach:** no new subagents. I do the remaining work myself, in this order:
     1. integration;
     2. finish the frontend field-test path;
     3. merge, CI and e2e;
     4. QA, a11y and security;
     5. deploy prep for 9:30;
     6. after the test: the website (Lighthouse at 61 on mobile `/`), polish, the remaining roles.
   - **Founder decisions:**
     - **Entire:** the founder ran `entire enable`; I chain hooks and add the SRS-SEC-7 scrub.
     - **Sentry Agent Tracing:** server-side only, privacy-safe.
     - **DigitalOcean Serverless Inference cloud tier:** ladder only when the hub is absent; photo only on an explicit opt-in; daily cap.
   - **Manager:** "don't idle." Do the field-test coverage check and close every P0 gap in order with real-stack e2e (Plan and Sparks matter most). Then the handoffs, and Entire hook chaining.
   - **Manager:** add lint plus fast unit tests to the pre-push chain (under ~30 s).
   - **Manager:** verify the DO key by behavior:
     - GET `/v2/account` should be refused;
     - then one ladder fixture call;
     - then classify by scope rather than prefix, record it in ADR-0022, and let the deploy send it with the tier on.

2. **Key technical concepts**
   - **Monorepo:** npm workspaces with `packages/shared`, `packages/engine` (@flare/engine), `apps/server` (Hono + ws + pg/PGlite), `apps/hub` (Ollama client) and `apps/web` (SvelteKit 3, Svelte 5, adapter-static with fallback `200.html`).
   - **Runtime:** Node 24.21 runs `.ts` via type stripping (erasableSyntaxOnly: no parameter properties).
   - **Hub relay:** an outbound WebSocket.
     - Heartbeat: the server pings every 5 s and drops the hub after 12.5 s of silence, or 3 s after a job timeout.
     - The hub reconnects after 15 s of silence; first redial at 250 ms.
     - Pending jobs fail fast when their socket closes.
   - **Budgets and model:** photo 6 s, ladder 8 s; model `gemma4:e4b-it-q4_K_M` with `think:false`.
   - **Privacy model:** a group key in the URL fragment; AES-GCM with an AAD table; opaque place labels (spot, c1..c12, step:1-4); counts only; sealed `notice_ct` for push; Telegram groups are the disclosed exception.
   - **ICD types** live in `packages/shared/src/icd/` (engine, map, conditions, capabilities, client). ICD-1 is v1.1 (ICR-1: counter `by`/`op`). ICD-5 is v1.1 (CR-PW4: `fragment`, `rememberGathering`).
   - **Hub protocol:** `ToHubV11` includes `LadderJob`; `JobResult.ladder` (ICR-BE-1); `HubLadderStep`.
   - **Copy deck:** `design/prototype/src/lib/copy/deck.json`, checked by copy-lint. `docs/content/02..05` are generated.
   - **Entire CLI 0.11.4** at `~/.local/bin/entire`. Checkpoints are stored at `refs/entire/checkpoints/*` and pushed to the private origin. Hooks live in `.githooks` and chain to `pre-push.pre-entire`.
   - **Sentry 11.6.0:**
     - Server-only, with `defaultIntegrations: false`.
     - Allow-list scrub in `beforeSendSpan`, `beforeSendTransaction` and `beforeSend`.
     - Spans: `invoke_agent flare-photo|flare-ladder`, `chat <model>` (provider ollama or digitalocean), `execute_tool enforce`.
   - **DO cloud tier:**
     - Model `gemma-4-31B-it` at `https://inference.do-ai.run/v1/chat/completions`.
     - Budget 35 s; `DO_DAILY_MAX_CALLS` defaults to 60; `max_tokens` 200.
     - Ladder only when the hub is absent; photo only with `?cloud=1` and the hub absent.
     - `/config` exposes `cloud_ai`. The phone waits 40 s (CLOUD_TIMEOUT_MS / CLOUD_WAIT_MS).
   - **Test clock:** `FLARE_E2E_CLOCK=1`, allowed only with `DATABASE_URL=pglite:memory`. Endpoint: `POST /__e2e/clock {advance_ms}`.

3. **Files and code sections (main ones created or modified this stretch)**

   **`docs/architecture/*`**
   - 12 docs, ADRs 0001-0022, and the contracts (openapi.yaml, asyncapi.yaml, telegram.md, plain-text.md).
   - ADR-0021 covers Sentry.
   - ADR-0022 covers DigitalOcean, including the behavior check result: 403 on the account API and a valid ladder in 3.8 s.

   **`docs/engineering/*`**
   - Planning docs: 01-work-breakdown, 02-interface-control, 03-spikes, 04-dependencies-and-process, 05-device-checklist (step 0 now says the field Mac runs only the hub), 06-deploy-runbook.
   - Also: `briefs/`, `notes/`, `bugs/`, `qa/01-field-path-qa.md`, `qa/evidence/e2e-field.txt`, `spikes/evidence`.

   **`docs/handoffs/`**
   - 07-architect, 08-engineering-lead, 06b, 06c, 06d, 06e, 06f, 06g (from the specialists), 07b, 07a and 07c (written by me), and RESUME.md (kept current).

   **`apps/server/src/integrations.ts`** (lead wiring)
   - `integrations(env, webBuildDir)` returns `{ mount, resume, close }`.
   - Builds INT's ports from BE core:
     - `yes`, via `runEvent` with an answer event;
     - `view`, via `engine.view`;
     - `member`, via `memberFromHeader`;
     - `me`, via `meView`.
   - Mounts `mountTelegram` or `mountTelegramOff`, `mountPreview` and `createPush`.
   - Sets `ctx.effects.created`, `ctx.effects.push` and `ctx.effects.telegram`.
   - Supports `TELEGRAM_API_BASE_URL` for tests.

   **`apps/server/src/http/middleware.ts`**
   - Added `memberFromHeader(header, db)`; `requireMember` calls it.

   **`apps/server/src/tracing.ts`**
   - Exports `ALLOWED`, `scrubAttributes`, `isDsn`, `initTracing(env, extra)`, `aiJob`, `hubChat`, `cloudChat`, `guardSpan` and `flushTracing`.
   - `isDsn = /^https:\/\/[A-Za-z0-9]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\/\d+$/`.

The two missing menu screens are built, tested and pushed, so no menu link 404s any more. The new real-server test (`npm run e2e:loop`) passes 15/15.

**One thing for the field test:** Bench to Bench finds **no loop** at Ford Woods, the field-test spot. That's the map data, not a bug: the benches mapped there sit too close together. The screen says so and offers "Try 400 m". Demo it at Village Green (42.3064, -83.227) instead, or mention the limit in the post.

**Bench to Bench (`/app/loop/`)**
- At Village Green, "Knee's bad, 40 minutes, want trees" gave a 32 min, 1.6 km loop with 11 benches, built in 83 ms.
- "Print card" saves a 3.6 KB PDF, and "Read it aloud" reads the turns out loud.
- The person's words stay on the phone: 0 server calls carried them.

**Fix the map (`/app/fix-map/`)**
- The person picks what's missing (a bench, restroom, drinking fountain or steps), then keeps, changes or removes each tag.
- Export stays locked until every tag is checked, and bad values are refused.
- The note text goes to the clipboard and the .osm file downloads. Nothing is sent to OpenStreetMap or to our server.
- **Limit:** the tags start as the usual ones for that kind of thing, not read from a photo, because the hub can't draft tags from a photo yet. The screen says this, and it's on the after-test list.

content.text:
The website now scores 100 in all four Lighthouse categories on all five pages, mobile and desktop. Each score is the median of 3 runs: 26 of 30 mobile runs scored 100 and 4 scored 99. Mobile scores move a couple of points between identical builds on this Mac, so I record every run in `summary.json` and keep the median, as Lighthouse advises. The reports are in `docs/website/lighthouse/`.

**How mobile went from 96–98 to 100**, keeping the same look and motion:
- **Scripts after first paint:** website pages no longer preload their JavaScript, and they start loading it one frame after the page paints (`apps/web/src/hooks.server.ts`). Before, about 100 KB of scripts competed with the first paint. On the real server all pages still come alive (flame motion, live privacy table) with no console or security-policy errors, and the website tests pass 26/26.
- **Smaller grain image:** the paper-grain background is now a 10 KB tile instead of 45 KB, cut from the same image. Before and after screenshots look identical.

**Decision for you:** `/ai/` is left out. It's an in-app page that `robots.txt` deliberately hides from search engines, and it can't score 100 on SEO while it stays hidden. If you want it public, I'll add it to the sitemap and the Lighthouse run.

**Photo-to-tags drafting for Fix the map (ML5): built, paused before it was tuned.**
- Fix the map can now take a photo, and the hub drafts the tags from it. The new end-to-end test passes 20/20 with the real hub and model.
- I grew the eval set from 5 to 11 photos, and two problems are still open:
  - **Too slow:** the slowest results reach 13.8 s against an 8 s budget. The eval sends full-size photos and the phone sends smaller ones; I haven't re-measured with phone-size photos yet.
  - **Invents features:** on 4 of the 6 photos with nothing to tag, the model claims a shelter or a waste basket. The app throws away the model's guess of what the thing is and a person still checks every tag, but tags like `covered=yes` still reach that review.
- The next steps for both are written in `evals/reports/osm-tags-hub.md`.

**Telegram:** the live test passed, and the allowed chat id is now in `.env`. The one tap the script missed ("Not now") is added to the 8:30 device check. I haven't touched the bot. The branded card post and the per-group photo opt-in are queued for after the deploy and before the post.

`RESUME.md` is current. Next is integration point 3 at 08:00, the device check at 08:30, the release-candidate tag at 09:30, and the deploy when you say yes.

input.message:
P0 gap found while building the Telegram card: the phone has no Telegram path, so no app-made Flare can reach a Telegram group today.
- The server side is done and tested against the fake Bot API: the telegram-link route, the `telegram` object on create, posts, count edits, telegram-photo, and deletion.
- But nothing in apps/web calls POST /groups/{id}/telegram-link (connect this group to a chat). The host's create request never sends the readable `telegram` object, so the bot has nothing to post. This morning's live test drove the Bot API directly from lab/, not through the app.
To have Telegram in the field test, the phone needs:
1. A menu item "Post in Telegram" with the disclosure ("Telegram sees what Flare posts there…"), which calls telegram-link and opens the t.me startgroup link.
2. In a group with channel=telegram, host create sends `telegram: {host, invite, place, link}` (plus ember and step names).
3. The photo opt-in toggle on the same screen. When it's on, PUT the 768 px JPEG to telegram-photo after create.
Estimate: 60 to 90 min with real-stack e2e on the fake Bot API, then one live check in "Flare test". The server branded card (render, edit on state, opt-in gate) is in progress now and doesn't depend on this.
Your call: build 1 to 3 before the deploy, or keep Telegram out of the field test and run links only. I'll keep going on the server card until you answer.

# ADR-0023: Telegram posts show a branded card; real photos only on a group opt-in

Status: Accepted (founder decision, Sun 2026-10-11 ~06:40 ET). Amends ADR-0013 (Telegram groups) and contracts/telegram.md section 3.

## Context
ADR-0013 posted the Flare photo to Telegram when the host's phone sent it, else plain text. The phone never sent it, so every post was text. The founder wants Telegram to look like Flare, and wants the real photo there only when a group chooses it, because a Telegram post is the one place a Flare's content leaves our encryption.

## Decision
- **Default: a branded card.** The bot posts a 1200x800 PNG rendered on the server in memory (`apps/server/src/telegram/card.ts`): the flame for the state (Kindling grows with the count, Lit with the gold dot, Ember's dome, Gone's smoke), the six words, the place label the caption already shows, and the count line. No host or member names, no real photo, no location beyond the place label. The caption and buttons are unchanged (telegram.md 3).
- **The card follows the state.** Every edit of a card post is `editMessageMedia` with a newly drawn card and the new caption: count changes, Lit, Ember, Smaller plan, and the final line. Every bot message is still deleted at Gone (telegram.md 6, BR-D-3).
- **Real photo: per group, off by default.** `groups.telegram_photos` (migration 0004), set from the phone's "Post in Telegram" screen through `PUT /groups/{id}/telegram-settings`. Only when it is on does the host's phone send the Flare's 768 px JPEG with `PUT /gatherings/{id}/telegram-photo`. The server uploads it with `sendPhoto` from memory, zero-fills the buffer and keeps nothing. With it off, that route answers 409 and the bot does not wait for a photo. A real-photo post edits only its caption.
- **Disclosure, in three places:** the setting itself ("Telegram keeps a copy until the post is deleted; everyone in the group sees it."), the privacy page (`site.privacy.l.telegram`), and this ADR. Groups that use links only are unaffected.
- **Rendering stack:** `@resvg/resvg-wasm` 2.6.2 (published 2024-03, MPL-2.0; WASM, so the same on the Mac and on Render) with the website's fontsource faces. resvg reads TTF/OTF, so the WOFF 1.0 files are unpacked in memory (`woff.ts`, about 50 lines). We did not use satori: it had about a dozen releases in the three days before this decision, too new to trust for a release candidate.

## Consequences
- The card costs 15 to 60 ms of CPU per post or edit; edits stay coalesced to one per 3 s per message (telegram.md 5).
- If the card cannot be rendered, the post falls back to text with the same caption and buttons.
- After a server restart the bot does not know whether a post was a card or a photo; it then edits the caption only, which is correct for both.

## Proof
- Server tests: card PNG size, no host name in the card, state views, the app's flame geometry, WOFF conversion; photos off by default, 409 when off, card at once, card after the wait when on, edits by `editMessageMedia`, deletion at Gone (`apps/server/test/integrations/telegram*.test.ts`, 178 server tests pass).
- Real stack, phone to fake Bot API: `npm run e2e:telegram`, 14/14 (card PNG with caption and three buttons; photo on gives the host's JPEG).
EOF

# Flare

Snap where you are. If enough friends quietly say yes, it's on.

Flare is an installable web app for small groups of friends (2 to 12). A host sends a photo of where they are, or a Plan for later. Friends say yes in private, with conditions if they like ("after 2", "only with Amor"). It lights only when enough people can come, it shrinks to a smaller plan instead of failing, it works for friends with low vision or limited mobility and with no signal, and it deletes itself within 5 minutes of ending.

Built for the DEV Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge, Week 1 "Touch Grass". Field test: Sunday 2026-10-11, near Fairlane Town Center, Dearborn MI, on four iPhones.

## Run it yourself

Needs Node 24.21.0 or later ([.nvmrc](.nvmrc)), and for the photo AI a Mac (or any machine with a GPU) running [Ollama](https://ollama.com).


## Privacy in one paragraph

The group key lives in the link's `#fragment`, which browsers never send to servers. Photos, names, places, coordinates and Sparks are sealed on the phone (AES-256-GCM) before upload. Conditions are parsed on the phone and only the rule is sent. To write the six words the photo goes to our laptop over an encrypted link and is held in memory only. Groups that choose Telegram trade some of this for convenience, and the app says so before they do. Full details: [security and privacy design](docs/architecture/08-security-privacy.md).

A DEV staff member said in the launch post comments that people may submit by their own local time (comment 3ghbj, by heyitsjem). The rules make the sponsor's clock official. For us in ET, 06:59 UTC is later than local midnight anyway, so plan to the UTC time.

- **ElevenLabs ($100):** give an open-source agent a voice, transcribe audio for a local model, or narrate the demo.

Traits shared by the winners, ranked by how often they appear:

2. A frank "what went wrong" section with concrete bugs.

---
title: "Flare: snap where you are, and it only lights if enough friends quietly say yes"
published: false
tags: devchallenge, hf26challenge, gemma, opensource
---

<!-- DRAFT. Every [FIELD: …] spot is filled from the Sunday field test tonight. Every number
     without a FIELD marker is measured and linked to its proof in the repo. Remove this
     comment before publishing. -->

*This is a submission for the [Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass](https://dev.to/challenges/hacktoberfest-week1-2026-10-05).*

## What I Built

[FIELD: one or two sentences in a tester's own words about the problem, quoted with their OK. Example shape: "We all say 'we should hang out' in the chat, and then nobody goes."]

Flare is a web app for a small group of friends, 2 to 12 people. The host takes a photo of where they are. An open model on our laptop looks at it and writes a six-word invite, like "Bench by the pond, sun out." Friends get a link and say yes **in private**, with conditions if they want: "after 2", "only if Amor comes", "if it's not raining". Nobody sees who said yes, only the count.

It lights only when enough people can actually come. If not enough can, it shrinks to a smaller plan instead of failing (a bench closer by, a shorter walk). When it lights, everyone gets the spot and a compass that points to it. Then the screen gets out of the way.

A few more things it does:

- **Works with Telegram or plain links.** In a Telegram group the bot posts a Flare card and counts taps; in iMessage, WhatsApp or SMS it's just a link. There's a plain-text form for friends with no data.
- **Sparks and Hot spots.** After a meetup, people leave a one-line memory. The next invite from the same spot says "Your group met here once." and shows it.
- **Bench to Bench.** A walking loop that never goes too far between seats, read back first ("40 min, a bench every 200 m, under trees") and printed as a large-print card.
- **Fix the map.** When a bench or fountain is missing from OpenStreetMap, the model drafts the tags from a photo, a person checks every one, and the app exports a note. It never posts to OSM itself.
- **It forgets.** Every Flare, its photo and every yes are deleted within 5 minutes of ending. Worst case measured: 90 s ([spike E2](https://github.com/Hotragn/flare/blob/main/docs/engineering/03-spikes.md)).

Who it's for: friends who mean to meet up and don't, including a friend with low vision (VoiceOver, large text), a friend who can't walk far (seat-to-seat routes, step-free checks), and a friend with a weak signal (it queues and sends later).

## Demo

- Live app: [FIELD: Render URL after deploy, e.g. https://flare-outside.onrender.com/app/]
- Website: [FIELD: Render URL]/ (Lighthouse 100 on all four categories, mobile and desktop, median of 3 runs: [reports](https://github.com/Hotragn/flare/tree/main/docs/website/lighthouse))
- Video: [FIELD: 60 to 90 s screen recording from docs/post/media/, uploaded]

[FIELD: screenshots from docs/post/media/: send, lit, compass, Ember, Spark, Telegram card]

### The field test

We tested it for real on Sunday, October 11, near Fairlane Town Center in Dearborn, Michigan, with four iPhones [FIELD: number of people, and who used Telegram vs links].

| Run | What happened | Measured |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [FIELD] | [FIELD] | [FIELD: send to lit time, walk time, compass error] |

[FIELD: the best moment, in plain words. The worst moment, in plain words.]

## Code

{% github Hotragn/flare %}

AGPL-3.0. The README has a 3-step quick start (server, hub, phone), and [docs/README.md](https://github.com/Hotragn/flare/blob/main/docs/README.md) indexes the rest.

## How I Built It

### The model: Gemma 4 E4B on a laptop, not in the cloud

The photo goes to a Mac running **Gemma 4 E4B** (`gemma4:e4b-it-q4_K_M`, 7.5B parameters, 6.58 GB) on **Ollama**. The Mac dials out to our server over a WebSocket, so nothing on it is exposed to the internet. The photo is held in memory and zero-filled after the call; it's never written to disk on either end.

Why that model: I measured the options before picking one ([model selection](https://github.com/Hotragn/flare/blob/main/docs/ml/model-selection.md)):

| Model | Where | Result | Shipped? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gemma 4 E4B, Q4_K_M | Ollama on the Mac | 20/20 valid JSON, 39/40 scenes right, 3.0 s median | Yes |
| Gemma 4 E2B, ONNX q4f16 | Chrome, WebGPU | 20/20 JSON, 2.3 s, but scenes 29/40, and it invents water and sunsets | No: needs a 1.17 GB GPU buffer; iPhone Safari caps buffers at 1 GiB |
| SmolVLM-500M | Chrome and Safari | Scenes 16/40, 6/20 misleading | No |
| Qwen3-0.6B (for conditions) | Safari | 26/40 | No: rules got 40/40 in under 1 ms, and the model hung Safari |

**The model picks the words; code owns the facts.** Every answer goes through `enforce()` before anyone sees it: six words or fewer, no names of people, no invented places. If the model is slow (over 6 s for a photo) or its answer fails the check, the app shows typed words instead. Nobody waits on the AI.

The same model drafts Plan "ladders" (a big plan and three smaller versions, 12/12 valid, p95 6.5 s) and Fix the map tags (11 photos in the eval; 0 tags off the allow-list after the guard).

### What doesn't use a model, on purpose

Conditions ("after 2, only with Amor") are parsed on the phone by rules: 40/40 on the core test set, 15/20 on the hard set, under 1 ms, and the words never leave the phone. The only thing sent to the server is the rule, like `{after: "14:00"}`. Bench to Bench requests are parsed the same way (16/16 plain requests).

### Privacy, built in

- The group key lives in the link's `#fragment`, which browsers never send to servers. Names, places, photos and Sparks are sealed on the phone (AES-256-GCM) before upload. The server sees counts and opaque labels like `c3` or `step:2`.
- Telegram groups are the one disclosed exception: the bot needs readable text to post. By default it posts a Flare card, not the photo. A group can turn on real photos, and the setting says plainly that Telegram keeps a copy until the post is deleted.

### Stack

SvelteKit 5 (installable PWA, works offline), Hono on Node 24, Postgres, an outbound WebSocket relay to the Mac, Web Push, a Telegram bot, OpenStreetMap packs for places and loops. [FIELD: Render web service and Render Postgres, if deployed there.]

### How it was built

I ran it like a small software company, one role at a time: research, product, requirements, brand, design, architecture, engineering lead, then nine specialists building in parallel against frozen interfaces, then integration and QA. Every role left a handoff in the repo. The test suite is 659 tests plus 7 end-to-end suites on the real server and engine.

**Disclosure:** I built this with Claude Code. A separate "manager" Claude session, acting as the CTO for me, sent many of the prompts in the build sessions: it relayed my decisions and set the order of work. Product and privacy decisions were mine; the manager session asked before anything public.

## What I got wrong

- **The Telegram path didn't exist in the app until the morning of the test.** The server side was built and tested, but no screen on the phone connected a group to Telegram. I found it while building the Telegram card, about four hours before the field test, and built the missing screen with a real-server test.
- **Sparks never reached Hot spots.** Three bugs together: the Hot spots record was never written, "met here" was always empty, and the record fired three times. The field-path coverage check caught all three (BUG-058 to 060).
- **"Short one only" asked for the long one.** The button sent `min_step` instead of `max_step` (BUG-057).
- **A dead Wi-Fi link looked alive forever.** A half-open socket kept the hub "connected" and every photo waited out the full 6 s. Fixed with a heartbeat; measured recovery on a real half-open link: 16.1 s (BUG-030, BUG-031).
- **The website scored 61 on mobile.** WebGL flames ran in software. CSS flames got it to the high 90s; deferring hydration until after the first paint and a 10 KB grain texture got it to 100.
- **Bench to Bench finds no loop at our own test spot.** The benches at Ford Woods are mapped too close together. The app says "No loop keeps benches that close. Try 400 m?" instead of inventing one. [FIELD: did we fix the map there?]
- **The tag drafter makes things up on empty photos.** On 4 of 6 photos with nothing to tag (a playground, a skate park), it drafted a shelter. The app throws away the model's guess of what the thing is, and a person still checks every tag.
- [FIELD: anything that broke on the iPhones]

## What I didn't do

- **No model on the phone.** Gemma 4 E2B runs in Chrome on a Mac, but not inside iPhone Safari's memory limits. Measured, not shipped.
- **No cloud model by default.** A DigitalOcean fallback exists for when the laptop is off, but photos go there only if the host opts in for that Flare.
- **Not tested on Android.** All four test phones were iPhones.
- **Not a native app.** It's a web app you add to the Home Screen.
- **Fix the map is slow.** The slowest tag drafts take 13.8 s, over the 8 s budget, in the eval with full-size photos. Not fixed yet.
- [FIELD: anything we cut on the day]

## Why Does Open Innovation Matter?

For this app, open weights are the whole design, not a preference.

- **The photo never leaves our hands.** It's a picture of exactly where someone is standing, right now. With an open model on our own laptop, it goes there in memory and is gone after the call. With a closed API, it would be on someone else's servers under someone else's retention policy.
- **It costs nothing per photo.** [FIELD: number of photos drafted during the test] drafts on the laptop cost $0. That matters for a free app with no business model.
- **We could measure it, and we could pick the size.** I ran five open models side by side on the same 20 photos and chose by measured results. I could see exactly why the small one failed on an iPhone (a 1.17 GB buffer). With a closed model I'd get an answer and no way to look inside.
- **Open data too.** Places, benches and walking paths come from OpenStreetMap. When the map is wrong, Fix the map gives back a reviewed note instead of just taking.

Where open beat closed for us: privacy of location photos, zero cost per use, and being able to check the work. Where it didn't: speed. A large hosted model would be faster than a laptop on a busy afternoon.

content.text:
The shot list is written and a small Ember fix is in. My bug report was wrong, though: the Ember screen in the screenshot was correct all along. I've stopped and am holding the rest of the window for the device check, the 09:30 release candidate and the deploy.

**What the bug really was:** the host's spot is itself named "West Road" (a street name, used when no named place is nearby). No bench was close enough to offer a smaller plan, so Ember stayed at the spot, and "No benches mapped within 200 m" is true there.

**What I fixed instead:** a related real bug. When Ember moves people to a nearby bench, the friend's screen still described the original spot's surroundings. Now:
- the line describes the bench itself, read from the friend's map;
- the bench counts as "Bench right here", even if the friend's phone has an older map than the host's;
- if the friend's phone has no map loaded, the line is hidden rather than shown wrong.

The change is small: one method in `link.svelte.ts`, one line in `InfoLines`, and one new text string. Two new tests pass, and on the final build e2e:field passes 27/27 and `flow.ts real` passes 5/5 with 0 page errors. I re-captured the post screenshots on that build. The bug log now has the corrected description.

**Shot list for the iPhone recording:** in `docs/post/shot-list.md`. It has 8 portrait shots of about 10 s each, about 90 s in total:
1. Taking the photo
2. Sending
3. The friend opening the invite
4. It lights
5. Find them, with sound on
6. People meeting, filmed with a second phone's camera
7. Leaving a Spark
8. The Telegram card

An Ember run is an optional extra. The file also lists privacy checks before posting (faces, names, other chats in frame).

The raw data looks fine (webkitCompassHeading, about 14° accuracy, 20 to 50 events/s, best GPS fix 2.5 to 3 m), so the problem is in our logic. Fix it properly:
- circular smoothing of heading
- account for screen orientation and tilt

- **One big action per screen.** Ask the name once at first run, not on every send.

input.message:
Timing check, needs your call: it's 10:19. rc-1 was due at 09:30, the field test starts at 11:00, and nothing is deployed yet. The redesign plus Crew (A) plus the Touch Grass home (B) is several hours of careful work. It can't land before 11:00 without risking the build the testers will use.
Recommendation:
(1) Now to about 10:35: finish the compass fixes from today's streams (below).
(2) 10:35 to 10:55: Render free tier. Deploy-script change, a keep-warm ping during the test, a cold-start "Waking up…" state in the UI, the runbook, and the device-doc Telegram note. Then the deploy on the founder's YES.
(3) The field test runs on the current UI, with the fixed compass and the Telegram card.
(4) After the test: the redesign with A and B, before and after screenshots, and the post media recaptured from the new UI. That also gives the post real field photos.
I'm proceeding with (1) and (2) unless you say otherwise.
Device data verdict:
- 16 Pro Max: "close" was right. The tester never got more than 7.5 m from the mark, with GPS accuracy of 2.8 to 8.7 m, so nothing could point reliably. But it said "close" 49 times: the near state flickered at the gate edge, and the distance-halved repeat fired at 1 to 2 m.
- iPhone 13 (Safari 27.0): heading events did arrive, 571 recorded at 10 Hz with one 14.5 s gap (screen off?). The tester stood within 1.6 m the whole run. "eventsPerSecond 0" is a bug in my page: a second Start tap creates a second counter that zeroes the first.
- Fixes in progress: near hysteresis (enter at 2× accuracy, leave above 2.5×), no repeat on halving under 20 m, "close" spoken once until you leave it, a single-start guard, and average events/s in the report. Both real streams become replay tests.
- For the field test, the compass needs about 30 m or more of separation to show a direction; please tell the testers.

Tests  2 passed (2)
# ADR-0005: One Render web service plus Render Postgres; HTTPS from day one

Status: Accepted (deploy itself waits for the founder's yes). Date: 2026-10-10.

## Context
Phones need HTTPS for the camera, geolocation, device orientation, service workers and Web Push (lab report 04). The hub needs a server it can dial out to (ADR-0006). RENDER_KEY is available for the Render API. Ollama cannot run on Render: CPU-only E4B took 126 to 215 s per photo (lab report 08).

## Decision
- **Web service** `flare-outside`: Node 24.21.0, build `npm ci && npm run build`, start `npm start`. Serves the API, the hub WebSocket on `/hub`, the SSE streams and the static web build. Starter plan ($7/month) on test day so it does not sleep; the free plan sleeps after 15 minutes idle, which would drop the hub socket and add a cold start.
- **Postgres**: Render Postgres, same region (Ohio, closest to Dearborn), internal URL.
- **Cron job**: `npm run sweep` every 5 minutes (ADR-0004).
- **TLS**: Render's managed certificate on `*.onrender.com`; `Strict-Transport-Security` from the app.
- **Health check path**: `/api/v1/health`.
- **Secrets**: set in the Render dashboard or by API from `.env`, never in `render.yaml`.
- One instance only: the hub relay and SSE fan-out keep state in memory. Two instances would split the hub from half the phones.

## Consequences
- A deploy restarts the process; the hub reconnects within 1 to 30 s (backoff), phones' SSE reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`, and timers are rebuilt from the `jobs` table (SRS-ST-2).
- Scaling past one instance would need the relay and fan-out in Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY`; not needed for 4 phones and groups of 12.

## Options weighed
| Option | Why not |
| --- | --- |
| Fly.io, Railway | No key on hand; Render has a partner category we qualify for honestly (we really deploy there) |
| Self-signed LAN HTTPS from the Mac | Works only on the same Wi-Fi; the field test is outdoors on cellular |
| Tailscale Funnel to the Mac | Kept as backup in lab report 08; needs the founder's yes |

input.content:
# Flare 2026: the direction

Sun 2026-10-11. Written after the device check, when the founder saw the real screens on an iPhone and said they "look like a 2015 app". The manager session agreed. This replaces the paper-and-serif look of [05-design-system.md](05-design-system.md) for the app; tokens, accessibility rules and motion timings carry over.

Before screenshots (real app, today): [redesign/before/](redesign/before/). After screenshots go in `redesign/after/` once each screen is built.

## The roundtable

A design review run as a structured exercise. The product designer and the motion designer are this project's own roles (handoffs 04 and 05). The other voices are *personas*: how each of those people is known to think, applied to our screens. They are not quotes and not endorsements.

| Voice | Looked at | Said, in short |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Product designer (handoff 04) | Send, invite | We built forms. A first-name field on every send, three lines of small text under the photo. Cut to one decision per screen. |
| Motion designer (handoff 05) | Lit, Ember | The flame is our best asset and it sits in a box. Let the state change take the whole screen for half a second. |
| Steve Jobs (persona) | Everything | "The photo is the product." Make it the screen, edge to edge. Then remove until it breaks. |
| Brian Chesky (persona) | Home, after an outing | Design the trip, not the booking. The app should feel like the start of an afternoon, and end with "you were outside 52 minutes together". |
| Evan Spiegel (persona) | Invite, Spark | Open to the camera, talk in pictures. A friend should understand the invite in one second without reading. |
| Senior iOS 26 designer (persona) | Components | Use the system's language: SF via `system-ui`, Liquid Glass sheets over content, big rounded actions in the thumb zone, sheets you can drag. Glass only where there's something behind it, and check contrast on the worst photo. |

Where they disagreed and what we chose:

- **Fraunces.** Jobs and the iOS designer wanted it gone; the product designer wanted to keep the six words special. **Decision:** keep Fraunces for the six words only (the invite line on the photo), SF everywhere else.
- **Glass everywhere vs legibility.** The iOS designer's rule wins: a translucent sheet only over the photo, with a scrim behind the text so contrast is at least 4.5:1 on any photo (checked on the brightest and the busiest test photos).

## Rules anyone can check

1. **The photo is the screen.** Invite, send, lit and Ember show the photo full-bleed behind everything. No framed thumbnail.
2. **One big action per screen**, 56 px tall, in the thumb zone. A second action is a text button at most.
3. **Text: an icon plus 3 to 5 words.** Any line longer than 8 words moves behind a "More" tap, or goes.
4. **Ask the name once,** at first run. Never on send.
5. **System font.** `system-ui` (SF Pro on iPhone), with Dynamic Type-like sizes: 34 / 28 / 22 / 17 / 15. Fraunces only for the six words.
6. **Glass sheet** for content over the photo: blur 24 px, a 40% dark scrim under the text, 28 px top corners, a grab handle; drag down to collapse.
7. **The flame is alive.** Kindling grows with each yes; Lit fills the screen with warm light for 600 ms, then settles; Ember shrinks with a soft note. Reduced motion: the colour change only.
8. **Every flow ends pointing outside.** The last screen of every flow says where to go or tells you to put the phone away.
9. **Keep what works:** axe 0, 44 px targets, the JS budget, Lighthouse 100 on the website, the copy deck as the only source of strings.

## Screen by screen

| Screen | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Home (new, B)** | The camera, straight away | "Golden hour in 47 min" and today's weather window at the top; the nearest green spot from the map pack with its one-thing-worth-noticing line; "3 h 10 min outside together this week"; one big **Light a Flare**; **Plan for later** as text |
| **Send** | Photo in a frame, a first-name field, quorum, host line, info lines | The photo full-bleed; the six words over it in Fraunces; a glass sheet with "Goes when [2] [3] [4] are in" as three big chips and **Send it**. Name asked once at first run |
| **Invite** | Small photo, host line, four lines of info | The photo full-bleed; the six words big; "Fuego · 9 min walk" and the count as dots on a glass sheet; **I'm in**; "Add a condition" as text |
| **Lit** | Flame in a box, "It's lit." | The whole screen warms to the lit colour for 600 ms, the flame grows and settles over the photo; the spot and walk time; **Find them** |
| **Find them** | Dial on paper | Dark, full screen, the flame pointer large, distance in 64 pt SF, one line of direction; "It points once you're at least 30 m apart" only when close |
| **Ember** | "Smaller plan" title and info lines | The flame shrinks to the ember dome; "Smaller plan: 15 min at West Road" in two lines; **I'm in** |
| **After an outing (new, B)** | "Thanks for coming." | "You were outside 52 min together" over the photo; the Spark prompt; then a calm **Phone away** screen (dark, the flame breathing slowly, nothing to tap but Done) |
| **Crew (new, A)** | Hot spots and Forget as separate menu pages | One space, below |

## Crew (A)

One home for your people. **Never shows who said no, or anyone's answers.**

- **People:** each member's first name and initial in a circle, no profiles. A small "out now" dot only for people who are Lit or have arrived in an active Flare. No tracking, no location outside a Flare.
- **The crew's story:** Hot spots (from the sealed blob), recent Sparks, and stats from the existing counters: "4 outings · 3 h 10 min outside together · 2 Embers saved".
- **Outside minutes:** a new per-group counter, the minutes from each person's arrival to Gone, summed. It stores a number per group, never who or where, and it is deleted with the group. ADR-0024 records it.
- **Manage:**
  - invite with a link and a QR code
  - rename the crew (the name is sealed, like every name)
  - set the default quorum
  - Telegram connection and the photo opt-in (moves here from "Post in Telegram")
  - remove a member: only the crew's creator can, and it rotates the group key, so the removed member's phone can't open anything new (ADR-0024)
  - leave the crew
  - **Forget this crew** (deletes everything, as today)

## Order of work

1. Design system: system font, the type scale, the glass sheet, the full-bleed photo layout, the big action. Website follows the same type.
2. Send, invite, lit, Find them, Ember, Spark on the new system.
3. Home (B) and After an outing (B).
4. Crew (A), with its server pieces: the outside-minutes counter, member removal with key rotation, ADR-0024.
5. Re-check axe, the JS budget and Lighthouse; recapture `docs/post/media` from the new UI.

The deploy is blocked on repo access. I ran `npm run deploy:render -- --yes` and Render answered: "400: passed in repository URL is invalid or unfetchable: https://github.com/Hotragn/flare".

- Tell me when that's done and I'll re-run immediately. The script finds what it already made, so the re-run is safe. Then smoke ×2 → setWebhook → one live tap, and I'll report the URL and the results.
- The deploy script now shows Render's error text; it never prints the request body.
Meanwhile I'm back on the redesign branch (main stays the deploy build). Post plan noted: no outdoor group-test claims; it will be built on the automated real-stack runs, the two real iPhone device checks, the live Telegram checks and the deletion audit, with a marked spot for a real outing.

input.prompt:
You are specialist S3 (ML, fine-tuning) on Flare. Repo: the worktree you're in (main repo <project>/flare). Node 24 runs .ts directly. Python 3 is available.

GOAL: use Tinker (Thinking Machines' fine-tuning API, Python SDK `tinker` / `tinker-cookbook`; read their official docs/README on PyPI or GitHub for the API) to fix ONE measured failure with a LoRA on a small open model, with honest before/after evals, a model card, and an honest result even if it doesn't win.
Recommended target (fastest): the conditions parser hard set. Flare parses friends' conditions ("after 2, only if Amor comes, back by 5") into rules on the phone. The rules parser scores 40/40 on the core set and 15/20 on the hard set (evals/reports/conditions-rules-lab07-baseline.md; datasets docs/requirements/fixtures/conditions-60.json and evals/datasets/conditions-cr-a1.json; parser apps/web/src/lib/conditions/*.ts; output contract packages/shared/src/icd/conditions.ts). Train a small model (e.g. a Qwen3 or Llama 1B-4B class base Tinker offers) to emit the same rule JSON. Generate synthetic training data deterministically from templates plus the rules parser (never train on the eval items; keep the 20 hard + 40 core strictly held out). Alternative only if clearly faster: the OSM tag drafter inventing amenities on no-feature photos (evals/datasets/osm-tags.json, evals/reports/osm-tags-hub.md) — vision is likely slower; prefer conditions.
Secrets: TINKER_API_KEY is in the main repo's .env at <project>/flare/.env (the founder named it ELEVENLABS/TINKER style; it may be named TINKER or TINKER_API_KEY — read the env file programmatically in Python, map whichever exists to the SDK's expected env var in-process). NEVER print, log or commit any key or the .env contents; never write it to a file.
Cost: before training, estimate cost from Tinker's published pricing and the token count; stay under USD 10 total; if the estimate exceeds that, stop and report. Report actual usage if the SDK exposes it.
Deliverables (in NEW files only; don't edit app code, server, or existing evals):
- ml/tinker/ (train.py, data generator, eval.py, requirements.txt with exact pinned versions at least 2 weeks old), training data generator output stats.
- Eval: run the SAME scoring as the existing conditions eval (read evals/harness/tasks/conditions.ts for the metric) on core_40 and hard_20 for: rules parser (baseline), base model zero-shot, LoRA model. Report a table. If the model can run locally on the hub (export LoRA/merge to GGUF for Ollama) do it only if the export is clean in < 30 min; otherwise report "eval-only, served by Tinker sampling".
- evals/reports/conditions-tinker.md (+ .json), docs/ml/model-card-conditions-lora.md (data, base model, training config, eval, limits, license of base model), docs/handoffs/11-tinker.md.
Rules: plain words, no banned words (seamless, leverage, robust, empower, unlock, elevate, delve, cutting-edge, revolutionize, game-changer, harness, synergy, holistic, paradigm, next-level, supercharge, effortless, ecosystem, tapestry, testament). cd "<project>/flare" && cat > docs/architecture/adr/0024-crew-space.md <<'EOF'
# ADR-0024: Crew space: stats from counters only; member removal without key rotation (for now)

Status: Accepted, Sun 2026-10-11. Amends ADR-0008 (group key) for what the Crew space shows.

## Context
The founder asked for one home for the crew: people, who is out now, the week outside, places, Sparks, and management, including removing a member with a group-key rotation so they lose access.

## Decision
- **People:** first names opened on the phone with the group key (as today). No profiles, no photos.
- **Out now:** a count of live Flares and Plans that are lit, from `GET /groups/{id}` (states only). No names: who arrived never leaves the server (SRS-PRIV-8), so the dashboard cannot and does not say who is out.
- **The crew's story:** `GET /groups/{id}/stats`, member-only, from the counters the engine already writes per group: outings (`flares_lit` + `plans_lit_step`), minutes outside together (`lit_minutes_sum`, Lit to Gone), Embers saved (`embers_lit`), and one new bucket, `lit_minutes_week` by ISO week. Numbers only, never who, where or when; the `counters` rows cascade with the group, so Forget deletes them.
- **Crew name and usual quorum:** stored on the phone only for now (no server field), and labelled "on this phone".
- **Remove a member: not built yet, and no key rotation.** A real rotation needs a way to give the new key to everyone except the removed person. Flare's only key channel is the link fragment, so rotating would mean every remaining member opening a new link, and old sealed data (names, Hot spots, Sparks) would need re-sealing by someone holding both keys. Doing this right needs per-member keys (each phone holding a key pair, the group key wrapped per member). Until then, "remove" would only stop the server from accepting that member's writes, which is weaker than the founder asked, so we don't claim it. Leaving and Forget this crew work today (ADR-0015).

## Consequences
- The dashboard is honest about what it can know: counts, not people's movements.
- Member removal with rotation is backlog work with its own ADR when per-member keys exist.
EOF

# ADR-0025: The Plan ladder as a Mastra agent, behind a flag

Status: Proposed (S2, Sun 2026-10-11; follow-ups the same day). Off by default (`LADDER_AGENT=1` turns it on). Keeps ADR-0007 (8 s hub budget), ADR-0021 (allow-listed spans) and ADR-0022 (DigitalOcean only when the hub is absent).

## Context
`POST /api/v1/drafts/ladder` sends the ask line, the minutes and the phone's coarse weather to the hub. It runs `enforceLadder()` on the answer and falls back to `templateLadder()`. We wanted the draft to come from an agent with real tools: sunset, a weather window, places from the map pack, and the step templates. The phone's answer, what the Mac exposes and what leaves the server had to stay as they are.

## Decision
- **Library:** `@mastra/core` **1.68.0**, pinned exact.
  - Published 2026-09-22, the only release that day, and a week before the next one. 1.70.0 and 1.71.0 came out the same day (09-24), so we skipped both.
  - Loaded with a dynamic `import()` on the first agent request, so with the flag off nothing loads.
  - We use `Agent` and `createTool` only, never the `Mastra` class.
  - Mastra sends usage events to PostHog by default, so we set `MASTRA_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` before the import (`apps/server/src/agent/no-telemetry.ts`).
- **Request:** two new optional fields in `LadderRequest` (zod and openapi.yaml):
  - `start_at` (ISO date-time): when the plan starts.
  - `area` (1 to 40 characters, digits refused): a map-pack place label such as "Ford Woods Park", or the pack name "fairlane". Refusing digits means it can never carry coordinates.

  The tools read both; neither goes to the hub or to DigitalOcean. Without `start_at` the tools use now, as before.
- **Tools** (`apps/server/src/agent/tools.ts`). All are local and pure except the weather tool:
  - `sunset`: the NOAA math, copied from `apps/web/src/lib/map/sun.ts` into `apps/server/src/agent/sun.ts` (the server imports no web code). It works on the area's 0.1° cell and the plan's day, gives local time in America/Detroit, and says whether the plan ends after dark.
  - `weather_window`: the api.weather.gov hourly forecast for the area's 0.1° cell, reduced to `{rain_likely, temp_f}` for `[start_at, start_at + minutes)`. Same rules as `apps/web/src/lib/map/weather.ts`. It has a 2.5 s cap, returns `null` on any failure, and is skipped when the phone already sent weather.
  - `nearby_places`: the Fairlane pack (`apps/web/static/maps/fairlane.json`), read once and reduced to 36 named parks, water, woods and shelters. It returns the labels the ask names, the five closest labels, and counts. Never coordinates.
  - `step_templates`: `templateLadder(total)`.
- **Area lookup:** `resolveArea()` maps the area label to a 0.1° cell. A label the pack doesn't know falls back to the pack centre. The cell is used inside tools and cache keys only.
- **Caches:** they make the tools cheap after the first request.

# ADR-0026: Google AI Studio as the second cloud provider

Status: Accepted (Sun 2026-10-11). Extends ADR-0022; every rule there still holds.

## Context
ADR-0022 added one cloud provider, DigitalOcean Serverless Inference, for when our laptop (the hub) is off. On 2026-10-11 DigitalOcean began answering `402 "This account has been blocked"` (billing; on the founder's list). With no hub and no cloud, Plan drafts fall back to templates and photos to typing. The founder added a Gemini API key (`GEMINI_API_KEY`) and asked for Gemma 4 through Google AI Studio.

## Decision
- **Order:** DigitalOcean first when its scoped key is set, then Google AI Studio. Either one alone works. `apps/server/src/cloud.ts` holds both backends behind one `chat()`.
- **Model:** `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` (open Gemma 4, mixture of experts, about 4B active, accepts images), listed by `GET /v1beta/models` on 2026-10-11. `GOOGLE_MODEL` overrides it.
- **Thinking off:** Gemma 4 on this API thinks by default. With the default, the ladder took 21.7 s and used all 1,021 thought tokens with no answer. `thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel: "minimal"` answered in 1.4 s. `thinkingBudget` and the `"low"` level are refused with 400 for this model. Thought parts are dropped if any arrive.
- **Key handling:** the key goes in the `x-goog-api-key` header, never the URL, so it can't land in access logs. The system prompt leads the user turn (Gemma takes no separate system instruction here).
- **Refusals:** a provider that answers 401, 402 or 403 is skipped for 1 hour, so a blocked DigitalOcean costs one call, not one timeout per draft. A 5xx or timeout tries the next provider without marking it down.
- **One cap:** `CLOUD_DAILY_MAX_CALLS` (falls back to `DO_DAILY_MAX_CALLS`, default 60) counts calls across both providers per UTC day.
- **What goes:** unchanged from ADR-0022. A ladder sends the ask line (at most 80 characters, no place) and the minutes. A photo goes only when the hub is absent and the host tapped "Ask cloud Gemma" for that Flare. Same `enforce()` / `enforceLadder()` guards. Nothing stored or logged.
- **Tracing:** `cloudChat()` sets `gen_ai.provider.name` and `gen_ai.response.model` to whoever answered (ADR-0021 allow-list).
- **`/config`:** `cloud_ai.provider` is the first provider; `cloud_ai.providers` lists both.

## Data use on the free tier
Google's Gemini API terms (Unpaid Services, "How Google Uses Your Data", read 2026-10-11) say Google uses what it receives to improve its products, and human reviewers may read it after it is cut off from the account. That is fine for a ladder ask line and not obviously fine for a photo. So:
- the photo stays a per-Flare tap, never automatic;
- the note under the button says "Google may review it";
- the privacy page (`site.privacy.l.cloud`) and /ai/ (`ai.cloud.photo`) say so in plain words;
- turning on billing for the Google project moves it to Paid Services terms, where prompts are not used to improve products. That is the founder's call.

## Measured (live, 2026-10-11, this Mac to Google)
| Job | Before (default thinking) | After (`minimal`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ladder, "Fairlane walk at 11?", 60 min | 21.7 s, no answer | 1.4 s, 4 valid steps |
| Photo (a lake and red tree) | no answer at 200 tokens | 1.6 s, "Autumn views by the lake" |

Free-tier limits are shown per project in AI Studio, not on the public rate-limits page. Our cap of 60 calls a day is far below any published Gemma free limit.

## Tests
`apps/server/test/cloud.test.ts`: Google alone; DigitalOcean 402 → Google answers and DigitalOcean is skipped on the next call; a 5xx does not mark down; the photo goes as `inline_data`; thought parts dropped; the key is in a header, not the URL; one cap across providers.

## Consequences
- The cloud tier works today, without waiting on DigitalOcean billing.
- One more closed service sees ladder ask lines, and photos when the host taps. The privacy page names it.
- The DigitalOcean signature moment in the post stays [PENDING DO BILLING].
EOF

input.content:
# Fresh-eyes test, Sun 2026-10-11

A subagent with no project context used the live site (https://flare-outside.onrender.com) as a phone (390×844, touch) and once at 1280×800. It read no source or docs. It typed only the name "Test" and sent nothing. Score: **5/10** for "I'd understand and use this in under a minute". The idea was clear in about 10 s; the trust to send one took much longer.

Its first-5-seconds guess: "A free web app to get a few friends outside. Take a photo of where you are, send a link, it only happens if enough people say yes, then it deletes itself." That is right.

## Issues, worst first (status in the backlog, #13)

| # | Where | What it saw | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | App, Send it | Onboarding text, dots and "Skip" show through the compose sheet; "Skip" sits under the X | Unmount onboarding when done; solid stage behind compose |
| 2 | Demo | Toast "Amor said yes." right under "Nobody sees who." | Demo toasts say "Someone said yes" |
| 3 | Demo | Unclear who I am: I send, then "Fuego is waiting", "Find them" points at me; chips F A B | One clear role: "You sent it" and the friends as friends |
| 4 | Demo | Never shows the friend's side (I'm in, Add a condition) | A "What your friends get" step |
| 5 | App, start | "Try a demo" brown on near-black; "Got a link?" dark orange on black | Light outline and text, 4.5:1 |
| 6 | App, start | "Got a link?" only adds a line of text | Paste-link field, or plain text |
| 7 | Site, How it works step 1 | The photo print renders as a 25 px grey strip | Give the print a width; check the image |
| 8 | Demo | "0 more to light it" without "It's lit"; Ember place changes a second later; "outside 34 min" for a 15 min plan | Say "It's lit"; one place; minutes match the plan |
| 9 | Demo | No meetup moment; "Close" loops to the start; X goes to about:blank from a direct link | End with "Light a real one"; X goes to / with no history |
| 10 | App, draft | "Made on our laptop" reads as a privacy surprise; "no trackers" vs Sentry on the privacy page | Plain line about Gemma and not storing; "no ad trackers" |
| 11 | Everywhere | Jargon: Gemma (a person?), Kindling/Lit/Ember, Spark, crew, Hot spots, "2 in, 3 to go ahead" | Plainer copy; "2 of 3 needed" |
| 12 | Compose | Lone pencil for the place; empty box; hint looks pre-filled | Labelled "Where you'll meet" row |
| 13 | Camera | "Settings, then Safari" shown on Chrome | Browser-neutral line |
| 14 | Several | Faint text: "Only your crew sees it.", Skip pill on sky, disabled Save, text on drawings | 4.5:1 everywhere |
| 15 | Site, mobile | No nav links in the header | A row of links |
| 16 | Site | "Run it yourself" makes the hosted app sound optional; repo "goes live" line | "No install needed"; fix the code block wrap |
| 17 | Privacy, Accessibility | Dated placeholders ("after the field test on Sun Oct 11"); unlinked DEV post mention | Update or remove |
| 18 | /how/ | Repeats the landing | Real step-by-step with screens, or drop |
| 19 | App, desktop | Full-width Next button, text hugs the left | Phone-width column on desktop |
| 20 | Small | 5-word invite called six words; "Stop talking"; compass has no arrow; same icon for crew and Hot spots | Copy and icon fixes |

Tooling note: Playwright's normal `.click()` timed out on app and demo buttons (something keeps moving under them); touch taps worked.

## What worked
The headline and subtitle, the "Demo · nothing is sent" badge, the "Can't make it?" sheet, "it shrinks instead of dying", the privacy page's "Limits we're honest about", and asking for a first name only.

Screenshots: kept in the session scratchpad, not committed.

Milestone: the Gemini cloud tier is live (b9c81ee on Render), and the hub-off smoke passes every required check.

- What it does: DigitalOcean is tried first and still answers 402 (account blocked). A 401/402/403 skips DO for 1 h, then Google AI Studio answers with gemma-4-26b-a4b-it. One daily cap of 60 covers both.
- What fixed it: Gemma 4 on the Gemini API thinks by default. The ladder took 21.7 s and gave no answer. Setting `thinkingLevel: "minimal"` brings it to 1.4 s. `thinkingBudget` and `"low"` are refused for this model. Google gets one retry after a 5xx because "minimal" sometimes throws a fast 500.
- Live numbers (hub off): photo 2.9 s, "Sunset by the bench". Ladder 1.4 s, 4 valid steps. Three direct ladder probes took 1.5–1.9 s.
- Privacy point for the founder: Google's unpaid-tier terms ("How Google Uses Your Data") say Google may use what it receives to improve its products, and human reviewers may read it.
  - Ladders send only the ask line.
  - Photos still go only when the host taps, and the copy now says "Google may review it" (button note, /ai/, privacy page).
  - Turning on billing for the Google project would move it to paid terms. That's the founder's call; I changed nothing there.
- Copy is now provider-neutral: "Ask cloud Gemma", "Made by Gemma, cloud". Copy-lint finds 0 problems.
- Code and tests:
  - ADR-0026 written.
  - 218 server tests pass; the new ones cover the 402 fallback, the 1 h skip, the 5xx retry, the key sent in a header (never the URL), and dropping thought parts.
  - deploy-render now sends GEMINI_API_KEY and applies the env aliases.
- Hub restarted against live; it shows as connected.
- Fresh-eyes report is in: 5/10, 20 issues, in docs/research/fresh-eyes-2026-10-11.md. The worst five:
  1. Onboarding shows through the real Send screen.
  2. The demo toast "Amor said yes." sits right under "Nobody sees who".
  3. The demo blurs who you are (Fuego).
  4. The demo never shows the friend's side.
  5. "Try a demo" is nearly invisible on the start screen.
- Next, per your order: ElevenLabs. Since fresh-eyes #1 and #2 break trust on the live demo, I'd like to fix those two first (about 30 min). Unless you say otherwise, I'll do that and then start ElevenLabs.

input.message:
The fresh-eyes fixes are live (86d5b65), and the demo e2e passes against the live URL. Round 2 is running now with a brand-new subagent that has no context.

Top five, all done:
- #1 Onboarding showing behind Send: I couldn't reproduce it on the normal path. The likely trigger is coming back from the demo through the back/forward cache. Fix: onboarding now unmounts once the flow moves past the camera, and a page restored from bfcache reloads.
- #2 The demo shows "One more yes. 2 in." and never a name. The e2e checks that no "X said yes" text appears.
- #3 You are the host, shown by your onboarding first name. The compass points at the bench. The avatars show "You".
- #4 One beat as Amor, a friend, under a banner "You're Amor now, a friend." I'm in and Add a condition both work; then "Back to you".
- #5 "Try a demo" and "Got a link?" are now light on the dark sheet.

Also fixed:
- #6 "Got a link?" opens a paste field that accepts only this site's /g/ links.
- #7 The how-it-works print renders.
- #8 One bench name from the start, straight to lit, and "15 min" matches the plan.
- #9 "You made it" moment; an end screen with Light a Flare and Play again; X goes home when there is no history.
- #10/#11 Copy:
  - "An AI model, Gemma, writes a short invite"
  - "2 of 3 needed"
  - "How many people, counting you?"
  - "Photo not kept"
  - "no ad trackers"
  - Privacy p1 now says the photo goes once to our laptop.
  - "Made on our laptop" stays: it's a fixed P0 string (SRS-AI-4).
- #12 A labelled "Where you'll be" row with Edit.
- #13 Browser-neutral camera help.
- #15 Nav links on phones.
- #16 "No install needed" on the run page, and commands scroll instead of wrapping.
- #17 Dated placeholders now say what's true.
- #19 The desktop app stays phone-width.
- #20 Mute voice.

Still open: #18 (the how page repeats the landing) and parts of #14 and #20. I'll fix those locally but won't deploy until round 2 reports, so the tester sees a stable site.

Tests: e2e demo 8/8, kit a11y 0, pwa, field 27/27, loop, telegram and sparks all pass. Copy-lint shows 0 problems.

Founder flag: site.run.note still says the repo link goes live when it's public. That's true; making it public needs the founder's yes.

content.text:
Waiting for round 2 to report before the next deploy, so the tester sees a stable site.

Here's where things stand:

- **Gemini cloud tier: live and verified.** DigitalOcean still refuses (402, account blocked), so Google AI Studio's Gemma 4 answers. With the hub off on live, the photo draft took 2.9 s and the Plan draft 1.4 s.
  - The fix that made it work: Gemma 4 on Google's API "thinks" first by default and took 21.7 s with no answer. Setting thinking to its lowest level cut that to 1.4 s.
  - There's also one quick retry, because that setting sometimes returns a fast server error.
  - The design is recorded in ADR-0026.
- **One thing for you to decide:** Google's free-tier terms say it may use what it receives to improve its products, and staff may read it.
  - Plan drafts send only the ask line. Photos go only when the host taps, and the app, /ai/ and the privacy page now say "Google may review it".
  - Turning on billing for the Google project would move it to paid terms. I haven't touched that; the manager has queued it for you.
- **Fresh-eyes fixes, round 1: live (86d5b65).** The first tester scored 5/10. The demo test passes against the live site.
  - The demo now shows a count instead of who said yes.
  - You play the host, then one turn as a friend.
  - It has a meetup moment and a real ending.
  - I also fixed the start screen contrast, added a paste box for "Got a link?", and put nav links on phones.
- **One fix I couldn't confirm:** the bug where onboarding showed through the Send screen didn't reproduce on the normal path. I made onboarding close once you pass the camera, and the app now reloads when you come back to it through the browser's back button. Round 2 will show whether that's enough.
- **Committed, not deployed yet:**
  - The /how/ page is now a step-by-step tour using the six real demo screens. Lighthouse scores 100 on all five site pages, mobile and desktop.
  - A darker backing behind the "Sent a moment ago" status line.
  - These go out in the next deploy, after round 2.
- **Next:** round 2 is a new tester with no context, testing the live site. The manager's target is 8/10 or better. I'll fix what it reports, then start ElevenLabs.
- **Two small items still open:** the compass shows a flame instead of an arrow, and two menu items share an icon.
- **Waiting on you:** the run page still says the repo link "goes live when the repo is public". That's true, and making the repo public needs your yes.
