On a phone (390x844, touch, geolocation granted) I covered the home page, the full demo, and the real app up to the "Send it" screen. I never tapped Send it, never shared, never signed in. Then I did a short desktop pass at 1280x800. All screenshots are in <tmp>/904c52d9-f200-4552-8ce5-05e400952efa/scratchpad/fresh2/
  
  Click timeouts: every one came from my own selectors, not the site, and no tap() fallback was needed. Two causes. The 2/3/4 buttons are radios, so the hidden input sits over the visible "3". The Edit button's accessible name is "Edit where you'll be", not "Edit". "Save it" and "Continue" are correctly disabled while their fields are empty. Escape does not close the "Add a condition" sheet.
  
  ## 1. First 5 seconds on the home page (m01-home-fold.png)
  - **What I think it is:** an app for getting friends to meet up outside. You send a photo invite, and the plan only happens if enough people say yes.
  - **Who it's for:** friend groups who keep failing to make plans in group chat.
  - **What I'd do:** tap "Try a demo".
  - **What confused me:**
    - On the phone, a large phone mockup fills most of the first screen. The headline only starts around 600px down, and the two buttons are cut off at the bottom edge.
    - The mockup uses names I don't know ("From Fuego", "Access unknown here") before anything explains them.
    - "then deletes itself" made me wonder what gets deleted: the plan, the photo, or my data.
  
  ## 2. Issues, worst first
  
  1. **Two "where" fields on the Send screen, and they disagree** (real app, u01-send.png, u03-typed.png, u04-edit.png)
     - **What I saw:** a "Where are you?" text box ("e.g. the bench by the pond"). Below it, "Where you'll be: Not set yet" with an Edit button. After I typed "the bench by the pond" in the first box, the second still said "Not set yet". Tapping Edit opened a second empty box with no placeholder.
     - **Why it hurts:** this is the last screen before sending. I didn't know which box matters, or whether my plan would go out with no place.
     - **Fix:** keep one field. Or fill "Where you'll be" from "Where are you?" and say how the two differ (e.g. "Meet somewhere else? Edit").
  
  2. **The demo threw away the place I typed** (demo, d03-edit.png then e01.png)
     - **What I saw:** I entered "By the pond bench" and tapped Send it. The next screen said "You're waiting at Ford Woods Park, by the pond."
     - **Why it hurts:** it feels broken right away, and makes me distrust the real app.
     - **Fix:** use the typed text in the rest of the demo. Or lock that field in the demo and label it "sample".
  
  3. **The demo hands me a script with names I don't know** (e01.png, f01-amor.png)
     - **What I saw:** right after sending, the main button says "Be Amor". Then "You're Amor now, a friend", and the invite says "Fuego is at Ford Woods Park". Later "Benny" shows up on the final screen (j03.png). The condition placeholder says "only with Amor" while I am Amor (g01-condition.png).
     - **Why it hurts:** nobody has told me who Amor, Fuego or Benny are, so "Be Amor" means nothing.
     - **Fix:**
       - Change the button to "See what your friend gets" or "Switch to a friend's view (Amor)".
       - Show the sender as "You (Fuego)", or use my name.
       - Don't use the current role's name in the placeholder.
  
  4. **Adding a condition said yes for me and then never showed the condition** (g01-condition.png, g02-check0.png)
     - **What I saw:** I typed "only if back by 5 PM" and tapped "Check it". It went straight to "You're in." with nothing about my condition.
     - **Why it hurts:** "Check it" sounds like a preview, not a commitment. I couldn't tell whether the condition was saved.
     - **Fix:**
       - Rename the button to "I'm in, if this holds".
       - Show the condition on the "You're in" screen ("You're in if: back by 5 PM").
  
  5. **The numbers in the demo don't add up**
     - **What I saw:**
       - I picked 3 people. The "Ember" stage says "One friend is enough" (h04.png), yet the end screen says "3 of you are here" (j01-here.png).
       - The spot shows "Bench right here" next to "6 min walk" (h04.png). The compass then says 120 m (i02-find.png).
       - The flame card in the real app says "Need 1 more" before anything is sent, and no count has been picked yet (t02.png).
     - **Why it hurts:** the whole idea is "it goes ahead only if enough say yes", so the counts must be right.
     - **Fix:**
       - Use one set of demo values throughout.
       - Hide the "Need N more" card until a count is chosen.
       - Change "Bench right here" to "Bench at the spot".
  
  6. **The first screen fold is mostly mockup, and the buttons are cut off** (phone home, m01-home-fold.png)
     - **Why it hurts:** the headline and "Try a demo" are what a newcomer needs, and they are pushed to the bottom edge. On top of that, the sticky header takes about 108px of the 844px screen.
     - **Fix:**
       - On phones, put the headline and buttons above the mockup, or shrink the mockup.
       - Fit the nav links into one shorter row, or hide them behind a menu.
  
  7. **Strange or unexplained copy in the real app** (t01.png, t02.png)
     - **What I saw:**
       - "Made on our laptop · Photo not kept." Whose laptop?
       - "Writing six words…" produced five ("Meet by the calm water").
       - While loading, a faded "Use mine" button looks disabled and is unclear.
       - "Edit anything", but the headline doesn't look editable.
     - **Fix:**
       - "Written by an AI on the Flare team's computer. Your photo isn't stored."
       - "Writing a short invite…"
       - "Write my own" instead of "Use mine".
       - Make the headline look tappable, or drop "Edit anything".
  
  8. **The demo starts mid-flow** (d01.png)
     - **What I saw:** it opens on the Send screen with a ready-made photo and title. For about a second the picture is a dark navy block, which looks broken. Earlier home-page text had already called it a photo that "develops like a print".
     - **Why it hurts:** the demo skips the main hook (snap a photo, get AI words).
     - **Fix:** start the demo with a sample photo that develops and gets its words. Or show a one-line intro: "This is a pretend invite. Tap Send it."
  
  9. **"Read how a Flare works, step by step" shows the same text again** (/how/, w05-m-how.png)
     - **What I saw:** the /how/ page repeats the home sections almost word for word.
     - **Why it hurts:** the link promises more detail and gives none.
     - **Fix:** add real step-by-step screens to /how/, or remove the link.
  
  10. **Smaller items**
      - **Doubled input box:** text inputs show an inner box inside the outer border (d03-edit.png, u01-send.png). It looks like a rendering glitch.
      - **Lowercase sentence start:** the compass line begins "the bench by the willow is straight ahead" (i02-find.png).
      - **"Pocket it":** used twice for different things (dismiss after yes, dismiss after arrival). The meaning isn't obvious; "Done" or "Close" is clearer.
      - **Menu:** it opens with 10 items, including technical ones ("Phone check", "AI on this phone"), which is a lot for a first visit (t00-menu.png).
      - **No way back to the site:** the app has no link to the home page apart from the menu footer.
  
  ## 3. What worked
  - The headline "Get your friends outside." plus the one-line summary explains the idea fast.
  - The "It shrinks instead of dying" section (Kindling / Lit / Ember / Gone) is a clear, memorable idea with good icons (m03-home-scroll3.png).
  - The demo always shows "Demo · nothing is sent", and the end screen offers a clear "Light a Flare" / "Play again".
  - The demo can be finished start to end. "Skip 30 min" with "Not enough yet. Skip ahead to see it shrink" is a smart way to show the time-based stage (h03.png).
  - In the real app, the photo upload worked and the AI invite came back in about 3 seconds. When the camera was blocked, it fell back clearly to "Pick a photo" (s01.png).
  - "Can't make it?" gives a gentle confirm with an easy "I'm coming" undo (h05.png).
  - The end-of-walk card ("You were outside 15 min together" plus my one line) and "Phone away. Look up." are charming (j03.png, j04.png).
  - Desktop looks good: clear hero, the mockup sits beside the text, and the demo is centred in a phone-width column (w01-desk-home.png, w03-desk-demo.png).
  - There is no sideways scrolling on the phone. All site pages return 200, and an unknown page returns a proper 404.
  - The privacy and accessibility points are concrete and easy to read.
  
  ## 4. Score: 6/10
  I got the idea in under 10 seconds, but the role switching with unexplained names, the ignored place, the counts that don't match, and the two place fields before sending would leave a stranger unsure they did it right within a minute.

Fresh-eyes round 2 scored 6/10, up from 5. Everything it raised is fixed and live as 0842d28, and round 3 is now testing the live site with a new tester that has no context.

**What round 2 found, and what I changed:**
- **Two place fields on Send that disagreed:** there's now one. The "Where you'll be" row only shows when the map has already named the spot.
- **The demo dropped the place you typed:** it now keeps it.
- **Names nobody explained:**
  - The demo now opens with "A sample invite from you, {name}. Tap Send it."
  - The switch button is "Friend's view", and its banner says "Now you're Amor, a friend of {name}."
- **A condition was saved without telling you:** it now shows "You're in if: back by 5 PM".
- **Numbers that didn't match:** the bench is 40 m, the walk is 2 min, and the compass says 150 m. The "here" count and the faces now follow the real count.

- **Text boxes showed a box inside a box on photos:** now there's one box.
- **/how/:** on phones each step is a row, with a small screenshot beside its line.

**Checks:**
- **Lighthouse:** 100 on all five pages, mobile and desktop. /how/ dipped to 99 until I gave phones smaller images.
- **App JS budget (150 KB):** /app went over at 151.2 KB once the new copy was added. Onboarding and the Plan screens now load only when needed, which brings it to 149 KB.
- **Plan screen:** no automated test covers it, so I opened it by hand. It works.
- **Tests:** every e2e suite passes, and the unit tests pass. On the live site, the demo e2e and the smoke check both pass.

result.output:
<!--
  Talking compass (SRS-CMP-1..7). Feels like following a warm light:
  - the pointer is the brand pin-flame, turned toward your friend;
  - three distance rings pull in as you get closer (one ring per halving of distance);
  - facing within 15° lights the flame and its glow, with a tick (haptic or tone).
  bearing: degrees relative to where the phone points (0 = ahead).
  Motion (docs/design/motion.md 3.5): the needle follows on a spring; locking on lights
  the dot, sends one ring of light out and starts the breathing glow. Lock at < 15°,
  release at > 25°, so a shaky hand doesn't flicker it.
-->
<script lang="ts">
  import { t } from "#lib/copy/index.ts";
  import { onMount, untrack } from "svelte";
  import { FLAME, HOLE, ring as ringPath } from "../brand";
  import { feedback } from "#lib/motion/feedback.ts";
  import { speechDue, type Spoken } from "#lib/motion/speech.ts";
  import { unwrapAngle } from "#lib/compass/guide.ts";
  let {
    name = "Fuego",
    meters = 400,
    bearing = -18,
    status = "pointing",
    cues = false,
    speak = false,
    onfacing,
  }: {
    name?: string;
    meters?: number;
    bearing?: number;
    status?: "pointing" | "facing" | "near" | "no-orientation" | "no-gps";
    /** Play the facing tick (haptic, or a tone where there is no vibration) when it locks on. Off in static screens. */
    cues?: boolean;
    /** Speak the line with the SRS-CMP-2 cadence (speechSynthesis). */
    speak?: boolean;
    onfacing?: (on: boolean) => void;
  } = $props();

  const lockNow = (b: number, st: string, was: boolean) => st === "facing" || (st === "pointing" && Math.abs(b) < (was ? 25 : 15));
  let locked = $state(untrack(() => lockNow(bearing, status, false)));
  let pulse = $state(0);
  let mounted = false;
  let lastTick = -1e9;
  $effect(() => {
    const next = lockNow(bearing, status, untrack(() => locked));
    if (next === untrack(() => locked)) return;
    locked = next;
    if (!mounted) return;
    onfacing?.(next);
    if (next) {
      pulse += 1;
      const now = performance.now();
      if (cues && now - lastTick > 3000) { lastTick = now; feedback("facing"); }
    }
  });
  onMount(() => { mounted = true; });

  const facing = $derived(locked);
  // The needle turns the short way: 170° to -170° is a 20° turn, never a full spin.
  let shown = $state(untrack(() => bearing));
  $effect(() => {
    shown = unwrapAngle(untrack(() => shown), bearing);
  });
  const a = $derived(Math.abs(bearing));
  const dir = $derived(t(a < 15 ? "compass.dir.ahead" : a < 45 ? (bearing < 0 ? "compass.dir.slightLeft" : "compass.dir.slightRight") : a > 135 ? "compass.dir.behind" : bearing < 0 ? "compass.dir.left" : "compass.dir.right"));
  const km = $derived(meters >= 1000 ? (Math.round(meters / 100) / 10).toString() : "");
  const spoken = $derived(status === "no-gps" ? t("compass.noGps") : status === "near" ? t("compass.near", { name }) : status === "no-orientation" ? t("compass.spokenNoDir", { name, meters }) : km ? t("compass.spokenKm", { name, km, direction: dir }) : t("compass.spoken", { name, meters, direction: dir }));
  // Closeness 0 (far, 800 m+) to 1 (here). Rings tighten toward the flame.
  const close = $derived(Math.max(0, Math.min(1, 1 - Math.log2(Math.max(meters, 25) / 25) / 5)));
  const flameD = `${FLAME} ${ringPath(HOLE.cx, HOLE.cy, HOLE.r)}`;
  const line = $derived(facing && status !== "no-orientation" ? t("compass.ahead", { name }) : spoken);

  // Speech cadence (SRS-CMP-2): again when the bearing moves 30° or more, the distance halves, or 60 s pass.
  let said: Spoken | null = null;
  let clock = $state(0);
  $effect(() => {
    if (!speak) return;
    const id = setInterval(() => (clock = Date.now()), 5000);
    return () => clearInterval(id);
  });
  $effect(() => {
    void clock;
    const now: Spoken = { text: line, bearing, meters, at: Date.now() };
    if (!speak || typeof speechSynthesis === "undefined" || status === "no-gps") return;
    if (!speechDue(said, now)) return;
    said = now;
    speechSynthesis.cancel();
    speechSynthesis.speak(new SpeechSynthesisUtterance(now.text));
  });
</script>

<div class="compass" class:facing>
  <div class="dial" aria-hidden="true" style:--close={close}>
    <svg viewBox="0 0 240 240">
      {#each [0, 1, 2] as i}
        <circle class="ring" cx="120" cy="120" r={112 - i * 22 - close * 30} style:opacity={0.35 + i * 0.2} />
      {/each}
      <circle class="glow" cx="120" cy="120" r="70" />
      {#key pulse}{#if pulse}<circle class="lock" cx="120" cy="120" r="70" />{/if}{/key}
      {#if status === "pointing" || status === "facing"}

out=[];i=0
# walk text; at each "{" that opens a style rule (not @media), prefix selectors
res=''
pos=0
pat=re.compile(r'([^{}]+)\{')
def fix(sel):
  parts=[x.strip() for x in sel.split(',')]
  o=[]
  for x in parts:
    if not x: continue
    if x.startswith('@') or x.startswith('.site') or x.startswith('from') or x.startswith('to') or re.match(r'^\d+%$',x): o.append(x)
    else: o.append('.site '+x)
  return ', '.join(o)
depth_media=False
while True:
  m=pat.search(s,pos)
  if not m: res+=s[pos:]; break
  pre=s[pos:m.start(1)]
  sel=m.group(1)
  # strip leading comments/whitespace from the selector text
  lead=re.match(r'(\s*(?:/\*.*?\*/\s*)*)',sel,re.S).group(1)
  core=sel[len(lead):]
  if core.strip().startswith('@'):
    res+=pre+sel+'{'
  else:
    res+=pre+lead+fix(core.rstrip())+' {'
  pos=m.end()
open(p,'w').write(res)
EOF

cat > docs/architecture/adr/0027-elevenlabs-voice.md <<'EOF'
# ADR-0027: ElevenLabs for a warm compass voice and Voice Spark

Status: Accepted (Sun 2026-10-11).

## Context
Flare's compass talks so a friend who can't look at the screen (low vision, bright sun, hands busy) can still find the group (SRS-CMP-1). It used the phone's built-in voice, which on many phones sounds flat or robotic. The founder asked for ElevenLabs as the signature voice, with two limits: use it only to voice text Flare itself generates, plus an opt-in way for a person to say their own Spark. Never record group conversations: the people around you didn't agree to it, and Flare's promise is that it leaves nothing behind.

The ElevenLabs account is on the free tier: 10,000 characters a month (0 used when this was written), 3 custom voices, premade voices available.

## Decision

### 1. Warm voice for the compass: recorded once, shipped as files
- **What it says.** A fixed set of 54 short lines from the copy deck, recorded once by `scripts/gen-voice.ts` into `apps/web/static/voice/` with a manifest:
  - distances: 5 to 95 m in steps of 5, 100 to 950 m in steps of 50, and 1 to 5 km;
  - directions: slightly left/right, to your left/right, behind you;
  - other lines: "Straight ahead.", "You're close. Look around.", hold flat, no GPS, and figure 8.
- **No names.** The lines never include the friend's or the spot's name. A spoken compass line that includes a place name would have to send that name to ElevenLabs at run time. These clips leave that out, and the name stays on screen.
- **Cost and size.** 698 characters, once: 7% of a month's free allowance. 54 MP3 files at 64 kbps, 684 KB in all. A re-run keeps existing clips and spends nothing.
- **Opt-in on this phone.** My needs now has a Warm voice choice and a "Hear it" sample. Turning it on stores `flare.voice=warm` and saves every clip in the Cache API (`flare-voice-1`), so it works with no signal. Turning it off deletes that cache. The clips stay off the service-worker precache.
- **Playback.** `lib/compass/voice.ts`:
  - `clipsFor()` maps the compass state to one or two clips, for example `["m-150", "dir-slightLeft"]`.
  - `playWarm()` plays them in order from the cache.
  - The phone's own voice is the fallback when a clip is missing or audio can't play.
  - The player loads only on phones that turned the warm voice on, which keeps it inside the 150 KB JS budget.
  - The repeat rules stay the same (SRS-CMP-2).
- **Server.** `.mp3` is now served as `audio/mpeg`. The CSP is `media-src 'self' blob:`, because cached clips play as blob URLs.

### 2. Voice Spark: your own words, said instead of typed
- **When it's offered.** "Say it" appears on the Spark screen only when `/config` reports `voice.spark: true`, which needs `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` on the server, and only when the browser can record.
- **Recording.** One tap starts it and a second tap stops it. It stops by itself at 10 s and shows a countdown. Tapping suits more people than hold-to-talk. The microphone is released the moment recording stops.
- **What the server does.** `POST /api/v1/voice/spark` accepts audio types only, up to 400 KB. It sends the clip once to ElevenLabs Scribe (`scribe_v2`, English, no audio-event tags) and returns `{text}`, at most 140 characters. The buffer is zero-filled in a `finally` block. Nothing is stored or logged.
- **Failures and limits.** A 503 means the server has no key. `text: null` means Scribe failed, and the person types instead. The server caps transcriptions at `VOICE_SPARK_DAILY_MAX` a day (default 40).
- **After the words come back.** They land in the text field for the person to edit. The Spark is then sealed on the phone as before. The "no AI help" rule (BR-K-1 to K-3) still holds, because this only writes down the person's own words.

### 3. What we will not do
- Record anyone other than the person who tapped.
- Listen in the background, or record a gathering or a conversation.
- Send ElevenLabs a name, a place, an invite or anything sealed.

## Privacy
- The privacy page gains `site.privacy.l.voice`:
  - the compass voice ships with the app and sends nothing;
  - Say it sends up to 10 s of your own voice once, after you tap;
  - Flare keeps no audio;
  - ElevenLabs may keep it under its own terms.
- ElevenLabs is the one closed API in Flare's voice path. Its zero-retention mode is an enterprise feature, so we don't claim it.

## Measured (2026-10-11)
- **Clips.** Generating all 54 used 698 characters. Each clip is 1 to 2 s long; "You're close. Look around." is 1.5 s.
- **Scribe on our own clips.** It returned "You're close. Look around" in 492 ms and "150 meters" in 420 ms, both word for word (scribe_v2; scribe_v1 matched).

## Tests
- `apps/web/test/flow/voice.test.ts`: distance rounding, directions, facing, near, no heading and no GPS map to the right clips. Every clip the compass can ask for exists and matches the generator's buckets. No clip text holds anything but fixed words.
- `apps/server/test/voice.test.ts`: off without a key (503, and `/config` says false); Scribe gets the person's audio with the key in a header; non-audio is refused (415); over 400 KB is refused (413); a Scribe failure returns `text: null`; the daily cap holds.
- `apps/web/test/e2e/sparks.ts`: in Chrome, "Say it" records a real MediaRecorder clip from a synthetic microphone, sends `audio/webm` once, and the words land in the field to edit. Headless Chrome hangs on audio-only `getUserMedia`, so the test gives that page a tone as its microphone.

## Consequences
- The compass has a warm voice that works offline and costs nothing per use.
- A person can say their Spark. That sends their own voice to one closed service, only when they tap, and the privacy page says so.
- Adding a new compass line now means adding a deck key, adding a clip id in `gen-voice.ts` and `voice.ts`, and running `node scripts/gen-voice.ts`. The unit test catches a clip that is missing.
EOF

input.message:
Round 3 is fixed, the Plan e2e is in, and ElevenLabs is live as 8260be8. Smoke and the live demo e2e both pass.

Fresh-eyes round 3 scored 5/10. I've capped rounds at 3, as you asked.
- **Main cause:** site.css was global, and SvelteKit keeps it loaded after a client-side move from the website into /app/.
  - The site's .hero rule (a navy fill) covered your photo on Send.
  - The site's .art rule (230 px tall) squashed the onboarding photo.
  - Fix: every site.css rule is now scoped under .site. I checked by navigating site → demo and site → app.
- **Also fixed:**
  - Sheets: a close button on every sheet, and the menu stops 72 px short of the top so there's backdrop to tap.
  - Demo:
    - Conditions now go through the real parser, so nonsense gets "I didn't catch that", and the banner shows the read-back.
    - After the friend's view: "Back to you, {name}. One more yes: 2 in."
    - Benny's yes now shows before "It's lit".
  - Plan dates now stack on phones.
  - Honesty: the privacy page said the weather lookup happens only for Plans. It also happens when Home opens, and the line now says so.
- **Still open:** 8 issues, ranked, in docs/research/fresh-eyes-2026-10-11.md. Round 4 runs after the feature work.

**Plan e2e (new, npm run e2e:plan), 12/12 passing.** It runs Home → P1, which now loads on demand → P2 → send. Amor answers "step 3 or smaller" through the read-back, and Kai says yes. At the deadline the plan solves at step 3 and lights for both phones. Then Amor fades once.
- **Real bug it found:** on a phone with no saved first name, Send on P2 silently did nothing. P2 now asks for the name, as H3 does.

**ElevenLabs (ADR-0027)**
- **Warm compass voice:** 54 fixed lines (distances, directions, close, hold flat, no GPS), recorded once by scripts/gen-voice.ts with the premade voice Sarah.
  - Cost: 698 of the free 10,000 characters, and 684 KB in total.
  - Privacy: no names or places, so nothing of anyone's reaches ElevenLabs.
  - Opt-in under My needs, with a "Hear it" sample. When it's on, the clips are cached on the phone so it works offline. The phone's own voice is the fallback.
- **Voice Spark:** "Say it" on the Spark screen.
  - You tap, and it records up to 10 s of your own voice. Scribe v2 turns that into words for you to edit.
  - The audio is zero-filled and never stored. The server has a daily cap.
  - Live probe: 0.72 s, word for word.
  - The privacy page and NOTICE are updated. I don't claim zero retention, because ElevenLabs offers that on enterprise plans only.
  - Never other people, never conversations.
- **Not built:** reading the invite aloud in the warm voice. It would mean sending sealed text out of the phone, so I left it out on purpose.

**Tests:** all pass.
- Unit: 674/62/26. The new tests cover the clip mapping and that every clip shipped; the server voice tests cover off without a key, 415, 413, null on failure, and the cap.
- e2e: sparks now includes Say it, using a synthetic mic because headless Chrome hangs on audio-only getUserMedia. demo, plan, loop, telegram, field 27/27, pwa and kit a11y 0 all pass.
- Lighthouse is 100 on all five pages. JS budget: /g/ 149 KB and /app 149.5 KB, because the Plan screens and Say it now load on demand.

**Next:** the website feature cards and the "Built with" strip.

content.text:
The fresh-eyes round 3 fixes, the Plan e2e and ElevenLabs are all live as 8260be8. The smoke check and the demo test against the live site both pass.

**Round 3 (5/10, the last round per the manager's pacing):**
- **Main bug:** the website's styles were global, and they stay loaded when you tap from the website into the app. Two of the site's rules hit the app's own screens: one put a navy block over your photo on Send, the other squashed the onboarding photo. Every website style is now limited to website pages.
- **Also fixed:**
  - Sheets have a close button, and the menu leaves room to tap outside it.
  - In the demo, conditions go through the real parser, and it says "Back to you" after the friend's view.
  - The Plan date fields stack on phones.
  - The privacy page said the weather lookup happens only for Plans. It also happens when Home opens, and it now says so.
- **Still open:** 8 smaller issues, ranked, in `docs/research/fresh-eyes-2026-10-11.md`. Round 4 runs after the feature work.

**Plan e2e (`npm run e2e:plan`, 12/12):** it covers creating a plan, a condition, the deadline solve and a fade. It found a real bug: on a phone with no saved first name, sending a Plan silently did nothing. The Plan screen now asks for the name, the same way the Send screen does.

**ElevenLabs:**
- **Warm compass voice:** 54 fixed lines (distances, directions, "You're close"), recorded once and shipped with the app.
  - Cost: 698 of the free 10,000 characters a month, once.
  - Privacy: no names or places, so nothing of yours reaches ElevenLabs.
  - It's opt-in under My needs, with a "Hear it" sample, and works offline once turned on. The phone's own voice is the fallback.
- **Voice Spark:** a "Say it" button on the Spark screen.
  - You tap, and it records up to 10 seconds of your own voice. Scribe turns that into words for you to edit.
  - Flare keeps no audio. On the live site it came back word for word in 0.72 s.
  - It never records other people or conversations.
- **Not built:** reading the invite aloud in the warm voice. That would send encrypted invite text off the phone, so I left it out on purpose.
- **Docs:** the privacy page, the NOTICE credit and ADR-0027 are updated. The privacy page doesn't claim ElevenLabs deletes recordings, because that guarantee is only on its enterprise plans.

**Checks:** all unit tests and e2e suites pass, Lighthouse is 100 on all five site pages, and both app pages are under the 150 KB JS budget (149 KB and 149.5 KB).

Next up are the website feature cards and the "Built with" strip. Still yours to decide: Google billing, DigitalOcean billing, and making the repo public.

cd "<project>/flare" && cat > docs/architecture/adr/0028-voice-flares.md <<'EOF'
# ADR-0028: Voice Flares, the invite from what the host says, on our laptop

Status: Accepted (Sun 2026-10-11).

## Context
A Flare starts with a photo, and Gemma 4 on the hub writes the invite and the place line from it. Some people can't take a useful photo: people who are blind or have low vision, or who are in the dark or have their hands full. The backlog asked for Voice Flares (#9): say it, and Gemma 4 writes the invite.

## What we checked
- **Ollama reports audio.** For `gemma4:e4b-it-q4_K_M`, Ollama 0.40.2 lists the capabilities `completion, vision, audio, tools, thinking` (`/api/show`).
- **Audio goes in `images`.** The model hears audio passed base64 in a message's `images` field. A field named `audio` is ignored.
- **Transcription works.** One of our own warm-voice clips came back as "You're close. Look around." in 2 s.
- **The voice prompt works.** Voice prompt v1, given a `say` recording of "I'm at the pond in Ford Woods Park. Come sit on the bench with me, the light is really nice.", answered `{"invite": "Meet at the pond bench.", "alt": "The pond in Fordwoods Park has nice light to sit on the bench."}` in 3.7 s. A second sentence ("Walk to the cider mill after work? I'm by the big oak at Fairlane Green.") took 3.5 s.

## Decision
- **Phone.** The camera screen has "Say it instead".
  - One tap starts recording and a second tap stops it. It stops by itself at 10 s.
  - The phone converts the clip to 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV (`lib/voice/flare.ts`) and sends it once to `POST /api/v1/drafts/voice`.
  - Nothing is kept on the phone, and the microphone is released at once.
  - The control loads only when the camera screen shows (JS budget).
- **Server.** WAV only (RIFF....WAVE), at most 400 KB.
  - It relays the audio to the hub as a `voice-draft` job (asyncapi `voiceJob`: a header, then one binary frame) with an 8 s budget, like the ladder.
  - It runs `enforce()` again on the answer.
  - The buffer is zero-filled on every path, and nothing is stored or logged.
  - The words heard never come back, only `{invite, alt, tier}`.
  - It counts `tier_ran.voice.{tier}`.
- **No cloud tier.** A voice is more personal than a photo, so it stays on the open model on our own laptop. If the hub is absent, slow or hears no place, the response is `tier: rules`. The phone then says "Didn't catch a place. Take a photo or try again."
- **Hub.** The frame must start with RIFF, or the result is `bad_audio` and the model is never called. The hub uses voice prompt v1 (`packages/shared/src/prompts/voice.ts`): only places and things the person said, no names, faces or bodies, and an empty answer when no place is heard. It runs `enforce()` and makes no retry: at temperature 0 a retry gives the same answer. The audio is zero-filled after the job.
- **Send.** With no photo, Send shows the invite over the outdoor scenery and asks for the place if the map didn't name one.

## Tests
- `apps/hub/test/voice.test.ts`:
  - audio in, a guarded draft out, with the voice prompt and the audio passed as media;
  - an empty answer is `unusable_answer`;
  - a frame that isn't WAV is `bad_audio` and never reaches the model.
- `apps/server/test/contract.test.ts` (`draftFromVoice`): the template when no hub is connected, 400 for a file that isn't WAV, 413, and 415.
- `apps/web/test/e2e/voice-flare.ts` runs on the real stack on this Mac: real server, real hub, real Gemma 4.
  - The `say` fixture plays in as the microphone. A real MediaRecorder records it and the phone converts it to WAV (167 KB).
  - "Meet at the pond bench" comes back in 3.3 s, and Send shows it over the scenery with no photo.

## Consequences
- A person who can't take a photo can still send a Flare by speaking for 10 seconds, and their voice goes only to our own laptop.
- Asyncapi gains `voiceJob` and `voiceBytes`, and the result error enum gains `bad_audio`. A hub on the old code ignores the job, and the server falls back to the template after 8 s.
EOF

input.command:
cd "<project>/flare" && cat > docs/architecture/adr/0029-crew-atlas.md <<'EOF'
# ADR-0029: Crew Atlas, your crew's places drawn on the phone

Status: Accepted (Sun 2026-10-11).

## Context
The backlog (#9) asked for a Crew Atlas: the crew's outings, Sparks and Hot spots as a private map of its places, with facts that come only from data. The crew's places live in the sealed Hot spots blob, which only members' phones can open. Each entry has the place key (an OSM id from the map pack), the name, how many times the crew met there and the last day, and no coordinates.

## Decision
- **Drawing.** The Atlas is drawn on the phone (`lib/components/CrewAtlas.svelte`) at the top of the Crew space, when the crew has places.
  - **Positions** come from the map pack already on the phone: `place_key` → `items[3]` → lat and lon. Typed places with no OSM id are listed but not drawn.
  - **Context** comes from the same pack: water, woods, parks, streets and benches inside the box, at most 1,200 points.
  - **Nothing is fetched for it.** There are no map tiles and no requests, so where the crew meets never leaves the phone. The only network use is the pack file, which the app already loads.
- **Facts only from data.** "Met once · Oct 11" or "Met 3 times · last Oct 4", from the blob's count and last day. Dot size grows with the count, at 6 + 3·log2(count) px.
- **No AI caption.** The backlog imagined Gemma writing the Atlas. Gemma runs on the hub, so a written caption would mean sending the crew's decrypted places off the phone, which breaks the Hot spots promise (BR-K-6). The facts read just as well from templates, so we left the model out.
- **Accessibility.** The SVG is `role="img"` with a label ("Map of 3 places your crew met"), and the list of facts underneath carries the same information as text.
- **Budget.** The component and the map module load on demand from the Crew page.

## Tests
`apps/web/test/e2e/sparks.ts` runs on the real stack. It creates a real Hot spot: a Flare lights, a friend arrives, and the host ends it. The Crew page then shows the Atlas with "West Road · Met once · Oct 11" (`docs/frontend/evidence/e2e-crew-atlas.png`).

## Consequences
- The crew gets a map of where it goes outside, private by construction.
- When a crew uses more than one map pack, the Atlas draws the places found in the pack named by `area`, which is Fairlane by default.
EOF

input.message:
Milestone: the website feature cards, JS headroom, Voice Flares and the Crew Atlas are all done and pushed. The last deploy is building now.

**Website feature cards and "Built with" (#14)**
- Ten cards, one per feature that exists today. Each has a 240x360 WebP of the real screen (4 to 10 KB) and one line. A single "Try a demo" sits at the end.
- Unbuilt features get no card, so automations aren't there yet.
- "Built with" lists Gemma 4, Google AI Studio, DigitalOcean ("paused for now"), ElevenLabs, Sentry, Mastra, OSM, Render and SvelteKit, each with what it does in Flare. These are plain links; nothing is fetched from those sites.
- Lighthouse dipped to 99 on mobile home. The hero screenshot had become the LCP, and Chrome's wide lazy margin let 10 card images compete with it. Fixed with a 300 w hero at high priority and card images that load within 400 px of view. All 5 pages are back at 100, mobile and desktop.
- Side fix: the demo's shrink beat no longer flashes "0 more to light it".

**JS headroom**
- The deck shipped all 900 strings to every page. 197 website-only strings (5.9 KB gzipped) now ship with the website only, via deck.json?site.
- /app went from 150.3 to 145.7 KB, and /g/ from 149.7 to 144.9 KB.
- The next big win is zod → zod/mini: zod alone is 22.7 KB gzipped in the app. That touches about 70 schema lines shared with the server, so I've queued it rather than risk it today.

**Voice Flares (ADR-0028)**
- The open model handles it, on our laptop. Ollama 0.40.2 reports audio for gemma4:e4b, and the model hears WAV passed in the `images` field.
- On the camera screen, "Say it instead" records up to 10 s, converts it on the phone to 16 kHz WAV, and sends it to POST /api/v1/drafts/voice. The server passes it to the hub as a new voice-draft job (asyncapi voiceJob). Voice prompt v1 asks for the same {invite, alt} a photo gets, and enforce() runs on both sides.
- It is hub-only: there is no cloud tier for voices. The audio is zero-filled, and the words heard never come back.
- Live, through Render to this Mac's hub: "Meet at the pond bench" in 3.6 s.
- The real-stack e2e (npm run e2e:voice) passes. It plays a macOS `say` fixture into the microphone, then runs a real MediaRecorder recording, the phone's WAV conversion, the server, the hub and Gemma.
- Hub and contract tests are added, and the privacy page has a new line.
- The live hub is restarted on the new code.

**Crew Atlas (ADR-0029)**
- Hot spots have OSM ids, so the phone's own map pack places them on an SVG map, with water, woods, streets and benches for context.
- No tiles and no requests, so the crew's places never leave the phone.
- It shows facts only, such as "Met once · Oct 11", with dot size by count.
- There's no Gemma caption on purpose: it would mean sending decrypted places to the hub.
- The sparks e2e on the real stack shows the Atlas. It loads on demand.

**Tests:** unit tests are 678/62/26. e2e (plan, voice, sparks, demo, loop, telegram, field, pwa) passes, and kit a11y has 0 violations.

**Next:** automations, then Sentry depth, the page audit, fresh-eyes round 4, media and the post.

# ADR-0030: Automations, what runs by itself and what doesn't

Status: Accepted (Sun 2026-10-11).

The backlog (#7) asked for automation with guardrails: opt-in, rate-limited, an off switch and no tracking. Here is what runs by itself, what was added today, and what we left out and why.

| Automation | Status | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plan auto-solve at the deadline | Already there | The engine's `plan_deadline` job; the server sweeps every 60 s and at boot (ADR-0005) |
| Fade check, "still coming?" | Already there | `still_coming` push when a Plan gets smaller (BR-P-6) |
| Locked Plan saved for offline use | Already there | PWA outbox and saved view (`savedAt`) |
| **Reminder 30 min before a Plan starts** | **New** | When a Plan lights more than 30 min before its start, the engine schedules `plan_reminder` at start − 30 min. The timer pushes `plan_soon` to the people going: "{step} starts at {time}. Time to head out." The text is built on the phone from the sealed notice, so the server sees only the event name. The job is unscheduled when the Plan ends. Migration 0005 allows the new job kind |
| **Weather-aware Ember** | **New** | When Home's 2-hour forecast says rain is likely, the host's phone puts covered seats first in the Ember list. A seat counts as covered if it is tagged `covered=yes` or `shelter=yes`, or is within 25 m of a mapped shelter. The engine picks the first seat everyone passed, and that seat's name reads "the bench by the willow, under cover", so friends see why. All on the phone; the server never learns the weather or the spot |
| **Tell the chat** | **New** | On the host's Lit screen, one tap opens the share sheet (or copies) with "It is lit. Meet us at {spot}." and the same link as the invite. A place only, never who |
| Golden-hour nudge (a push) | Not built | Home already shows "Golden hour in 47 min" with one tap to Light a Flare. A push at golden hour would need the server to know where each crew is, which it never does (ADR-0001). A local notification at a set time isn't available to web apps without push |
| Weekly recap (a push or Telegram post) | Not built | The Crew space already shows this week's minutes outside from the counters (ADR-0024). A pushed recap needs a weekly job per crew at a sensible local hour, and the server doesn't know a crew's time zone. Left for after the challenge |

## Guardrails
- **Nothing tracks anyone.**
  - The reminder goes only to the people in the Plan's set.
  - The covered-seat ordering happens on the host's phone.
  - Tell the chat sends nothing until the host shares it.
- **Rate.**
  - One reminder per Plan.
  - Tell the chat is a tap.
  - The Ember ordering changes nothing when the forecast is dry.

## Tests
- `packages/engine/test/plan.test.ts`:
  - lighting at the deadline schedules `plan_reminder` at start − 30 min, and the timer pushes `plan_soon` to the set;
  - no reminder when the Plan lights less than 30 min before it starts;
  - a stale reminder after the Plan is gone does nothing.
- `apps/web/test/flow/covered.test.ts`: a `covered=yes` tag or a shelter within 25 m counts as covered; an open bench doesn't.
- `apps/server/test/db.test.ts`: migration 0005 applies once and is idempotent.
- `e2e:plan` and `e2e:field` still pass.
EOF

## Amendment (Sun 2026-10-11): route performance and server errors
- **Route performance.** A sampled share of API requests (`FLARE_HTTP_SAMPLE`, default 0.2) becomes one `http.server` transaction each.
  - Name: the method and the API area only, for example `PUT:gatherings`.
  - Attributes: `flare.route` (the same token), `flare.status` (`2xx`, `4xx` or `5xx`) and `flare.ok`.
  - Never sent: the path, ids, the query, headers or bodies. `routeToken()` builds the name from the first path segment after `/api/v1/`.
- **Server errors.** An unhandled error (not an `ApiError`) is captured with its class and a fingerprint of class plus route token. `scrubEvent()` still drops the message, request, user, tags, breadcrumbs and frame variables.
- **The Mastra agent** was already traced (ADR-0025):
  - the run is `invoke_agent flare-ladder` with `flare.agent`;
  - each tool is `execute_tool <name>` (sunset, weather_window, nearby_places, step_templates, enforce_ladder, keep_asked);
  - model calls are `chat <model>` with the provider that answered.
- **Tests.** `apps/server/test/tracing.test.ts` adds a run with sampling at 1 against a route that throws a TypeError whose message holds a marker phrase and a UUID. The envelope has `GET:health`, `GET:boom`, `TypeError` and `flare.status`, and contains neither the marker, `/api/v1` nor the UUID.
EOF

13	## What I Built
14	
15	[FIELD: one or two sentences in a tester's own words about the problem, quoted with their OK. Example shape: "We all say 'we should hang out' in the chat, and then nobody goes."]
16	
17	Flare is a web app for a small group of friends, 2 to 12 people. The host takes a photo of where they are. An open model on our laptop looks at it and writes a six-word invite, like "Bench by the pond, sun out." Friends get a link and say yes **in private**, with conditions if they want: "after 2", "only if Amor comes", "back by 5", "10 minutes' walk at most". Nobody sees who said yes, only the count.
18	
19	It lights only when enough people can actually come. If not enough can, it shrinks to a smaller plan instead of failing (a bench closer by, a shorter walk). When it lights, everyone gets the spot and a compass that points to it. Then the screen gets out of the way.
20	
21	A few more things it does:
22	
23	- **Works with Telegram or plain links.** In a Telegram group the bot posts a Flare card and counts taps; in iMessage, WhatsApp or SMS it's just a link. There's a plain-text form for friends with no data.
24	- **Sparks and Hot spots.** After a meetup, people leave a one-line memory. The next invite from the same spot says "Your group met here once." and shows it.
25	- **Bench to Bench.** A walking loop that never goes too far between seats, read back first ("40 min, a bench every 200 m, under trees") and printed as a large-print card.
26	- **Fix the map.** When a bench or fountain is missing from OpenStreetMap, the model drafts the tags from a photo, a person checks every one, and the app exports a note. It never posts to OSM itself.
27	- **It forgets.** Every Flare, its photo and every yes are deleted within 5 minutes of ending. Worst case measured: 90 s ([spike E2](https://github.com/Hotragn/flare/blob/main/docs/engineering/03-spikes.md)).
28	
29	Who it's for: friends who mean to meet up and don't, including a friend with low vision (VoiceOver, large text), a friend who can't walk far (seat-to-seat routes, step-free checks), and a friend with a weak signal (it queues and sends later).

54	
55	## How I Built It
56	
57	### The model: Gemma 4 E4B on a laptop, not in the cloud
58	
59	The photo goes to a Mac running **Gemma 4 E4B** (`gemma4:e4b-it-q4_K_M`, 7.5B parameters, 6.58 GB) on **Ollama**. The Mac dials out to our server over a WebSocket, so nothing on it is exposed to the internet. The photo is held in memory and zero-filled after the call; it's never written to disk on either end.
60	
61	Why that model: I measured the options before picking one ([model selection](https://github.com/Hotragn/flare/blob/main/docs/ml/model-selection.md)):
62	
63	| Model | Where | Result | Shipped? |
64	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
65	| Gemma 4 E4B, Q4_K_M | Ollama on the Mac | 20/20 valid JSON, 39/40 scenes right, 3.0 s median | Yes |
66	| Gemma 4 E2B, ONNX q4f16 | Chrome, WebGPU | 20/20 JSON, 2.3 s, but scenes 29/40, and it invents water and sunsets | No: needs a 1.17 GB GPU buffer; iPhone Safari caps buffers at 1 GiB |
67	| SmolVLM-500M | Chrome and Safari | Scenes 16/40, 6/20 misleading | No |
68	| Qwen3-0.6B (for conditions) | Safari | 26/40 | No: rules got 40/40 in under 1 ms, and the model hung Safari |
69	
70	**The model picks the words; code owns the facts.** Every answer goes through `enforce()` before anyone sees it: six words or fewer, no names of people, no invented places. If the model is slow (over 6 s for a photo) or its answer fails the check, the app shows typed words instead. Nobody waits on the AI.
71	
72	The same model drafts Plan "ladders" (a big plan and three smaller versions, 12/12 valid, p95 6.5 s) and Fix the map tags (11 photos in the eval; 0 tags off the allow-list after the guard).
73	
74	### What doesn't use a model, on purpose
75	
76	Conditions ("after 2, only with Amor") are parsed on the phone by rules: 40/40 on the core test set, 15/20 on the hard set, under 1 ms, and the words never leave the phone. The only thing sent to the server is the rule, like `{"type": "after", "at": "…T18:00:00Z"}`, never the words. Bench to Bench requests are parsed the same way (16/16 plain requests).
77	
78	### Privacy, built in
79	
80	- The group key lives in the link's `#fragment`, which browsers never send to servers. Names, places, photos and Sparks are sealed on the phone (AES-256-GCM) before upload. The server sees counts and opaque labels like `c3` or `step:2`.
81	- Telegram groups are the one disclosed exception: the bot needs readable text to post. By default it posts a Flare card, not the photo. A group can turn on real photos, and the setting says plainly that Telegram keeps a copy until the post is deleted.
82	
83	### Stack
84	
85	SvelteKit 5 (installable PWA, works offline), Hono on Node 24, Postgres, an outbound WebSocket relay to the Mac, Web Push, a Telegram bot, OpenStreetMap packs for places and loops. [FIELD: Render web service and Render Postgres, if deployed there.]
86	
87	### How it was built
88	
89	I ran it like a small software company, one role at a time: research, product, requirements, brand, design, architecture, engineering lead, then nine specialists building in parallel against frozen interfaces, then integration and QA. Every role left a handoff in the repo. The test suite is over 650 tests plus 7 end-to-end suites on the real server and engine.
90	
91	**Disclosure:** I built this with Claude Code. A separate "manager" Claude session, acting as the CTO for me, sent many of the prompts in the build sessions: it relayed my decisions and set the order of work. Product and privacy decisions were mine; the manager session asked before anything public.
92	
93	## What I got wrong
94	
95	- **The Telegram path didn't exist in the app until the morning of the test.** The server side was built and tested, but no screen on the phone connected a group to Telegram. I found it while building the Telegram card, about four hours before the field test, and built the missing screen with a real-server test.
96	- **Sparks never reached Hot spots.** Three bugs together: the Hot spots record was never written, "met here" was always empty, and the record fired three times. The field-path coverage check caught all three (BUG-058 to 060).
97	- **"Short one only" asked for the long one.** The button sent `min_step` instead of `max_step` (BUG-057).
98	- **A dead Wi-Fi link looked alive forever.** A half-open socket kept the hub "connected" and every photo waited out the full 6 s. Fixed with a heartbeat; measured recovery on a real half-open link: 16.1 s (BUG-030, BUG-031).
99	- **The website scored 61 on mobile.** WebGL flames ran in software. CSS flames got it to the high 90s; deferring hydration until after the first paint and a 10 KB grain texture got it to 100.
100	- **Bench to Bench finds no loop at our own test spot.** The benches at Ford Woods are mapped too close together. The app says "No loop keeps benches that close. Try 400 m?" instead of inventing one. [FIELD: did we fix the map there?]
101	- **The tag drafter makes things up on empty photos.** On 4 of 6 photos with nothing to tag (a playground, a skate park), it drafted a shelter. The app throws away the model's guess of what the thing is, and a person still checks every tag.
102	- [FIELD: anything that broke on the iPhones]
103	
104	## What I didn't do
105	
106	- **No model on the phone.** Gemma 4 E2B runs in Chrome on a Mac, but not inside iPhone Safari's memory limits. Measured, not shipped.
107	- **No cloud model by default.** A DigitalOcean fallback exists for when the laptop is off, but photos go there only if the host opts in for that Flare.
108	- **Not tested on Android.** All four test phones were iPhones.
109	- **Not a native app.** It's a web app you add to the Home Screen.
110	- **Fix the map is slow.** The slowest tag drafts take 13.8 s, over the 8 s budget, in the eval with full-size photos. Not fixed yet.
111	- [FIELD: anything we cut on the day]
112	
113	## Why Does Open Innovation Matter?
114	
115	For this app, open weights are the whole design, not a preference.
116	
117	- **The photo never leaves our hands.** It's a picture of exactly where someone is standing, right now. With an open model on our own laptop, it goes there in memory and is gone after the call. With a closed API, it would be on someone else's servers under someone else's retention policy.
118	- **It costs nothing per photo.** [FIELD: number of photos drafted during the test] drafts on the laptop cost $0. That matters for a free app with no business model.
119	- **We could measure it, and we could pick the size.** I ran five open models side by side on the same 20 photos and chose by measured results. I could see exactly why the small one failed on an iPhone (a 1.17 GB buffer). With a closed model I'd get an answer and no way to look inside.
120	- **Open data too.** Places, benches and walking paths come from OpenStreetMap. When the map is wrong, Fix the map gives back a reviewed note instead of just taking.
121	
122	Where open beat closed for us: privacy of location photos, zero cost per use, and being able to check the work. Where it didn't: speed. A large hosted model would be faster than a laptop on a busy afternoon.
123	
124	## My Agent Session
125	
126	[FIELD: Entire session links for the key build sessions, scrubbed of emails before publishing (scripts/scan-sessions.ts --public found 100 to remove)]

128	## Prize Categories

130	- **Gemma:** Gemma 4 E4B runs locally on Ollama for photo invites, Plan ladders and map tags, chosen against Gemma 4 E2B and three other open models on the same test set, with code checking every answer ([eval results](https://github.com/Hotragn/flare/blob/main/docs/ml/eval-results.md)).
131	- **Entire:** [FIELD: one line, with the session links above]
132	- **Sentry Agent Tracing:** [FIELD: one line plus a trace screenshot from the deployed server: hub vs fallback tiers, latency]

A DEV staff member said in the launch post comments that people may submit by their own local time (comment 3ghbj, by heyitsjem). The rules make the sponsor's clock official. For us in ET, 06:59 UTC is later than local midnight anyway, so plan to the UTC time.

### Template sections, in order

1. Opening line: "This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass" (with the challenge link)
2. What I Built (what it does, how it gets people outside, who it's for)
3. Demo (deployed link or video)
4. Code (GitHub embed)
5. How I Built It (which open-source AI, and how the project is built around it)
6. Why Does Open Innovation Matter?
7. My Agent Session (optional)
8. Prize Categories (list each one, or remove)

Front matter tags in the template: `devchallenge, hf26challenge`.

### Category rules that matter to our stack

From the hub page:

- **Gemma ($200):** use Gemma, run it locally, fine-tune it, or serve it through Google Cloud or another provider.
- **Render ($200):** use Render as the AI runtime, host an agent's front end, or run Hermes or OpenClaw.
- **MongoDB Atlas ($100):** Atlas as the data layer, Atlas Vector Search for retrieval, agent memory, or the database behind an app on an open-weight model.
- **Entire ($100):** share the agent sessions behind the project in the write-up, or search past agent work to explain why code exists.
- **ElevenLabs ($100):** give an open-source agent a voice, transcribe audio for a local model, or narrate the demo.
- **Sentry Agent Tracing ($100):** show setup, latency, tokens, cost, what you found and how you debugged it, with traces or screenshots.

Every entry is judged for every category it qualifies for. Partner credits (Render, Tinker, Backboard, ElevenLabs) are claimed at hacktoberfest.com/my/promos.

| Temporal | [PaidYet](https://dev.to/prateek11rai/paidyet-for-the-friend-who-says-kal-bhej-dunga-p5l) | Not read (503). The listing says it is a Telegram bot with local Gemma and Temporal reminders. |

Traits shared by the winners, ranked by how often they appear:

1. A named person and their problem in their own words, near the top.
2. A frank "what went wrong" section with concrete bugs.
3. Measured numbers, usually in a table.
4. An open-model argument tied to that person (privacy, cost, offline), not a generic one.
5. One specific line per claimed partner category.
6. Code-enforced guardrails: the model picks the words, code owns the facts.

---
title: "Flare: snap where you are, and it only lights if enough friends quietly say yes"
published: false
tags: devchallenge, hf26challenge, gemma, opensource
---

<!-- DRAFT for the founder's review. [FIELD: ...] marks what only the founder can fill:
     a quote, the video, image uploads, Entire links, a Sentry screenshot, the repo going public.
     [PENDING DO BILLING] marks the DigitalOcean claim, held until billing is fixed.
     Every number here is measured; the proof is named next to it. Remove this comment
     before publishing. -->

*This is a submission for the [Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass](https://dev.to/challenges/hf26).*

## What I Built

[FIELD: one or two sentences in the founder's own words about the problem. Shape: "My friends and I say 'we should go for a walk' in the group chat every week, and then nobody goes."]

Flare is a free web app for a small group of friends. You take a photo of where you are. Gemma 4, an open model running on our own laptop, looks at it and writes a short invite ("Meet by the quiet water's edge"). Your friends get a link and tap **I'm in**, in private. Everyone sees the count, never who.

It goes ahead only if enough people can actually come. If not enough say yes within 30 minutes, it doesn't fail: it shrinks to a smaller plan, such as 15 minutes at a bench nearby. When it lights, everyone gets the spot and a compass that talks them there. Afterwards it says how long you were outside together, and then it deletes itself.

It's for friends who mean to meet up and don't. That includes the friend with low vision (the compass talks, buzzes and has a warm recorded voice, and you can *say* a Flare instead of photographing one), the friend who can't walk far (benches, step-free checks, loops from bench to bench), and the friend with a weak signal (it queues and sends later).

## Demo

- **Try it with no setup:** [flare-outside.onrender.com/app/demo/](https://flare-outside.onrender.com/app/demo/). Three demo friends run on a demo clock, and nothing is sent. You send a Flare, become your friend Amor for one tap, skip 30 minutes to watch it shrink, then follow the compass. The demo runs the real rules engine in your browser.
- **The live app:** [flare-outside.onrender.com/app/](https://flare-outside.onrender.com/app/). The site is [flare-outside.onrender.com](https://flare-outside.onrender.com/) and scores Lighthouse 100 in all four categories, mobile and desktop, on all five pages.
- **Video:** [FIELD: 60 to 90 s screen recording, docs/post/shot-list.md]

[FIELD: upload these from docs/post/media/ and replace the paths]

![The photo, with the invite Gemma 4 wrote from it](docs/post/media/01-host-words.jpg)
![The friend's invite: the count, never names](docs/post/media/02-friend-invite.jpg)
![It's lit](docs/post/media/03-friend-lit.jpg)
![Too few in 30 minutes: it shrinks to a smaller plan](docs/post/media/06-friend-ember.jpg)
![A Voice Flare: Gemma 4 heard "I'm at the pond in Ford Woods Park, come sit on the bench with me"](docs/post/media/08-voice-flare-send.png)
![The Crew Atlas, drawn on the phone](docs/post/media/09-crew-atlas.png)

### How I tested it

I haven't run a group meetup with it yet, so I won't claim one. [FIELD: replace this line if a real outing happens before posting.] Here is what was tested:

| What | How | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The whole loop on the real stack | Chrome at iPhone size against the real server, the real Gemma 4 hub on this Mac, the engine and Postgres | 10 end-to-end suites pass, including the field run (27/27), Plans, Voice Flares, Sparks, Telegram and offline |
| Two real iPhones | A device-check page on an iPhone 16 Pro Max and an iPhone 13, for the compass, haptics and sound | Found 3 bugs, all fixed (below) |
| A simulated Saturday | 48 made-up friends in 4 groups play Flares and Plans against the real server ([GIF](docs/post/media/sim/fairlane-sim-42.gif), labelled Simulation) | 11 of 12 lit (91.7%); median time to Lit 14.75 min for Flares; 1 of 2 Embers saved a plan; all 12 gatherings deleted afterwards, and the deletion audit passes |
| Strangers | 4 rounds of a "fresh eyes" tester with no context using the live site | Scores 5, 6, 5, [FIELD: round 4]/10. Every round's issues were fixed and redeployed |
| Accessibility | axe on 22 pages × 2 widths × light and dark | 0 findings, and every target at least 44 px |

## Code

{% github Hotragn/flare %}

[FIELD: the repo is private until the founder makes it public.] AGPL-3.0. The README has a 3-step quick start (server, hub, phone), and `docs/README.md` indexes the rest: 30 architecture decision records, the requirements and the evals.

## How I Built It

### One open model with three senses: Gemma 4 E4B on a laptop

The phone sends the photo to a Mac running **Gemma 4 E4B** (`gemma4:e4b-it-q4_K_M`) on **Ollama**. The Mac dials out to the server over a WebSocket, so nothing on it is open to the internet. The photo stays in memory and is zero-filled after the call.

Gemma 4 does three jobs in Flare:

| Sense | Job | Measured |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vision | Photo → a short invite and a one-line scene for friends who can't see the photo | 20/20 valid JSON, 39/40 scenes right, 3.0 s median |
| Audio | **Voice Flare:** you say where you are and what you want to do, and the invite is written from that | "Meet at the pond bench" in 3.3 to 3.7 s, from audio alone |
| Text | Plan "ladders": a big plan and three smaller versions | 13 asks, p95 5.1 s; Fix the map tags, 0 off the allow-list |

The audio part surprised me. Ollama 0.40.2 reports `audio` as a capability for this model, and it hears WAV passed in the same `images` field a photo uses. A field named `audio` is ignored. The phone records up to 10 s and converts it to 16 kHz mono WAV, and the hub writes the same `{invite, alt}` a photo would get. The voice never leaves our laptop and is never stored. The words it heard aren't sent back, only the invite.

I picked the model by measuring the options on the same test set:

| Model | Where | Result | Shipped? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gemma 4 E4B, Q4_K_M | Ollama on the Mac | 20/20 JSON, 39/40 scenes, 3.0 s | Yes |
| Gemma 4 E2B, ONNX q4f16 | Chrome, WebGPU | 2.3 s, but 29/40 scenes; it invents water and sunsets | No: it needs a 1.17 GB GPU buffer, and iPhone Safari caps buffers at 1 GiB |
| SmolVLM-500M | Chrome and Safari | 16/40 scenes, 6/20 misleading | No |
| Qwen3-0.6B (for conditions) | Safari | 26/40 | No: the rules got 40/40 in under 1 ms, and the model hung Safari |

**The model picks the words; code owns the facts.** Every answer goes through `enforce()` before anyone sees it: six words or fewer, no names, no invented places. If the model is slow or the answer fails the check, the app shows typed words instead. Nobody waits on the AI.

### When the laptop is off: Gemma 4 in the cloud

Our laptop isn't always on, so the server has a cloud tier: Gemma 4 26B A4B on **Google AI Studio**. Plan drafts use it when the hub is away. A photo goes there only if the host taps "Ask cloud Gemma" for that one Flare, and the note under the button says Google's free tier may review it.

One finding saved this tier. Gemma 4 on that API thinks before it answers by default. A Plan draft took 21.7 s and spent all 1,021 thought tokens without answering. With `thinkingLevel: "minimal"` it answers in 1.4 s, and a photo in 1.6 s.

**DigitalOcean** Serverless Inference is wired in as the first cloud provider, with Gemma 4 31B: a Plan draft took 20.9 s and a photo 27.2 s in the probe. A provider that refuses (401/402/403) is skipped for an hour. [PENDING DO BILLING: our account is blocked for billing, so Google answers today; the fallback is tested.]

### An agent that never lets a plan die: Mastra

The Plan ladder can be drafted by a **Mastra** agent with four local tools: sunset time, a weather window for the plan's hours, nearby places from the map pack, and step templates. Measured on 13 asks against the current route: p95 5.1 s vs 5.5 s, and the weather tool matched the plan's window 7/7. The agent adds a median of 12 ms. It ships behind a switch (`LADDER_AGENT=1`), and whatever the agent says still goes through the same guard.

### A measured failure, and what fine-tuning taught the rules: Tinker

Conditions like "after 2, only if Amor comes, back by 5" are parsed **on the phone by rules**, so the words never leave it. The rules missed new phrasings: 15/40 on a fresh hard set. I fine-tuned a Qwen3.5-4B LoRA on **Tinker** (3,000 synthetic examples, rank 32, about $2.40). It read 38/40.

I couldn't ship it. It runs on Tinker's servers, and conditions must stay on the phone. So I used its errors to teach the rules new phrasing families. On a blind set written *before* the rules changed, the rules went from 20/40 to 30/40, still under 1 ms with no network. The LoRA's 38/40 shows the gap that's left.

### A warm voice that sends nothing: ElevenLabs

The compass talks: "150 meters, slightly left." The phone's own voice can sound flat, so the compass can use a warm voice instead.

A live voice would have had to send the spot's name to a cloud service. So I recorded 54 fixed lines once with **ElevenLabs** (distances, directions, "You're close. Look around."). That cost 698 characters of the free 10,000, and the clips ship with the app as 684 KB of MP3. No names and no places are in them, they work offline, and the phone's own voice is the fallback. Scribe read the clips back word for word in 420 to 492 ms.

**Voice Spark:** after a meetup you can *say* your one-line memory instead of typing it. Up to 10 s of your own voice goes once to ElevenLabs Scribe, the words come back for you to edit, and no audio is kept (live: 0.72 s). Flare never records anyone else or a conversation.

### Debugging without seeing anyone's words: Sentry

**Sentry Agent Tracing** covers the AI path on the server:
- every job (`invoke_agent flare-photo`, `flare-voice`, `flare-ladder`);
- every model call (`chat gemma4:e4b`, with the provider that actually answered: hub, Google or DigitalOcean);
- every guard and agent tool (`execute_tool enforce`, `nearby_places`, `weather_window`).

The same tracing also covers sampled route performance and server errors.

The design rule is an allow-list. Only tier, model, timing, ok and error class leave the server. Route names are tokens like `PUT:gatherings`, never paths, and error messages are dropped. A test runs the real routes with marker phrases and UUIDs in the inputs, captures every envelope, and fails if any of them shows up.

[FIELD: one trace screenshot from the live project, showing a Plan draft where the hub was away and `gen_ai.provider.name` says google, with its latency.]

### Privacy, built in

- **The group key lives in the link's `#fragment`,** which browsers never send to servers. Names, places, photos and Sparks are sealed on the phone (AES-256-GCM). The server sees counts and labels like `c3`.
- **The Crew Atlas is drawn on the phone.** It's a map of where your crew meets, made from the sealed Hot spots and the map pack already on the phone. No map tiles and no requests. I didn't let Gemma write a caption for it, because that would mean sending the decrypted places to our laptop.
- **Within 5 minutes of the end, the Flare, its photo and every yes are deleted.** The worst case measured was 90 s.

### Stack and process

- **Stack:** SvelteKit (an installable PWA that works offline), Hono on Node 24, Postgres on Render, the WebSocket relay to the Mac, Web Push, a Telegram bot, and OpenStreetMap packs. The JS budget is 150 KB gzipped per page, and the app is at 146.
- **Process:** I ran it like a small software company, one role at a time: research, product, requirements, design, architecture, then specialists building against frozen interfaces, then QA. Each role left a handoff in the repo. There are 769 unit and contract tests and 10 end-to-end suites.

**Disclosure:** I built this with Claude Code. A separate "manager" Claude session, acting as CTO for me, sent many of the prompts: it relayed my decisions and set the order of work. Product and privacy decisions were mine, and anything public waited for my yes.

## What I got wrong

- **The website's styles leaked into the app.** On a phone, your photo on the Send screen sat under a navy block, and the onboarding photo was squashed to 230 px. The cause: SvelteKit keeps the website's CSS after you tap from the website into the app, and its `.hero` and `.art` rules hit the app's own. A tester with no context found it. Every website rule is now scoped.
- **The demo broke its own promise.** It said "Nobody sees who" and, right under that, "Amor said yes." It now says "One more yes. 2 in."
- **A Plan with no saved first name did nothing.** You tapped Send and nothing happened. The new Plan end-to-end test found it; the screen now asks for the name.
- **The compass said "close" 49 times** on a real iPhone 16 Pro Max walk. It now waits for a margin before it says "close" again, and only repeats when the distance halves.
- **The compass froze on an exact 180° turn.** The smoothing averaged the two directions to nothing. It's fixed with shortest-arc smoothing and a replay test.
- **The device check read 0 compass events a second on an iPhone 13.** A second Start tap had attached a second counter.
- **Gemma's thinking ate the cloud budget** (21.7 s, no answer) until I turned it to minimal.
- **Sparks never reached Hot spots.** Three bugs: the record was never written, "met here" was always empty, and it fired three times.
- **"Short one only" asked for the long one.** A `min_step` should have been `max_step`.

## What I didn't do

- **No model on the phone.** Gemma 4 E2B runs in Chrome on a Mac, but not inside iPhone Safari's memory limit. Measured, not shipped.
- **No golden-hour push, no weekly recap push.** Home shows "Golden hour in 47 min", and the crew page shows this week's time outside. A push would need the server to know where a crew is and what time zone it's in, and it never knows either.
- **The invite isn't read in the warm voice.** That would send the sealed invite text off the phone.
- **Not tested on Android,** and not a native app: it's a web app you add to the Home Screen.

## Why Does Open Innovation Matter?

For this app, open weights are the design, not a preference.

- **A photo of where you're standing, or your voice saying it, is about as personal as data gets.** With an open model on our own laptop, it goes there in memory and is gone after the call. With a closed API, it would sit on someone else's servers under their retention rules. The one closed service in Flare, ElevenLabs Scribe, gets your voice only when you tap "Say it", and the privacy page says so.
- **It costs nothing per photo.** A free app with no business model can't pay per call. The laptop costs $0 per draft, and the cloud fallback runs on a free tier with a daily cap.
- **I could measure it and pick the size.** I ran five open models on the same photos and chose by results. I could see exactly why the small one failed on an iPhone (a 1.17 GB buffer). I could fine-tune one in 6 minutes for $2.40 to learn what the rules were missing.
- **Open data too.** Benches, restrooms and paths come from OpenStreetMap. When the map is wrong, Fix the map drafts a reviewed note to give back.

Where open beat closed for us: privacy, cost, and being able to check the work. Where it didn't: speed on a busy laptop, which is why there's a cloud fallback.

## My Agent Session

[FIELD: Entire checkpoint links for the key build sessions, made public after the scrub (scripts/scan-sessions.ts --public). Suggested: the Voice Flare session (Gemma hearing audio for the first time) and the round-3 fresh-eyes fix (finding the CSS leak).]

## Prize Categories

- **Gemma:** Gemma 4 E4B sees (photo to invite), hears (Voice Flare: 3.3 s from audio to invite on our laptop) and writes (Plan ladders), chosen against four other open models on one test set, with code checking every answer. Gemma 4 26B A4B is the cloud fallback.
- **ElevenLabs:** 54 compass lines recorded once (698 characters) so the compass's warm voice sends nothing, and Scribe turns a person's own 10-second Spark into words with no audio kept.
- **Sentry Agent Tracing:** every AI job, model call and guard traced, plus route performance and server errors, under an allow-list a test proves. [FIELD: trace screenshot]
- **Mastra:** a Plan agent with four local tools: p95 5.1 s vs 5.5 s for the old route, and weather matched 7/7, behind a switch.
- **Tinker:** a measured failure (15/40), a $2.40 LoRA that read 38/40, and the rules it taught: 20/40 to 30/40 on a blind set, on the phone.
- **Entire:** [FIELD: one line with the session links above]
- **DigitalOcean:** [PENDING DO BILLING]

[FIELD: thanks, with permission, to anyone who tried it]

*This is a submission for the [Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass](https://dev.to/challenges/hacktoberfest-week1-2026-10-05).*

## What I Built

It's 4 PM on a Saturday. Someone in the group chat writes "we should go for a walk". Three people react with a thumbs up. Nobody goes.

Flare starts there. You take a photo of where you are. Gemma 4, an open model on our own laptop, writes the invite: "Meet by the quiet water's edge". Your friends get a link and tap **I'm in**, in private. Everyone sees the count, never who. It goes ahead only if enough people can come. If not enough say yes in 30 minutes, it shrinks to a smaller plan, such as 15 minutes at a bench nearby, instead of dying.

Now picture the friend with low vision. Gemma has already turned the photo into a line they can hear: "A calm lake with tall grass and red autumn trees." When it lights, the compass talks them in: "150 meters, slightly left." It buzzes and sounds a tone when they face the right way. If a photo isn't possible, they *say* where they are, and Gemma writes the invite from their voice.

[FIELD: the founder's quote. Suggested: "My friends and I say 'let's go outside' every weekend and then scroll past it. I wanted the yes to be private, and the plan to get smaller instead of dying."]

Afterwards it says how long you were outside together, and then it deletes itself.

### At a glance

| What happens | The open piece doing it | Proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A photo becomes the invite and a line to hear | Gemma 4 E4B on Ollama, on our laptop | [39/40 scenes, 3.0 s](#gemma-4-sees-hears-and-writes) |
| You say it instead, and Gemma writes it | Gemma 4 E4B hearing audio | [3.3 s, no audio kept](#gemma-4-sees-hears-and-writes) |
| A plan that gets smaller instead of failing | The rules engine, plus a Mastra agent for Plan steps | [11 of 12 lit in a 48-friend simulation](#how-i-tested-it) |
| A compass with a warm voice | ElevenLabs clips recorded once, offline | [698 characters, nothing sent](#a-voice-that-sends-nothing-elevenlabs) |
| Everything about the meetup deleted | Postgres cascade and an audit route | [within 5 min; worst case 90 s](#privacy-built-in) |
