## How I Built It

### Gemma 4 sees, hears and writes

The phone sends the photo to a Mac running **Gemma 4 E4B** (`gemma4:e4b-it-q4_K_M`) on **Ollama**. The Mac dials out to the server over a WebSocket, so nothing on it is open to the internet. The photo stays in memory and is zero-filled after the call.

| Sense | Job | Measured |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vision | Photo → a short invite, plus a scene line for friends who can't see it | 20/20 valid JSON, 39/40 scenes right, 3.0 s median |
| Audio | **Voice Flare:** you say where you are, and it writes the invite | "Meet at the pond bench" in 3.3 to 3.7 s |
| Text | Plan "ladders": a big plan and three smaller versions | 13/13 valid, p95 5.5 s |

The audio part surprised me. Ollama 0.40.2 lists `audio` for this model, and it hears 16 kHz WAV passed in the same `images` field a photo uses. A field named `audio` is ignored. The phone records up to 10 s, and the hub writes the same `{invite, alt}` a photo gets. The voice never leaves our laptop, and the words heard aren't sent back.

I picked the model by measuring the options on one test set:

| Model | Where | Result | Shipped? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gemma 4 E4B, Q4_K_M | Ollama on the Mac | 20/20 JSON, 39/40 scenes, 3.0 s | Yes |
| Gemma 4 E2B, ONNX q4f16 | Chrome, WebGPU | 2.3 s, but 29/40 scenes; it invents water and sunsets | No: it needs a 1.17 GB GPU buffer, and iPhone Safari caps buffers at 1 GiB |
| SmolVLM-500M | Chrome and Safari | 16/40 scenes, 6/20 misleading | No |
| Qwen3-0.6B (for conditions) | Safari | 26/40 | No: rules got 40/40 in under 1 ms |

**The model picks the words; code owns the facts.** Every answer passes `enforce()` before anyone sees it: six words at most, no names, no invented places. If the model is slow or the answer fails the check, the app shows typed words. Nobody waits on the AI.

### When the laptop is off: Google AI Studio and DigitalOcean

When our laptop is off, the server falls back to Gemma 4 in the cloud. Plan drafts use it automatically. A photo goes only if the host taps "Ask cloud Gemma" for that Flare, and the note under the button says Google's free tier may review it.

**Google AI Studio** serves Gemma 4 26B A4B. One finding saved it: by default Gemma 4 thinks first on that API. A Plan draft took 21.7 s and spent all 1,021 thought tokens without answering. With `thinkingLevel: "minimal"` it answers in 1.4 s, and a photo takes 1.6 s.

**DigitalOcean** Serverless Inference is wired in as the first provider, with Gemma 4 31B. In the probe a Plan draft took 20.9 s and a photo 27.2 s. A provider that refuses is skipped for an hour, so the fallback costs one call, not a timeout per draft. [PENDING DO BILLING: the account is blocked for billing today, so Google answers; the fallback is tested.]

### An agent with local tools: Mastra

A **Mastra** agent can draft the Plan ladder with four local tools: sunset time, a weather window for the plan's hours, nearby places from the map pack, and step templates. On 13 asks it had a p95 of 5.1 s against 5.5 s for the old route, the weather tool matched the window 7/7, and the agent itself added 12 ms. It ships behind a switch, and its answer goes through the same guard.

### A fine-tune that taught the rules: Tinker

Conditions like "after 2, only if Amor comes, back by 5" are parsed **on the phone by rules**, so the words never leave it. The rules missed new phrasings: 15/40 on a fresh hard set.

I fine-tuned a Qwen3.5-4B LoRA on **Tinker**: 3,000 synthetic examples, rank 32, 6 minutes, about $2.40. It read 38/40. It runs on Tinker's servers, though, and conditions must stay on the phone. So I used its errors to teach the rules new phrasings. On a blind set written before the rules changed, they went from 20/40 to 30/40, still under 1 ms with no network.

### A voice that sends nothing: ElevenLabs

The compass talks, and the phone's own voice can sound flat. A live voice would have had to send the spot's name to a cloud service. So I recorded 54 fixed lines once with **ElevenLabs**: distances, directions, and "You're close. Look around." That cost 698 characters of the free 10,000, and the lines ship with the app as 684 KB of MP3. They hold no names or places and work offline, and the phone's own voice is the fallback.

**Voice Spark:** after a meetup you can say your one-line memory. Up to 10 s of your own voice goes once to ElevenLabs Scribe, and the words come back for you to edit (0.72 s live). No audio is kept. Flare never records anyone else or a conversation.

### Debugging without anyone's words: Sentry

**Sentry Agent Tracing** follows the AI path. It traces:
- each job: `invoke_agent flare-photo`, `flare-voice` and `flare-ladder`;
- each model call: `chat gemma4:e4b`, with the provider that answered (hub, Google or DigitalOcean);
- each guard and agent tool: `enforce`, `nearby_places` and `weather_window`.

It also samples route performance and catches server errors.

Only an allow-list leaves the server: tier, model, timing, ok and error class. Route names are tokens like `PUT:gatherings`, never paths, and error messages are dropped. A test runs the real routes with marker phrases and UUIDs in the inputs, and fails if any of them reach an envelope.

[FIELD: a trace from the live project: a Plan draft with the hub away, `gen_ai.provider.name: google`, and its latency.]

### Privacy, built in

- The group key lives in the link's `#fragment`, which browsers never send to servers. Names, places, photos and Sparks are sealed on the phone with AES-256-GCM. The server sees counts and labels like `c3`.
- The **Crew Atlas**, a map of where your crew meets, is drawn on the phone from the sealed Hot spots and the local map pack. It loads no tiles and makes no requests. I left out a Gemma caption, because it would mean sending decrypted places to the laptop.
- Within 5 minutes of the end, the Flare, its photo and every yes are deleted. The worst case measured was 90 s.

**Stack:** SvelteKit (a PWA that works offline), Hono on Node 24, Postgres on Render, the WebSocket relay to the Mac, Web Push, a Telegram bot and OpenStreetMap packs. The JS budget is 150 KB gzipped per page; the app is at 146.

**Process:** I ran it like a small company, one role at a time: research, product, requirements, design, architecture, specialists building against frozen interfaces, then QA. Each role left a handoff in the repo. There are 769 unit and contract tests.

**Disclosure:** I built this with Claude Code. A separate "manager" Claude session, acting as CTO for me, sent many of the prompts and set the order of work. Product and privacy decisions were mine, and anything public waited for my yes.

## What I got wrong

- **The website's styles leaked into the app.** On phones, your photo on the Send screen sat under a navy block. SvelteKit keeps the website's CSS after you tap into the app, and its `.hero` rule hit the app's `.hero`. A tester with no context found it, and every website rule is now scoped.
- **The demo broke its own promise.** It said "Nobody sees who" right above "Amor said yes." Now it says "One more yes. 2 in."
- **A Plan with no saved name did nothing.** You tapped Send and nothing happened. A new end-to-end test found it.
- **The compass said "close" 49 times** on an iPhone 16 Pro Max walk. It now holds a margin and repeats only when the distance halves.
- **The compass froze on an exact 180° turn.** The two directions averaged to nothing. It's fixed with shortest-arc smoothing.
- **Gemma's thinking ate the cloud budget** (21.7 s, no answer) until I set it to minimal.
- **Sparks never reached Hot spots.** Three bugs: the record was never written, "met here" was always empty, and it fired three times.

## What I didn't do

- **No model on the phone.** Gemma 4 E2B runs in Chrome on a Mac but not inside iPhone Safari's memory limit.
- **No golden-hour or weekly-recap push.** Home shows golden hour, and the Crew page shows the week. A push would need the server to know where a crew is and its time zone, and it never knows either.
- **The invite isn't read in the warm voice.** That would send sealed text off the phone.
- **No Android testing, no native app.** It's a web app you add to the Home Screen.

## Why Does Open Innovation Matter?

- **A photo of where you stand, or your voice saying it, is about as personal as data gets.** On an open model on our own laptop, it lives in memory and is gone after the call. The one closed service in the voice path, ElevenLabs Scribe, hears you only when you tap "Say it", and the privacy page says so.
- **It costs nothing per photo.** A free app can't pay per call. The laptop costs $0 per draft, and the cloud fallback is capped daily.
- **I could look inside.** I ran five open models on the same photos and picked by results. I could see exactly why the small one failed on an iPhone: a 1.17 GB buffer. I fine-tuned one in 6 minutes to learn what my rules were missing.
- **Open data too.** Benches, restrooms and paths come from OpenStreetMap, and Fix the map drafts a reviewed note to give back.

Open lost on one thing: speed on a busy laptop. That's what the cloud fallback is for.

  - **What I think it is:** a free web app for getting friends outside. You snap a photo of where you are, friends say yes in private, and the plan only goes ahead if enough people can come. The headline and the one-line description make this clear right away.
  - **Who it's for:** friends who keep failing to make plans in a group chat.
  - **What I'd do:** tap "Try a demo". It is the filled orange button and the obvious first choice.

    - The phone picture in the hero is labelled "From Fuego", and I couldn't tell if Fuego is a person or a feature.
    - The page is very long (02-home-full.png is about 16,000 px tall at phone width), and in the "How it works" section "Need 1 more. / 2 of 3 needed" sits between steps with no clear tie to either one.

     - **Why it hurts:** the most important idea, the host's view versus the friend's view, gets muddled, and you lose track of whose screen you are on.
     - **Fix:** show a role banner every time the role changes ("You're Fuego again, the host"). Keep a small "Playing as: Fuego (host)" or "Amor (friend)" chip next to "Demo · nothing is sent". Label the final avatars "Fuego (you)" and "Amor".

"Smaller plan: 15 min at the bench by the willow" appears with three buttons ("Find them", "I'm here", "Can't make it") and no hint which to tap or why the plan shrank.
     - **Fix:** add one coach line for each later step, for example "Not enough said yes, so it shrank to a short bench stop. Tap Find them."
  
  5. **The compass screen mixes up "your friend" and "the place".**
     - **Where:** 14b-find-them-later.png.
     - **What I saw:** The title is "Find them". The main text says "The bench by the willow is straight ahead". The footer says "Finds your friend. Not for navigation…". The distance stayed at 150 m the whole time.
     - **Why it hurts:** I can't tell if it points to a person or a bench, and saying it is "not for navigation" sounds odd on a screen whose job is to point the way.
     - **Fix:** pick one target and use it everywhere ("Amor is at the bench by the willow, 150 m, straight ahead"). Reword the disclaimer to "A rough pointer. Not for emergencies."

     - **"Access unknown here":** this is jargon. Fix: "No info on benches or restrooms here".
     - **"Test is waiting at West Road.":** this refers to me in the third person, on my own screen. Fix: "You'll wait at West Road (friends see: Test is waiting…)".
  
  7. **The suggested spot and the actual spot don't match.**
     - **Where:** 20-app-start.png vs 26-photo-1.png and 27-send-screen.png.

     - **Where:** 01-home-fold.png.
     - **What I saw:** The nav lists four items in a row ("How it works / Privacy / Accessibility / Run it"), and "Run it" is meant for developers.
     - **Fix:** move "Run it" to the footer, or rename it "Host your own".

The intro could offer the demo sooner. My first tap failed only because I expected "Light a Flare" there; that was my selector, not the site.

  - **Pitch:** the headline and the one-line description explain the idea in seconds. The hero art is warm, and nothing scrolls sideways at phone width.
  - **Demo labelling:** "Demo · nothing is sent" is shown on every demo screen, which is reassuring. The demo flows end to end with no dead ends, and it finishes on a clear "That's Flare. Try it with your friends." with "Light a Flare" and "Play again" (19-demo-closed.png). From there "Light a Flare" goes straight to the real app.
  - **Conditions:** I typed "back by 5, 10 min walk at most" in my own words. It came back as two clear chips and "Got it: … Right?", with "Yes, I'm in" and "Fix it". This felt clever and trustworthy.
  - **The yes count:** "3 more to light it / Nobody sees who" with the ring and dots is clear.
  - **The shrinking plan:** this idea comes through well in the demo.
  - **Real app:**
    - **No-camera fallback:** when the camera was off, it offered "Pick a photo" and "Say it instead" without fuss.
    - **Invite writing:** the AI invite took about 3 seconds, the photo appeared as a nice print, and "Write my own" is always available.
    - **Defaults and context:** the people count defaults to 2, and the start screen shows weather and golden-hour timing, which is a good touch.

Round 5 and the pre-review pass are done. I'm holding for the founder.

**Round 5: 6/10.** The first run was cut off by the usage limit, so I reran it with a new tester. Final scores across five rounds: 5, 6, 5, 6, 6. The post and REVIEW.md state these honestly, including that round 5's fixes shipped after its score.

Round 5's fixes are live as 75ed2a7:
- The demo shows "You: Fuego, the host" or "You: Amor, a friend" on every step.
- New coach lines for the second half: "Not enough said yes, so it shrank. Tap Find them." and "It points to the bench. Tap I'm here when you arrive."
- In the demo, "Back to you" and "Next" replace "Pocket it".
- Copy changes: "Use this", "No bench or restroom info here", "Host your own" in the nav, and the home example now names a third friend ("only if Sam comes").

input.command:
cd "<project>/flare" && cat > docs/architecture/adr/0031-remember-this.md <<'EOF'
# ADR-0031: Remember this, a conversation note made only with everyone's consent

Status: Accepted (Sun 2026-10-11, founder decision). Replaces ADR-0027's "never record a conversation" with the rule below.

## The rule
- **Per Flare or Plan, off by default.** The host turns it on (`PUT /remember {on}`), and it is never on for a crew all the time. Turning it off clears every consent and any recording.
- **Each person agrees on their own phone,** separately from I'm in (`PUT /remember/consent {ok}`).
  - If anyone who said yes doesn't agree, it's off for everyone.
  - If someone joins later without agreeing, it's off for everyone.
  - The screen says "Recording is off for this Flare." and never who. That's the same rule as the yes count.
  - The rule is one pure function, `rememberState()` in `apps/server/src/core/remember.ts`. It returns flags only: `on`, `ready`, `recording`, `recording_until`.
- **Recording.** When it's lit and everyone agreed, anyone can tap Record. It records up to 60 s on that phone, after the line "Only your group. Stop if others are close." Every phone in the group shows a recording sign, live (SSE event `remember`). Anyone can stop it for everyone, and a no stops it at once.
- **The words.** ElevenLabs Scribe v2, `diarize=true`, turns the audio into lines labelled Speaker 1, Speaker 2 and so on, with no names. The audio is zero-filled right after the call and none is kept. ElevenLabs may keep it under its own terms, and the privacy page says so.
- **The note.** The lines go back to the recording phone, which seals them with the Flare key (aad `r:{gathering}`). The server stores only that sealed blob, so it never holds the words in plain text.
- **The summary.** Gemma on the hub writes one line: summary prompt v1, `enforceSummary()` on the hub and on the server (3 to 16 words, no speaker labels, no long numbers or links). With the hub off there's no summary, and the words never go to a cloud model.
- **Where it shows.** The note shows in the Remember this sheet while the gathering is live. It is deleted at Gone with everything else: both tables cascade with the gathering, and the deletion audit checks them as DS12.
- **Never** listens in the background, and never records without the host turning it on and everyone agreeing.

## Measured (this Mac, 2026-10-11)
- **Scribe on a 10 s, two-voice `say` clip:** 787 ms direct and 720 ms through the app. Two speakers, labels only.
- **End to end:** stop tap → transcription → hub summary → sealed note shown on the other phone: 5.3 s. Gemma's line: "Friends enjoyed the beautiful view of the pond and geese together."

## Tests
- `apps/server/test/remember.test.ts`, properties with fast-check:
  - ready exactly when on, lit and every yes agreed;
  - any no makes it off for everyone;
  - a late joiner without consent makes it off;
  - the result never holds a member id, and doesn't depend on order;
  - recording only while ready and inside its 60 s.
  - Also covered: the transcript lines and the summary guard.
- `apps/server/test/contract.test.ts`: host-only on; consent; a no stops a recording; stop for everyone; the sealed note; 503 without ElevenLabs; no hub means no summary; 409 when not everyone agreed. No member id appears in any answer.
- `apps/web/test/e2e/remember.ts`, on the real stack with two phones:
  - the host turns it on and the friend agrees on their own phone;
  - the sign shows live on the other phone, and the friend stops it for everyone;
  - a real Scribe call and the real hub summary;
  - the note reaches the other phone with speaker labels and no names.
EOF

input.prompt:
You are the frontend engineer fixing a LIVE bug in Flare. Flare is a SvelteKit/Svelte 5 PWA in an npm-workspaces monorepo; the web app is apps/web, and the copy deck is design/prototype/src/lib/copy/deck.json, mirrored in docs/content/02-copy-deck.md. You are in a git worktree branched from main (commit 7792e2c or later). Commit on your branch often. Do NOT push, deploy, or merge. I (the lead) will merge.

THE BUG
The founder sent a real Flare by WhatsApp and opened it in Brave on an iPhone. The invite (apps/web/src/lib/screens/I1Invite.svelte) had a dim indoor photo, but only the top third of the screen showed the photo. The six-word headline sat right on it and the sheet covered the rest, so you couldn't see the place, which is the whole point of the photo. The send screens H2Develop.svelte and H3Send.svelte, and the shared apps/web/src/lib/components/PhotoPrint.svelte, have the same problem. No test caught it: every test used bright daylight photos on a full Safari viewport.

FIXES
1. The photo is the content. Text and the sheet never cover the main part of the image.
   - Show the photo at its natural aspect ratio in the top area. Cap its height sensibly so the main action (I'm in / Send) still fits on a 375x667 screen without scrolling, or with at most a small scroll.
   - Put the six words below the photo, or on a short gradient band at the photo's bottom edge only.
   - The sheet starts collapsed below the photo.
   - Tapping the photo opens it full screen. Use an accessible dialog with a 44 px close button, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the photo.
   - Apply the same rule on H2Develop and H3Send.
2. Dark photos. On the phone, draw the decoded photo onto a tiny canvas (for example 32x32) and measure its average luminance. If it's dark, for example a mean below ~0.35, brighten it FOR DISPLAY ONLY with a CSS filter, for example brightness(1.35) contrast(1.05), scaled to how dark it is. Never touch the sealed or uploaded photo bytes. Photos are blob or object URLs, so the canvas is same-origin. Guard against tainted canvases with try/catch. Put the logic in a small pure module with a unit test (vitest, like apps/web/test/flow/*.test.ts).
3. The "Your yes is private" chip (find it with grep in the deck and the screens): make it a single line at 375 px. Once someone closes it, it stays closed: store that in localStorage with a try/catch.
4. New gates, so the bug can't come back. Add a Playwright e2e script like the others in apps/web/test/e2e/ (look at how demo.ts or telegram.ts start the stack, and add an npm script e2e:photo-fit in the root package.json).
   - Test photos: a real dark indoor photo and a tall portrait photo. Look in the repo first (docs/credits/photos.md, apps/web/static, test fixtures). If there is no real indoor photo, make a dark version of a real public-domain photo that is already in the repo (with sharp or a canvas), label it honestly in the test as "darkened real photo", and say so in your report. Do NOT download anything from the internet.
   - Viewports: 390x664 (Brave or a WhatsApp in-app browser with a bottom bar), 375x667 (iPhone SE), and the current ones (390x844).
   - Overlap check: at first paint, compute the photo's bounding rect and the rects of every text element and of the sheet. Fail if their union covers more than 25% of the photo's area.
   - Run it on I1Invite (the friend's link page), H2Develop and H3Send.
   - Also check that the dark photo gets the display filter and that the stored or sent photo is unchanged.
   - Save before and after screenshots at 390x664 for invite, develop and send to docs/frontend/evidence/photo-fit/ (before = run the check on main's build first, after = yours).

RULES
- Writing rules for any copy: plain words, a number for every claim, no em dashes, buttons ≤3 words, UI messages ≤12 words, no "just". Banned words: seamless, leverage, robust, empower, unlock, elevate, delve, cutting-edge, revolutionize, game-changer, harness, synergy, holistic, paradigm, next-level, supercharge, effortless, ecosystem, tapestry, testament.
- Copy changes go through the deck JSON plus the md mirror. `node design/prototype/scripts/copy-lint.mjs` must report 0 problems.
- Don't change these strings: cond.didntCatch, compass.disclaimer, app.tier.hub, and anything about "Made on our laptop".
- Do NOT touch the invite.where, invite.whereWalk, lit.notice, push.lit or sms.lit templates, or the spot-naming code in host.svelte.ts. The lead is fixing "is at Near X" grammar there.
- Do NOT touch lab/, .env, or the untracked apps/web/static/scenic/ or the -640/-1280 files in apps/web/static/scenery/. Never stage them; use explicit git add paths.
- Never print secrets. .env is at <project>/flare/.env if the e2e needs it; read it only through the existing scripts.
- Another subagent (app-motion) is adding motion to the app on its own branch. Keep your edits to layout. Don't redo animations.
- Gates you must pass and report numbers for:
  - `cd apps/web && npx svelte-check --threshold warning`: 0/0
  - `npm run lint`
  - `npm test`
  - copy-lint 0
  - the existing e2e suites that cover these screens: at least demo, sparks, telegram and loop (see package.json)
  - axe 0 (whatever script the repo uses, e.g. the kit a11y e2e)
  - JS budget: /app and /g/ under 150 KB (the repo has a budget script; /app was 147.5 KB, so keep the additions tiny and lazy-load the full-screen viewer if needed)
  - Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

REPORT (short): commit hash(es), files changed, the overlap % per screen and viewport before and after, the gate results with numbers, the screenshot paths, and anything you couldn't do. Target: done within about 75 minutes. If time runs short, ship fixes 1 to 3 plus the overlap gate first.

input.message:
New detail from the founder: in Brave on an iPhone, neither the WhatsApp button nor the general Share button opened anything, so the cause is our code. The likely cause is that Send awaits the seal and the POST and only then calls navigator.share or opens the link, so WebKit has dropped the tap's activation and we swallow the NotAllowedError.

Fix:
- Create the Flare first. Then show a "Share" step where the tap calls navigator.share synchronously with the URL that's already ready.
- Never swallow an error. On any failure other than AbortError, show "Copy link" with a toast.
- Keep the Telegram-linked path as it is: there the server posts the card and no share sheet opens (flow.postedToTelegram on main).

Test in Playwright WebKit with a slow network (an await before share). In share-matrix.md, write down exactly what you verified and in which browser.

# Field test 1: the live app with real friends (Sun Oct 11, 2026, evening, Dearborn)

Only what was observed. The founder's screenshots are in the manager chat. Open questions are marked ASK.

## Setup
- The host (founder, as Fuego) on an iPhone, using Brave. Two real friends (Amor and one more) on their own phones. Live build b6fd014 or aee8348.
- The link went over WhatsApp Business, and the friends opened it in their browsers.

## Timeline
- 8:20 PM: the host sends a Flare: a photo of a dim indoor light, quorum 3 ("2 more to light it"). Gemma's invite: "Meet under the warm light". The invite shows "Fuego is at Near [street]."
- Before sending: both the WhatsApp button and the Share button did nothing in Brave. ASK: how the link was finally sent (copy and paste?).
- 8:22 PM: a friend types "After 10min, a quick visit works". The readback says "Got it: after 10 AM. Right?" The friend caught it on the readback.
- 8:24 PM: a friend types "10min only with you". The app answers "I didn't catch that. Try 'after 2' or 'only with Amor'."
- The friend types "in 10 minutes", which is accepted, and taps I'm in.
- The friends said yes. The host got no buzz. The audit shows 0 push subscriptions, so this device had no push.
- 8:36 PM, live audit (/api/v1/audit): pass. 1 gathering, 3 responses, 1 photo, 1 job, 1 Spark; 0 rows past their end.
- The deletion watch is running, to log when the gathering's rows reach 0.

## Bugs found (5), all sent to the build as top priority
1. On the invite and the send screens, the headline and sheet cover the photo, so you can't see the place. A dark photo makes it worse.
2. The "Near {street}" spot name flows into "{host} is at {spot}", giving "is at Near [street]".
3. The condition parser: "10min" (no space) read as a clock time; a bare hour took AM at 8 PM; "a quick visit" silently dropped.
4. The parser: "only with you" not understood. The hint examples didn't fit the moment ("after 2" at 8 PM, and possibly the reader's own name).
5. Sharing: neither the WhatsApp nor the Share button opened anything in Brave. Suspected cause: the tap's user activation is lost after an await.
6. The alert: "We'll buzz you when it's lit" is promised with no push subscription. An iPhone browser tab can't buzz.

## What worked
- WhatsApp to the invite page.
- The private count ("2 more to light it. Nobody sees who.").
- The readback caught the misread before it counted.
- "in 10 minutes" parsed.
- It lit. ASK: the time it lit.
- A Spark was left.
- The audit passes live.

## ASK the founder
- Did it light, and at what time? Did anyone meet in person? Was the compass or "I'm here" used?
- Did the host end it ("We're done"), and when? The deletion watch will measure from then.
- Each friend's one honest line, their OK to be quoted, and how they want to be named.

Status: live bugs 2, 3, 5 and the Near-X grammar are deployed (deploy started); live smoke is pending. Bugs 1 (photo) and 4 (share) are with two workers and not live yet.

- Bug 2/3, conditions (2751410, now live):
  - The friend's "After 10min, a quick visit works" at 8:22 PM read before as "Got it: after 10 AM. Right?". It now reads "Got it: you can come in 10 min. Right?", followed by "I didn't catch: a quick visit works".
  - "10min only with you" used to fail. It now reads "Got it: only with Fuego, you can come in 10 min."
  - All 9 delay forms from your list pass at 8:22 PM, 9 AM and 11:50 PM.
  - A bare hour now picks the next one coming: "after 10" at 8:22 PM is 10 PM, and at 9 AM it is 10 AM.
  - "with you", "if you're there", "you and me" and "only if you come" now mean the host.
  - When a parse fails, it shows tap-to-fill chips: "Come in 10 min", "Only if Fuego's there", "After 9 PM", "15 min walk max".
  - The hint uses examples from the time of day and the host. The fixed SRS-COND-8 string is unchanged in the deck and in parseError; only the on-screen line uses cond.didntCatchNow. Say if the founder wants SRS-COND-8 itself changed.
  - A fast-check property checks that a time never resolves before now.
  - blind_40 is 30/40 before and 30/40 after, so no regression. core 40/40, hard_20 20/20, fresh 40/40.
  - The friend's sentences sit in a new conditions-live test (10 tests) rather than in hard_20, so hard_20 stays a fixed 20.
- Bug 5, buzz (just deployed):
  - "We'll buzz you" now shows only when this device has a live push subscription with alerts granted.
  - Otherwise Sent says "Keep this open and the sound on." with the 2-step Home Screen install, or "Telegram will ping the group when it's lit." when the crew is linked.
  - Coming back to the tab shows "{n} friends said yes. It's lit." and plays the lit sound if audio was unlocked.
  - The tab title reads "It's lit · Flare" or "Waiting · Flare". setAppBadge is called on Home Screen installs.
  - A test checks the Sent line never says buzz without push.
- Bug 1, grammar part (live): every template now reads "Fuego is near [street]". That covers invite.where, invite.whereWalk, lit.notice, push.lit, sms.lit and the Telegram bot copy. A test runs a street, a park and a bench spot through all six.
- Bug 1, photo fit: with a worker (layout, dark-photo display filter, the private chip, the e2e:photo-fit overlap gate under 25% at 390×664 and 375×667). I'll send the 390×664 before/after shots when it's live.
- Bug 4, share: with a worker. It's fixing the activation loss: share is called synchronously in the tap once the Flare exists, there's a real wa.me anchor, a Copy link toast as the fallback, a WebKit slow-network test, and an honest share-matrix.md.
- Also live:
  - site-motion is merged (all 5 site pages Lighthouse 100, axe 0, /app 148.9 KB).
  - The automations are live: Again, Telegram direct send, and auto I'm here with Undo.
- Sounds of the spot: cut. No code was built. It now appears only as one row in the AI page's "Measured, not shipped".
- Field test 1 is copied to docs/research/field-test-1.md.
- app-motion is paused at 4119624. flame-gl.ts has been on main since FE1; it isn't new from app-motion. I'll check its diff against budget, trace and reduced motion when I merge.
- The "Since launch" counters are queued after bugs 1 and 4.

input.message:
LIVE: bug 6 (service worker) and bug 4 (share) are both in b924c32d85a7. /api/v1/health and the site footer both read "Build b924c32d85a7", and live smoke passes.

Bug 6 cause:
- The SW answered any precached path from its cache before looking at the network, and the prerendered "/" and "/how/" are precached, so pages were cache-first forever.
- A new SW also waited for a "Reload?" prompt that nothing ever showed.

Bug 6 fix:
- Navigations are now network-first with no timeout. The cache answers only when the network fails.
- skipWaiting on install, clients.claim on activate. An open page does a full load on its next in-app link, and a missing old chunk triggers a reload.
- New e2e:sw-update uses two real builds (N, then N+1 served from the same origin): one reload shows N+1's HTML, 32/32 of the JS that ran is N+1's, the new SW takes over in 1.8 s with no prompt, there are 0 missing chunks and 0 page errors, and offline still opens. 8/8 pass. e2e:pwa 19/19.

One-time step for the founder's and friends' phones:
- Open https://flare-outside.onrender.com, wait about 5 s, and reload once. The old worker fetches the new one, and the new one takes over at once.
- Check that the footer says "Build b924c32d85a7" (or newer).
- If it still shows the old home: Settings, then Safari (or Brave), then Advanced, then Website Data, delete the onrender.com entry, and open again.

Share (bug 4), live:
- Send no longer auto-shares after the await. Share is now the main button on Sent and is called synchronously in the tap, with no fetch between the tap and the call.
- Any error other than AbortError shows "Share did not open. Tap Copy link." and the button becomes "Copy link".
- WebKit plus Chrome e2e with a 1.5 s API delay: 27/27.
- Not tested on a real iPhone: the iOS share sheet, WA Business and Brave are listed as unverified in docs/frontend/evidence/share-matrix.md.

Lifetime answer: a Lit Flare ends by timer at created_at + 4 h (BR-F-5, engine LIT_CAP_MS), and the delete job runs 60 s after Gone. The 8:20 PM field-test Flare goes Gone at about 12:20 AM ET and should be deleted by about 12:21 AM, with the sweep as a backstop.

Next: merging bug 1 (photo fit). It needs a budget trim first, because /app is at 150.2 KB with the share fix and the photo fix adds 0.4 KB.

input.message:
New founder brief for "Why it matters". Your site-motion work is merged and live. Start a fresh branch from main b91c704 (rebase your worktree or create a new branch), and don't push or deploy.

DATA: use only the newest data, and verify every figure against its primary source.
1. BLS ATUS 2025 release, June 25, 2026 (USDL-26-1022, https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/atus_06252026.htm). Adults who socialized or communicated on an average day went from 38% (2015) to 30% (2025), and the time among those who did went from 41 to 35 min. Use the release's exact wording, and footnote its own caveat: no interviews from Oct 1 to Nov 12, 2025, because of the shutdown. If you can't read the page, because bls.gov blocked you before, say so and don't use the numbers from memory.
2. Our own 2003–2025 series from the ATUS multi-year microdata (time with friends; time outdoors away from home, TEWHERE).
   - This needs file downloads from bls.gov/tus/data.htm, and I don't have the founder's yes for downloads yet.
   - Don't download them. List the exact files you would need, with their sizes from the page, and I'll ask.
   - Meanwhile, keep the published Kannan and Veazie 2023 series for 2003–2020, labelled "latest published analysis", and don't extend it.
   - Drop the NHAPS indoor chart only if a verified replacement exists. Otherwise keep it, with its year shown plainly.
3. Loneliness: replace Gallup/Meta 2023 with the WHO Commission on Social Connection report of June 30, 2025: 1 in 6 people affected by loneliness, and about 871,000 deaths a year linked to it. Cite who.int, and read the figures there.
4. Keep White et al. 2019 (120 min a week), with its year in the label.

CHARTS: one clean system.
- Each title is the takeaway sentence.
- Lines carry direct labels at their ends; no legend.
- One accent colour (the flare) for the main series, grey for context, and at most 3 light gridlines.
- Label the 2020 dip "pandemic", and mark the latest point with its value.
- If the time-outdoors chart ships, make it a single 24-hour bar in minutes.
- Show 120 min as 8 blocks of 15 that fill like small flames on scroll: "Eight Flares make 120." It stays still under reduced motion.
- Each chart gets a small source line with a link, and a visually hidden data table.
- At 375 px, labels are at least 13 px and never overlap. Dark mode works.

GATES: Lighthouse 100 on all 5 pages (mobile and desktop), axe 0, copy-lint 0, svelte-check 0/0, npm test, the budget, and reduced motion still. Record every source and figure in docs/research/why-it-matters-sources.md.

content.text:
All six live bugs from tonight's field test are fixed, and live smoke passes on build 68afd9b. The founder's outdoor test can go ahead.

**Fixed and live:**
- **Old pages on returning phones:** the service worker served cached site pages forever and never let a new version take over. Pages now come from the network first, and a new version takes over at once. A test with two real builds passes 8/8, and the founder's iPhone shows the new build in the footer.
- **Photo covered:** text and the sheet covered 63–73% of the photo; now 0% on invite, develop and send, at three phone sizes. Dark photos are brightened on screen only; the stored photo is unchanged. A new end-to-end check guards it.
- **"After 10min" read as 10 AM:** delays like "10min" and "in 10" now work. A time with no AM/PM picks the next one coming, and "with you" means the host. Words the parser can't read are named back instead of dropped, and after a miss it offers rule chips to tap. The blind 40-sentence eval is 30/40 before and after, so no regression.
- **Share did nothing in Brave:** the share call came after the page waited on the server, so the browser no longer counted it as part of the tap. It now runs right on the tap, with a Copy link fallback. 27/27 checks pass in Chrome and WebKit. It's still not tested on a real iPhone or with WhatsApp Business.
- **"We'll buzz you" with no push:** that line now shows only when the phone really has alerts set up. Otherwise it says to keep the page open, or that Telegram will ping the group.
- **"Fuego is at Near [street]":** now "is near" in all six templates.

**Also live:**
- **Automations:** Again on Home; Telegram-linked Send posting directly; automatic "I'm here" within 30 m with a 10 s Undo.
- **Since launch:** six totals on the site, counting from 10:16 PM ET. Test traffic is excluded.
- **Merges:** both motion branches. The app's JS is 148.3 KB on /app and 147.9 KB on /g/, under the 150 KB budget.
- **Site:** the nav fits at 375 px, and the hero image was recaptured. Lighthouse scores 100 on all five pages, phone and desktop.
- **Tests:** 828 unit tests pass.

**Cut or off:**
- **Sounds of the spot:** cut. The lab found Gemma caught 8 of 12 voice clips at best, against a 100% bar. It appears only as a "Measured, not shipped" row on the AI page.
- **Remember this:** stays switched off.

**Post:** the reworked draft is on main at `docs/post/draft.md`: 1,713 words, about 185 left under the cap for the founder's sections, and 7 of 8 images. It doesn't claim anyone met in person yet.

**Still running:**
- **Fresh-eyes round 6:** a new tester with no context, using a dark photo and answering the WhatsApp-poll question.
- **"Why it matters":** the charts are being redone with the 2025 data.

**Needs the founder's yes:** our own 2003–2025 time-use series means downloading survey data files from bls.gov. Until then, the chart uses the published 2003–2020 numbers, labelled as the latest published analysis.
